* the GS on a thread of its own (`gs_thread.cpp`). To the EE the GS is a
  sink: the host answers CSR reads itself, and nothing it does comes back
  before the frame is shown. So the EE side writes each call that feeds it
  (a quadword from XGKICK, a run of PATH2 or PATH3 words, a privileged
  register) into a ring, and the GS thread makes the same calls in the same
  order - the GS model, the GPU bridge, the renderer's recording - while the
  EE, VIF1 and VU1 go on. At the end of a frame, before anything reads the
  GS (the picture, the GPU's frame, dumps), `SyncGs` waits for the ring to
  empty; a scripted run draws the same pictures. Timed sections are kept
  per thread, so the report's shares can add up to more than 100%.
  The car select from 23 s to 15 s; the race script from about 90 s to 56 s.

## VU microprograms compiled ahead of time

The vector units run microprograms the game uploads at run time (MPG), so
the analysis never sees them as code. A run records them instead:

```sh
burnout3.exe <elf> <run args> --vu-interpret --vu-record games/burnout3/build/vu_programs.txt
python engine/tools/port.py --game games/burnout3 build    # compiles what was recorded
```

`--vu-record` writes each program a run starts - the unit, the address and
the instruction pairs reachable from there - and the targets of jumps to a
register's address (JR, JALR), as programs of their own; runs add to the
file, and `--vu-interpret` makes sure every jump is seen by the interpreter.
The file holds the game's microcode: it stays in build/.

`port.py` hands it to `engine/tools/vurecomp.py`, which writes C++ into the
port's generated sources: each program as blocks of straight-line code (from
a branch target to the next delay slot), each instruction pair's registers,
fields and operation constants. What a pair does is the interpreter's own
steps (`ps2host::VuCore`, vu_core.h) - the stalls, the FMAC's and the
divider's latencies, the flags reaching the lower instructions four cycles
late, all of it - so a compiled program ends in the state the interpreter
would, to the cycle. `Vu::Run` takes a program compiled from the code now in
instruction memory (checked word for word: an MPG may have replaced it) and
the interpreter otherwise, and goes back to compiled code wherever a branch
lands on a block.

The interpreter stays the reference. `VuCompiledIsTheInterpreter` (host
tests) compiles 120 random programs as the build goes and runs each from six
random states both ways, comparing every register, flag, pipeline, cycle and
byte of data memory; delaying one result by a cycle fails it in 397 of 720
runs. The report's VU line says how many pairs ran compiled, how many
programs were entered and how many were found stale.

Since: what the compiled code does is still the interpreter's model to the
cycle (VuCompiledIsTheInterpreter compares every register, flag, pipeline
and cycle), but much less of it is done at run time. Each step was argued
sound and checked by that test and the scripted runs' pictures:

* a stall check that can never stall is left out: VF0; a field written four
  or more pairs before in the block (a pair takes a cycle at least, a result
  lands four after its issue); a field the block has not written, from its
  fourth pair (one written before the block lands by the entry cycle + 3);
* the MAC flags are found four lanes at once, and not cleaned again (every
  operation that sets them leaves clean fields);
* flags land lazily - when a lower instruction reads or sets them, the queue
  is full, or the run ends - which is what eager landing would have left;
* operands an earlier FMAC of the block left clean are not cleaned again
  (vurecomp tracks it field by field);
* a block keeps the cycle and the run's state in locals (MSVC re-read them
  from memory after every store), and runs whole or not at all - so its
  pairs check no limit, and an FMAC's flags that a later FMAC of the block
  (four or more pairs from its end) pushes over, with no flag instruction
  between, are never pushed: only STATUS's sticky bits are gathered;
* a program is compared with instruction memory only when it has been
  written since (an MPG or a store into it), not on every entry.

Building for AVX2 was tried: compiled programs then differ from the
interpreter in 4 of 720 random runs, so the port stays on SSE2.

The pairs macro mode shares (MOVE, MR32, MFIR, MTIR, DIV, SQRT, RSQRT;
OPMULA, OPMSUB, ITOF, FTOI, ABS) are VuCore steps of their own rather than
a trip through macro mode's COP2; the R register's few go that way still.

Burnout 3, the car select and the race recorded: 67 programs, 11,364 pairs;
every pair of either run compiled (428 million and 2.46 billion). The car
select 32 s to 24 s on the same build (`--vu-interpret` for the
comparison); the race script about 2 minutes.

### Fast mode (`--vu-fast`)

Most of a compiled pair's time went to the MAC and STATUS flags: the four
lanes' zero and sign bits, the sticky bits, and the queue they land through
four cycles later - about 30% of every pair. Few programs read them: of
Burnout 3's 70 VU1 programs, 40 never do, and the other 30 read MAC alone
(FMAND, FMOR), never STATUS. So vurecomp writes a second set of blocks for
each VU1 program that never reads or sets STATUS (`fast_drops`), in which an
FMAC computes no flags at all unless a MAC reader can see them: a walk of the
program from the pair after it - branches and delay slots as they run, the
FMAC's own pair taken as a delay slot too where a branch is before it - up to
where a later FMAC's flags have landed for certain (four pairs on), or the
program's end. A reader reached first, a jump to a register's address or
code not recorded keep the flags. The newest flags landed at any reader are
then always an FMAC's that kept them, and the cycles are the exact model's,
so every reader reads what it would have.

What it gives up: the flags a run leaves at its end, which a later run could
read before an FMAC of its own lands (the EE never reads VU1's flags; VU0
programs are always exact). `VuFastIsTheExactButFlags` (host tests) runs the
corpus's programs without STATUS readers both ways from random states -
every register, CLIP, Q, P, pipeline, cycle and byte of memory the same, the
flags different - and `regress.py --vu-fast` checks a scripted run's
pictures against the exact ones (it refuses `--update`).

Burnout 3: 5,841 of its 8,970 VU1 FMACs leave their flags out; `--vu-bench`
on 6,000 race runs 5.82 -> 4.93 ns a pair; VIF1's worker in the real-time
race ~71% -> ~60% busy; the car select, the training race and the race draw
every picture as the exact VU does.

## Code that exists only at run time

Some code is never where the analysis looks for it:

* **copied code** - start-up code keeps kernel extensions as data and copies
  them into kernel RAM (Burnout 3 installs three: the alarm services, and two
  more), then runs them there;
* **unreached code** - functions in the executable that no call reaches and no
  pointer table names: virtual methods, stored callbacks, tail-call targets.

The analysis recovers what it can of the second kind from the gaps between the
functions it found (`engine/ps2decomp/gaps.py`). For the rest, the host records
every call to an address with no translation whose bytes it finds in the
executable (`--discover`), and `port.py` translates that code at the address it
runs from and builds again, until a run finds nothing new. A call to a copy of a
function already translated runs that translation directly.

These translations are not verified - the interpreter never runs them - and the
generated source says so.

**Overlays** - code a game loads from its disc over free memory, several of them
at the same address in turn - are decompiled as games of their own
(ARCHITECTURE.md, *Overlays*) and listed in the game's `game.json`
(`"overlays": ["overlays/game", ...]`). port.py builds each overlay's
translations in a namespace of its own, and a table of its functions with the
first 16 bytes of each one's original code. A call into an overlay's range runs
the function of the overlay whose code is in memory there; a FlushCache, which
a program issues after loading code, makes calls look again.

## Overrides

`ps2host::Override(address, function, name)` replaces the guest function at an
address with a host implementation. It is the mechanism for:

* **hardware redirection** - library routines that drive the GS, VU1 or the IOP
  are replaced by host code that does the same job with the PC's facilities;
* **enhancements** - resolution, frame rate, input, widescreen: hook the
  function that decides it. A game's 2D that is built in packets the game
  keeps from frame to frame can be changed on its way to the GS instead:
  `SetPath2Filter` (run.h) hands the port each VIF1 DIRECT block as a copy,
  with the guest address it came from (Mister Mosquito's HUD in a wider
  picture: its vertices tagged where they are made, placed there).

Prefer overriding a whole library routine (`sceGsSyncV`, `sceSifCallRpc`) to
emulating the hardware it touches: the routine's contract is smaller than the
hardware's, and `names.csv` already identifies many of them. Routines every
game links - the SDK's - are overridden by name in the engine
(`engine/host/src/sdk.cpp`), wherever the game's names table gives that name,
so a new game gets them as soon as its routines are named.

## What the host provides, by stage

1. **Boot** (done): memory map with its mirrors (kuseg, kseg0, kseg1) and IOP
   RAM; ELF loading; dispatch; kernel services for start-up (SetupThread,
   SetupHeap, FlushCache); the syscall table in guest kernel RAM, so SetSyscall
   and programs that read or patch the table behave as on the console; DMA
   completing at once; GS vertical blank; the EE timers in host time, with
   their interrupts (`timers.cpp`).
2. **Threads** (done): EE threads as host fibers under the kernel's
   strict-priority scheduler; semaphores, sleep and wake-up block and resume.
3. **Interrupts** (vertical blank and DMA done): handlers run at a safe point,
   which is the running thread's next loop head (`lifted::loop_head_hook`) or
   between threads. Vertical blank comes 60 times a second in real time, or at
   once when every thread waits. INTC_STAT (0x1000F000) holds the causes
   raised since the game cleared them (writing 1 clears): libgraph's
   sceGsSyncV clears VBLANK_START and polls it; a port names that poll an
   idle loop (`AddIdleLoop`) so it is waited for asleep. DMA completion is posted by the transfer and
   delivered after the store that started it. Alarms (SetAlarm) run their
   callbacks at the first frame at or past their time.
4. **IOP services** (begun): the host answers the SDK's SIF commands as the
   IOP would (`iop.cpp`): RPC bind and call answered with RPC-end packets in
   the EE's receive buffer and the SIF0 DMA interrupt, run by the scheduler.
   Servers are host functions registered by id (`RegisterRpcServer`); a server
   with none still binds and its calls are noted with their callers, which
   names the library function behind each. CD/DVD (`cdvd.cpp`) reads the
   user's disc image (`disc.cpp`, ISO 9660, `--disc`). Also done: file I/O
   (`fileio.cpp`), module loading (`loadfile.cpp`: loads succeed and run
   nothing) and the controller manager's handshake (`dbc.cpp`). Servers for
   modules a game ships on its own disc belong to its port
   (`games/<g>/port/iop_servers.cpp`). Pads, sound and memory cards follow.
   DMA channels VIF0, VIF1 and GIF are walked (`dma.cpp`), chains included,
   and VIF1's stream is decoded (`vif.cpp`).
   **A game's own IOP modules run** in an R3000 interpreter (`iop_vm.cpp`).
   Each is loaded from the disc and relocated, and its imports are bound to
   the host's IOP libraries (`iop_libs.cpp`, by the numbers in
   `engine/data/iop_exports.csv`). Its threads run under the IOP kernel's
   scheduler, and its SIF commands go to and from the EE. The port names the
   modules to run: `ps2host::iop::RunModule("RWA.IRX")`. Prefer this to
   rewriting a module's protocol; sound drivers are the usual case. The iopheap
   server (`iopheap.cpp`) shares the interpreter's heap. `--iop-trace` logs
   every library call a module makes.
5. **Graphics** (begun): a software GS (`gs.cpp`, `gs_draw.cpp`,
   `gs_memory.cpp`) takes GIF packets from all three paths. It keeps local
   memory in the GS's own swizzled layouts and rasterises sprites, triangles
   and lines with texturing, fog, alpha, depth and destination alpha tests,
   blending and FBMSK, primitives queued and drawn in parallel bands of rows
   (each pixel still sees them in order). PATH3 waits while VIF1 masks it and
   goes one EOP-ended group per unmask, as the GIF lets it. The displayed
   picture goes to the window (`--window`) or BMP files (`--frames`). VU1 runs microprograms in an interpreter
   (`vu.cpp`). Its upper half goes through the runtime's verified VU0
   arithmetic; the pipeline timing microcode can see (stalls, Q/P latency,
   flags 4 cycles late, LOI's I read by the next bundle) is modelled, and
   `engine/tools/vuhazards.py` lists where a program depends on it. VIF1
   (`vif.cpp`) loads it with MPG and UNPACK and starts it with
   MSCAL, and its XGKICKs are PATH1; VU0 micro mode runs `vcallms`. The
   GPU renderer is under way: engine/docs/GPU.md.
6. **Audio** (begun): the SPU2 (`spu2.cpp`) decodes, envelopes and mixes its
   voices at 48 kHz, with the reverb libsd sets; `--audio` plays them and `--audio-wav` records them.
   **Input**: a DualShock 2 on the window's game controller (SDL3) and the keyboard (`dbc.cpp`). Then saves and
   enhancements.

7. **The IPU** (`ipu.cpp`): the MPEG decoder libmpeg drives, so a game's
   movies play. Registers IPU_CMD (BUSY in bit 63, VDEC's and FDEC's
   result), IPU_CTRL, IPU_BP (BP, IFC, FP) and IPU_TOP; the FIFOs at
   0x10007000/0x10007010; DMA channels 3 (FROM_IPU) and 4 (TO_IPU), which the
   generic "completed at once" handling leaves to it. The commands BCLR,
   BDEC, VDEC, FDEC, SETIQ, SETVQ, CSC, PACK and SETTH (IDEC is reported, not
   modelled), over the MPEG-1/2 VLC tables (`ipu_tables.inc`, generated
   from annex B) and an IEEE 1180 reference IDCT.
   * A command runs in steps (a header field, a macroblock), each all or
     nothing: it reads ahead through the FIFO and on into what channel 4 has
     yet to transfer - its source chain walked on a copy - and only a step
     that finishes takes the bits, MADR, QWC and TADR moving by the
     quadwords taken. A step that runs out of data waits, BUSY; what it
     changed is put back (the DC predictors), as it will run again.
   * Channel 4 keeps the FIFO full; restarted in a block, the tag it came
     from (CHCR's TAG field, kept as the hardware keeps it) says whether the
     chain ends after it - a `refe` fence does. libmpeg stops and restarts
     the channel around its other transfers and rewinds MADR by IFC + FP.
   * After a macroblock, BDEC goes over a slice's zero stuffing to the next
     start code and says so in SCD, as libmpeg expects.
   Checked against FFmpeg's decode of the same streams (games/burnout3
   FINDINGS, "Movies"): every picture of the boot movies within IDCT
   rounding.

Each stage is measured the same way: run, read the report, implement what
stopped it.

```

`gpu/CMakeLists.txt`:

```txt
# The port's display on the GPU: SDL3 for the window, input and events, Vulkan
# for the picture. Vulkan reaches every platform the port aims at - Windows,
# Linux and Android natively, macOS through MoltenVK - and gives the control a GS
# renderer needs; SDL3 hides each platform's window and input. Both come from
# their releases at configure time (FetchContent), so nothing is installed on
# the machine and nothing of theirs is committed.
#
# Stage one presents the software GS's picture (a copy and a scaled blit, no
# shaders). The GPU GS renderer builds on this device and swapchain.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(ps2gpu CXX C)

include(FetchContent)
set(FETCHCONTENT_QUIET ON)

FetchContent_Declare(vulkan_headers
    GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Headers.git
    GIT_TAG v1.4.363
    GIT_SHALLOW TRUE)
FetchContent_Declare(volk
    GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/zeux/volk.git
    GIT_TAG vulkan-sdk-1.4.363.0
    GIT_SHALLOW TRUE)
FetchContent_Declare(sdl3
    GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL.git
    GIT_TAG release-3.4.18
    GIT_SHALLOW TRUE)

set(SDL_SHARED OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(SDL_STATIC ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(SDL_TEST_LIBRARY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(SDL_EXAMPLES OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(VOLK_PULL_IN_VULKAN ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(vulkan_headers)
set(VOLK_HEADERS_ONLY OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(VULKAN_HEADERS_INSTALL_DIR "${vulkan_headers_SOURCE_DIR}" CACHE PATH "" FORCE)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(volk sdl3)

# Shaders: GLSL compiled to SPIR-V at build time by glslang, from its release
# like the others, and embedded as arrays (glslang --vn).
FetchContent_Declare(glslang
    GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang.git
    GIT_TAG vulkan-sdk-1.4.363.0
    GIT_SHALLOW TRUE)
set(ENABLE_OPT OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(ENABLE_HLSL OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(ENABLE_GLSLANG_BINARIES ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(GLSLANG_TESTS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(BUILD_TESTING OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(GLSLANG_ENABLE_INSTALL OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(glslang)

set(PS2GPU_SHADER_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/shaders)
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY ${PS2GPU_SHADER_DIR})
set(PS2GPU_SHADER_HEADERS)
foreach(shader gs.vert gs.frag date.vert date.frag swizzle.comp decode.comp depth_load.frag patch.comp fxaa.comp downsample.comp
               smaa_edges.comp smaa_weights.comp smaa_blend.comp)
    string(REPLACE "." "_" name ${shader})
    set(out ${PS2GPU_SHADER_DIR}/${name}.h)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${out}
        COMMAND glslang-standalone -V --target-env vulkan1.3 --vn spirv_${name}
                -I${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/third_party/smaa
                -o ${out} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/${shader}
        DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/${shader} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/gs_address.glsl
                ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/smaa_common.glsl ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/third_party/smaa/SMAA.glsl
                glslang-standalone
        COMMENT "glslang ${shader}")
    list(APPEND PS2GPU_SHADER_HEADERS ${out})
endforeach()
# The fragment shader without its second output, for devices without
# dual-source blending.
set(out ${PS2GPU_SHADER_DIR}/gs_frag_single.h)
add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${out}
    COMMAND glslang-standalone -V --target-env vulkan1.3 -DSINGLE_OUTPUT --vn spirv_gs_frag_single
            -o ${out} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/gs.frag
    DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/gs.frag glslang-standalone
    COMMENT "glslang gs.frag (single output)")
list(APPEND PS2GPU_SHADER_HEADERS ${out})
# The swizzle straight to and from a colour target (a storage image).
set(out ${PS2GPU_SHADER_DIR}/swizzle_image_comp.h)
add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${out}
    COMMAND glslang-standalone -V --target-env vulkan1.3 -DIMAGE --vn spirv_swizzle_image_comp
            -o ${out} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/swizzle.comp
    DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/swizzle.comp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/gs_address.glsl
            glslang-standalone
    COMMENT "glslang swizzle.comp (a target's image)")
list(APPEND PS2GPU_SHADER_HEADERS ${out})
# The texture decode straight into a texture's image (a storage image).
set(out ${PS2GPU_SHADER_DIR}/decode_image_comp.h)
add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${out}
    COMMAND glslang-standalone -V --target-env vulkan1.3 -DTO_IMAGE --vn spirv_decode_image_comp
            -o ${out} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/decode.comp
    DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/decode.comp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/gs_address.glsl
            glslang-standalone
    COMMENT "glslang decode.comp (into a texture's image)")
list(APPEND PS2GPU_SHADER_HEADERS ${out})
# ...and from a depth buffer, sampled.
set(out ${PS2GPU_SHADER_DIR}/swizzle_depth_comp.h)
add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${out}
    COMMAND glslang-standalone -V --target-env vulkan1.3 -DDEPTH_IMAGE --vn spirv_swizzle_depth_comp
            -o ${out} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/swizzle.comp
    DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/swizzle.comp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/gs_address.glsl
            glslang-standalone
    COMMENT "glslang swizzle.comp (a depth buffer)")
list(APPEND PS2GPU_SHADER_HEADERS ${out})
# ...and blending in the shader, from a copy of the target (a factor over 1).
set(out ${PS2GPU_SHADER_DIR}/gs_frag_blend.h)
add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${out}
    COMMAND glslang-standalone -V --target-env vulkan1.3 -DSHADER_BLEND --vn spirv_gs_frag_blend
            -o ${out} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/gs.frag
    DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/shaders/gs.frag glslang-standalone
    COMMENT "glslang gs.frag (blending in the shader)")
list(APPEND PS2GPU_SHADER_HEADERS ${out})
add_custom_target(ps2gpu_shaders DEPENDS ${PS2GPU_SHADER_HEADERS})

add_library(ps2gpu STATIC
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/src/vulkan_display.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/src/gpu.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/src/gs_renderer.cpp)
add_dependencies(ps2gpu ps2gpu_shaders)
target_include_directories(ps2gpu PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/include PRIVATE ${PS2GPU_SHADER_DIR}
                           ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/third_party/smaa)
target_compile_features(ps2gpu PUBLIC cxx_std_17)
target_link_libraries(ps2gpu PUBLIC SDL3::SDL3-static PRIVATE volk::volk Vulkan::Headers)
if(MSVC)
    target_compile_options(ps2gpu PRIVATE /W3 /Z7)        # symbols for --sample, as ps2host has
endif()

add_executable(ps2gpu_smoke ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/tests/display_smoke.cpp)
target_link_libraries(ps2gpu_smoke PRIVATE ps2gpu)
add_executable(ps2gpu_tests ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/tests/renderer_tests.cpp)
target_link_libraries(ps2gpu_tests PRIVATE ps2gpu)

```

`gpu/include/ps2gpu/display.h`:

```h
/*
 * The port's display: a window showing the console's picture, and the keyboard,
 * game controller and window events that come with it.
 *
 * Display is what the host talks to; VulkanDisplay (SDL3 + Vulkan) is the one
 * implementation so far. Stage one presents a finished picture - the software
 * GS's - scaled to the window; a GPU GS renderer will draw into the same
 * swapchain later.
 */

#ifndef PS2GPU_DISPLAY_H
#define PS2GPU_DISPLAY_H

#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace ps2gpu {

class Display {
public:
    virtual ~Display() = default;

    /* Shows a picture: 32-bit pixels, BGRA in memory (B first), rows top-down,
       scaled to the window. False when the window is gone. */
    virtual bool Present(const std::uint32_t* pixels, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) = 0;

    /* Shows a picture the GPU already has: the top-left width x height of a
       VkImage (on the display's own device, as its 64-bit handle), in
       `layout` (a VkImageLayout) and left in it, copied to the window on the
       GPU - no read-back, no upload. Whatever drew into it must have been
       submitted to the queue before. False when the window is gone, or a
       display cannot. */
    virtual bool PresentImage(std::uint64_t image, int layout, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) {
        (void)image, (void)layout, (void)width, (void)height;
        return false;
    }

    /* PresentImage, the picture shown at `due` (a steady_clock time, in
       nanoseconds since its epoch) rather than now: the image is copied at
       once (it may be drawn over next), and a thread of the display's shows
       it then - so pictures reach the screen evenly however unevenly they
       were finished. The newest picture wins: one not yet shown when the
       next comes is never shown. */
    virtual bool PresentImageAt(std::uint64_t image, int layout, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height,
                                std::uint64_t due_ns) {
        (void)due_ns;
        return PresentImage(image, layout, width, height);
    }

    /* Handles the window's events; false once it has been closed. Alt+Enter
       toggles fullscreen. */
    virtual bool Pump() = 0;

    /* How evenly pictures went to the screen since the last call (--frame-times):
       presents, and the time between them - mean, standard deviation and
       longest, in milliseconds. */
    struct Pacing { std::uint64_t presents = 0; double mean_ms = 0, jitter_ms = 0, longest_ms = 0; };
    virtual Pacing TakePacing() { return {}; }
    /* Pictures shown a second, over the last half second or so: the FPS
       counter's (F1), apart from TakePacing so it takes nothing from it. */
    virtual double PresentsPerSecond() const { return 0.0; }

    /* Vertical sync: each picture waits for the screen's refresh (no
       tearing, FIFO), or goes at once (IMMEDIATE, or MAILBOX where that is
       all there is). */
    virtual void SetVsync(bool on) { (void)on; }
    virtual bool Vsync() const { return false; }

    /* The window's height in the screen's pixels (0 when not known). */
    virtual std::uint32_t PixelHeight() const { return 0; }

    /* Fullscreen (borderless, the desktop's resolution) or a window. */
    virtual void SetFullscreen(bool on) { (void)on; }
    virtual bool Fullscreen() const { return false; }
    /* The picture's shape on the screen, width over height: 4:3 as a
       television showed it (the default), 16:9, or 0 - the window's own
       shape, filled. Letterboxed or pillarboxed in the window otherwise. */
    virtual void SetAspect(float aspect) { (void)aspect; }
    /* Anti-aliasing: the picture shown as drawn (the default); its edges
       smoothed (FXAA, or SMAA's three passes) before it is scaled to the
       window; or, drawn larger than shown (supersampling), averaged down to
       the shown size rather than scaled. */
    enum class AntiAliasing { kOff, kFxaa, kDownsample, kSmaa };
    virtual void SetAntiAliasing(AntiAliasing mode) { (void)mode; }
    /* The window's shape in the screen's pixels, width over height (0 when
       not known). */
    virtual float WindowAspect() const { return 0.0f; }
    /* A panel over the picture, at the window's top left: BGRA pixels
       (opaque), rows top-down; none when empty. */
    virtual void SetOverlay(std::vector<std::uint32_t> pixels, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) {
        (void)pixels, (void)width, (void)height;
    }
    /* The window's title (taken up by the window's own thread, in Pump). */
    virtual void SetTitle(const std::string& title) { (void)title; }
    /* F12, or L3 with R3 on a controller, since the last call: a capture asked for. */
    virtual bool TakeCapture() { return false; }
    /* Tab since the last call: the texture pack turned on or off. */
    virtual bool TakeTexturePackToggle() { return false; }
    /* F1 since the last call: the FPS counter turned on or off. */
    virtual bool TakeFpsToggle() { return false; }

    /* Whether the window has the keyboard, and whether a key is down - by SDL
       scancode (SDL_SCANCODE_*), which names keys by position. */
    virtual bool Focused() const = 0;
    virtual bool KeyDown(int scancode) const = 0;

    /* The first game controller, as a DualShock 2 reads: false when none is
       plugged in. */
    struct PadState {
        std::uint16_t buttons = 0;      // bit n: DualShock 2 input n held (libpad's order:
                                        // Select L3 R3 Start Up Right Down Left L2 R2 L1 R1
                                        // Triangle Circle Cross Square)
        std::uint8_t sticks[4] = {0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80};   // right X, Y, left X, Y; 0x80 centred
        std::uint8_t l2 = 0, r2 = 0;    // the triggers' travel, 0-255
        std::uint8_t family = 0;        // whose it is (its buttons' names): ControllerFamily
    };
    enum ControllerFamily : std::uint8_t { kOtherController, kPlayStationController, kXboxController };
    virtual bool Pad(PadState* state) const { (void)state; return false; }
    /* Every controller plugged in, in the order they were (SDL's id, the
       name it gives, its family) - and one's own state by its id: false when
       it is gone. */
    struct ControllerInfo {
        std::uint32_t id = 0;
        std::string name;
        std::uint8_t family = 0;
    };
    virtual std::vector<ControllerInfo> Controllers() const { return {}; }
    virtual bool PadOf(std::uint32_t id, PadState* state) const { (void)id, (void)state; return false; }
    /* The controller's motors, 0-65535 each (the low-frequency, large one;
       the high-frequency, small one), until set again - 0, 0 stops them.
       Taken up by the window's own thread (Pump). SetRumble sets every
       controller's, SetRumbleOf one's. */
    virtual void SetRumble(std::uint16_t large, std::uint16_t small) { (void)large, (void)small; }
    virtual void SetRumbleOf(std::uint32_t id, std::uint16_t large, std::uint16_t small) {
        (void)id, (void)large, (void)small;
    }
    /* The controllers SetTriggerEffects is for: none named, every one. */
    virtual void SetTriggerTargets(std::vector<std::uint32_t> ids) { (void)ids; }
    /* A controller's adaptive triggers (a DualSense's; others have none):
       off, a resistance from `start` (0-255 of the travel) of `force`
       (0-255), or a vibration from `start` of `force` at `frequency` (Hz),
       until set again. Taken up by the window's own thread (Pump), and
       again when a controller is plugged in. */
    struct TriggerEffect {
        enum Kind : std::uint8_t { kOff, kResistance, kVibration } kind = kOff;
        std::uint8_t start = 0, force = 0, frequency = 0;
        bool operator==(const TriggerEffect& o) const {
            return kind == o.kind && start == o.start && force == o.force && frequency == o.frequency;
        }
    };
    virtual void SetTriggerEffects(TriggerEffect left, TriggerEffect right) { (void)left, (void)right; }
    /* The controller left as it was found, at once (the game is ending):
       its motors stopped, its triggers' effects off. */
    virtual void ReleaseController() {}

    /* The mouse over the window, in the picture's terms: x and y from 0 to 1
       across the game's picture as it is shown (inside its letterbox; outside
       it they go past 0 or 1). `held` the buttons down (bit 0 left, 1 middle,
       2 right), `pressed` those that went down since the last call, `wheel`
       the notches turned since (up positive), `moved` whether it moved. */
    struct MouseState {
        bool over = false;              // the pointer is in the window
        float x = 0.0f, y = 0.0f;
        std::uint32_t held = 0, pressed = 0;
        float wheel = 0.0f;
        bool moved = false;
    };
    virtual bool TakeMouse(MouseState* state) { (void)state; return false; }
    /* The game's own mouse pointer: RGBA pixels (rows top-down), the point
       that clicks at (hot_x, hot_y); scaled with the window. Shown while
       ShowGameCursor(true) - otherwise the system's (hidden in fullscreen). */
    virtual void SetCursorArt(std::vector<std::uint32_t> rgba, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height,
                              std::uint32_t hot_x, std::uint32_t hot_y) {
        (void)rgba, (void)width, (void)height, (void)hot_x, (void)hot_y;
    }
    virtual void ShowGameCursor(bool on) { (void)on; }

    /* Told each picture PresentImageAt was given: shown (when it was due, when
       it was), or dropped unshown (shown_ns 0) - on the presenting thread. */
    using PresentObserver = std::function<void(std::uint64_t due_ns, std::uint64_t shown_ns, bool dropped)>;
    virtual void SetPresentObserver(PresentObserver observer) { (void)observer; }

    /* The GPU and driver, for the report. */
    virtual std::string Describe() const = 0;

    /* The window's device as a Gpu, for a GsRenderer to draw with: one
       Vulkan instance and device for both (owned by the display). */
    virtual class Gpu* SharedGpu() = 0;
};

/* A window with a Vulkan swapchain; null, with `error` saying why, when there is
   no Vulkan device or window to be had. */
std::unique_ptr<Display> CreateVulkanDisplay(const char* title, int width, int height, std::string* error);

}  // namespace ps2gpu

#endif  /* PS2GPU_DISPLAY_H */

```

`gpu/include/ps2gpu/gs_renderer.h`:

```h
/*
 * The GS on the GPU (engine/docs/GPU.md, stage two): primitives the host's GS
 * model has assembled, drawn with Vulkan into render targets that stand for
 * regions of the GS's local memory.
 *
 * Drawn so far: triangles - flat or Gouraud, scissored - textured or not, with
 * the GS's four texture functions, its alpha test, its blending and its depth
 * test, into 32-bit targets at the native resolution, which read back for
 * testing against the software GS (engine/host/src/gs_draw.cpp). Textures arrive decoded: the host
 * reads them out of local memory (swizzle, CLUT, TEXA) into RGBA and names
 * them with a key of its choosing. Depth is a 32-bit float buffer holding
 * Z / 2^32. The destination alpha test, fog and FBMSK are next.
 *
 * Colours are in the GS's terms throughout: 0-255 per channel, with 0x80 as
 * 1.0 where the GS multiplies (vertex colour against texture, alpha as a blend
 * factor).
 *
 * Gpu is the device without a window (tests, off-screen work); a Display's
 * device can stand in for it later.
 */

#ifndef PS2GPU_GS_RENDERER_H
#define PS2GPU_GS_RENDERER_H

#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace ps2gpu {

/* Told each time the CPU waited for the GPU (a command buffer's slot to come
   back): why, and from when to when (steady clock, nanoseconds) - for the
   host's profiler (PS2HOST_PROFILE). On the waiting thread. */
using GpuWaitObserver = void (*)(const char* why, std::uint64_t from_ns, std::uint64_t to_ns);
void SetGpuWaitObserver(GpuWaitObserver observer);

/* A Vulkan instance and device with one graphics queue (Vulkan 1.3: dynamic
   rendering). Opaque; created headless. */
class Gpu {
public:
    virtual ~Gpu() = default;
    virtual std::string Describe() const = 0;
};
std::unique_ptr<Gpu> CreateGpu(std::string* error);

/* A vertex as the GS has it after XYOFFSET: position in pixels (the GS samples
   at whole pixel coordinates), colour 0-255, and the texture coordinate as
   S/Q, T/Q over the texture's size (with UV, the host passes u / 16 / width,
   v / 16 / height and q = 1). */
struct GsVertex {
    float x, y;
    std::uint32_t z;
    std::uint8_t r, g, b, a;
    float s, t, q;
    std::uint8_t fog = 0xFF;            /* F: 255 keeps the colour, 0 is all FOGCOL */
};

/* TEX0.TFX: how the texel and the vertex colour combine. */
enum class TextureFunction : std::uint32_t { Modulate = 0, Decal = 1, Highlight = 2, Highlight2 = 3 };

/* ALPHA's operands: Cv = (A - B) * C / 128 + D. */
enum class BlendColour : std::uint32_t { Source = 0, Dest = 1, Zero = 2 };
enum class BlendAlpha : std::uint32_t { Source = 0, Dest = 1, Fix = 2 };

/* The state a batch of triangles is drawn with. */
struct GsDrawState {
    std::uint32_t fbp = 0, fbw = 1, psm = 0;            /* FRAME: the target */
    std::uint32_t fbmsk = 0;                             /* FRAME.FBMSK: bits not written */
    std::uint32_t width = 640, height = 448;            /* how much of it to make */
    std::int32_t scissor_x0 = 0, scissor_y0 = 0, scissor_x1 = 639, scissor_y1 = 447;   /* inclusive */
    bool gouraud = true;                                 /* else the last vertex's colour */
    /* A sprite (PRIM 6): on a target drawn larger, sampled where the GS
       samples - at its pixel's centre - not between (a 2D blit's strips met
       at seams of texels from beyond them). */
    bool sprite = false;
    /* A sprite (PRIM 6) at any internal resolution: what blends by the
       destination's alpha in the shader (ShaderBlend). */
    bool sprite_prim = false;

    /* Texturing (PRIM.TME): a texture uploaded under this key. */
    bool textured = false;
    std::uint64_t texture = 0;
    TextureFunction tfx = TextureFunction::Modulate;
    bool tcc = true;                                     /* TEX0.TCC: the texel's alpha counts */
    bool bilinear = false;                               /* TEX1: the four texels around */
    /* TEX1's mipmapping, per pixel (0: none - `bilinear` throughout): bit 1
       set, MXL in bits 2-4, MMIN 5-7, MMAG 8, LCM 9, L 10-11, K 16-27 (as
       TEX1 has them). A texture decoded with MXL + 1 levels holds levels 1
       and on below level 0 (GsTextureDecode). */
    std::uint32_t mip = 0;
    /* CLAMP: WMS/WMT 0 REPEAT, 1 CLAMP, 2 REGION_CLAMP (to MIN..MAX), 3
       REGION_REPEAT (MIN is a mask, MAX ORed in). */
    std::uint32_t wms = 0, wmt = 0, minu = 0, maxu = 0, minv = 0, maxv = 0;
    std::uint32_t tw = 0, th = 0;                        /* TEX0's size (0: the texture's own) */
    /* ...or a target sampled as the texture (render to texture): TEX0's TBP is
       the target's FBP * 32 and TBW its FBW. 24- and 16-bit texture formats
       read it as the GS would - TEXA's alpha, 16-bit colour to 5 bits. */
    bool texture_target = false;
    std::uint32_t tex_fbp = 0, tex_fbw = 0, tex_target_psm = 0;
    std::uint32_t tex_format = 0;                        /* 0 32-bit, 1 24-bit, 2 16-bit, 4 PSMT8H through the CLUT */
    std::uint32_t ta0 = 0, ta1 = 0x80;                   /* TEXA */
    bool aem = false;

    /* The alpha test (TEST.ATE, ATST, AREF, AFAIL). What a failing pixel
       writes: AFAIL 0 KEEP nothing, 1 FB_ONLY its colour (not depth), 2
       ZB_ONLY its depth (not colour), 3 RGB_ONLY its colour without alpha
       (not depth) - drawn as a second pass over the failing pixels. */
    bool alpha_test = false;
    std::uint32_t atst = 1, aref = 0, afail = 0;         /* ATST 1 is ALWAYS */

    /* The destination alpha test (TEST.DATE, DATM): a pixel is drawn only
       where the target's alpha bit (its alpha's top bit) equals DATM. */
    bool date = false;
    std::uint32_t datm = 0;

    /* Blending (PRIM.ABE) with ALPHA's operands and FIX. */
    bool blend = false;
    BlendColour a = BlendColour::Source, b = BlendColour::Dest, d = BlendColour::Dest;
    BlendAlpha c = BlendAlpha::Source;
    std::uint32_t fix = 0x80;
    bool pabe = false;                                   /* PABE: blend only where As >= 0x80 */

    /* Fog (PRIM.FGE): C = (F * C + (255 - F) * FOGCOL) / 256, colour only. */
    bool fog = false;
    std::uint32_t fogcol = 0;                            /* FOGCOL: R, G, B in bytes 0-2 */

    /* Depth (ZBUF, TEST.ZTE/ZTST): a depth buffer named by ZBP, as large as
       the target. ZTST 0 NEVER, 1 ALWAYS, 2 GEQUAL, 3 GREATER - the GS keeps
       the larger Z. Without `depth` nothing is tested or written. */
    bool depth = false;
    std::uint32_t zbp = 0, ztst = 1;
    bool depth_write = true;                             /* !ZBUF.ZMSK */
};

/* A texture in GS local memory, and how its texels expand: TEX0's TBP0 (in
   blocks), TBW, PSM and size, CLAMP's modes and region, TEXA, CSA, and the
   CLUT as the GS model holds it (256 RGBA entries; palettized formats). */
struct GsTextureDecode {
    std::uint32_t tbp = 0, tbw = 1, psm = 0, tw = 1, th = 1;
    std::uint32_t wms = 0, wmt = 0, minu = 0, maxu = 0, minv = 0, maxv = 0;
    std::uint32_t texa_lo = 0;      // TA0, and AEM at bit 15
    std::uint32_t ta1 = 0, csa = 0;
    /* Mipmap levels (1-7): level n, TW-n by TH-n from level_tbp[n] and
       level_tbw[n] (MIPTBP1/2), goes below level n-1 in the same image, at
       its left edge - the image tw wide, as tall as all of them. */
    std::uint32_t levels = 1;
    std::uint32_t level_tbp[7] = {}, level_tbw[7] = {};
    /* The CLUT as the GS model holds it, or null: the CLUT the GPU holds
       (ClutFromMemory, ClutRows) at this point of what is recorded. */
    const std::uint32_t* clut = nullptr;
};

/* A CLUT load (TEX0's CLD) from GS local memory, as the host's GS model does
   one: CBP (blocks), CPSM, CSA, an 8-bit texture's 256 entries or a 4-bit
   one's 16, 16-bit entries expanded by TEXA (TA0 and AEM at bit 15, TA1). */
struct GsClutLoad {
    std::uint32_t cbp = 0, cpsm = 0, csa = 0;
    bool eight = true;
    std::uint32_t texa_lo = 0, ta1 = 0;
};

class GsRenderer {
public:
    virtual ~GsRenderer() = default;
    /* The internal resolution: targets and depth buffers drawn `scale` times
       as large each way (1-4); textures, memory and everything read back
       stay in GS pixels. Changing it drops every target and depth buffer:
       what the GPU drew must be in local memory first; they come back from
       it. */
    virtual std::uint32_t Scale() const { return 1; }
    virtual void SetScale(std::uint32_t scale) { (void)scale; }
    /* A texture, RGBA in memory (alpha as the GS has it, 0x80 is 1.0), rows
       top-down. Replaces what the key named. */
    virtual void UploadTexture(std::uint64_t key, const std::uint32_t* pixels, std::uint32_t width,
                               std::uint32_t height) = 0;
    /* A texture pack's replacement: an image of its own under `id`, shared by
       every texture it replaces. `format` 0 RGBA8 (alpha as the GS's: 0x80
       is 1.0), 1-4 BC1, BC2, BC3, BC7 as a DDS stores them; `levels` (mipmap
       levels) largest first, one after another in `data`. False if the GPU
       cannot take it (block compression it lacks). Replacements the draws
       have not used for a while go when they take more than a budget of
       GPU memory: HasReplacement says whether one is still there. */
    virtual bool UploadReplacement(std::uint64_t id, std::uint32_t format, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height,
                                   std::uint32_t levels, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t bytes) {
        (void)id, (void)format, (void)width, (void)height, (void)levels, (void)data, (void)bytes;
        return false;
    }
    virtual bool HasReplacement(std::uint64_t id) const { (void)id; return false; }
    /* The texture under `key` drawn as replacement `id`: finer than the GS's
       TW x TH (the draw's tw, th), sampled in its own texels at the same
       places. Until the key is uploaded or decoded again. */
    virtual void UseReplacement(std::uint64_t key, std::uint64_t id) { (void)key, (void)id; }
    /* Whether block-compressed replacements can be uploaded as they are. */
    virtual bool BlockCompression() const { return false; }
    /* A depth buffer's contents, one Z per pixel, rows top-down: what local
       memory holds there (the GS's Z, unsigned). */
    virtual void UploadDepth(std::uint32_t zbp, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height,
                             const std::uint32_t* z) = 0;
    /* A target's contents from local memory, RGBA rows top-down (made, at
       this size, if there was none). */
    virtual void UploadTarget(std::uint32_t fbp, std::uint32_t fbw, std::uint32_t psm, const std::uint32_t* pixels,
                              std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height) = 0;
    /* Forgets a texture (after what is recorded has used it). */
    virtual void ReleaseTexture(std::uint64_t key) = 0;
    /* Whether a target exists for (FBP, FBW, PSM) - what a draw can sample. */
    virtual bool HasTarget(std::uint32_t fbp, std::uint32_t fbw, std::uint32_t psm) const = 0;
    /* Triangles, three vertices each, in GS order. */
    virtual void DrawTriangles(const GsDrawState& state, const GsVertex* vertices, std::size_t count) = 0;
    /* Runs what has been drawn. */
    virtual void Flush() = 0;
    /* Hands what has been recorded to the GPU without waiting for it (once a
       frame, say), so that the GPU draws while the CPU goes on rather than
       all at once when something next waits. */
    virtual void Kick() {}
    /* GS local memory on the GPU: 4 MB, as the GS lays it out, which targets
       and depth buffers are swizzled into and out of without the CPU. Blocks
       are 256 bytes; [begin, end) in blocks. Nothing waits but MemoryRead. */
    /* The CPU's copy of blocks, into the GPU's. */
    virtual void MemoryWrite(std::uint32_t begin, std::uint32_t end, const std::uint8_t* bytes) = 0;
    /* The GPU's copy of blocks, into `bytes` (runs what is recorded, waits). */
    virtual void MemoryRead(std::uint32_t begin, std::uint32_t end, std::uint8_t* bytes) = 0;
    /* Words of the GPU's copy patched under masks - `count` of (word index,
       value, mask), the mask's bits set taken from the value - in turn with
       what is recorded, nothing waiting: part of a block written over what
       the GPU drew there, without bringing it back. */
    virtual void MemoryPatch(const std::uint32_t* words, std::size_t count) { (void)words, (void)count; }
    /* A target's rows [first_row, rows), `cols` wide, into GPU memory at FBP
       as its PSM lays them out (CT32, CT24, CT16, CT16S); false if there is
       none. */
    virtual bool TargetToMemory(std::uint32_t fbp, std::uint32_t fbw, std::uint32_t psm, std::uint32_t cols,
                                std::uint32_t rows, std::uint32_t first_row = 0) = 0;
    /* A target, made at this size if there is none, loaded from GPU memory. */
    virtual void TargetFromMemory(std::uint32_t fbp, std::uint32_t fbw, std::uint32_t psm, std::uint32_t width,
                                  std::uint32_t height) = 0;
    /* The same for the depth buffer at ZBP of this size, laid out by ZPSM
       (Z32, Z24, Z16, Z16S) FBW pages wide. */
    virtual bool DepthToMemory(std::uint32_t zbp, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height, std::uint32_t fbw,
                               std::uint32_t zpsm, std::uint32_t cols, std::uint32_t rows,
                               std::uint32_t first_row = 0) = 0;
    virtual void DepthFromMemory(std::uint32_t zbp, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height, std::uint32_t fbw,
                                 std::uint32_t zpsm) = 0;
    /* A texture decoded from GPU memory, as the host's software GS decodes
       one (GsTextureDecode); replaces what the key named. */
    virtual void TextureFromMemory(std::uint64_t key, const GsTextureDecode& decode) = 0;
    /* The GPU's CLUT - the 256 RGBA entries textures decoded on the GPU with
       no CLUT of their own read - loaded from GPU memory, in order with what
       is recorded: a CLUT the GPU drew never waits to come back. */
    virtual void ClutFromMemory(const GsClutLoad& load) = 0;
    /* Rows of the GPU's CLUT (16 entries each; bit r of `rows` for row r)
       from the host's copy, `clut` being all 256 entries. */
    virtual void ClutRows(const std::uint32_t* clut, std::uint32_t rows) = 0;
    /* A depth buffer's Z (the GS's, unsigned), rows top-down; false if there
       is none of that size. */
    virtual bool ReadDepth(std::uint32_t zbp, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height,
                           std::vector<std::uint32_t>* z) = 0;
    /* A texture's texels, RGBA, rows top-down; false if there is none. */
    virtual bool ReadTexture(std::uint64_t key, std::vector<std::uint32_t>* pixels, std::uint32_t* width,
                             std::uint32_t* height) = 0;
    /* A target to show as it is on the GPU (Display::PresentImage): what has
       been drawn is handed to the GPU first, and the target's image (its
       64-bit handle), its layout (a VkImageLayout) and size are given; false
       if there is none or it has not been drawn. */
    /* For the TargetFromMemory / TargetRowsFromMemory calls that follow: an
       image drawn larger (the internal resolution) keeps its own colour
       where memory differs from it in alpha alone - another view's write
       into its alpha (Burnout 3's depth into the frame's alpha, through a
       16-bit view) leaves the picture as fine as it was drawn, rather than
       as memory holds it (a GS pixel a square). Where the colour differs,
       memory's, as ever. */
    virtual void ReloadKeepsColour(bool keep) { (void)keep; }
    /* TargetFromMemory / DepthFromMemory for rows [first_row, first_row +
       rows) alone (the rest of the image as it is). */
    virtual void TargetRowsFromMemory(std::uint32_t fbp, std::uint32_t fbw, std::uint32_t psm, std::uint32_t width,
                                      std::uint32_t height, std::uint32_t first_row, std::uint32_t rows) {
        (void)first_row, (void)rows;
        TargetFromMemory(fbp, fbw, psm, width, height);
    }
    virtual void DepthRowsFromMemory(std::uint32_t zbp, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height, std::uint32_t fbw,
                                     std::uint32_t zpsm, std::uint32_t first_row, std::uint32_t rows) {
        (void)first_row, (void)rows;
        DepthFromMemory(zbp, width, height, fbw, zpsm);
    }
    virtual bool DisplayTarget(std::uint32_t fbp, std::uint32_t fbw, std::uint32_t psm, std::uint64_t* image,
                               int* layout, std::uint32_t* width, std::uint32_t* height) {
        (void)fbp, (void)fbw, (void)psm, (void)image, (void)layout, (void)width, (void)height;
        return false;
    }
    /* A target's pixels, RGBA in memory, rows top-down; false if there is none. */
    virtual bool ReadTarget(std::uint32_t fbp, std::uint32_t fbw, std::uint32_t psm,
                            std::vector<std::uint32_t>* pixels, std::uint32_t* width,
                            std::uint32_t* height) = 0;
    /* The same at the internal resolution, every pixel (a capture). */
    virtual bool ReadTargetFull(std::uint32_t fbp, std::uint32_t fbw, std::uint32_t psm,
                                std::vector<std::uint32_t>* pixels, std::uint32_t* width, std::uint32_t* height) {
        return ReadTarget(fbp, fbw, psm, pixels, width, height);
    }
};
std::unique_ptr<GsRenderer> CreateGsRenderer(Gpu& gpu, std::string* error);
/* Where the renderer keeps what it learns between runs: a folder (the PC
   settings'), for its pipeline cache (gpu_pipeline_cache.bin) and the
   pipelines the game has drawn with (gpu_pipelines.txt) - made again at the
   start, from the cache, so none is built in the middle of a race. Set
   before CreateGsRenderer; "" (a scripted run) keeps nothing. */
void SetPipelineCacheDir(const std::string& dir);
/* Pipelines a game is known to draw with (keys as gpu_pipelines.txt has
   them), made by the renderer's worker from the start as the last runs'
   are - a player's first run then makes none in the middle of a race. Keys
   of an older engine are only made in vain. Set before CreateGsRenderer. */
void SetPipelineHints(const std::uint32_t* keys, std::size_t count);

/* How often the CPU has waited for the GPU to finish what was submitted, and
   for how long in all: "N submissions, S s waiting". */
std::string SubmitStats();
/* What went into the command buffers since the last call: barriers, layout
   transitions, compute dispatches, draws, rendering passes, feedback copies. */
std::string RendererCounters();
/* The GPU's time on the frames' command buffers, in all (nanoseconds; 0
   where the GPU keeps no time). */
std::uint64_t GpuBusyNanoseconds();
/* PS2HOST_GPU_PROFILE: the GPU's time since the last call, by what it did. */
std::string GpuProfileReport();

}  // namespace ps2gpu

#endif  /* PS2GPU_GS_RENDERER_H */

// The destination alpha test's setup pass: where the target's alpha bit (the
// top bit of its alpha, 0x80 and up) equals DATM, the pixel survives and the
// stencil is set; the draw that follows is tested against it.

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D target;

layout(push_constant) uniform Params {
    layout(offset = 16) uint datm;
} p;

void main() {
    float alpha = texelFetch(target, ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy), 0).a * 255.0;
    uint bit = alpha >= 127.5 ? 1u : 0u;
    if (bit != p.datm) discard;
}
