```comp
#version 450
// A texture decoded from GS local memory on the GPU, texel for texel as the
// host's software GS decodes one (engine/host/src/gs_draw.cpp, TexelAt): the
// coordinates wrapped by CLAMP's mode (the region modes at decode time), the
// texel read in its format's layout (gs_memory.cpp's tables), then expanded:
// TEXA for 24- and 16-bit texels, the CLUT for palettized ones. Z formats
// read as their CT counterparts. Out: RGBA, rows top-down, tw wide - or,
// built with TO_IMAGE, straight into the texture's image (a storage image,
// set 1), the level's rows from row0: no staging buffer, no copy, and no
// barrier between a texture's levels (their rows are their own).

layout(local_size_x = 8, local_size_y = 8) in;

layout(std430, binding = 0) readonly buffer Memory { uint mem[]; };
layout(std430, binding = 1) writeonly buffer Linear { uint lin[]; };
layout(std430, binding = 2) buffer Clut { uint clut[256]; };
// The layout tables below, copied once into a buffer (mode 2, at start) and
// read from there texel by texel: a constant array indexed at run time is
// copied into each invocation's own memory on some GPUs (Intel's: decodes
// were more than half its frame), a buffer is read through the cache.
layout(std430, binding = 3) buffer Tables { uint tables[768]; };
#ifdef TO_IMAGE
layout(set = 1, binding = 0, rgba8) uniform writeonly image2D dst;
#endif

layout(push_constant) uniform Params {
    uint tbp, tbw, psm, tw, th;
    uint wms, wmt, minu, maxu, minv, maxv;
    uint texa_lo;       // TA0 (bits 0-7), AEM (bit 15)
    uint ta1;
    uint csa;
    uint mode;          // 0 a texture decoded; 1 a CLUT loaded (below); 2 the tables copied
    uint row0;          // TO_IMAGE: the level's first row in the image
} p;

const uint PSMCT32 = 0x00u, PSMCT24 = 0x01u, PSMCT16 = 0x02u, PSMCT16S = 0x0Au;
const uint PSMT8 = 0x13u, PSMT4 = 0x14u, PSMT8H = 0x1Bu, PSMT4HL = 0x24u, PSMT4HH = 0x2Cu;
const uint PSMZ32 = 0x30u, PSMZ24 = 0x31u, PSMZ16 = 0x32u, PSMZ16S = 0x3Au;

const uint kBlock32[32] = uint[](0, 1, 4, 5, 16, 17, 20, 21, 2, 3, 6, 7, 18, 19, 22, 23,
                                 8, 9, 12, 13, 24, 25, 28, 29, 10, 11, 14, 15, 26, 27, 30, 31);
const uint kBlockZ32[32] = uint[](24, 25, 28, 29, 8, 9, 12, 13, 26, 27, 30, 31, 10, 11, 14, 15,
                                  16, 17, 20, 21, 0, 1, 4, 5, 18, 19, 22, 23, 2, 3, 6, 7);
const uint kBlock16[32] = uint[](0, 2, 8, 10, 1, 3, 9, 11, 4, 6, 12, 14, 5, 7, 13, 15,
                                 16, 18, 24, 26, 17, 19, 25, 27, 20, 22, 28, 30, 21, 23, 29, 31);
const uint kBlock16S[32] = uint[](0, 2, 16, 18, 1, 3, 17, 19, 8, 10, 24, 26, 9, 11, 25, 27,
                                  4, 6, 20, 22, 5, 7, 21, 23, 12, 14, 28, 30, 13, 15, 29, 31);
const uint kBlockZ16[32] = uint[](24, 26, 16, 18, 25, 27, 17, 19, 28, 30, 20, 22, 29, 31, 21, 23,
                                  8, 10, 0, 2, 9, 11, 1, 3, 12, 14, 4, 6, 13, 15, 5, 7);
const uint kBlockZ16S[32] = uint[](24, 26, 8, 10, 25, 27, 9, 11, 16, 18, 0, 2, 17, 19, 1, 3,
                                   28, 30, 12, 14, 29, 31, 13, 15, 20, 22, 4, 6, 21, 23, 5, 7);
const uint kColumn32[64] = uint[](0, 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13, 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 14, 15,
                                  16, 17, 20, 21, 24, 25, 28, 29, 18, 19, 22, 23, 26, 27, 30, 31,
                                  32, 33, 36, 37, 40, 41, 44, 45, 34, 35, 38, 39, 42, 43, 46, 47,
                                  48, 49, 52, 53, 56, 57, 60, 61, 50, 51, 54, 55, 58, 59, 62, 63);
const uint kColumn16[128] = uint[](
    0, 2, 8, 10, 16, 18, 24, 26, 1, 3, 9, 11, 17, 19, 25, 27,
    4, 6, 12, 14, 20, 22, 28, 30, 5, 7, 13, 15, 21, 23, 29, 31,
    32, 34, 40, 42, 48, 50, 56, 58, 33, 35, 41, 43, 49, 51, 57, 59,
    36, 38, 44, 46, 52, 54, 60, 62, 37, 39, 45, 47, 53, 55, 61, 63,
    64, 66, 72, 74, 80, 82, 88, 90, 65, 67, 73, 75, 81, 83, 89, 91,
    68, 70, 76, 78, 84, 86, 92, 94, 69, 71, 77, 79, 85, 87, 93, 95,
    96, 98, 104, 106, 112, 114, 120, 122, 97, 99, 105, 107, 113, 115, 121, 123,
    100, 102, 108, 110, 116, 118, 124, 126, 101, 103, 109, 111, 117, 119, 125, 127);
const uint kColumn8[128] = uint[](
    0, 4, 16, 20, 32, 36, 48, 52, 2, 6, 18, 22, 34, 38, 50, 54,
    8, 12, 24, 28, 40, 44, 56, 60, 10, 14, 26, 30, 42, 46, 58, 62,
    33, 37, 49, 53, 1, 5, 17, 21, 35, 39, 51, 55, 3, 7, 19, 23,
    41, 45, 57, 61, 9, 13, 25, 29, 43, 47, 59, 63, 11, 15, 27, 31,
    96, 100, 112, 116, 64, 68, 80, 84, 98, 102, 114, 118, 66, 70, 82, 86,
    104, 108, 120, 124, 72, 76, 88, 92, 106, 110, 122, 126, 74, 78, 90, 94,
    65, 69, 81, 85, 97, 101, 113, 117, 67, 71, 83, 87, 99, 103, 115, 119,
    73, 77, 89, 93, 105, 109, 121, 125, 75, 79, 91, 95, 107, 111, 123, 127);
const uint kColumn4[256] = uint[](
    0, 8, 32, 40, 64, 72, 96, 104, 2, 10, 34, 42, 66, 74, 98, 106,
    4, 12, 36, 44, 68, 76, 100, 108, 6, 14, 38, 46, 70, 78, 102, 110,
    16, 24, 48, 56, 80, 88, 112, 120, 18, 26, 50, 58, 82, 90, 114, 122,
    20, 28, 52, 60, 84, 92, 116, 124, 22, 30, 54, 62, 86, 94, 118, 126,
    65, 73, 97, 105, 1, 9, 33, 41, 67, 75, 99, 107, 3, 11, 35, 43,
    69, 77, 101, 109, 5, 13, 37, 45, 71, 79, 103, 111, 7, 15, 39, 47,
    81, 89, 113, 121, 17, 25, 49, 57, 83, 91, 115, 123, 19, 27, 51, 59,
    85, 93, 117, 125, 21, 29, 53, 61, 87, 95, 119, 127, 23, 31, 55, 63,
    192, 200, 224, 232, 128, 136, 160, 168, 194, 202, 226, 234, 130, 138, 162, 170,
    196, 204, 228, 236, 132, 140, 164, 172, 198, 206, 230, 238, 134, 142, 166, 174,
    208, 216, 240, 248, 144, 152, 176, 184, 210, 218, 242, 250, 146, 154, 178, 186,
    212, 220, 244, 252, 148, 156, 180, 188, 214, 222, 246, 254, 150, 158, 182, 190,
    129, 137, 161, 169, 193, 201, 225, 233, 131, 139, 163, 171, 195, 203, 227, 235,
    133, 141, 165, 173, 197, 205, 229, 237, 135, 143, 167, 175, 199, 207, 231, 239,
    145, 153, 177, 185, 209, 217, 241, 249, 147, 155, 179, 187, 211, 219, 243, 251,
    149, 157, 181, 189, 213, 221, 245, 253, 151, 159, 183, 191, 215, 223, 247, 255);

const uint kMask = (4u << 20) - 1u;

// Where each table is in the buffer (mode 2 writes them there in this order).
const uint kAtBlock32 = 0u, kAtBlockZ32 = 32u, kAtBlock16 = 64u, kAtBlock16S = 96u, kAtBlockZ16 = 128u,
           kAtBlockZ16S = 160u, kAtColumn32 = 192u, kAtColumn16 = 256u, kAtColumn8 = 384u, kAtColumn4 = 512u;

void CopyTables() {
    const uint i = gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
    if (gl_GlobalInvocationID.y != 0u || i >= 768u) return;
    uint v;
    if (i < 32u) v = kBlock32[i];
    else if (i < 64u) v = kBlockZ32[i - 32u];
    else if (i < 96u) v = kBlock16[i - 64u];
    else if (i < 128u) v = kBlock16S[i - 96u];
    else if (i < 160u) v = kBlockZ16[i - 128u];
    else if (i < 192u) v = kBlockZ16S[i - 160u];
    else if (i < 256u) v = kColumn32[i - 192u];
    else if (i < 384u) v = kColumn16[i - 256u];
    else if (i < 512u) v = kColumn8[i - 384u];
    else v = kColumn4[i - 512u];
    tables[i] = v;
}

uint Page(uint ppr, uint px, uint py) { return p.tbp + 32u * (py * max(ppr, 1u) + px); }

uint Byte(uint a) { return (mem[a >> 2] >> ((a & 3u) * 8u)) & 0xFFu; }

// The texel at (x, y), raw, as the format stores it.
uint Raw(uint x, uint y) {
    const uint psm = p.psm;
    if (psm == PSMT8) {
        const uint block = Page(p.tbw / 2u, x / 128u, y / 64u) + tables[kAtBlock32 + ((y % 64u) / 16u) * 8u + (x % 128u) / 16u];
        const uint row = y % 16u;
        return Byte((block * 256u + tables[kAtColumn8 + (row % 8u) * 16u + x % 16u] + (row >= 8u ? 128u : 0u)) & kMask);
    }
    if (psm == PSMT4) {
        const uint block = Page(p.tbw / 2u, x / 128u, y / 128u) + tables[kAtBlock16 + ((y % 128u) / 16u) * 4u + (x % 128u) / 32u];
        const uint row = y % 16u;
        const uint index = tables[kAtColumn4 + (row % 8u) * 32u + x % 32u] + (row >= 8u ? 256u : 0u);
        const uint b = Byte((block * 256u + index / 2u) & kMask);
        return (index & 1u) != 0u ? b >> 4 : b & 15u;
    }
    if (psm == PSMCT16 || psm == PSMCT16S || psm == PSMZ16 || psm == PSMZ16S) {
        const uint i = ((y % 64u) / 8u) * 4u + (x % 64u) / 16u;
        const uint at = psm == PSMCT16 ? kAtBlock16 : psm == PSMCT16S ? kAtBlock16S : psm == PSMZ16 ? kAtBlockZ16 : kAtBlockZ16S;
        const uint b = tables[at + i];
        const uint a = ((Page(p.tbw, x / 64u, y / 64u) + b) * 256u + tables[kAtColumn16 + (y % 8u) * 16u + x % 16u] * 2u) & kMask;
        return (mem[a >> 2] >> ((a & 2u) * 8u)) & 0xFFFFu;
    }
    // The 32-bit layouts: CT32, CT24, Z32, Z24, and T8H/T4HL/T4HH in CT32's top byte.
    const uint i = ((y % 32u) / 8u) * 8u + (x % 64u) / 8u;
    const uint b = tables[((psm == PSMZ32 || psm == PSMZ24) ? kAtBlockZ32 : kAtBlock32) + i];
    const uint a = ((Page(p.tbw, x / 64u, y / 32u) + b) * 256u + tables[kAtColumn32 + (y % 8u) * 8u + x % 8u] * 4u) & kMask;
    const uint w = mem[a >> 2];
    if (psm == PSMT8H) return w >> 24;
    if (psm == PSMT4HL) return (w >> 24) & 15u;
    if (psm == PSMT4HH) return w >> 28;
    return w;
}

uint Wrap(int i, uint size, uint mode, uint lo, uint hi) {
    if (mode == 0u) return uint(i) & (size - 1u);
    if (mode == 1u) return uint(clamp(i, 0, int(size) - 1));
    if (mode == 2u) return uint(clamp(i, int(lo), int(hi)));
    return (uint(i) & lo) | hi;
}

// A texel as the GS expands it: TEXA for 24- and 16-bit texels, the CLUT for
// palettized ones.
uint Expand(uint raw) {
    const uint psm = p.psm;
    const uint ta0 = p.texa_lo & 0xFFu;
    const bool aem = (p.texa_lo & 0x8000u) != 0u;
    if (psm == PSMT8 || psm == PSMT8H) return clut[raw & 0xFFu];
    if (psm == PSMT4 || psm == PSMT4HL || psm == PSMT4HH) return clut[(p.csa * 16u + (raw & 15u)) & 0xFFu];
    if (psm == PSMCT24 || psm == PSMZ24) {
        const uint rgb = raw & 0xFFFFFFu;
        return rgb | ((aem && rgb == 0u) ? 0u : ta0) << 24;
    }
    if (psm == PSMCT16 || psm == PSMCT16S || psm == PSMZ16 || psm == PSMZ16S) {
        const uint a = (raw & 0x8000u) != 0u ? p.ta1 : ((aem && (raw & 0x7FFFu) == 0u) ? 0u : ta0);
        return ((raw & 31u) << 3) | (((raw >> 5) & 31u) << 11) | (((raw >> 10) & 31u) << 19) | (a << 24);
    }
    return raw;
}

// Mode 1: a CLUT load (TEX0's CLD), as the host's Gs::LoadClut does one, from
// the GPU's copy of local memory: tbp is CBP, tbw 1, psm CPSM (CT32, CT16,
// CT16S), tw the entries (256 for an 8-bit texture, 16 for a 4-bit one at
// CSA), CSM1's arrangement - an 8-bit CLUT a 16x16 image with index bits 3 and
// 4 swapped, a 4-bit one 8x2. 16-bit entries expand by TEXA as they load.
void LoadClut() {
    const uint i = gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
    if (gl_GlobalInvocationID.y != 0u || i >= p.tw) return;
    const bool eight = p.tw == 256u;
    uint x, y;
    if (eight) {
        const uint q = (i & 0xE7u) | ((i & 0x08u) << 1) | ((i & 0x10u) >> 1);
        x = q % 16u;
        y = q / 16u;
    } else {
        x = i % 8u;
        y = i / 8u;
    }
    clut[eight ? i : (p.csa * 16u + i) % 256u] = Expand(Raw(x, y));
}

void main() {
    if (p.mode == 1u) {
        LoadClut();
        return;
    }
    if (p.mode == 2u) {
        CopyTables();
        return;
    }
    const uint u = gl_GlobalInvocationID.x, v = gl_GlobalInvocationID.y;
    if (u >= p.tw || v >= p.th) return;
    const uint x = Wrap(int(u), p.tw, p.wms, p.minu, p.maxu) & 2047u;
    const uint y = Wrap(int(v), p.th, p.wmt, p.minv, p.maxv) & 2047u;
#ifdef TO_IMAGE
    // The bytes as an RGBA8 image stores them (c / 255 back to c exactly).
    imageStore(dst, ivec2(int(u), int(p.row0 + v)), unpackUnorm4x8(Expand(Raw(x, y))));
#else
    lin[v * p.tw + u] = Expand(Raw(x, y));
#endif
}

```

`gpu/shaders/depth_load.frag`:

```frag
#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
// A depth buffer from GS local memory on the GPU, drawn: one triangle over
// the image (date.vert's), each pixel's Z read from memory as the swizzle
// reads it and written as the depth (Z / 2^32) - a depth image cannot be a
// storage image, and through a linear buffer a 3x depth buffer's copy was
// most of the GPU's time. Pixels outside the rows asked for are left alone.

layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer Memory { uint mem[]; };
layout(push_constant) uniform Params {
    uint bp;            // base, in 256-byte blocks
    uint bw;            // width, in 64-pixel units
    uint psm;
    uint cols, rows;    // the rectangle moved, rows from row0
    uint stride;        // (the swizzle's)
    uint to_memory;     // (the swizzle's)
    uint depth;         // (the swizzle's)
    uint row0;          // the first row
    uint scale;         // the image's pixels to a GS pixel, each way (the internal resolution)
} p;

#include "gs_address.glsl"

void main() {
    const uint k = max(p.scale, 1u);
    const uvec2 at = uvec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) / k;
    if (at.x >= p.cols || at.y < p.row0 || at.y >= p.row0 + p.rows) discard;
    const uint a = Address(at.x, at.y);
    const uint w = mem[a >> 2];
    uint v;
    if (Is16()) v = (w >> ((a & 2u) * 8u)) & 0xFFFFu;
    else if (p.psm == PSMCT24 || p.psm == PSMZ24) v = w & 0xFFFFFFu;
    else v = w;
    gl_FragDepth = float(v) * (1.0 / 4294967296.0);
}

```

`gpu/shaders/downsample.comp`:

```comp
#version 450
// Supersampling's last step (ANTI-ALIASING, SSAA): a picture drawn larger
// than the window shows it, brought down to the shown size by averaging all
// of it - each shown pixel the mean of an even grid of samples over the
// source pixels it covers (exact boxes at a whole ratio), where a single
// bilinear sample (a blit) would leave most of them out and alias again.

layout(local_size_x = 8, local_size_y = 8) in;
layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D picture;
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, rgba8) uniform writeonly image2D shown;
layout(push_constant) uniform Size { vec2 texel; ivec2 size; } size;     // texel: the source's

void main() {
    const ivec2 p = ivec2(gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy);
    if (p.x >= size.size.x || p.y >= size.size.y) return;
    const vec2 ratio = vec2(textureSize(picture, 0)) / vec2(size.size);    // source pixels per shown one
    const ivec2 n = clamp(ivec2(ceil(ratio - 0.001)), ivec2(1), ivec2(8));
    vec3 sum = vec3(0.0);
    for (int j = 0; j < n.y; ++j)
        for (int i = 0; i < n.x; ++i) {
            const vec2 at = (vec2(p) + (vec2(i, j) + 0.5) / vec2(n)) / vec2(size.size);
            sum += textureLod(picture, at, 0.0).rgb;
        }
    imageStore(shown, p, vec4(sum / float(n.x * n.y), 1.0));
}

```

`gpu/shaders/fxaa.comp`:

```comp
#version 450
// FXAA (after Timothy Lottes' FXAA 3.11, its PC quality preset trimmed):
// the finished picture's edges smoothed before it is scaled to the window
// (ANTI-ALIASING). A pixel whose neighbours differ enough in brightness is
// on an edge: the edge's direction and its ends are found along it, and the
// pixel takes a sample from across the edge, as far as it lies from its
// nearer end.

layout(local_size_x = 8, local_size_y = 8) in;
layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D picture;
layout(set = 0, binding = 1, rgba8) uniform writeonly image2D smoothed;
layout(push_constant) uniform Size { vec2 texel; ivec2 size; } size;

const float kEdgeMin = 0.0312;      // darker than this: never an edge
const float kEdgeRatio = 0.125;     // the local contrast that makes one
const float kSubpixel = 0.75;       // how much single-pixel detail is softened
const int kSteps = 10;
const float kStep[kSteps] = float[](1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0);

float Luma(vec3 c) { return dot(c, vec3(0.299, 0.587, 0.114)); }
vec3 At(vec2 uv) { return textureLod(picture, uv, 0.0).rgb; }
float LumaAt(vec2 uv) { return Luma(At(uv)); }

void main() {
    const ivec2 p = ivec2(gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy);
    if (p.x >= size.size.x || p.y >= size.size.y) return;
    const vec2 t = size.texel;
    const vec2 uv = (vec2(p) + 0.5) * t;
    const vec3 centre = At(uv);
    const float m = Luma(centre);
    const float n = LumaAt(uv + vec2(0, -t.y)), s = LumaAt(uv + vec2(0, t.y));
    const float w = LumaAt(uv + vec2(-t.x, 0)), e = LumaAt(uv + vec2(t.x, 0));
    const float lo = min(m, min(min(n, s), min(w, e)));
    const float hi = max(m, max(max(n, s), max(w, e)));
    const float range = hi - lo;
    if (range < max(kEdgeMin, hi * kEdgeRatio)) {
        imageStore(smoothed, p, vec4(centre, 1.0));
        return;
    }
    const float nw = LumaAt(uv + vec2(-t.x, -t.y)), ne = LumaAt(uv + vec2(t.x, -t.y));
    const float sw = LumaAt(uv + vec2(-t.x, t.y)), se = LumaAt(uv + vec2(t.x, t.y));

    // Horizontal or vertical: where brightness changes more.
    const float horizontal = abs(nw + sw - 2.0 * w) + 2.0 * abs(n + s - 2.0 * m) + abs(ne + se - 2.0 * e);
    const float vertical = abs(nw + ne - 2.0 * n) + 2.0 * abs(w + e - 2.0 * m) + abs(sw + se - 2.0 * s);
    const bool across_y = horizontal >= vertical;        // the edge runs along x; its other side is up or down
    float before = across_y ? n : w, after = across_y ? s : e;
    float step_across = across_y ? t.y : t.x;
    const float gradient_before = abs(before - m), gradient_after = abs(after - m);
    const bool towards_before = gradient_before >= gradient_after;
    const float gradient = 0.25 * max(gradient_before, gradient_after);
    float edge_luma;
    if (towards_before) {
        step_across = -step_across;
        edge_luma = 0.5 * (before + m);
    } else {
        edge_luma = 0.5 * (after + m);
    }

    // Along the edge (half a pixel across it), both ways, to its ends.
    vec2 edge = uv;
    vec2 along;
    if (across_y) {
        edge.y += 0.5 * step_across;
        along = vec2(t.x, 0);
    } else {
        edge.x += 0.5 * step_across;
        along = vec2(0, t.y);
    }
    vec2 uv_neg = edge - along, uv_pos = edge + along;
    float end_neg = LumaAt(uv_neg) - edge_luma, end_pos = LumaAt(uv_pos) - edge_luma;
    bool done_neg = abs(end_neg) >= gradient, done_pos = abs(end_pos) >= gradient;
    for (int i = 1; i < kSteps && !(done_neg && done_pos); ++i) {
        if (!done_neg) {
            uv_neg -= along * kStep[i];
            end_neg = LumaAt(uv_neg) - edge_luma;
            done_neg = abs(end_neg) >= gradient;
        }
        if (!done_pos) {
            uv_pos += along * kStep[i];
            end_pos = LumaAt(uv_pos) - edge_luma;
            done_pos = abs(end_pos) >= gradient;
        }
    }
    const float dist_neg = across_y ? uv.x - uv_neg.x : uv.y - uv_neg.y;
    const float dist_pos = across_y ? uv_pos.x - uv.x : uv_pos.y - uv.y;
    const bool nearer_neg = dist_neg < dist_pos;
    const float length_ = dist_neg + dist_pos;
    // Only where the edge's end changes the other way from the pixel: there
    // the step it makes lies on this side.
    const bool darker = m - edge_luma < 0.0;
    const bool right_side = ((nearer_neg ? end_neg : end_pos) < 0.0) != darker;
    float offset = right_side ? 0.5 - min(dist_neg, dist_pos) / length_ : 0.0;

    // A single pixel standing out (no long edge): softened by its neighbours.
    const float average = (2.0 * (n + s + w + e) + nw + ne + sw + se) / 12.0;
    const float sub = clamp(abs(average - m) / range, 0.0, 1.0);
    const float sub_smooth = (-2.0 * sub + 3.0) * sub * sub;
    offset = max(offset, sub_smooth * sub_smooth * kSubpixel);

    vec2 at = uv;
    if (across_y) at.y += offset * step_across;
    else at.x += offset * step_across;
    imageStore(smoothed, p, vec4(At(at), 1.0));
}

```

`gpu/shaders/gs.frag`:

```frag
#version 450
// The GS's per-pixel work, in its own terms (0-255, with 0x80 as 1.0 where it
// multiplies): the texture function, then the alpha test. Blending is the
// fixed-function blender's; the GS's factor - source alpha or FIX over 128 -
// goes out as the second output (dual-source blending), since the alpha
// written is the source alpha as it is. Compiled a second time with
// SINGLE_OUTPUT for devices without dual-source blending, and a third with
// SHADER_BLEND: the GS's blend done here, from a copy of the target - for a
// factor the blender cannot have (FIX over 0x80: more than 1.0, which a
// fixed-point target clamps to 1).
#ifdef SHADER_BLEND
#define SINGLE_OUTPUT
layout(set = 2, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D destination;
#endif

layout(location = 0) in vec4 shade;
layout(location = 1) noperspective in vec3 coordinate;
layout(location = 2) noperspective in float fog;
layout(location = 3) flat in vec4 range;   // a sprite's S, T at its first and last pixels (gs.vert)

layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D texture_image;
// The same image's texels as 32-bit words (R in bits 0-7, A in 24-31): the
// four texels a bilinear sample mixes in one gather - one read of the
// texture rather than four (Sample).
layout(set = 0, binding = 1) uniform usampler2D texture_words;
// The GPU's CLUT (decode.comp's), 256 entries as the GS expands them: a target
// read as PSMT8H (tex_format 4) indexes it by its alpha byte.
layout(std430, set = 1, binding = 0) readonly buffer Clut { uint clut[256]; };

layout(push_constant) uniform Params {
    layout(offset = 16) uint textured;
    uint tfx;           // 0 MODULATE, 1 DECAL, 2 HIGHLIGHT, 3 HIGHLIGHT2
    uint tcc;           // the texel's alpha counts
    uint atst;          // 0 NEVER, 1 ALWAYS, 2 LESS, 3 LEQUAL, 4 EQUAL, 5 GEQUAL, 6 GREATER, 7 NOTEQUAL
    uint aref;
    uint fix_factor;    // blend with FIX rather than the source alpha
    uint fix;
    uint afail;         // which pixels this pass draws: 0 passing, 1 failing, 2 all
    uint fge;           // fog
    uint fogcol;        // FOGCOL, R G B in bytes 0-2
    uint pabe;          // which pixels this pass draws: 0 all, 1 As >= 0x80, 2 As < 0x80
    uint bilinear;      // bit 0: the four texels around, else the nearest; bits 1 and on: Mip
    uint wms, wmt;      // CLAMP: 0 REPEAT, 1 CLAMP, 2 REGION_CLAMP, 3 REGION_REPEAT
    uint minu, maxu, minv, maxv;
    uint tw, th;        // TEX0's size (0: the image's own)
    uint tex_format;    // a target read as 0 32-bit, 1 24-bit, 2 16-bit texels, 4 PSMT8H through the CLUT
    uint texa;          // TEXA: TA0 in bits 0-7, TA1 8-15, AEM 16
    uint image_size;    // the bound image's size in its pixels, width in bits 0-15, height 16-31 - not
                        // asked of the image (textureSize: a sampler's message per pixel on some GPUs)
    uint logic;         // FBMSK masking part of a channel: 1 the AND pass, 2 the OR pass, 0 neither
    uint keep;          // ...the bits FBMSK keeps, RGBA bytes as the target holds them
    uint scale;         // a target drawn larger (the internal resolution): its pixels to a GS texel
    uint blend_ops;     // bits 0-7, SHADER_BLEND: ALPHA's A, B, C, D, two bits each; 8-15: Snap's scale;
                        // 16: a 16-bit target (five bits a channel stored)
} p;

// What a draw may use, from its parameters (gs_renderer.cpp's Features): a
// pipeline made for a kind of draw leaves out the rest - the same results,
// the work and registers of what it never does gone (an integrated GPU's
// time at 2x was this shader's: the whole of it, everything a draw might
// do, for every pixel). Everything by default: the shader as it is.
layout(constant_id = 0) const uint kFeatures = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
const uint kTextured = 1u, kReplaced = 2u, kMip = 4u, kLinear = 8u, kExpand = 16u, kFine = 32u, kSnap = 64u,
           kFog = 128u, kAlphaTest = 256u, kPabe = 512u, kLogic = 1024u, kSixteen = 2048u;
bool Has(uint feature) { return (kFeatures & feature) != 0u; }
const float kEdge = 1.0 / 16384.0;       // Sample's nudge past a texel's edge

float Ta0() { return float(p.texa & 255u); }
float Ta1() { return float((p.texa >> 8) & 255u); }
bool Aem() { return ((p.texa >> 16) & 1u) != 0u; }
ivec2 ImageSize() { return ivec2(int(p.image_size & 0xFFFFu), int(p.image_size >> 16)); }

// A target drawn larger: its pixels to a GS texel (1 where none can be).
uint Scale() { return Has(kFine) ? p.scale : 1u; }

// A texel coordinate wrapped as CLAMP says, as the software GS's Wrap. A
// target drawn larger (Fine) is addressed in its own pixels: its size and a
// region's bounds scaled; REGION_REPEAT's masks do not scale (Texel takes
// those in GS texels).
int Wrap(int i, int size, uint mode, uint lo, uint hi, int k) {
    // (A power of two - TEX0's sizes are, and a target drawn at 2x or 4x -
    // wraps by its mask, the same for negative i: two integer divisions a
    // call otherwise, four calls a bilinear pixel.)
    if (mode == 0u) return k == 1 || (size & (size - 1)) == 0 ? (i & (size - 1)) : ((i % size) + size) % size;
    if (mode == 1u) return clamp(i, 0, size - 1);
    if (mode == 2u) return clamp(i, int(lo) * k, int(hi) * k + k - 1);
    return (i & int(lo)) | int(hi);
}

// Whether the texture is a target drawn larger, addressed in its own pixels.
bool Fine() { return Scale() > 1u && p.wms != 3u && p.wmt != 3u; }

ivec2 TextureSize() {
    return p.tw != 0u ? ivec2(int(p.tw), int(p.th)) : ImageSize();
}

// A texel as the GS expands it: TEXA's alpha for 24- and 16-bit texels, a
// target read as PSMT8H through the CLUT.
vec4 Expand(vec4 t) {
    if (!Has(kExpand)) return t;
    if (p.tex_format == 4u) {                       // PSMT8H: the alpha byte indexes the CLUT
        const uint c = clut[uint(t.a) & 255u];
        return vec4(float(c & 255u), float((c >> 8) & 255u), float((c >> 16) & 255u), float(c >> 24));
    }
    bool black = t.r + t.g + t.b == 0.0;
    if (p.tex_format == 1u) {                       // 24-bit: TEXA's alpha
        t.a = (Aem() && black) ? 0.0 : Ta0();
    } else if (p.tex_format == 2u) {                // 16-bit: 5 bits a channel, alpha by its bit
        bool bit = t.a >= 128.0;
        t.rgb = floor(t.rgb / 8.0) * 8.0;
        black = t.r + t.g + t.b == 0.0;
        t.a = bit ? Ta1() : ((Aem() && black) ? 0.0 : Ta0());
    }
    return t;
}

vec4 Fetch(ivec2 at) { return Expand(floor(texelFetch(texture_image, at, 0) * 255.0 + 0.5)); }
vec4 Unpack(uint w) { return Expand(vec4(float(w & 255u), float((w >> 8) & 255u), float((w >> 16) & 255u), float(w >> 24))); }

vec4 Texel(int u, int v) {
    const int k = Fine() ? int(Scale()) : 1;
    ivec2 size = TextureSize() * k;
    ivec2 at = ivec2(Wrap(u, size.x, p.wms, p.minu, p.maxu, k), Wrap(v, size.y, p.wmt, p.minv, p.maxv, k));
    if (k == 1) at &= 2047;
    // A target drawn larger with REGION_REPEAT: the GS texel, and the middle
    // of its square.
    if (k == 1 && Scale() > 1u) at = at * int(Scale()) + int(Scale() / 2u);
    // A target may be smaller than TEX0 says: what lies beyond is not drawn here.
    at = min(at, ImageSize() - 1);
    return Fetch(at);
}

// A texel of mipmap level n (n > 0: a texture from memory, never a target):
// TW-n by TH-n, below the levels before it at the image's left edge
// (gs_renderer.cpp's TextureFromMemory), a region's bounds shifted as its
// coordinates are.
vec4 Texel(int u, int v, int n) {
    if (n == 0) return Texel(u, v);
    const ivec2 size = max(TextureSize() >> n, ivec2(1));
    ivec2 at = ivec2(Wrap(u, size.x, p.wms, p.minu >> n, p.maxu >> n, 1),
                     Wrap(v, size.y, p.wmt, p.minv >> n, p.maxv >> n, 1));
    at = clamp(at, ivec2(0), size - 1);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) at.y += max(TextureSize().y >> i, 1);
    return Fetch(at);
}

// Texel's addresses for the four texels around (u0, v0) in level n, worked
// out together (x0, x1, y0, y1): a bilinear sample otherwise repeats the
// size, wrap and mip work four times. The same texels as Texel's.
ivec4 Neighbours(ivec2 i0, int n) {
    const int k = n == 0 && Fine() ? int(Scale()) : 1;
    const ivec2 size = n == 0 ? TextureSize() * k : max(TextureSize() >> n, ivec2(1));
    ivec2 a = ivec2(Wrap(i0.x, size.x, p.wms, p.minu >> n, p.maxu >> n, k),
                    Wrap(i0.y, size.y, p.wmt, p.minv >> n, p.maxv >> n, k));
    ivec2 b = ivec2(Wrap(i0.x + 1, size.x, p.wms, p.minu >> n, p.maxu >> n, k),
                    Wrap(i0.y + 1, size.y, p.wmt, p.minv >> n, p.maxv >> n, k));
    if (n == 0) {
        if (k == 1) { a &= 2047; b &= 2047; }
        if (k == 1 && Scale() > 1u) { a = a * int(Scale()) + int(Scale() / 2u); b = b * int(Scale()) + int(Scale() / 2u); }
        a = min(a, ImageSize() - 1);
        b = min(b, ImageSize() - 1);
    } else {
        a = clamp(a, ivec2(0), size - 1);
        b = clamp(b, ivec2(0), size - 1);
        int offset = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) offset += max(TextureSize().y >> i, 1);
        a.y += offset;
        b.y += offset;
    }
    return ivec4(a.x, b.x, a.y, b.y);
}

// The texel at (u, v) in level 0's texels, in level n: the nearest, or the
// four around (u - 0.5, v - 0.5) mixed per channel as the GS mixes them: in
// sixteenths (its coordinates' 4 fractional bits), each step truncated - a
// game that filters its last frame back in relies on the loss (the software
// GS's Texel).
vec4 Sample(vec2 uv, int n, bool linear) {
    if (Fine()) uv *= float(Scale());               // in the target's own pixels
    uv /= float(1 << n);
    // A coordinate the GS has on a texel's edge (its fixed point: sprites'
    // texels one to a pixel) comes out of the GPU's interpolation a hair to
    // either side, as the GPU rounds: nudged on (kEdge: about a float's
    // last bit at a coordinate of 1024 - larger nudges took coordinates
    // genuinely just short of an edge over it too), every GPU takes the same
    // texel.
    if (!linear) return Texel(int(floor(uv.x + kEdge)), int(floor(uv.y + kEdge)), n);
    const ivec2 xy = ivec2(floor((uv - 0.5) * 16.0 + kEdge * 16.0));
    const ivec2 i0 = xy >> 4;
    const vec4 f = vec4(xy & 15, 0, 0);
    const ivec4 at = Neighbours(i0, n);
    vec4 c00, c10, c01, c11;
    if (at.y == at.x + 1 && at.w == at.z + 1) {
        // Side by side in the image (almost always - not where a wrap or a
        // clamp parts them): gathered at the corner they share.
        const uvec4 w = textureGather(texture_words, vec2(at.yw) / vec2(ImageSize()), 0);
        c01 = Unpack(w.x);
        c11 = Unpack(w.y);
        c10 = Unpack(w.z);
        c00 = Unpack(w.w);
    } else {
        c00 = Fetch(at.xz);
        c10 = Fetch(at.yz);
        c01 = Fetch(at.xw);
        c11 = Fetch(at.yw);
    }
    const vec4 top = c00 + floor((c10 - c00) * f.x / 16.0), bottom = c01 + floor((c11 - c01) * f.x / 16.0);
    return top + floor((bottom - top) * f.y / 16.0);
}

// A texture pack's replacement (GsRenderer::UploadReplacement): finer than
// the GS's TW x TH, with mipmap levels of its own (levels - 1 in tex_format's
// bits 9-11), its texels RGBA as they are (alpha 0x80 is 1.0, as the GS's). Placed
// over the GS's texels: CLAMP's modes and region in them, k replacement
// texels to one; filtered as the game filters, with the level the pixel's
// footprint in the replacement's texels asks for (the GS's LOD knows only its
// own texels).
bool Replaced() { return Has(kReplaced) && (p.tex_format & 0x100u) != 0u; }

ivec2 ReplacedSize(int n) { return textureSize(texture_image, n); }

int ReplacedWrap(int i, int size, uint mode, uint lo, uint hi, float k) {
    if (mode == 0u) return ((i % size) + size) % size;
    if (mode == 1u) return clamp(i, 0, size - 1);
    if (mode == 2u) return clamp(i, int(floor(float(lo) * k)), int(ceil(float(hi + 1u) * k)) - 1);
    // REGION_REPEAT: the GS's texel masked, the replacement's texels within it kept.
    const int g = int(floor(float(i) / k));
    return int(float((g & int(lo)) | int(hi)) * k) + (i - int(float(g) * k));
}

vec4 ReplacedTexel(int u, int v, int n, vec2 k) {
    const ivec2 size = ReplacedSize(n);
    ivec2 at = ivec2(ReplacedWrap(u, size.x, p.wms, p.minu, p.maxu, k.x),
                     ReplacedWrap(v, size.y, p.wmt, p.minv, p.maxv, k.y));
    at = clamp(at, ivec2(0), size - 1);
    return floor(texelFetch(texture_image, at, n) * 255.0 + 0.5);
}

vec4 ReplacedLevel(vec2 r, int n, bool linear) {
    const vec2 k = vec2(ReplacedSize(n)) / vec2(TextureSize());      // its texels to a GS texel, at this level
    r /= float(1 << n);
    if (!linear) return ReplacedTexel(int(floor(r.x)), int(floor(r.y)), n, k);
    const vec2 xy = r - 0.5;
    const ivec2 i0 = ivec2(floor(xy));
    const vec2 f = xy - vec2(i0);
    const vec4 c00 = ReplacedTexel(i0.x, i0.y, n, k), c10 = ReplacedTexel(i0.x + 1, i0.y, n, k);
    const vec4 c01 = ReplacedTexel(i0.x, i0.y + 1, n, k), c11 = ReplacedTexel(i0.x + 1, i0.y + 1, n, k);
    return mix(mix(c00, c10, f.x), mix(c01, c11, f.x), f.y);
}

// `r`: where in level 0's texels; `footprint`: its derivatives' larger length.
vec4 ReplacedSample(vec2 r, float footprint) {
    const uint m = p.bilinear;
    const bool linear = (m & 2u) == 0u ? (m & 1u) != 0u : ((m >> 8) & 1u) != 0u || ((m >> 5) & 7u) >= 4u;
    const int last = int((p.tex_format >> 9) & 7u);
    const float lod = clamp(log2(max(footprint, 1e-6)), 0.0, float(last));
    const int n = int(floor(lod));
    const vec4 c0 = ReplacedLevel(r, n, linear);
    if (!linear || n >= last || lod == float(n)) return floor(c0 + 0.5);
    return floor(mix(c0, ReplacedLevel(r, n + 1, linear), lod - float(n)) + 0.5);
}

// TEX1's mipmapping (GsDrawState::mip, in p.bilinear): the GS's LOD from the
// pixel's Q - (log2(1/|Q|) << L) + K, or K alone (LCM) - magnifies (MMAG,
// level 0) up to 0, else minifies by MMIN: 2 and 4 the nearest level, 3 and 5
// the two around mixed; 4 and 5 bilinear within a level. The GS's own
// selection, not the GPU's: the levels it picks at any internal resolution
// (the software GS's ChooseLevel).
vec4 Sample(vec2 uv) {
    const uint m = p.bilinear;
    if (!Has(kMip) || (m & 2u) == 0u) return Sample(uv, 0, Has(kLinear) && (m & 1u) != 0u);
    const int mxl = int((m >> 2) & 7u);
    const uint mmin = (m >> 5) & 7u;
    float lod = float(int(m << 4) >> 20) / 16.0;    // K, 4 fractional bits
    const float q = coordinate.z != 0.0 ? abs(coordinate.z) : 1.0;     // as the software GS's
    if (((m >> 9) & 1u) == 0u) lod += -log2(q) * float(1u << ((m >> 10) & 3u));
    if (lod <= 0.0) return Sample(uv, 0, ((m >> 8) & 1u) != 0u);
    const bool linear = mmin == 4u || mmin == 5u;
    if (mmin == 2u || mmin == 4u) return Sample(uv, int(min(floor(lod + 0.5), float(mxl))), linear);
    lod = min(lod, float(mxl));
    const int n = int(floor(lod));
    const float f = lod - float(n);
    const vec4 c0 = Sample(uv, n, linear);
    if (n >= mxl || f == 0.0) return c0;
    const vec4 c1 = Sample(uv, n + 1, linear);
    return floor(c0 + (c1 - c0) * f + 0.5);
}

#ifdef SINGLE_OUTPUT
layout(location = 0) out vec4 colour;
#else
layout(location = 0, index = 0) out vec4 colour;
layout(location = 0, index = 1) out vec4 factor;
#endif

void main() {
    vec4 v = round(shade * 255.0);
    vec4 c = v;
    if (Has(kTextured) && p.textured != 0u) {
        vec2 uv = coordinate.xy / coordinate.z * vec2(TextureSize());
        // A sprite on a target drawn larger: sampled as finely as the target
        // is drawn, within the coordinates the GS reads at its first and last
        // pixels (gs_renderer.cpp's DrawTriangles: further, where it meets
        // another), and - REPEAT, the sprite within one copy of the texture -
        // not wrapping round to its far side (a tile's edge: seams).
        const uint snap = (p.blend_ops >> 8) & 255u;
        if (Has(kSnap) && snap > 1u) {
            const vec2 size = vec2(TextureSize());
            const vec2 lo = min(range.xy, range.zw), hi = max(range.xy, range.zw);
            uv = clamp(uv, lo * size, hi * size);
            const float inset = p.bilinear != 0u ? 0.5 : 0.001;
            if (p.wms == 0u && lo.x >= 0.0 && hi.x <= 1.0) uv.x = clamp(uv.x, inset, size.x - inset);
            if (p.wmt == 0u && lo.y >= 0.0 && hi.y <= 1.0) uv.y = clamp(uv.y, inset, size.y - inset);
        }
        // The footprint in a replacement's texels, from the coordinates before
        // the sprite's clamp above (whose edges would read as a large one).
        vec4 t;
        if (Replaced()) {
            const vec2 k = vec2(ReplacedSize(0)) / vec2(TextureSize());
            const vec2 r = coordinate.xy / coordinate.z * vec2(TextureSize()) * k;
            const vec2 dx = dFdx(r), dy = dFdy(r);
            t = ReplacedSample(uv * k, sqrt(max(dot(dx, dx), dot(dy, dy))));
        } else {
            t = Sample(uv);
        }
        vec3 product = floor(t.rgb * v.rgb / 128.0);
        if (p.tfx == 0u) {
            c.rgb = product;
            c.a = p.tcc != 0u ? floor(t.a * v.a / 128.0) : v.a;
        } else if (p.tfx == 1u) {
            c.rgb = t.rgb;
            c.a = p.tcc != 0u ? t.a : v.a;
        } else if (p.tfx == 2u) {
            c.rgb = product + v.a;
            c.a = p.tcc != 0u ? t.a + v.a : v.a;
        } else {
            c.rgb = product + v.a;
            c.a = p.tcc != 0u ? t.a : v.a;
        }
        c = min(c, vec4(255.0));
    }

    if (Has(kFog) && p.fge != 0u) {
        // Towards FOGCOL as F falls, colour only.
        float f = round(fog * 255.0);
        vec3 fc = vec3(float(p.fogcol & 0xFFu), float((p.fogcol >> 8) & 0xFFu), float((p.fogcol >> 16) & 0xFFu));
        c.rgb = floor((f * c.rgb + (255.0 - f) * fc) / 256.0);
    }

    // (Without kAlphaTest: the test ALWAYS, and no pass of failing pixels -
    // nothing discarded, as the GPU likes it: depth tested before shading.)
    if (Has(kAlphaTest)) {
        uint a = uint(c.a);
        bool pass = true;
        switch (p.atst) {
            case 0u: pass = false; break;
            case 2u: pass = a < p.aref; break;
            case 3u: pass = a <= p.aref; break;
            case 4u: pass = a == p.aref; break;
            case 5u: pass = a >= p.aref; break;
            case 6u: pass = a > p.aref; break;
            case 7u: pass = a != p.aref; break;
            default: break;
        }
        // The renderer draws AFAIL as passes: 0 keeps the passing pixels, 1 the
        // failing ones (with only what AFAIL writes), 2 all of them.
        if (p.afail == 0u && !pass) discard;
        if (p.afail == 1u && pass) discard;
    }
    if (Has(kPabe)) {
        if (p.pabe == 1u && c.a < 128.0) discard;
        if (p.pabe == 2u && c.a >= 128.0) discard;
    }

#ifdef SHADER_BLEND
    // Cv = ((A - B) * C >> 7) + D, clamped (COLCLAMP), as the software GS.
    vec4 dst = round(texelFetch(destination, ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy), 0) * 255.0);
    uint ops = p.blend_ops & 255u;
    vec3 op_a = (ops & 3u) == 0u ? c.rgb : (ops & 3u) == 1u ? dst.rgb : vec3(0.0);
    vec3 op_b = ((ops >> 2) & 3u) == 0u ? c.rgb : ((ops >> 2) & 3u) == 1u ? dst.rgb : vec3(0.0);
    float op_c = ((ops >> 4) & 3u) == 0u ? c.a : ((ops >> 4) & 3u) == 1u ? dst.a : float(p.fix);
    vec3 op_d = ((ops >> 6) & 3u) == 0u ? c.rgb : ((ops >> 6) & 3u) == 1u ? dst.rgb : vec3(0.0);
    c.rgb = clamp(floor((op_a - op_b) * op_c / 128.0) + op_d, 0.0, 255.0);
#endif
    // A 16-bit target keeps the top five bits of each colour byte.
    if (Has(kSixteen) && ((p.blend_ops >> 16) & 1u) != 0u) c.rgb = floor(c.rgb / 8.0) * 8.0;
    colour = c / 255.0;
    // A partly masked channel: the target ANDed with what FBMSK keeps, then
    // ORed with the rest of the source's bits (the pipelines' logic ops).
    if (Has(kLogic)) {
        if (p.logic == 1u) colour = unpackUnorm4x8(p.keep);
        if (p.logic == 2u) colour = unpackUnorm4x8(packUnorm4x8(c / 255.0) & ~p.keep);
    }
#ifndef SINGLE_OUTPUT
    float k = p.fix_factor != 0u ? float(p.fix) : c.a;
    factor = vec4(k / 128.0);
#endif
}

```

```vert
#version 450
// A GS vertex: position in pixels, colour 0-255 (normalised by the attribute
// format), texture coordinate S, T, Q. The GS samples a pixel at its whole
// coordinates and Vulkan at its centre, so positions move half a pixel.

layout(location = 0) in vec2 position;
layout(location = 1) in vec4 colour;
layout(location = 2) in vec3 stq;
layout(location = 3) in uint z;     // the GS's Z, unsigned; larger is nearer
layout(location = 4) in float fog;  // F, 0-1
// A sprite on a target drawn larger: the S, T the GS reads at its first and
// last pixels (s0, t0, s1, t1) - the texture coordinates kept inside them.
layout(location = 5) in vec4 range;

layout(push_constant) uniform Target {
    vec2 size;          // the target, in pixels
} target;

layout(location = 0) out vec4 shade;
// The GS interpolates S, T and Q linearly across the screen and divides per
// pixel: no perspective correction of its own.
layout(location = 1) noperspective out vec3 coordinate;
layout(location = 2) noperspective out float fog_out;
layout(location = 3) flat out vec4 range_out;

void main() {
    vec2 ndc = (position + 0.5) / target.size * 2.0 - 1.0;
    gl_Position = vec4(ndc, float(z) / 4294967296.0, 1.0);
    shade = colour;
    coordinate = stq;
    fog_out = fog;
    range_out = range;
}
```

`gpu/shaders/gs_address.glsl`:

```glsl
// GS local memory's layout: a pixel's byte address (GS User's Manual,
// chapter 8; the tables are engine/host/src/gs_memory.cpp's). The including
// shader declares push constants `p` with bp (base, 256-byte blocks), bw
// (width, 64-pixel units) and psm.
const uint PSMCT32 = 0x00u, PSMCT24 = 0x01u, PSMCT16 = 0x02u, PSMCT16S = 0x0Au;
const uint PSMZ32 = 0x30u, PSMZ24 = 0x31u, PSMZ16 = 0x32u, PSMZ16S = 0x3Au;

const uint kBlock32[32] = uint[](0, 1, 4, 5, 16, 17, 20, 21, 2, 3, 6, 7, 18, 19, 22, 23,
                                 8, 9, 12, 13, 24, 25, 28, 29, 10, 11, 14, 15, 26, 27, 30, 31);
const uint kBlockZ32[32] = uint[](24, 25, 28, 29, 8, 9, 12, 13, 26, 27, 30, 31, 10, 11, 14, 15,
                                  16, 17, 20, 21, 0, 1, 4, 5, 18, 19, 22, 23, 2, 3, 6, 7);
const uint kBlock16[32] = uint[](0, 2, 8, 10, 1, 3, 9, 11, 4, 6, 12, 14, 5, 7, 13, 15,
                                 16, 18, 24, 26, 17, 19, 25, 27, 20, 22, 28, 30, 21, 23, 29, 31);
const uint kBlock16S[32] = uint[](0, 2, 16, 18, 1, 3, 17, 19, 8, 10, 24, 26, 9, 11, 25, 27,
                                  4, 6, 20, 22, 5, 7, 21, 23, 12, 14, 28, 30, 13, 15, 29, 31);
const uint kBlockZ16[32] = uint[](24, 26, 16, 18, 25, 27, 17, 19, 28, 30, 20, 22, 29, 31, 21, 23,
                                  8, 10, 0, 2, 9, 11, 1, 3, 12, 14, 4, 6, 13, 15, 5, 7);
const uint kBlockZ16S[32] = uint[](24, 26, 8, 10, 25, 27, 9, 11, 16, 18, 0, 2, 17, 19, 1, 3,
                                   28, 30, 12, 14, 29, 31, 13, 15, 20, 22, 4, 6, 21, 23, 5, 7);
const uint kColumn32[64] = uint[](0, 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13, 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 14, 15,
                                  16, 17, 20, 21, 24, 25, 28, 29, 18, 19, 22, 23, 26, 27, 30, 31,
                                  32, 33, 36, 37, 40, 41, 44, 45, 34, 35, 38, 39, 42, 43, 46, 47,
                                  48, 49, 52, 53, 56, 57, 60, 61, 50, 51, 54, 55, 58, 59, 62, 63);
const uint kColumn16[128] = uint[](
    0, 2, 8, 10, 16, 18, 24, 26, 1, 3, 9, 11, 17, 19, 25, 27,
    4, 6, 12, 14, 20, 22, 28, 30, 5, 7, 13, 15, 21, 23, 29, 31,
    32, 34, 40, 42, 48, 50, 56, 58, 33, 35, 41, 43, 49, 51, 57, 59,
    36, 38, 44, 46, 52, 54, 60, 62, 37, 39, 45, 47, 53, 55, 61, 63,
    64, 66, 72, 74, 80, 82, 88, 90, 65, 67, 73, 75, 81, 83, 89, 91,
    68, 70, 76, 78, 84, 86, 92, 94, 69, 71, 77, 79, 85, 87, 93, 95,
    96, 98, 104, 106, 112, 114, 120, 122, 97, 99, 105, 107, 113, 115, 121, 123,
    100, 102, 108, 110, 116, 118, 124, 126, 101, 103, 109, 111, 117, 119, 125, 127);

const uint kMask = (4u << 20) - 1u;

uint Page(uint px, uint py) { return p.bp + 32u * (py * max(p.bw, 1u) + px); }

// Generic callers retain the push-constant format. Common image transfers
// specialize it at pipeline creation, allowing the driver to remove branches.
layout(constant_id = 0) const uint specialized_format = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
uint Format() { return specialized_format == 0xFFFFFFFFu ? p.psm : specialized_format; }
bool Is16() { return Format() == PSMCT16 || Format() == PSMCT16S || Format() == PSMZ16 || Format() == PSMZ16S; }

// The byte address of pixel (x, y).
uint Address(uint x, uint y) {
    if (Is16()) {
        // These tables are bit permutations. Express them directly rather
        // than dynamically indexing shader-local constant arrays per pixel.
        const uint bx = (x >> 4u) & 3u, by = (y >> 3u) & 7u;
        const bool s = Format() == PSMCT16S || Format() == PSMZ16S;
        uint b = ((bx & 1u) << 1u) | (by & 1u);
        b |= s ? ((bx & 2u) << 3u) | ((by & 2u) << 2u) | (by & 4u)
               : ((bx & 2u) << 2u) | ((by & 2u) << 1u) | ((by & 4u) << 2u);
        if (Format() == PSMZ16 || Format() == PSMZ16S) b ^= 24u;
        const uint block = Page(x / 64u, y / 64u) + b;
        const uint column = ((x & 1u) << 1u) | ((x & 6u) << 2u) | ((x & 8u) >> 3u) |
                            ((y & 1u) << 2u) | ((y & 6u) << 4u);
        return (block * 256u + column * 2u) & kMask;
    }
    const uint bx = (x >> 3u) & 7u, by = (y >> 3u) & 3u;
    uint b = (bx & 1u) | ((bx & 2u) << 1u) | ((bx & 4u) << 2u) | ((by & 1u) << 1u) |
             ((by & 2u) << 2u);
    if (Format() == PSMZ32 || Format() == PSMZ24) b ^= 24u;
    const uint block = Page(x / 64u, y / 32u) + b;
    const uint column = (x & 1u) | ((x & 6u) << 1u) | ((y & 1u) << 1u) | ((y & 6u) << 3u);
    return (block * 256u + column * 4u) & kMask;
}

```

`gpu/shaders/patch.comp`:

```comp
#version 450
// Words of GS local memory patched in place, each under a mask: a transfer
// that wrote part of a block the GPU holds newer, its bytes put over the
// GPU's without the block brought back to the CPU first (the CPU would wait
// for every draw before it). Eight words a dispatch, in the push constants:
// (word, value, mask) - a mask of 0 is no word.

layout(local_size_x = 8) in;

layout(std430, binding = 0) buffer Memory { uint mem[]; };     // 4 MB

layout(push_constant) uniform Patch { uvec4 words[8]; } patch_words;

void main() {
    const uvec4 w = patch_words.words[gl_LocalInvocationID.x];
    if (w.z != 0u) mem[w.x] = (mem[w.x] & ~w.z) | (w.y & w.z);
}
```

`gpu/shaders/smaa_common.glsl`:

```glsl
// SMAA 1x as three compute passes (ANTI-ALIASING: SMAA): each pass's pixel
// computes the offsets SMAA's vertex shader would hand its pixel shader,
// then runs that pixel shader (gpu/third_party/smaa/SMAA.glsl, its HIGH
// preset). The picture's size in the push constant: 1/w, 1/h, w, h.

layout(local_size_x = 8, local_size_y = 8) in;
layout(push_constant) uniform Metrics { vec4 rt; } metrics;

#define SMAA_GLSL_4 1
#define SMAA_RT_METRICS metrics.rt
#define SMAA_PRESET_HIGH 1
#define SMAA_DISCARD            // a pixel with no edge: its edges stay 0
#include "SMAA.glsl"

ivec2 Pixel() { return ivec2(gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy); }
bool Outside(ivec2 p) { return p.x >= int(metrics.rt.z) || p.y >= int(metrics.rt.w); }
vec2 TexCoord(ivec2 p) { return (vec2(p) + 0.5) * metrics.rt.xy; }
```

`gpu/shaders/swizzle.comp`:

```comp
#version 450
#extension GL_GOOGLE_include_directive : require
// GS local memory on the GPU: pixels moved between an image's rows (linear,
// one 32-bit value a pixel) and the GS's swizzled layout (GS User's Manual,
// chapter 8; the tables are engine/host/src/gs_memory.cpp's). One invocation
// a pixel. Colour is RGBA8 as the targets hold it; depth is the depth image's
// float, Z / 2^32.

layout(local_size_x = 8, local_size_y = 8) in;

layout(std430, binding = 0) buffer Memory { uint mem[]; };     // 4 MB
layout(std430, binding = 1) buffer Linear { uint lin[]; };
#ifdef IMAGE
// Compiled a second time with IMAGE: a colour target's pixels straight from
// and to the image (no copy of it through Linear - at 3x those copies were
// most of the GPU's time).
layout(set = 1, binding = 0, rgba8) uniform image2D target;
#endif
#ifdef DEPTH_IMAGE
// ...and with DEPTH_IMAGE: a depth buffer's Z sampled straight from it, to
// memory (depth_load.frag brings it back).
layout(set = 1, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D depth_image;
#endif

layout(push_constant) uniform Params {
    uint bp;            // base, in 256-byte blocks
    uint bw;            // width, in 64-pixel units
    uint psm;
    uint cols, rows;    // the rectangle moved, from (0, 0)
    uint stride;        // the linear rows' length, in pixels
    uint to_memory;     // 1: linear -> memory; 0: memory -> linear
    uint depth;         // the linear side is depth (float)
    uint row0;          // the image's row that linear row 0 holds
    uint scale;         // the image's pixels to a GS pixel, each way (the internal resolution)
    uint keep_colour;   // memory -> image, 32-bit: the square's colour kept where memory differs in alpha alone
} p;

#include "gs_address.glsl"
layout(constant_id = 1) const uint specialized_direction = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
layout(constant_id = 2) const uint specialized_scale = 0u;
layout(constant_id = 3) const uint specialized_depth = 0xFFFFFFFFu;

uint To16(uint c) {
    return ((c >> 3) & 31u) | (((c >> 11) & 31u) << 5) | (((c >> 19) & 31u) << 10) | ((c >> 31) << 15);
}

uint From16(uint c) {
    return ((c & 31u) << 3) | (((c >> 5) & 31u) << 11) | (((c >> 10) & 31u) << 19) |
           ((c & 0x8000u) != 0u ? 0x80000000u : 0u);
}

void main() {
    const uint direction = specialized_direction == 0xFFFFFFFFu ? p.to_memory : specialized_direction;
    const uint depth = specialized_depth == 0xFFFFFFFFu ? p.depth : specialized_depth;
    const uint x = gl_GlobalInvocationID.x, y = gl_GlobalInvocationID.y;
    if (x >= p.cols || y >= p.rows) return;
    // In each GS 16-pixel column, x and x+8 occupy the low/high half
    // of one word. Complete columns can be packed by one invocation,
    // without four contending atomic operations per word. Partial columns
    // retain the masked atomic path so pixels outside the rectangle survive.
    const bool paired=direction==1u && Is16() && p.bw<=32u && p.cols<=max(p.bw,1u)*64u &&
                      p.row0+p.rows<=1024u && (x&~15u)+16u<=p.cols;
    if(paired && (x&8u)!=0u) return;
    const uint a = Address(x, y + p.row0);
    const uint word = a >> 2;
    // The image's pixels for GS pixel (x, y): a square of scale x scale,
    // all of it filled from memory; the one at its middle (k/2, k/2) taken to
    // memory - the one a primitive covers when the GS pixel's centre is
    // covered (a sprite's edge at a half pixel - Burnout 3's channel shuffle
    // - left the square's first one out, and its column stale).
    const uint k = specialized_scale == 0u ? max(p.scale, 1u) : specialized_scale;
    const uint li = (y * k) * p.stride + x * k;
    const uint mid = li + (k / 2u) * p.stride + k / 2u;
#if defined(IMAGE) || defined(DEPTH_IMAGE)
    const ivec2 at = ivec2(x * k, (y + p.row0) * k);
#endif
    const bool z24 = Format() == PSMCT24 || Format() == PSMZ24;
    if (direction == 1u) {
#ifdef IMAGE
        uint v = packUnorm4x8(imageLoad(target, at + ivec2(k / 2u)));
#elif defined(DEPTH_IMAGE)
        uint v = floatBitsToUint(texelFetch(depth_image, at + ivec2(k / 2u), 0).r);
#else
        uint v = lin[mid];
#endif
        if (depth == 1u) v = uint(clamp(uintBitsToFloat(v) * 4294967296.0, 0.0, 4294967040.0));
        if (Is16()) {
            if(paired) {
#ifdef IMAGE
                uint other=packUnorm4x8(imageLoad(target,at+ivec2(8u*k+k/2u,k/2u)));
#elif defined(DEPTH_IMAGE)
                uint other=floatBitsToUint(texelFetch(depth_image,at+ivec2(8u*k+k/2u,k/2u),0).r);
#else
                uint other=lin[mid+8u*k];
#endif
                if(depth==1u) other=uint(clamp(uintBitsToFloat(other)*4294967296.0,0.0,4294967040.0));
                const uint low=depth==1u?(v&0xFFFFu):To16(v);
                const uint high=depth==1u?(other&0xFFFFu):To16(other);
                mem[word]=low|(high<<16);
                return;
            }
            const uint shift = (a & 2u) * 8u;
            const uint h = depth == 1u ? (v & 0xFFFFu) : To16(v);
            // Two pixels share the word: each changes only its own half.
            atomicAnd(mem[word], ~(0xFFFFu << shift));
            atomicOr(mem[word], h << shift);
        } else if (z24) {
            mem[word] = (mem[word] & 0xFF000000u) | (v & 0xFFFFFFu);    // the top byte is not the pixel's
        } else {
            mem[word] = v;
        }
    } else {
        const uint w = mem[word];
        uint v;
        if (Is16()) {
            const uint h = (w >> ((a & 2u) * 8u)) & 0xFFFFu;
            v = depth == 1u ? h : From16(h);
        } else {
            v = z24 ? (w & 0xFFFFFFu) : w;
        }
        const uint value = depth == 1u ? floatBitsToUint(float(v) * (1.0 / 4294967296.0)) : v;
#ifdef IMAGE
        // Memory differing from the square's middle (what went to memory) in
        // alpha alone: each pixel keeps its colour, takes memory's alpha.
        const bool keep = p.keep_colour == 1u && k > 1u && !Is16() && !z24 &&
                          ((packUnorm4x8(imageLoad(target, at + ivec2(k / 2u))) ^ value) & 0xFFFFFFu) == 0u;
        for (uint dy = 0u; dy < k; ++dy)
            for (uint dx = 0u; dx < k; ++dx) {
                const ivec2 xy = at + ivec2(dx, dy);
                vec4 c = unpackUnorm4x8(value);
                if (keep) c = vec4(imageLoad(target, xy).rgb, c.a);
                imageStore(target, xy, c);
            }
#else
        for (uint dy = 0u; dy < k; ++dy)
            for (uint dx = 0u; dx < k; ++dx) lin[li + dy * p.stride + dx] = value;
#endif
    }
}

```

`gpu/src/gpu.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * VulkanGpu: an instance and a device with one graphics queue, no window.
 * Vulkan 1.3 for dynamic rendering (drawing without render pass objects).
 */

#include "gpu_internal.h"

#include <cctype>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace ps2gpu {

void SetGpuWaitObserver(GpuWaitObserver observer) { g_wait_observer = observer; }

namespace {
/* A GPU's preference: PS2HOST_GPU=<part of its name> (any case: "intel",
   "4070") first - a laptop's integrated GPU measured beside its discrete
   one - then a discrete GPU. */
int DeviceScore(const VkPhysicalDeviceProperties& p) {
    int score = p.deviceType == VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_DISCRETE_GPU ? 2 : 1;
    if (const char* want = std::getenv("PS2HOST_GPU")) {
        std::string name = p.deviceName, part = want;
        for (char& ch : name) ch = char(std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)));
        for (char& ch : part) ch = char(std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(ch)));
        if (!part.empty() && name.find(part) != std::string::npos) score += 10;
    }
    return score;
}
}  // namespace

bool VulkanGpu::Init(std::string* error) {
    auto fail = [&](const char* what, VkResult r) {
        char text[160];
        std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "%s failed (VkResult %d)", what, int(r));
        if (error) *error = text;
        return false;
    };
    VkResult r = volkInitialize();
    if (r != VK_SUCCESS) return fail("volkInitialize (is there a Vulkan driver?)", r);
    VkApplicationInfo app{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_APPLICATION_INFO};
    app.pApplicationName = "ps2gpu";
    app.apiVersion = VK_API_VERSION_1_3;
    VkInstanceCreateInfo ici{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_INSTANCE_CREATE_INFO};
    ici.pApplicationInfo = &app;
    if ((r = vkCreateInstance(&ici, nullptr, &instance)) != VK_SUCCESS) return fail("vkCreateInstance", r);
    volkLoadInstance(instance);

    std::uint32_t n = 0;
    vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices(instance, &n, nullptr);
    std::vector<VkPhysicalDevice> list(n);
    vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices(instance, &n, list.data());
    int best = -1;
    for (VkPhysicalDevice candidate : list) {
        VkPhysicalDeviceProperties p;
        vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(candidate, &p);
        if (p.apiVersion < VK_API_VERSION_1_3) continue;
        std::uint32_t families = 0;
        vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties(candidate, &families, nullptr);
        std::vector<VkQueueFamilyProperties> props(families);
        vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties(candidate, &families, props.data());
        for (std::uint32_t f = 0; f < families; ++f) {
            if (!(props[f].queueFlags & VK_QUEUE_GRAPHICS_BIT)) continue;
            const int score = DeviceScore(p);
            if (score > best) {
                best = score;
                gpu = candidate;
                family = f;
            }
            break;
        }
    }
    if (!gpu) {
        if (error) *error = "no Vulkan 1.3 device with a graphics queue";
        return false;
    }
    VkPhysicalDeviceProperties p;
    vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(gpu, &p);
    describe_ = p.deviceName;

    const float priority = 1.0f;
    VkDeviceQueueCreateInfo qci{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_QUEUE_CREATE_INFO};
    qci.queueFamilyIndex = family;
    qci.queueCount = 1;
    qci.pQueuePriorities = &priority;
    VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan13Features v13{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_VULKAN_1_3_FEATURES};
    v13.dynamicRendering = VK_TRUE;
    v13.synchronization2 = VK_TRUE;
    // Dual-source blending: the GS's blend factor (source alpha or FIX, where
    // 0x80 is 1.0) is a second fragment output, not the alpha written.
    VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures supported;
    vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures(gpu, &supported);
    dual_source = supported.dualSrcBlend == VK_TRUE;
    VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures2 features{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_FEATURES_2};
    features.features.dualSrcBlend = supported.dualSrcBlend;
    features.features.logicOp = supported.logicOp;      // FBMSK's partly masked channels
    logic_op = supported.logicOp == VK_TRUE;
    features.features.textureCompressionBC = supported.textureCompressionBC;     // texture packs' DDS
    bc = supported.textureCompressionBC == VK_TRUE;
    features.pNext = &v13;
    VkDeviceCreateInfo dci{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_CREATE_INFO};
    dci.pNext = &features;
    dci.queueCreateInfoCount = 1;
    dci.pQueueCreateInfos = &qci;
    if ((r = vkCreateDevice(gpu, &dci, nullptr, &device)) != VK_SUCCESS) return fail("vkCreateDevice", r);
    // Device functions stay the loader's (volkLoadInstance): they dispatch by
    // handle, so the window's device and this one can live side by side. volk
    // keeps one global table; loading a device into it would point the other
    // device's calls at this one's driver entries (--window with --gpu-shadow
    // crashed so).
    vkGetDeviceQueue(device, family, 0, &queue);

    VkCommandPoolCreateInfo pci{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_INFO};
    pci.flags = VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT;
    pci.queueFamilyIndex = family;
    if ((r = vkCreateCommandPool(device, &pci, nullptr, &pool)) != VK_SUCCESS)
        return fail("vkCreateCommandPool", r);
    VkCommandBufferAllocateInfo cai{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER_ALLOCATE_INFO};
    cai.commandPool = pool;
    cai.level = VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_LEVEL_PRIMARY;
    cai.commandBufferCount = kSlots;
    if ((r = vkAllocateCommandBuffers(device, &cai, cmds)) != VK_SUCCESS)
        return fail("vkAllocateCommandBuffers", r);
    cmd = cmds[0];
    VkFenceCreateInfo fci{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_FENCE_CREATE_INFO};
    for (VkFence& f : fences)
        if ((r = vkCreateFence(device, &fci, nullptr, &f)) != VK_SUCCESS) return fail("vkCreateFence", r);
    MakeTimestamps();
    return true;
}

void VulkanGpu::MakeTimestamps() {
    // Only where the queue keeps time (timestampValidBits) and says how fast.
    std::uint32_t count = 0;
    vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties(gpu, &count, nullptr);
    std::vector<VkQueueFamilyProperties> families(count);
    vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties(gpu, &count, families.data());
    VkPhysicalDeviceProperties properties;
    vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(gpu, &properties);
    if (family >= count || families[family].timestampValidBits == 0 || properties.limits.timestampPeriod <= 0)
        return;
    VkQueryPoolCreateInfo qci{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_QUERY_POOL_CREATE_INFO};
    qci.queryType = VK_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP;
    qci.queryCount = 2 * kSlots;
    if (vkCreateQueryPool(device, &qci, nullptr, &timestamps_) != VK_SUCCESS) {
        timestamps_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
        return;
    }
    timestamp_ns_ = properties.limits.timestampPeriod;
    if (std::getenv("PS2HOST_GPU_PROFILE")) {
        qci.queryCount = kMarks * kSlots;
        if (vkCreateQueryPool(device, &qci, nullptr, &profile_) != VK_SUCCESS) profile_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    }
}

bool VulkanGpu::InitShared(VkInstance shared_instance, VkPhysicalDevice shared_gpu, VkDevice shared_device,
                           std::uint32_t shared_family, VkQueue shared_queue, bool shared_dual_source,
                           const std::string& describe, std::string* error) {
    owns_device = false;
    instance = shared_instance;
    gpu = shared_gpu;
    device = shared_device;
    family = shared_family;
    queue = shared_queue;
    dual_source = shared_dual_source;
    VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures supported;                 // the Display enables logicOp where there is one
    vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures(shared_gpu, &supported);
    logic_op = supported.logicOp == VK_TRUE;
    bc = supported.textureCompressionBC == VK_TRUE;     // (the Display enables it too)
    describe_ = describe;
    VkCommandPoolCreateInfo pci{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_INFO};
    pci.flags = VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT;
    pci.queueFamilyIndex = family;
    VkCommandBufferAllocateInfo cai{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER_ALLOCATE_INFO};
    VkFenceCreateInfo fci{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_FENCE_CREATE_INFO};
    if (vkCreateCommandPool(device, &pci, nullptr, &pool) != VK_SUCCESS) {
        if (error) *error = "vkCreateCommandPool failed";
        return false;
    }
    cai.commandPool = pool;
    cai.level = VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_LEVEL_PRIMARY;
    cai.commandBufferCount = kSlots;
    bool made = vkAllocateCommandBuffers(device, &cai, cmds) == VK_SUCCESS;
    for (VkFence& f : fences) made = made && vkCreateFence(device, &fci, nullptr, &f) == VK_SUCCESS;
    if (!made) {
        if (error) *error = "no command buffer or fence";
        return false;
    }
    cmd = cmds[0];
    MakeTimestamps();
    return true;
}

std::uint32_t VulkanGpu::FindMemory(std::uint32_t bits, VkMemoryPropertyFlags wanted) const {
    VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties mp;
    vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties(gpu, &mp);
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < mp.memoryTypeCount; ++i)
        if ((bits & (1u << i)) && (mp.memoryTypes[i].propertyFlags & wanted) == wanted) return i;
    return ~0u;
}

VulkanGpu::~VulkanGpu() {
    if (device) {
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> hold(g_queue_lock);
            vkDeviceWaitIdle(device);
        }
        for (VkFence f : fences)
            if (f) vkDestroyFence(device, f, nullptr);
        if (timestamps_) vkDestroyQueryPool(device, timestamps_, nullptr);
        if (pool) vkDestroyCommandPool(device, pool, nullptr);
        if (owns_device) vkDestroyDevice(device, nullptr);
    }
    if (instance && owns_device) vkDestroyInstance(instance, nullptr);
}

std::unique_ptr<Gpu> CreateGpu(std::string* error) {
    auto gpu = std::make_unique<VulkanGpu>();
    if (!gpu->Init(error)) return nullptr;
    return gpu;
}

}  // namespace ps2gpu
```

```h
/* The Vulkan objects behind ps2gpu::Gpu, for the library's own sources. */

#ifndef PS2GPU_GPU_INTERNAL_H
#define PS2GPU_GPU_INTERNAL_H

#include <volk.h>

#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <functional>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "ps2gpu/gs_renderer.h"

namespace ps2gpu {

/* SubmitStats: submissions, the time spent waiting for the GPU, and what
   waited (a read-back of which kind, a resize, a full ring). */
inline std::uint64_t g_submits = 0;
/* The one queue the renderer and the display share: Vulkan wants its
   submissions, presents and the device's wait-idle from one thread at a
   time, and the display presents from a thread of its own. */
inline std::mutex g_queue_lock;
inline double g_wait_seconds = 0;
inline GpuWaitObserver g_wait_observer = nullptr;      // SetGpuWaitObserver
/* The GPU's time on the command buffers handed over, in all (timestamps at
   each one's start and end; GpuBusyNanoseconds). */
inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> g_gpu_ns{0};
/* PS2HOST_GPU_PROFILE: the GPU's time by what it did (GpuProfileReport). */
enum ProfileKind { kProfOther, kProfDraw, kProfSwizzle, kProfLinear, kProfMemory, kProfFeedback, kProfDecode,
                   kProfUpload, kProfClear, kProfDate, kProfReadback, kProfKinds };
inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> g_profile_ns[kProfKinds] = {};
struct WaitReason { const char* why; std::uint64_t count; double seconds; };
inline WaitReason g_waits[16] = {};
inline void CountWait(const char* why, double seconds) {
    for (WaitReason& w : g_waits) {
        if (!w.why) w.why = why;
        if (w.why == why || std::string(w.why) == why) {
            ++w.count;
            w.seconds += seconds;
            return;
        }
    }
}

class VulkanGpu final : public Gpu {
public:
    ~VulkanGpu() override;
    bool Init(std::string* error);
    /* On a device someone else made and keeps (a Display's): only the command
       pool, command buffers and fences are this one's own. */
    bool InitShared(VkInstance instance, VkPhysicalDevice gpu, VkDevice device, std::uint32_t family, VkQueue queue,
                    bool dual_source, const std::string& describe, std::string* error);
    std::string Describe() const override { return describe_; }

    std::uint32_t FindMemory(std::uint32_t bits, VkMemoryPropertyFlags wanted) const;
    /* Records into the open command buffer (opening one if none is), to run
       at the next Submit: a frame's work goes to the GPU in one submission.
       A rendering pass left open (RecordInPass) is ended first. */
    template <typename F>
    void Record(F&& record);
    /* The same, leaving a rendering pass a previous call left open: for draws
       that continue it (end_pass says how to end one). */
    template <typename F>
    void RecordInPass(F&& record);
    std::function<void(VkCommandBuffer)> end_pass;
    /* Runs what has been recorded and waits for it, and for everything
       Flush handed over before; then what was waiting for that (AfterSubmit:
       freeing staging buffers, say) runs. */
    bool Submit(const char* why = "other");
    /* Hands what has been recorded to the GPU without waiting for it, so that
       the GPU works while the CPU goes on: the next recording goes into the
       next of kSlots command buffers (waiting only if that one is still
       running). What waited on the work handed over runs once it has run. */
    bool Flush();
    void AfterSubmit(std::function<void()> done) { after_submit_.push_back(std::move(done)); }
    bool recording() const { return open_; }
    /* PS2HOST_GPU_PROFILE: the GPU's time since the last mark (or the command
       buffer's start) counted as `kind` - a timestamp as the work before it
       ends. */
    void Mark(VkCommandBuffer c, int kind) {
        if (!profile_ || marks_[current_].size() >= kMarks) return;
        vkCmdWriteTimestamp(c, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_BOTTOM_OF_PIPE_BIT, profile_,
                            std::uint32_t(current_) * kMarks + std::uint32_t(marks_[current_].size()));
        marks_[current_].push_back(kind);
    }
    /* Counts command buffers begun: what was set in one is not in the next. */
    std::uint64_t recording_id() const { return recordings_; }
    static constexpr int kSlots = 3;
    /* The command buffer recording goes into (or will). */
    int slot() const { return current_; }
    /* Records with `record`, submits, and waits for it to finish. */
    template <typename F>
    bool Run(F&& record, const char* why = "other") {
        Record(std::forward<F>(record));
        return Submit(why);
    }

    VkInstance instance = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    VkPhysicalDevice gpu = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    VkDevice device = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    std::uint32_t family = 0;
    VkQueue queue = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    VkCommandPool pool = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    VkCommandBuffer cmd = VK_NULL_HANDLE;           /* the current slot's */
    VkCommandBuffer cmds[kSlots] = {};
    VkFence fences[kSlots] = {};
    bool dual_source = false;       /* dualSrcBlend: the GS's blending */
    bool logic_op = false;          /* logicOp: FBMSK's partly masked channels */
    bool bc = false;                /* textureCompressionBC: texture packs' DDS uploaded as they are */
    bool owns_device = true;

private:
    std::string describe_;
    bool open_ = false;
    std::uint64_t recordings_ = 0;
    // Two timestamps a slot: as its command buffer starts and as it ends.
    VkQueryPool timestamps_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    double timestamp_ns_ = 0;               // a tick, in nanoseconds
    bool stamped_[kSlots] = {};
    void MakeTimestamps();
    static constexpr std::uint32_t kMarks = 8192;
    VkQueryPool profile_ = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    std::vector<int> marks_[kSlots];
    std::vector<std::function<void()>> after_submit_;
    int current_ = 0;
    bool in_flight_[kSlots] = {};
    std::vector<std::function<void()>> slot_done_[kSlots];
    /* Waits for a slot's work, if handed over, and runs what waited on it;
       the time it waited goes to `why`. */
    bool Retire(int slot, const char* why);
};

template <typename F>
void VulkanGpu::RecordInPass(F&& record) {
    if (!open_) {
        vkResetCommandBuffer(cmd, 0);
        VkCommandBufferBeginInfo begin{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER_BEGIN_INFO};
        begin.flags = VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_USAGE_ONE_TIME_SUBMIT_BIT;
        vkBeginCommandBuffer(cmd, &begin);
        open_ = true;
        ++recordings_;
        if (timestamps_) {
            vkCmdResetQueryPool(cmd, timestamps_, 2 * std::uint32_t(current_), 2);
            vkCmdWriteTimestamp(cmd, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_TOP_OF_PIPE_BIT, timestamps_, 2 * std::uint32_t(current_));
        }
        if (profile_) {
            vkCmdResetQueryPool(cmd, profile_, std::uint32_t(current_) * kMarks, kMarks);
            marks_[current_].clear();
            Mark(cmd, kProfOther);
        }
    }
    record(cmd);
}

template <typename F>
void VulkanGpu::Record(F&& record) {
    RecordInPass([&](VkCommandBuffer c) {
        if (end_pass) end_pass(c);
        record(c);
    });
}

inline bool VulkanGpu::Retire(int slot, const char* why) {
    if (!in_flight_[slot]) return true;
    const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const bool ok = vkWaitForFences(device, 1, &fences[slot], VK_TRUE, UINT64_MAX) == VK_SUCCESS;
    const auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const double waited = std::chrono::duration<double>(end - start).count();
    g_wait_seconds += waited;
    if (g_wait_observer && waited > 0.0001)
        g_wait_observer(why, std::uint64_t(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(start.time_since_epoch()).count()),
                        std::uint64_t(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end.time_since_epoch()).count()));
    CountWait(why, waited);
    in_flight_[slot] = false;
    if (stamped_[slot]) {
        std::uint64_t ticks[2] = {};
        if (vkGetQueryPoolResults(device, timestamps_, 2 * std::uint32_t(slot), 2, sizeof ticks, ticks,
                                  sizeof ticks[0], VK_QUERY_RESULT_64_BIT) == VK_SUCCESS && ticks[1] > ticks[0])
            g_gpu_ns += std::uint64_t(double(ticks[1] - ticks[0]) * timestamp_ns_);
        stamped_[slot] = false;
    }
    if (profile_ && marks_[slot].size() > 1) {
        std::vector<std::uint64_t> ticks(marks_[slot].size());
        if (vkGetQueryPoolResults(device, profile_, std::uint32_t(slot) * kMarks, std::uint32_t(ticks.size()),
                                  ticks.size() * sizeof ticks[0], ticks.data(), sizeof ticks[0],
                                  VK_QUERY_RESULT_64_BIT) == VK_SUCCESS)
            for (std::size_t i = 1; i < ticks.size(); ++i)
                if (ticks[i] > ticks[i - 1])
                    g_profile_ns[marks_[slot][i]] += std::uint64_t(double(ticks[i] - ticks[i - 1]) * timestamp_ns_);
        marks_[slot].clear();
    }
    std::vector<std::function<void()>> done;
    done.swap(slot_done_[slot]);
    for (auto& f : done) f();
    return ok;
}

inline bool VulkanGpu::Flush() {
    if (!open_) return true;
    if (end_pass) end_pass(cmd);
    Mark(cmd, kProfOther);
    open_ = false;
    if (timestamps_) {
        vkCmdWriteTimestamp(cmd, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_BOTTOM_OF_PIPE_BIT, timestamps_, 2 * std::uint32_t(current_) + 1);
        stamped_[current_] = true;
    }
    vkEndCommandBuffer(cmd);
    VkSubmitInfo submit{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SUBMIT_INFO};
    submit.commandBufferCount = 1;
    submit.pCommandBuffers = &cmd;
    vkResetFences(device, 1, &fences[current_]);
    bool ok;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> hold(g_queue_lock);
        ok = vkQueueSubmit(queue, 1, &submit, fences[current_]) == VK_SUCCESS;
    }
    ++g_submits;
    in_flight_[current_] = ok;
    slot_done_[current_].swap(after_submit_);
    if (!ok) {                                      // nothing will run: nothing to wait for
        for (auto& f : slot_done_[current_]) f();
        slot_done_[current_].clear();
    }
    current_ = (current_ + 1) % kSlots;
    cmd = cmds[current_];
    return Retire(current_, "a full ring") && ok;
}

inline bool VulkanGpu::Submit(const char* why) {
    bool ok = Flush();
    // Oldest first: current_ is free, the one after it was handed over first.
    for (int i = 1; i <= kSlots; ++i) ok = Retire((current_ + i) % kSlots, why) && ok;
    std::vector<std::function<void()>> done;        // waited on nothing recorded
    done.swap(after_submit_);
    for (auto& f : done) f();
    return ok;
}

}  // namespace ps2gpu

#endif  /* PS2GPU_GPU_INTERNAL_H */
```

`gpu/src/gs_renderer.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * GsRenderer on Vulkan (gs_renderer.h): triangles batched by state and drawn
 * with dynamic rendering into R8G8B8A8 targets, one per (FBP, FBW, PSM).
 *
 * One vertex and one fragment shader (shaders/gs.vert, gs.frag) do the GS's
 * per-pixel work: the texture function, the alpha test. Blending is the
 * fixed-function blender's, with the GS's factor - source alpha or FIX, where
 * 0x80 is 1.0 - as the fragment's second output (dual-source blending): the
 * GS's Cv = (A - B) * C + D becomes a source and a destination factor and an
 * operation, one pipeline per ALPHA setting, made when first used.
 *
 * Everything is synchronous for now - a flush records, submits and waits - which
 * keeps the first steps simple to check; batching across frames and keeping the
 * GPU busy come once the output matches the software GS.
 */

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstdio>
#include <deque>
#include <fstream>
#include <set>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <map>
#include <mutex>
#include <tuple>
#include <unordered_map>

#include "gpu_internal.h"
#include "gs_frag.h"
#include "gs_frag_single.h"
#include "gs_frag_blend.h"
#include "gs_vert.h"
#include "date_frag.h"
#include "date_vert.h"
#include "swizzle_comp.h"
#include "swizzle_image_comp.h"
#include "swizzle_depth_comp.h"
#include "depth_load_frag.h"
#include "decode_comp.h"
#include "decode_image_comp.h"
#include "patch_comp.h"

namespace ps2gpu {

namespace {

struct PackedVertex {
    float x, y;
    std::uint8_t r, g, b, a;
    float s, t, q;
    std::uint32_t z;
    std::uint8_t fog, pad[3];
    float range[4];             // a sprite's S, T at its first and last pixels (gs.vert)
    float pad2[4];
};
// The vertex ring hands out 256-byte aligned runs, a batch's first vertex
// found by its offset: whole vertices to 256 bytes.
static_assert(256 % sizeof(PackedVertex) == 0, "a vertex must divide the ring's alignment");

/* A batch's vertices so far: room handed out a primitive at a time (Grow)
   and its fields written in place - no vertex built and then copied, nor
   its padding cleared (the vertex shader reads none of it). A splitscreen
   race appends ~400,000 a picture: push_back's temporary and copy were a
   twelfth of the GS thread. */
class PendingVertices {
public:
    std::size_t size() const { return size_; }
    bool empty() const { return size_ == 0; }
    void clear() { size_ = 0; }
    PackedVertex* data() { return data_.get(); }
    PackedVertex& operator[](std::size_t i) { return data_[i]; }
    PackedVertex* Grow(std::size_t n) {
        if (size_ + n > capacity_) {
            const std::size_t capacity = std::max<std::size_t>(capacity_ * 2, std::max<std::size_t>(size_ + n, 4096));
            std::unique_ptr<PackedVertex[]> data(new PackedVertex[capacity]);
            if (size_) std::memcpy(data.get(), data_.get(), size_ * sizeof(PackedVertex));
            data_ = std::move(data);
            capacity_ = capacity;
        }
        PackedVertex* at = data_.get() + size_;
        size_ += n;
        return at;
    }

private:
    std::unique_ptr<PackedVertex[]> data_;
    std::size_t size_ = 0, capacity_ = 0;
};

/* What the fragment shader is told, after the vertex shader's 16 bytes. */
struct FragmentParams {
    std::uint32_t textured, tfx, tcc, atst, aref, fix_factor, fix, afail, fge, fogcol, pabe;
    std::uint32_t bilinear, wms, wmt, minu, maxu, minv, maxv;
    std::uint32_t tw, th, tex_format;
    std::uint32_t texa;         // TA0 in bits 0-7, TA1 8-15, AEM 16
    std::uint32_t image_size;   // the bound image's pixels: width in bits 0-15, height 16-31
    std::uint32_t logic, keep;
    std::uint32_t scale;        // the texture's pixels to a GS texel (a target drawn larger: the internal resolution)
    std::uint32_t blend_ops;    // bits 0-7: blending in the shader, ALPHA's A, B, C, D, two bits each;
                                // 8-15: a sprite on a target drawn larger, the target's scale (0: none)
};
constexpr std::uint32_t kFragmentOffset = 16;

/* gs.frag's kFeatures: what a draw with these parameters may use (each bit
   as the shader has it), for a pipeline made without the rest. Kept in a
   pipeline key's bits 16-27, inverted: a key without them is the whole
   shader. */
constexpr int kFeatureShift = 16;
constexpr std::uint32_t kFeatureBits = 0xFFFu;
std::uint32_t Features(const FragmentParams& p) {
    std::uint32_t f = 0;
    if (p.textured) {
        f |= 1u;                                                    // kTextured
        if (p.tex_format & 0x100u) f |= 2u;                         // kReplaced
        if (p.bilinear & 2u) f |= 4u | 8u;                          // kMip (its levels may be bilinear)
        if (p.bilinear & 1u) f |= 8u;                               // kLinear
        if (p.tex_format & 0xFFu) f |= 16u;                         // kExpand
        if (p.scale > 1u) f |= 32u;                                 // kFine
        if (((p.blend_ops >> 8) & 255u) > 1u) f |= 64u;             // kSnap
    }
    if (p.fge) f |= 128u;                                           // kFog
    if (p.atst != 1u || p.afail == 1u) f |= 256u;                   // kAlphaTest: anything discarded by it
    if (p.pabe) f |= 512u;                                          // kPabe
    if (p.logic) f |= 1024u;                                        // kLogic
    if ((p.blend_ops >> 16) & 1u) f |= 2048u;                       // kSixteen
    return f;
}

struct Image {
    VkImage image = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    VkDeviceMemory memory = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    // Where in `memory` (ImageMemory: a piece of a block, of a size class -
    // class 0 its own allocation), and of which memory type.
    VkDeviceSize offset = 0;
    std::uint32_t piece_class = 0, memory_type = 0;
    VkImageView view = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    VkImageView words = VK_NULL_HANDLE;     /* an RGBA8 image's texels as 32-bit words (gs.frag's gather) */
    std::uint32_t width = 0, height = 0;    // in GS pixels
    std::uint32_t scale = 1;                // the image's pixels to a GS pixel, each way (targets, depth)
    std::uint32_t levels = 1;               // mipmap levels (a texture pack's replacements)
    std::uint32_t pw() const { return width * scale; }
```
