`host/include/ps2host/memory.h`:

```h
/*
 * Guest memory: the Emotion Engine's address space, as the game sees it.
 *
 *   RDRAM        32 MB at physical 0, seen through the kuseg (0x00000000),
 *                uncached (0x20000000), uncached-accelerated (0x30000000),
 *                kseg0 (0x80000000) and kseg1 (0xA0000000) windows
 *   scratchpad   16 KB at 0x70000000
 *   EE registers 64 KB at 0x10000000: timers, IPU, GIF, VIF, DMA, INTC, SIF
 *   VU memory    64 KB at 0x11000000: VU0/VU1 micro and data memory
 *   GS registers 8 KB at 0x12000000, the GS's privileged registers
 *   IOP RAM      2 MB at 0x1C000000, the I/O processor's memory as the EE sees it
 *   BIOS         4 MB at 0x1FC00000, read-only and zero unless supplied
 *
 * Everything else faults. Register windows are plain memory by default; a
 * Device can claim a register to give reads and writes their hardware meaning
 * (a DMA channel completing, the GS reporting a vertical blank).
 */

#ifndef PS2HOST_MEMORY_H
#define PS2HOST_MEMORY_H

#include <cstddef>
#include <functional>
#include <map>
#include <vector>

#include "ps2rt/types.h"

namespace ps2host {

constexpr u32 kRdramSize = 32u << 20;
constexpr u32 kScratchpadBase = 0x70000000u, kScratchpadSize = 16u << 10;
constexpr u32 kEeRegisterBase = 0x10000000u, kEeRegisterSize = 64u << 10;
constexpr u32 kVuMemoryBase = 0x11000000u, kVuMemorySize = 64u << 10;
constexpr u32 kGsRegisterBase = 0x12000000u, kGsRegisterSize = 8u << 10;
constexpr u32 kIopRamBase = 0x1C000000u, kIopRamSize = 2u << 20;
constexpr u32 kBiosBase = 0x1FC00000u, kBiosSize = 4u << 20;

/* A guest access that hits no memory. */
struct MemoryFault {
    u32 address;
    bool write;
};

class Memory {
public:
    Memory();

    /* Where `size` bytes at `address` live, or null if they span no memory. */
    u8* Translate(u32 address, u32 size);

    u64 Read(u32 address, u32 size);
    void Write(u32 address, u64 value, u32 size);
    /* `count` bytes, as that many one-byte Writes would store them: at once where
       they land in plain memory and no store is watched (a disc read, an RPC's
       answer - byte by byte, a megabyte took a million Writes). */
    void WriteBytes(u32 address, const u8* bytes, std::size_t count);
    /* And `count` bytes read, as one-byte Reads would. */
    void ReadBytes(u32 address, u8* bytes, std::size_t count);

    /* Device registers: a read hook returns the value to read; a write hook
       receives the value written (already stored as plain memory). Hooks are
       per 32-bit word, in the EE and GS register windows. */
    using ReadHook = std::function<u64(u32 address, u64 stored)>;
    using WriteHook = std::function<void(u32 address, u64 value)>;
    void OnRead(u32 address, ReadHook hook);
    void OnWrite(u32 address, WriteHook hook);

    u8* rdram() { return rdram_.data(); }
    u8* scratchpad() { return scratchpad_.data(); }

    /* Log every store that touches one of these guest addresses (--watch-write),
       with the value and the function storing it. */
    void WatchWrites(const std::vector<u32>& addresses);
    /* Whether any store is being watched: if not, a store to main RAM or the
       scratchpad (no register hooks there) may go straight through Translate. */
    bool watching() const { return !watched_.empty(); }

    /* The device registers the EE's thread read or wrote, by address, and how
       often (the run's report). Counted in arrays like the hooks: a map's
       lookup on each of the millions of accesses a game makes cost more than
       the access. */
    std::map<u32, u64> RegisterCounts(bool written) const;

private:
    std::vector<u8> rdram_, scratchpad_, ee_registers_, vu_memory_, gs_registers_, iop_ram_, bios_;
    std::vector<ReadHook> read_hooks_;      /* per register word, both windows */
    std::vector<WriteHook> write_hooks_;
    std::vector<u64> read_counts_, write_counts_;   /* per register word, as the hooks */
    std::vector<u32> watched_;               /* physical addresses */
    void Watched(u32 address, u64 value, u32 size);
};

/* The one guest address space; the generated Read/Write hooks use it. */
Memory& GuestMemory();

}  // namespace ps2host

#endif  /* PS2HOST_MEMORY_H */

```

`host/include/ps2host/path3.h`:

```h
/*
 * PATH3 held back by VIF1's MSKPATH3 (devices.cpp).
 *
 * GIF DMA data waits here while PATH3 is masked. A mask takes effect only at
 * the end of the GIF packet PATH3 is in - the one whose tag has EOP set - so
 * unmasking and masking again at once lets exactly one EOP-ended group of
 * packets through: Release(false). Release(true) lets all of it go (time
 * passing with PATH3 unmasked, or FLUSHA waiting for it).
 */

#ifndef PS2HOST_PATH3_H
#define PS2HOST_PATH3_H

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

namespace ps2host {

class Path3Queue {
public:
    void Push(std::uint32_t word) { held_.push_back(word); }
    void Push(const std::uint32_t* words, std::size_t count) { held_.insert(held_.end(), words, words + count); }
    bool empty() const { return size() == 0; }
    std::size_t size() const { return held_.size() - head_; }

    /* Hands words to `sink` (one run: words, count), up to the end of the
       first packet with EOP set (or all of them). */
    template <typename Sink>
    void ReleaseBlock(bool all, Sink&& sink) {
        const std::uint32_t* words = held_.data() + head_;
        const std::size_t held = size();
        std::size_t end = held;
        if (!all) {
            std::size_t at = 0;
            while (at + 4 <= held) {
                const std::uint64_t low = std::uint64_t(words[at]) | std::uint64_t(words[at + 1]) << 32;
                const std::uint64_t nloop = low & 0x7FFF, eop = (low >> 15) & 1;
                const std::uint64_t flg = (low >> 58) & 3, nreg = (low >> 60) ? (low >> 60) : 16;
                const std::uint64_t qwords = flg == 0 ? nloop * nreg : flg == 1 ? (nloop * nreg + 1) / 2 : nloop;
                at += 4 + std::size_t(qwords) * 4;
                if (eop) break;
            }
            end = std::min(at, held);
        }
        // Taken off before the sink runs: what it does may hold more. Into a
        // buffer kept for it, and what is left moved down only once a good
        // deal has gone (Burnout 3 holds a picture's textures here, 160,000
        // words, and lets them go a group at a time).
        // (A release within a release - the sink letting more go - takes a
        // buffer of its own: the outer one's sink is still reading going_.)
        std::vector<std::uint32_t> nested;
        std::vector<std::uint32_t>& buffer = releasing_ ? nested : going_;
        buffer.assign(words, words + end);
        head_ += end;
        if (head_ == held_.size()) {
            held_.clear();
            head_ = 0;
        } else if (head_ > held_.size() / 2 && head_ >= 65536) {
            held_.erase(held_.begin(), held_.begin() + std::ptrdiff_t(head_));
            head_ = 0;
        }
        if (buffer.empty()) return;
        if (&buffer == &nested) {
            sink(nested.data(), nested.size());
            return;
        }
        releasing_ = true;
        struct Done { bool& flag; ~Done() { flag = false; } } done{releasing_};
        sink(going_.data(), going_.size());
    }

    /* The same, a word at a time. */
    template <typename Sink>
    void Release(bool all, Sink&& sink) {
        ReleaseBlock(all, [&](const std::uint32_t* words, std::size_t count) {
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) sink(words[i]);
        });
    }

private:
    std::vector<std::uint32_t> held_;
    std::size_t head_ = 0;                  // words before it have gone
    std::vector<std::uint32_t> going_;      // what ReleaseBlock hands on
    bool releasing_ = false;
};

}  // namespace ps2host

#endif  /* PS2HOST_PATH3_H */
```

```h
/*

 * steady clock, exclusively (a section entered inside another pauses the

#define PS2HOST_PROFILE_H

public:
    explicit Timed(Section section);
    ~Timed();
    Timed(const Timed&) = delete;
    Timed& operator=(const Timed&) = delete;

private:
    Section section_;
};

   the translated code, the host's devices and the GPU bridge): a thousand
   times a second, the function it is in and seven callers. At the
```

```h
 * the report. Not part of the interface a game port uses (host.h).

    std::string what;

/* A fresh EE register context. VU0's vf0 reads (0, 0, 0, 1) in hardware: macro
   code multiplies by vf0w for a 1.0 (Burnout 3's menu fades do), so it starts
   so, and nothing writes it (lifted::Cop2 drops writes to vf0). */
inline lifted::Context NewContext() {
    lifted::Context c{};
    c.vf[0][3] = 0x3F800000u;
    return c;
}

    std::map<u32, u64> calls;                  /* function -> times called */

   system, saving a task's registers and jumping into another's - cannot run
   as nested native calls. Each guest stack runs on a host fiber of the EE
   thread running it instead, and the port's overrides of the game's switch

   there. Never in an interrupt handler. */

   when body returns, it is finished and the thread's own fiber resumes. */

   `held` the buttons down (bit 0 left, 1 middle, 2 right), and since the last
   call `pressed` those that went down, `wheel` the notches turned (up
   positive), `moved` whether it moved. False without a window that has one. */
struct HostMouseState {
    bool over = false;
    float x = 0.0f, y = 0.0f;
    u32 held = 0, pressed = 0;
    float wheel = 0.0f;
    bool moved = false;
};
bool TakeHostMouse(HostMouseState* state);
/* The game's own pointer (RGBA pixels, rows top-down, clicking at hot_x,
   hot_y), scaled with the window; shown while ShowHostCursor(true), the
   system's otherwise (hidden in fullscreen). */
void SetHostCursor(const u32* rgba, u32 width, u32 height, u32 hot_x, u32 hot_y);
void ShowHostCursor(bool on);
/* The window's controller's motors, as a DualShock 2's: the large one 0-255,
   the small one 0-255 (a DualShock 2's is on or off: 0 or 255). */
void HostRumble(u8 large, u8 small);
/* A controller's adaptive triggers (a DualSense's), left and right: off, a
   resistance from `start` (0-255 of the travel) of `force` (0-255), or a
   vibration from `start` of `force` at `frequency` Hz - until set again. */
struct HostTriggerEffect {
    enum Kind : u8 { kOff, kResistance, kVibration } kind = kOff;
    u8 start = 0, force = 0, frequency = 0;
};
void HostTriggerEffects(const HostTriggerEffect& left, const HostTriggerEffect& right);
/* The controller left as it was found (the game ending): motors stopped,
   trigger effects off. */
void ReleaseController();
/* Controllers (dbc.cpp): each frame, the devices write their state. */
void DbcFrame();
/* The DualShock 2's buttons as the game last read them (bit n: input n held,
   libpad's order - 3 is Start): the keyboard, the game controller and
   --press together. For hooks that act on a button as the game would. */
u16 PadButtonsHeld();
/* The device the player last pressed something on - a key, or a
   controller's button or stick (scripted presses are neither) - and the pad
   read (frame) it was, a press later than the last: kNone before any. */
enum class InputDevice { kNone, kController, kKeyboard };
InputDevice LastInputDevice(u64* frame = nullptr);
/* A game's own input, as DualShock 2 buttons held (bit n: input n), asked for
   each time the pad is read (once a frame, on the EE's thread, at the
   vertical blank): what the mouse means, say. */
void SetPadHook(u16 (*hook)());
/* --press: hold `button` (cross, start, up, ...) for 6 frames from `frame` -
   the player's, on port 0; `padN:button` scripted controller N's (from 1), a
   device of its own (HostDevices) a game can give a port (SetPortDevices). */
bool ScriptPress(const std::string& button, u64 from, u64 to, u8 pressure = 0xFF);
/* --key: hold a key (a Win32 virtual key) from frame `from` to `to`, as if
   the player held it in a window with the focus - a game's own keys
   (SetKeyboardMapper) tested in a scripted run. `key` is a letter or digit,
   a name (enter, escape, space, backspace, tab, up, down, left, right,
   lshift, rshift, lctrl, rctrl) or a virtual key's number (0x20). */
bool ScriptKey(const std::string& key, u64 from, u64 to);
/* Whether a scripted key is held now (HostKeyDown), and whether there are
   any (a scripted run's keys count as the focused window's). */
bool ScriptedKeyDown(int key);
bool KeysScripted();
/* --record-input FILE: every pad report the game reads that differs from the
   one before, as `frame byte byte ...` lines - buttons, sticks and pressures,
   whatever gave them. --replay-input FILE: those reports instead of the pad's,
   each from its frame on. With --virtual-time a recorded session replays
   exactly: a bug met by playing becomes a scripted run. False when the file
   cannot be opened or read. */
bool RecordInput(const std::string& path);
bool ReplayInput(const std::string& path);
/* --paced: a --virtual-time run's vertical blanks no closer than the
   display's, so a person can play it (and record it) at the game's speed. */
void SetPaced(bool on);
/* A game's own controls: the controller's state each pad read, before the
   game sees it - its buttons (DualShock 2 inputs, libpad's order) and their
   pressures to change as the filter likes; the keyboard and scripted presses
   are not given to it. LastInputDevice sees what the player pressed. */
void SetControllerFilter(void (*filter)(HostPadState* pad));
/* A game's own keys: the DualShock 2 inputs the keyboard holds (bit n: input
   n), asked each pad read in place of the host's keys (Backspace Select,
   Enter Start, the arrows the D-pad, 1 3 Q E L2 R2 L1 R1, V C X Z Triangle
   Circle Cross Square) - a game whose player chooses them. Read with
   HostKeyDown while WindowFocused. */
void SetKeyboardMapper(u16 (*mapper)());
/* --mouse FRAME:X,Y[,L|R|U|D]: the mouse at (X, Y) of the picture (0 to 1)
   from that frame - and its left or right button clicked, or the wheel
   turned up or down, then. With any, the window's own mouse is not read. */
bool ScriptMouse(const std::string& spec);
bool ScriptedMouse(HostMouseState* state);
/* Real time: vertical blanks that came while the last was still undelivered (threads.cpp). */
u64 LostVblanks();
/* Real time: how long the EE has slept with every thread waiting - its
   headroom (threads.cpp). */
u64 IdleNanoseconds();
/* The EE timers (timers.cpp): their registers, the host time to their next
   interrupt (< 0: none), and raising the interrupts that are due. */
void InstallTimers();
s64 NanosToNextTimerEvent();
void DeliverTimers();
/* The host's clock, in nanoseconds (timers.cpp), which the EE timers, alarms
   and the IOP's time follow. Real time by default. With --virtual-time it is
   the scheduler's: each spent loop budget advances it by a fixed slice and
   waiting skips it to the next event, so a scripted run is the same run on any
   machine, under any load. Chosen before anything reads it. */
u64 ClockNs();
void SetVirtualClock(bool on);
bool VirtualClock();
/* Disc reads: in a drive's time (a 24x CD's, after a seek - the console's), or

   or in real time when the player's "fast_loading" setting says so - off
   unless the game's port defaults it on (SetFastLoadingDefault), as a game may
   time things by its reads (Mister Mosquito's stage loader does). Scripted
   runs keep the drive's time, so their pictures stay as recorded. */
bool FastDisc();
/* Fast or not from now on: a settings menu's "fast_loading" taking effect at
   once (a scripted run's stays the drive's). */
void SetFastDisc(bool on);
void SetFastLoadingDefault(bool on);
/* VU1's fast mode (--vu-fast: no MAC/STATUS flags where nothing can read

void SetVuFastDefault(bool on);
```

`host/include/ps2host/texture_pack.h`:

```h
#pragma once
/* Texture packs: PCSX2's texture replacements, used as PCSX2 uses them.

   A pack is a folder of .dds and .png files - in folders of their own if it
   likes; only a file's name counts - each named for the texture it replaces
   as PCSX2 names it (GSTextureReplacements.cpp): XXH3 hashes of the texture's
   GS memory and of its CLUT, its region, and its format and size -

     <texture>-<bits>.dds              <texture>-<clut>-<bits>.dds
     <texture>-r<w>x<h>-<bits>.dds     <texture>-<clut>-r<w>x<h>-<bits>.dds

   hashes in hex, bits PSM | TW << 6 | TH << 10 (TCC at bit 14, ignored) |
   TEXA's TA0 << 15, AEM << 23, TA1 << 24 for 24- and 16-bit formats. The
   hash covers what PCSX2's HashTextureLevel does: a texture's blocks as GS
   memory holds them, or its texels expanded (16- and 24-bit formats, a
   region, one smaller than a block) - so a pack made for PCSX2 replaces the
   same textures here.

   Files are read in the background, the first time their texture is drawn:
   the texture as the game has it until then (a frame or two). */

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "ps2host/gs.h"

namespace ps2host {
namespace texture_pack {

/* A replacement as the renderer takes it (GsRenderer::UploadReplacement),
   under its file's `id`: RGBA8 (format 0; alpha as the GS's, 0x80 is 1.0, as
   PCSX2's packs have it) or BC1, BC2, BC3, BC7 (1-4) as the DDS stores them;
   `levels` largest first, one after another in `data`. A PNG's levels below
   the first are made here; a DDS has the ones it has (as PCSX2). */
struct Image {
    std::uint64_t id = 0;
    std::uint32_t format = 0, width = 0, height = 0, levels = 1;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> data;
};
enum Format : std::uint32_t { kRgba8 = 0, kBc1 = 1, kBc2 = 2, kBc3 = 3, kBc7 = 4 };

/* Whether the GPU takes block-compressed images; if not, DDS files are
   decoded to RGBA8 as they are read. */
void SetBlockCompression(bool on);

/* Which texture: PCSX2's TextureName, as its file names spell it. */
struct Name {
    std::uint64_t texture = 0, clut = 0;
    std::uint32_t region_w = 0, region_h = 0;
    std::uint32_t bits = 0;
    bool operator==(const Name& o) const {
        return texture == o.texture && clut == o.clut && region_w == o.region_w && region_h == o.region_h &&
               bits == o.bits;
    }
    std::string Text() const;           // as a file is named, without its extension
};

/* The pack in `directory` (and its folders): the files it has, by name. The
   number of them; 0 for none or no such folder. */
std::size_t Open(const std::string& directory);
std::size_t Count();

/* Whether replacements are drawn (Tab, the "texture_pack" setting). Each
   change bumps Generation: textures the game has already drawn come back as
   it has them, or replaced. */
bool Enabled();
void SetEnabled(bool on);
std::uint64_t Generation();

/* PCSX2's name for the texture TEX0 describes, CLAMP's region of it, with
   TEXA, from `memory` - and `clut`, the GS model's 256 entries (Gs::Clut). */
Name NameOf(const gs::Memory& memory, std::uint64_t tex0, std::uint64_t clamp, std::uint64_t texa,
            const std::uint32_t* clut);

/* The replacement for `name`: an override's, or the pack's (when it is on);
   null if there is none - or while its file is still being read (asked for
   here: `*pending` says so; a later call has it). */
std::shared_ptr<const Image> Find(const Name& name, bool* pending);

/* A game's own replacements (overrides), beside any pack and drawn whether
   the pack is on or not: the PNG `png` (alpha as the GS's, 0x80 opaque) for
   the texture `name` names - spelt as a pack file's name, without its
   extension; null clears that one. A PNG passed again (the same pointer) is
   not decoded again. False for a name or PNG that cannot be read. Each
   change bumps Generation. */
bool SetOverride(const std::string& name, const std::uint8_t* png, std::size_t bytes);
/* An override a game draws itself: its pixels (RGBA8 as a PNG's, rows top
   down, alpha as the GS's) as an image, its smaller levels made - kept to
   use (SetOverride below) as often as the game likes, no work again. */
std::shared_ptr<const Image> MakeImage(std::vector<std::uint32_t> rgba, std::uint32_t width, std::uint32_t height);
/* That image for the texture `name` names (as SetOverride's PNG); null
   clears it. False for a name that cannot be read. */
bool SetOverride(const std::string& name, std::shared_ptr<const Image> image);
void ClearOverrides();

/* Whether anything could be replaced: overrides, or a pack that is on. */
bool Active();
/* Whether a texture of these bits (PSM | TW << 6 | TH << 10) could be: the
   cheap test before NameOf's hashing. */
bool Wanted(std::uint32_t bits);

}  // namespace texture_pack
}  // namespace ps2host
```

`host/include/ps2host/timeline.h`:

```h
/*
 * The frame-pacing profiler: a timeline of every thread's work and of every
 * frame's way to the screen (PS2HOST_PROFILE=file). Each thread records into
 * its own buffer - what it was busy with (the profile.h sections, the VIF1
 * worker's and the GS thread's busy spans, the EE's idle waits), when each
 * vertical blank came, when each picture was due and when it was shown, the
 * pictures dropped and the blanks lost - and at the end:
 *
 *  - the file: Chrome's trace format (ui.perfetto.dev or chrome://tracing
 *    shows it), a lane a thread;
 *  - a summary (stderr): the frames shown, their intervals' percentiles, the
 *    dropped frames (a picture dropped before it was shown, a present
 *    interval past one and a half frames, a blank the EE lost) and for the
 *    worst, which thread was busy in the frame before it.
 *
 * PS2HOST_PROFILE_FROM=N starts recording at frame N (the race, not the
 * boot). Off (the variable unset) every call returns at once.
 */
#ifndef PS2HOST_TIMELINE_H
#define PS2HOST_TIMELINE_H

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>

namespace ps2host::timeline {

/* Whether recording is on (PS2HOST_PROFILE set, from its first frame). */
bool On();
/* Now, in the timeline's clock (steady, nanoseconds). */
std::uint64_t Now();
/* The calling thread's name ("EE", "GS", "VIF1 worker", "present"...): its
   lane's, the system's (debuggers and profilers show it), and one the
   threads' CPU report (ThreadCpu) counts. Always, profiling on or off. */
void NameThread(const char* name);
/* --frame-times: each named thread's share of a core since the last call
   ("EE 21%, VIF1 worker 46%, ..."), user and system time together. */
std::string ThreadCpu();
/* A span of work on the calling thread, [from, to); one of the same name
   ending within 20 us before it is extended instead (the file stays small). */
void Span(const char* name, std::uint64_t from_ns, std::uint64_t to_ns);
/* A moment on the calling thread. */
void Instant(const char* name, std::uint64_t at_ns, std::uint64_t value = 0);
/* A vertical blank delivered to the game: frame `frame` begins. */
void Frame(std::uint64_t frame);
/* A blank the EE was too busy for: lost to the game. */
void BlankLost();
/* A picture shown (due when, shown when), or dropped before it was. */
void Presented(std::uint64_t due_ns, std::uint64_t shown_ns);
void Dropped(std::uint64_t due_ns);
/* The file and the summary: at the run's end. */
void Finish();

}  // namespace ps2host::timeline

#endif  // PS2HOST_TIMELINE_H
```

`host/include/ps2host/vif.h`:

```h
/*
 * A VIF's command stream (EE User's Manual, chapter 6): VIFcodes and their
 * data, delivered to the VU behind the VIF and to the GS.
 *
 * MPG loads microprograms into the VU's instruction memory, UNPACK expands
 * packed vectors into its data memory (formats S/V2/V3/V4 of 32, 16 or 8 bits
 * and V4-5, with STMASK/STROW/STCOL masking, STMOD's offset and difference
 * modes, and STCYCL's skipping and filling writes), and MSCAL, MSCALF and MSCNT
 * run the microprogram - to its end, at once: the EE sees it done by the time
 * it could look. VIF1's double buffering (BASE, OFFSET, TOPS and the FLG bit of
 * UNPACK) and ITOP feed XTOP and XITOP. DIRECT and DIRECTHL carry GIF data on
 * PATH2; MSKPATH3 masks PATH3, which code that hands PATH3 over waits on.
 */

#ifndef PS2HOST_VIF_H
#define PS2HOST_VIF_H

#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace ps2host {

class Vu;

class VifStream {
public:
    /* The VU behind this VIF (VU1 for VIF1); none drops VU traffic. */
    Vu* vu = nullptr;
    bool double_buffered = false;   /* VIF1's BASE/OFFSET/TOPS */
    /* Called when MSKPATH3 masks (true) or unmasks (false) PATH3. */
    std::function<void(bool masked)> on_mask_path3;
    /* Each word of DIRECT/DIRECTHL data: GIF data on PATH2. */
    std::function<void(std::uint32_t word)> on_direct;
    /* DIRECT's data a run at a time, from guest address `from` (Words); when
       unset, a word at a time through on_direct. */
    std::function<void(const std::uint32_t* words, std::uint32_t count, std::uint32_t from)> on_direct_block;
    /* Commands worth seeing in a trace (FLUSHA), when set. */
    std::function<void(const char* what)> on_trace;

    /* The next 32-bit word of the stream, from the FIFO or a DMA transfer. */
    void Word(std::uint32_t word);
    /* `count` words from guest address `from`, as Word each (keeping
       g_dma_source), DIRECT's data handed on a run at a time. */
    void Words(const std::uint32_t* words, std::uint32_t count, std::uint32_t from);

    std::uint64_t commands() const { return commands_; }
    std::uint64_t data_words() const { return data_words_; }
    /* For the report: how often each command came, by name. */
    std::string Summary() const;

    // Registers the EE can read (VIF1_TOP, VIF1_TOPS, ITOP, ...).
    std::uint32_t top = 0, tops = 0, base = 0, offset = 0, itop = 0, itops = 0, dbf = 0;
    std::uint32_t mask = 0, mode = 0, row[4] = {}, col[4] = {};

private:
    enum class Data { None, Direct, Mpg, Unpack, Mask, Row, Col };
    std::uint32_t pending_ = 0;     /* data words still owed to the last command */
    Data data_ = Data::None;
    std::uint32_t cycle_length_ = 0, write_length_ = 0;     /* STCYCL's CL and WL */
    std::uint32_t data_index_ = 0;  /* words of the current command's data so far */
    std::uint32_t mpg_address_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t end_pc_ = 0;      /* where MSCNT continues */
    struct Unpack {
        std::uint32_t address = 0, format = 0, num = 0, written = 0;
        bool masked = false, unsigned_ = false;
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
    } unpack_;
    std::uint64_t commands_ = 0, data_words_ = 0;
    std::array<std::uint64_t, 128> by_command_{};

    /* Words of data an UNPACK of `num` elements in format `format` reads. */
    std::uint32_t UnpackWords(std::uint32_t format, std::uint32_t num) const;
    void UnpackData(std::uint32_t word);
    /* A run of UNPACK's data words: whole elements straight from them while
       none is left part-read, the rest a word at a time. */
    void UnpackRun(const std::uint32_t* words, std::uint32_t count);
    /* One element's components from its bytes, as UNPACK expands them. */
    void Element(const std::uint8_t* b, std::uint32_t c[4]) const;
    void UnpackFill();
    void WriteElement(const std::uint32_t value[4], bool from_data);
    void Start(std::uint32_t pc);
};

/* The VIF1 stream fed by stores to its FIFO, 0x10005000. */
VifStream& Vif1();
/* VIF0's, at 0x10004000; it feeds VU0. */
VifStream& Vif0();

}  // namespace ps2host

#endif  /* PS2HOST_VIF_H */

```

`host/include/ps2host/vu.h`:

```h
/*
 * The vector units in micro mode: a VU running a microprogram out of its own
 * instruction memory over its own data memory, as VIF1 starts VU1 (MSCAL) and
 * the EE starts VU0 (vcallms).
 *
 * A microinstruction is a pair: an upper instruction for the FMAC units and a
 * lower one for everything else, issued together. The upper encodes exactly as
 * VU0 macro mode's COP2 operations do, so it runs through the runtime's
 * lifted::Cop2 - the arithmetic verified against vu0.py - as do the lower
 * operations macro mode shares (MOVE, MR32, DIV, SQRT, RSQRT, MTIR, MFIR, the
 * R register, and the integer ALU). Loads, stores, branches, the flags, the
 * elementary functions and XGKICK are here.
 *
 * Within a pair the lower instruction reads its registers before the upper
 * writes them, and where both write the same field the upper's result stands.
 * An E bit ends the program after the pair that follows it.
 *
 * Timing is modelled where code can see it, in cycles: a pair reading a vector
 * field still being computed stalls until it lands (4 cycles after the FMAC or
 * load issued); Q arrives 7 cycles after DIV and SQRT, 13 after RSQRT, and P
 * after the EFU operation's latency, the old value readable meanwhile; and the
 * MAC, status and clip flags reach the lower instructions (FMAND, FCAND...) 4
 * cycles after the upper operation that set them. Hand-pipelined microcode -
 * Burnout 3's clip tests, which read the flags of the vertex before - depends
 * on all of these (engine/tools/vuhazards.py lists where).
 */

#ifndef PS2HOST_VU_H
#define PS2HOST_VU_H

#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <map>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "ps2rt/lifted.h"

namespace lifted { struct FmacOp; }

namespace ps2host {

struct VuRunState;

class Vu {
public:
    using u32 = std::uint32_t;
    using u64 = std::uint64_t;

    /* VU0 (4 KB of each memory) or VU1 (16 KB). */
    explicit Vu(int index);
    Vu(const Vu&) = delete;             /* its memory spans point into itself */
    Vu& operator=(const Vu&) = delete;

    /* Instruction and data memory: the VU's own, or (Attach) the EE's view of
       it at 0x11000000, which code also reads and writes directly. */
    struct Span {
        std::uint8_t* p;
        std::size_t n;
        std::uint8_t* data() const { return p; }
        std::size_t size() const { return n; }
    };
    Span micro, data;
    void Attach(std::uint8_t* micro_memory, std::uint8_t* data_memory);
    lifted::Context regs{};         /* vf, vc (VI0-15, R 20, I 21, Q 22), vacc */
    /* The flags as the lower instructions read them, and P. */
    u32 mac = 0, status = 0, clip = 0, p = 0;
    u32 top = 0, itop = 0;          /* what XTOP and XITOP read (VU1) */
    u32 resume = 0;                 /* where the last run ended: MSCNT continues there */

    /* XGKICK: each quadword of the GIF packet, as PATH1 delivers it. */
    std::function<void(u64 low, u64 high)> on_kick;
    /* ...or, when set, a packet's quadwords a contiguous run of words at a
       time (as data memory holds them; a run ends where memory wraps). */
    std::function<void(const u32* words, u32 count)> on_kick_block;
    /* Instruction memory was written (MPG, or a store into it): compiled
       programs are compared with it again before they next run. */
    void MicroWritten() { ++micro_generation_; }

    /* Runs from instruction address `pc` (bytes) to the end of the program;
       returns the instruction pairs executed. Stops after `limit` regardless. */
    u64 Run(u32 pc, u64 limit = u64(1) << 24);

    u64 pairs() const { return pairs_; }
    /* Of those, the pairs run compiled ahead of time (vu_core.h). */
    u64 compiled_pairs() const { return compiled_pairs_; }
    /* Compiled programs entered, found with other code in memory than they
       were compiled from, and the bytes compared to tell. */
    u64 compiled_entries() const { return compiled_entries_; }
    u64 compiled_stale() const { return compiled_stale_; }
    u64 compiled_checked() const { return compiled_checked_; }
    u64 kicks() const { return kicks_; }
    /* Whether Run takes compiled programs where it has them (the tests run
       the interpreter alone to compare). */
    bool use_compiled = true;
    /* --vu-fast: compiled VU1 programs that never read MAC or STATUS run
       blocks that do not compute them (VuCompiled::fast_blocks): faster, and
       exact but for those flags - which a later run reading them before an
       FMAC of its own lands would see. */
    bool fast = false;
    /* For tests: everything a run can change, the same in both (`flags`
       false: but the MAC and STATUS flags, landed, latest and in flight). */
    bool SameState(const Vu& other, bool flags = true) const;
    /* --vu-record: each program a run starts, and the code reachable from
       where it starts, to `path` (engine/tools/vurecomp.py compiles them). */
    static void RecordPrograms(const std::string& path);
    /* --vu-snapshot: from frame `from` on, `count` VU1 runs as they start -
       where, the registers and flags, both memories - to `path`, for
       --vu-bench. SnapshotFrame: the frame now (devices.cpp). */
    static void Snapshots(const std::string& path, u64 from, u32 count);
    static void SnapshotFrame(u64 frame);
    /* --vu-bench: those runs again, on a VU1 of its own, compiled where the
       port has them, in `passes` passes; the fastest pass's time a pair, and a
       hash of every run's registers and memory after (what a change to the
       VU must leave alone). Returns 0, or 1 when the file cannot be read. */
    static int Bench(const std::string& path, int passes = 5, bool fast = false);
    /* How often each program address was started, for reports. */
    const std::map<u32, u64>& starts() const;

    /* For tests: one 128-bit quadword of data memory. */
    u32* Quad(u32 address);

private:
    friend struct VuCore;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> own_micro_, own_data_;
    u32 data_mask_;                 /* in quadwords */
    u64 pairs_ = 0, kicks_ = 0, compiled_pairs_ = 0, compiled_entries_ = 0, compiled_stale_ = 0,
        compiled_checked_ = 0;
    std::vector<u64> start_counts_;         // runs started, by pair address (starts() as a map)
    mutable std::map<u32, u64> starts_;
    // Instruction memory's writes so far, and for each compiled program the
    // count when it was last found in memory: unchanged since, it still is
    // (2.3 million entries a race compared 4.4 GB of code otherwise).
    u64 micro_generation_ = 1;
    std::unordered_map<const void*, u64> held_at_;
    // The compiled program found at each pair address and its block table,
    // while instruction memory is as it was then (micro_generation_): a run
    // starts with an index, not three lookups by hash and one by tree.
    struct Entered {
        const void* program = nullptr;      // const VuCompiled*
        const void* table = nullptr;        // const std::vector<VuBlock>*
        u64 generation = 0;
        bool fast = false;
    };
    std::vector<Entered> entered_;

    // Compiled code: the vector registers that may hold fields the model's
    // Clean would change (bit r for VF r) - loaded so, or not known; the FMAC
    // cleans only those operands. Every bit is set as a run starts and when
    // the interpreter runs (it does not keep them); VF0 is always clean.
    u32 unclean_ = ~1u;
    bool acc_unclean_ = true;       // the same for ACC
    // An upper operation's result whose destination is VF0: the register
    // keeps 0, 0, 0, 1, but the MAC and status flags are this result's (a
    // test that only wants the signs - `msubz.xyzw vf00, ...` then FMAND -
    // writes nowhere).
    u32 discarded_[4] = {};

    /* Timing, in cycles (one per pair issued, plus stalls). */
    u64 cycle_ = 0;
    u64 vf_ready_[32][4] = {};      /* when each vector field's pending write lands */
    u32 q_next_ = 0, p_next_ = 0;   /* DIV's and the EFU's results in flight */
    u64 q_ready_ = 0, p_ready_ = 0;
    bool q_busy_ = false, p_busy_ = false;
    /* No earlier than the first of the busy Q and P lands (~0: neither is
       busy): what each pair looks at before landing them, one compare for
       four. LandNow sets it again. */
    u64 qp_due_ = ~u64(0);
    /* The FMAC sets the flags as it finishes: what upper instructions have
       produced so far, and what is still on its way to the lower's view. */
    u32 mac_latest_ = 0, status_latest_ = 0, clip_latest_ = 0;
    struct FlagWrite { u64 ready; u32 mac, status, clip; bool sets_mac, sets_clip; };
    /* In the order they were set, which is the order they land in (each
       lands 4 cycles after it was set, and time only goes forward): a ring,
       flag_head_ the oldest. */
    FlagWrite flag_queue_[8] = {};
    int flag_head_ = 0, flag_count_ = 0;
    void PushFlags(const FlagWrite& write);   /* (vu_core.h) */
    void Land();                    /* results whose time has come (a look, inline) */
    void LandNow();                 /* ...landing them */
    void LandAll();
    /* The CLIP judgements in flight (when each lands, its value): what
       SameState compares without the MAC and STATUS flags. */
    std::vector<std::pair<u64, u32>> ClipsInFlight() const;

    struct Pending;
    /* The interpreter, from where `state` stands. */
    void Interpret(VuRunState& state, u64 limit);
    /* Compiled programs from where `state` stands, as far as they go
       (vu_core.h); whether any ran. */
    bool RunCompiled(VuRunState& state, u64 limit);
    void Lower(u32 word, u32 pc, Pending& out, u32* branch);
    void Upper(u32 word, int* written_reg, u32* written_lanes, bool* set_flags,
               const lifted::FmacOp* fmac = nullptr);
    void Kick(u32 address);
};

/* VU1, which VIF1 loads and starts. */
Vu& Vu1();
/* VU0, which VIF0 loads and the EE starts (vcallms) or VIF0 does. */
Vu& Vu0();

}  // namespace ps2host

#endif  /* PS2HOST_VU_H */

```

`host/include/ps2host/vu_core.h`:

```h
/*
 * The vector units' steps, for microprograms compiled ahead of time.
 *
 * engine/tools/vurecomp.py turns the microprograms a game runs into C++: each
 * instruction pair one block of straight-line code, its registers, fields and
 * operations constants. That code works the Vu's state through VuCore, whose
 * steps are the interpreter's (vu.cpp: Run, Lower, Upper) taken apart - the
 * stalls and the pipelines included, so that a compiled program and the
 * interpreter end in the same state, to the cycle. The interpreter stays the
 * reference: VuCompiledIsTheInterpreter (host tests) runs random programs
 * both ways and compares everything.
 */

#ifndef PS2HOST_VU_CORE_H
#define PS2HOST_VU_CORE_H

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>

#include "ps2host/vu.h"
#include "ps2rt/vu_math.h"

#if defined(__AVX2__)
#include <immintrin.h>
#endif

#if defined(_MSC_VER)
#define PS2HOST_VU_INLINE __forceinline
#else
#define PS2HOST_VU_INLINE inline __attribute__((always_inline))
#endif

namespace ps2host {

/* What the lower instruction of a pair leaves for the end of the pair. */
struct Vu::Pending {
    PS2HOST_VU_INLINE Pending() {}  // (MSVC called the implicit one, not inlined)
    int vf = -1;                    // a vector register the lower writes
    u32 lanes = 0, value[4] = {};
    bool vc = false;                // the lower changed control registers
    u32 vc_after[32];               // ...to these (only when vc: a pair is not worth zeroing 128 bytes)
    bool p = false;
    u32 p_value = 0;
    int p_latency = 0;              // the EFU op's, in cycles
    int q_latency = 0;              // DIV, SQRT, RSQRT's
    bool q_set = false;             // compiled code: Q's next value (q_value), not through vc_after
    u32 q_value = 0;
    bool clean = false;             // compiled code: every field of `value` as Clean leaves it
};

inline void Vu::LandNow() {
    if (q_busy_ && q_ready_ <= cycle_) { regs.vc[lifted::kRegQ] = q_next_; q_busy_ = false; }
    if (p_busy_ && p_ready_ <= cycle_) { p = p_next_; p_busy_ = false; }
    qp_due_ = std::min(q_busy_ ? q_ready_ : ~u64(0), p_busy_ ? p_ready_ : ~u64(0));
    while (flag_count_ && flag_queue_[flag_head_].ready <= cycle_) {
        const FlagWrite& f = flag_queue_[flag_head_];
        if (f.sets_mac) { mac = f.mac; status = (status & ~0x3u) | (f.status & 0x3u); status |= f.status & 0xC0u; }
        if (f.sets_clip) clip = f.clip;
        flag_head_ = (flag_head_ + 1) & 7;
        --flag_count_;
    }
}

PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Vu::PushFlags(const FlagWrite& write) {
    if (flag_count_ < 8) flag_queue_[(flag_head_ + flag_count_++) & 7] = write;
}

PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Vu::Land() {
    // The flags land inline: nearly every pair has an FMAC's flags arriving,
    // and a call for each was 5% of a race. (Q, P and the flags are apart:
    // the order they land in within a cycle changes nothing.)
    while (flag_count_ && flag_queue_[flag_head_].ready <= cycle_) {
        const FlagWrite& f = flag_queue_[flag_head_];
        if (f.sets_mac) { mac = f.mac; status = (status & ~0x3u) | (f.status & 0x3u); status |= f.status & 0xC0u; }
        if (f.sets_clip) clip = f.clip;
        flag_head_ = (flag_head_ + 1) & 7;
        --flag_count_;
    }
    if (qp_due_ <= cycle_) LandNow();
}

/* Where a run stands between pairs. */
struct VuRunState {
    std::uint32_t pc = 0;
    std::uint32_t delayed = ~0u;    // a branch the pair before took: where the next pair goes after it
    bool stopping = false;          // the pair before had E: this one is the last
    std::uint64_t count = 0;        // pairs run
    bool done = false;              // the program has ended
};

/* A block of a compiled program: pairs run in a line from its first, the
   run's state then left where it goes next (s.pc), or done. */
using VuBlock = void (*)(Vu& vu, VuRunState& state, std::uint64_t limit);

/* A microprogram compiled ahead of time. `code` is what it was compiled
   from, as runs: a count of runs, then for each its byte address in
   instruction memory, its length in words and the words. Its blocks start at
   `starts` (byte addresses, ascending); a run goes from block to block while
   the next starts one of them, and to the interpreter otherwise. */
struct VuCompiled {
    int unit;                       // 0: VU0, 1: VU1
    std::uint32_t entry;            // where a run it was recorded from started
    const std::uint32_t* code;
    const std::uint32_t* starts;
    const VuBlock* blocks;
    std::uint32_t block_count;
    const VuBlock* fast_blocks = nullptr;   // the same without MAC and STATUS (--vu-fast), or none
};
/* Adds one to those Vu::Run looks for (the generated file does, as it starts). */
void RegisterVuProgram(const VuCompiled* program);

struct VuCore {
    using u32 = Vu::u32;
    using u64 = Vu::u64;
    using Pending = Vu::Pending;    // what the generated code holds a pair's lower writes in
    static constexpr u32 kNone = ~0u;
    static constexpr int kFmacLatency = 4;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ stalls
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u64& Cycle(Vu& v) { return v.cycle_; }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Wait(u64& t, const Vu& v, int reg, int lane) {
        t = std::max(t, v.vf_ready_[reg][lane]);
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void WaitQ(u64& t, const Vu& v) { if (v.q_busy_) t = std::max(t, v.q_ready_); }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void WaitP(u64& t, const Vu& v) { if (v.p_busy_) t = std::max(t, v.p_ready_); }
    /* Compiled code lands the flags lazily: an FMAC's flags arrive four
       cycles after it, and landing them at every pair (as the interpreter
       does) was a loop of thirty instructions a pair. Nothing sees the
       landed flags but the lower instructions that read or write them
       (Mac, Status, Clip below), and they land first whatever has arrived
       by now - so they see what eager landing would have left, in the same
       order. A full queue lands what has arrived before taking more, and a
       run lands everything as it ends (Run's LandAll). Q and P still land
       here. */
    /* The cycle is the block's own (a local the generated code keeps, and
       writes back to cycle_ as it leaves): MSVC read cycle_ again after every
       store otherwise. LandNow reads cycle_, so it is written back first. */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Issue(Vu& v, u64& cycle, u64 t) {
        cycle = t;
        if (v.qp_due_ <= t) {
            v.cycle_ = t;
            v.LandNow();
        }
    }
    /* Issue for a pair that neither reads Q or P nor starts what sets them
       (vurecomp.py: they land at the next pair that does - the same values
       wherever they are read). */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void IssueAt(u64& cycle, u64 t) { cycle = t; }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void LandFlags(Vu& v, u64 cycle) {
        while (v.flag_count_ && v.flag_queue_[v.flag_head_].ready <= cycle) {
            const Vu::FlagWrite& f = v.flag_queue_[v.flag_head_];
            if (f.sets_mac) {
                v.mac = f.mac;
                v.status = (v.status & ~0x3u) | (f.status & 0x3u);
                v.status |= f.status & 0xC0u;
            }
            if (f.sets_clip) v.clip = f.clip;
            v.flag_head_ = (v.flag_head_ + 1) & 7;
            --v.flag_count_;
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ lower
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Vi(const Vu& v, u32 r) { return v.regs.vc[r]; }
    /* setvi: only VI1-VI15 (the generator leaves out the others). */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void SetVi(Vu& v, u32 r, u32 value) { v.regs.vc[r] = value & 0xFFFF; }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32* Quad(Vu& v, u32 address) {
        return reinterpret_cast<u32*>(v.data.data() + std::size_t(address & v.data_mask_) * 16);
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Load(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, u32 address, int it, u32 dest) {
        const u32* q = Quad(v, address);
        out.vf = it;
        out.lanes = dest;
        std::memcpy(out.value, q, 16);
        out.clean = Clean4(q);
    }
    /* Whether Clean leaves all four fields as they are: no infinity or NaN
       exponent, and no denormal (a zero exponent with a mantissa). */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE bool Clean4(const u32* q) {
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
        const __m128i x = _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(q));
        const __m128i exponent = _mm_and_si128(x, _mm_set1_epi32(0x7F800000));
        const __m128i zero = _mm_setzero_si128();
        const __m128i huge = _mm_cmpeq_epi32(exponent, _mm_set1_epi32(0x7F800000));
        const __m128i denormal = _mm_andnot_si128(
            _mm_cmpeq_epi32(_mm_and_si128(x, _mm_set1_epi32(0x007FFFFF)), zero), _mm_cmpeq_epi32(exponent, zero));
        return _mm_movemask_epi8(_mm_or_si128(huge, denormal)) == 0;
#else
        for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane)
            if (lifted::Clean(q[lane]) != q[lane]) return false;
        return true;
#endif
    }
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Store(Vu& v, u32 address, int fs) {
        u32* q = Quad(v, address);
        const u32* from = v.regs.vf[fs];
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
        if constexpr (Dest == 15) {             // the quadword in one move (MSVC made four of the fields)
            _mm_storeu_si128(reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(q), _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(from)));
            return;
        }
#endif
        if constexpr ((Dest & 8) != 0) q[0] = from[0];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 4) != 0) q[1] = from[1];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 2) != 0) q[2] = from[2];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 1) != 0) q[3] = from[3];
    }
    /* ILW, ILWR: the first lane dest names (the generator gives it). */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Word(Vu& v, u32 address, int lane) { return Quad(v, address)[lane]; }
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void StoreVi(Vu& v, u32 address, u32 it) {     // ISW, ISWR
        u32* q = Quad(v, address);
        const u32 value = v.regs.vc[it] & 0xFFFF;
        if constexpr ((Dest & 8) != 0) q[0] = value;
        if constexpr ((Dest & 4) != 0) q[1] = value;
        if constexpr ((Dest & 2) != 0) q[2] = value;
        if constexpr ((Dest & 1) != 0) q[3] = value;
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Mfp(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, int it, u32 dest) {
        out.vf = it;
        out.lanes = dest;
        for (u32& x : out.value) x = v.p;
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Top(const Vu& v) { return v.top; }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Itop(const Vu& v) { return v.itop; }
    static void Kick(Vu& v, u32 address) { v.Kick(address); }
    /* Through macro mode's COP2 (MOVE, MR32, MTIR, MFIR, the R register, DIV,
       SQRT, RSQRT), its writes held back to the pair's end. */
    static void ThroughCop2(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, u32 word, int it, u32 dest) {
        u32 before_vc[32], before_vf[4];
        std::memcpy(before_vc, v.regs.vc, sizeof before_vc);
        std::memcpy(before_vf, v.regs.vf[it], sizeof before_vf);
        lifted::Cop2(v.regs, 0x4A000000u | (word & 0x01FFFFFF));
        if (std::memcmp(before_vf, v.regs.vf[it], sizeof before_vf) != 0) {
            out.vf = it;
            out.lanes = dest;
            std::memcpy(out.value, v.regs.vf[it], 16);
            std::memcpy(v.regs.vf[it], before_vf, sizeof before_vf);
        }
        if (std::memcmp(before_vc, v.regs.vc, sizeof before_vc) != 0) {
            out.vc = true;
            std::memcpy(out.vc_after, v.regs.vc, sizeof out.vc_after);
            std::memcpy(v.regs.vc, before_vc, sizeof before_vc);
        }
    }
    /* The lower operations macro mode shares, as ThroughCop2 would leave
       them: a vector write held back only if it changes the register, a VI
       write only if it changes the VI, Q's next value set. */
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
    /* Dest's fields as a lane mask (x the first lane). Registers are read
       and written whole, as 16 bytes: a field stored alone and the register
       then read whole is a store the processor cannot forward (a stall of a
       dozen cycles or more, every time). */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE __m128i LaneMask(u32 dest) {
        return _mm_cmpeq_epi32(_mm_and_si128(_mm_set1_epi32(int(dest)), _mm_set_epi32(1, 2, 4, 8)),
                               _mm_set_epi32(1, 2, 4, 8));
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE __m128i Blend(__m128i mask, __m128i taken, __m128i kept) {
        return _mm_or_si128(_mm_and_si128(mask, taken), _mm_andnot_si128(mask, kept));
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void HoldVf(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, int it, u32 dest, __m128i value) {
        if (it == 0) return;
        const __m128i before = _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(v.regs.vf[it]));
        const __m128i after = Blend(LaneMask(dest), value, before);
        if (_mm_movemask_epi8(_mm_cmpeq_epi32(after, before)) == 0xFFFF) return;
        out.vf = it;
        out.lanes = dest;
        _mm_storeu_si128(reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(out.value), after);
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Move(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, int it, int fs, u32 dest) {
        out.clean = !((v.unclean_ >> fs) & 1);
        HoldVf(v, out, it, dest, _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(v.regs.vf[fs])));
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Mr32(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, int it, int fs, u32 dest) {
        out.clean = !((v.unclean_ >> fs) & 1);
        HoldVf(v, out, it, dest, _mm_shuffle_epi32(_mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(v.regs.vf[fs])),
                                                   _MM_SHUFFLE(0, 3, 2, 1)));
    }
#else
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void HoldVf(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, int it, u32 dest, const u32 value[4]) {
        if (it == 0) return;
        u32 after[4];
        std::memcpy(after, v.regs.vf[it], 16);
        for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane)
            if (dest & (8u >> lane)) after[lane] = value[lane];
        if (std::memcmp(after, v.regs.vf[it], 16) == 0) return;
        out.vf = it;
        out.lanes = dest;
        std::memcpy(out.value, after, 16);
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Move(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, int it, int fs, u32 dest) {
        const u32 value[4] = {v.regs.vf[fs][0], v.regs.vf[fs][1], v.regs.vf[fs][2], v.regs.vf[fs][3]};
        out.clean = !((v.unclean_ >> fs) & 1);
        HoldVf(v, out, it, dest, value);
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Mr32(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, int it, int fs, u32 dest) {
        const u32* a = v.regs.vf[fs];
        const u32 value[4] = {a[1], a[2], a[3], a[0]};
        out.clean = !((v.unclean_ >> fs) & 1);
        HoldVf(v, out, it, dest, value);
    }
#endif
    /* An upper write of Dest's fields into `reg`: clean ones clean the
       register when they are all of it (else it stays as it was); others
       make it unknown. */
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Wrote(Vu& v, int reg, bool clean) {
        if (reg <= 0) return;
        if (!clean) v.unclean_ |= 1u << reg;
        else if constexpr (Dest == 15) v.unclean_ &= ~(1u << reg);
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Mfir(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, int it, int is, u32 dest) {
        u32 x = v.regs.vc[is] & 0xFFFF;
        if (x & 0x8000) x |= 0xFFFF0000u;
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
        HoldVf(v, out, it, dest, _mm_set1_epi32(int(x)));
#else
        const u32 value[4] = {x, x, x, x};
        HoldVf(v, out, it, dest, value);
#endif
    }
    /* MTIR: VI1-VI15 only (the generator leaves out the others). */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Mtir(Vu& v, Vu::Pending& out, int it, int fs, int fsf) {
        const u32 value = v.regs.vf[fs][fsf] & 0xFFFF;
        if (value == v.regs.vc[it]) return;
        out.vc = true;
        std::memcpy(out.vc_after, v.regs.vc, sizeof out.vc_after);
        out.vc_after[it] = value;
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Divide(Vu::Pending& out, u32 q, int latency) {
        out.q_set = true;
        out.q_value = q;
        out.q_latency = latency;
    }
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
    /* DIV and SQRT in single precision: one operation on clean operands,
       rounded once to single precision, is the model's double one narrowed
       (53 bits >= 2 x 24 + 2 for the nearest; toward zero, twice is once),
       and the result cleaned as Result does. Clamp: Clean of an operand
       going into arithmetic under DAZ (a VU run: VuRounding). */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Clamp(u32 bits) {
        return (bits & 0x7F800000u) == 0x7F800000u ? (bits & lifted::kSign) | lifted::kMax : bits;
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Div(const Vu& v, int fs, int fsf, int ft, int ftf) {
        const u32 num = v.regs.vf[fs][fsf], den = v.regs.vf[ft][ftf];
        if ((den & 0x7F800000u) == 0) return ((num ^ den) & lifted::kSign) | lifted::kMax;   // Value(den) == 0
        const __m128 q = _mm_div_ss(_mm_castsi128_ps(_mm_cvtsi32_si128(int(Clamp(num)))),
                                    _mm_castsi128_ps(_mm_cvtsi32_si128(int(Clamp(den)))));
        return lifted::Clean(u32(_mm_cvtsi128_si32(_mm_castps_si128(q))));
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Sqrt(const Vu& v, int ft, int ftf) {
        const u32 x = Clamp(v.regs.vf[ft][ftf]) & ~lifted::kSign;
        const __m128 root = _mm_sqrt_ss(_mm_castsi128_ps(_mm_cvtsi32_si128(int(x))));
        return lifted::Clean(u32(_mm_cvtsi128_si32(_mm_castps_si128(root))));
    }
#else
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Div(const Vu& v, int fs, int fsf, int ft, int ftf) {
        const u32 num = v.regs.vf[fs][fsf], den = v.regs.vf[ft][ftf];
        return lifted::Value(den) == 0.0 ? ((num ^ den) & lifted::kSign) | lifted::kMax
                                         : lifted::Result(lifted::Value(num) / lifted::Value(den));
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Sqrt(const Vu& v, int ft, int ftf) {
        return lifted::Result(std::sqrt(std::fabs(lifted::Value(v.regs.vf[ft][ftf]))));
    }
#endif
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Rsqrt(const Vu& v, int fs, int fsf, int ft, int ftf) {
        const u32 num = v.regs.vf[fs][fsf];
        const double root = std::sqrt(std::fabs(lifted::Value(v.regs.vf[ft][ftf])));
        return root == 0.0 ? (num & lifted::kSign) | lifted::kMax : lifted::Result(lifted::Value(num) / root);
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Efu(Vu::Pending& out, double value, int latency) {
        out.p = true;
        out.p_value = lifted::Result(value);
        out.p_latency = latency;
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE double Value(const Vu& v, int reg, int lane) {
        return lifted::Value(v.regs.vf[reg][lane]);
    }
    // The flag instructions read and set these (landed first: see Issue).
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32& Clip(Vu& v, u64 cycle) { LandFlags(v, cycle); return v.clip; }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32& ClipLatest(Vu& v) { return v.clip_latest_; }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32& Status(Vu& v, u64 cycle) { LandFlags(v, cycle); return v.status; }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32& StatusLatest(Vu& v) { return v.status_latest_; }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 Mac(Vu& v, u64 cycle) { LandFlags(v, cycle); return v.mac; }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ upper
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
    /* An FMAC operation: Op (vu_math.h's), Operand (0-3 a lane of ft, 4 Q,
       5 I, 6 ft), into To (-1 ACC; 0 VF0, which stays: the result goes to
       discarded_, for the flags). Flags 1 sets the flags as Flags<To, Dest>
       would after it, 2 as StickyFlags<To, Dest> - from the result as it
       is, not read back from where it went. */
    template <int Op, int Operand, int To, u32 Dest, int Known = 0, int SetFlags = 0>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Fmac(Vu& v, int fs, int ft) {
        lifted::Context& c = v.regs;
        __m128i a = _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(c.vf[fs]));
        __m128i b;
        if constexpr (Operand == 6) b = _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(c.vf[ft]));
        else if constexpr (Operand == 4) b = _mm_set1_epi32(int(c.vc[lifted::kRegQ]));
        else if constexpr (Operand == 5) b = _mm_set1_epi32(int(c.vc[lifted::kRegI]));
        else b = _mm_set1_epi32(int(c.vf[ft][Operand]));
        // Cleaned here where the block does not know them clean and the run
        // has not found them clean (unclean_); LanesSse then cleans neither.
        // A run has DAZ and FTZ on (VuRounding): clamped is clean enough
        // (ClampLanes), here and for the result.
        // MAX and MINI take their operands as they are, and may leave a
        // field unclean.
        constexpr bool kRaw = Op == lifted::kMax_ || Op == lifted::kMini;
        if constexpr ((Known & 1) == 0 && !kRaw)
            if ((v.unclean_ >> fs) & 1) a = lifted::ClampLanes(a);
        if constexpr ((Known & 2) == 0 && !kRaw) {
            if constexpr (Operand == 4 || Operand == 5) b = lifted::ClampLanes(b);
            else if ((v.unclean_ >> ft) & 1) b = lifted::ClampLanes(b);
        }
        // ACC as the operands: cleaned only where not known clean (MADD,
        // MSUB read it).
        __m128i acc = _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(c.vacc));
        if constexpr ((Known & 4) == 0 && (Op == lifted::kMadd || Op == lifted::kMsub))
            if (v.acc_unclean_) acc = lifted::ClampLanes(acc);
        const __m128i result = lifted::LanesSse<Op, Known | 7, true>(a, b, acc);
        // An FMAC's result is clean (MAX and MINI write no ACC): all four
        // fields of it make ACC clean.
        if constexpr (To < 0 && Dest == 15 && !kRaw) v.acc_unclean_ = false;
        else if constexpr (To < 0 && kRaw) v.acc_unclean_ = true;
        if constexpr (SetFlags == 1) FlagsOf<Dest>(v, result);
        else if constexpr (SetFlags == 2) StickyFlagsOf<Dest>(v, result);
        if constexpr (To > 0 && kRaw) v.unclean_ |= 1u << To;
        else if constexpr (To > 0 && Dest == 15) v.unclean_ &= ~(1u << To);    // all four fields, clean
        if constexpr (To == 0) {
            _mm_storeu_si128(reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(v.discarded_), result);
            return;
        } else if constexpr (Dest == 0) {
            return;
        } else {
            u32* to = To < 0 ? c.vacc : c.vf[To];
            if constexpr (Dest == 15) {             // all four: no blend (MSVC kept it, a mask of all ones)
                _mm_storeu_si128(reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(to), result);
                return;
            }
            const __m128i mask = _mm_set_epi32((Dest & 1) ? -1 : 0, (Dest & 2) ? -1 : 0, (Dest & 4) ? -1 : 0,
                                               (Dest & 8) ? -1 : 0);
            const __m128i old = _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(to));
            _mm_storeu_si128(reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(to),
                             _mm_or_si128(_mm_and_si128(mask, result), _mm_andnot_si128(mask, old)));
        }
    }
#else
    template <int Op, int Operand, int To, u32 Dest, int Known = 0, int SetFlags = 0>
    static void Fmac(Vu& v, int fs, int ft) {
        lifted::FmacOp f;
        f.op = Op;
        f.operand = Operand;
        f.to_acc = To < 0;
        f.fd = To > 0 ? u32(To) : 0;
        f.fs = u32(fs);
        f.ft = u32(ft);
        f.dest = Dest;
        if constexpr (To == 0) lifted::FmacResult(v.regs, f, v.discarded_);
        else lifted::RunFmac(v.regs, f);
        if constexpr (SetFlags == 1) Flags<To, Dest>(v);
        else if constexpr (SetFlags == 2) StickyFlags<To, Dest>(v);
    }
#endif
    /* Macro mode's COP2 operations, as it runs them (vu0.cpp's Cop2), without
       finding which each time. */
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Opmula(Vu& v, int fs, int ft) {
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
        const __m128i a = _mm_shuffle_epi32(_mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(v.regs.vf[fs])),
                                            _MM_SHUFFLE(3, 0, 2, 1));
        const __m128i b = _mm_shuffle_epi32(_mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(v.regs.vf[ft])),
                                            _MM_SHUFFLE(3, 1, 0, 2));
        __m128i* acc = reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(v.regs.vacc);
        const __m128i product = lifted::LanesSse<lifted::kMul, 0, true>(a, b, _mm_setzero_si128());
        _mm_storeu_si128(acc, Blend(LaneMask(Dest & 14), product, _mm_loadu_si128(acc)));
#else
        const u32 *a = v.regs.vf[fs], *b = v.regs.vf[ft];
        const u32 out[3] = {lifted::Result(lifted::Value(a[1]) * lifted::Value(b[2])),
                            lifted::Result(lifted::Value(a[2]) * lifted::Value(b[0])),
                            lifted::Result(lifted::Value(a[0]) * lifted::Value(b[1]))};
        if constexpr ((Dest & 8) != 0) v.regs.vacc[0] = out[0];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 4) != 0) v.regs.vacc[1] = out[1];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 2) != 0) v.regs.vacc[2] = out[2];
#endif
    }
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
    /* The same lanes at once: a.yzx times b.zxy, from ACC (LanesSse's MSUB,
       the model's number; lane w is worked and dropped). */
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Opmsub(Vu& v, int fd, int fs, int ft) {
        const __m128i a = _mm_shuffle_epi32(_mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(v.regs.vf[fs])),
                                            _MM_SHUFFLE(3, 0, 2, 1));
        const __m128i b = _mm_shuffle_epi32(_mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(v.regs.vf[ft])),
                                            _MM_SHUFFLE(3, 1, 0, 2));
        const __m128i acc = _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(v.regs.vacc));
        const __m128i result = lifted::LanesSse<lifted::kMsub, 0, true>(a, b, acc);
        if (fd == 0) {                                  // the flags' alone
            _mm_storeu_si128(reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(v.discarded_),
                             _mm_and_si128(result, _mm_set_epi32(0, -1, -1, -1)));
            return;
        }
        u32* to = v.regs.vf[fd];
        const __m128i mask = _mm_set_epi32(0, (Dest & 2) ? -1 : 0, (Dest & 4) ? -1 : 0, (Dest & 8) ? -1 : 0);
        const __m128i old = _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(to));
        _mm_storeu_si128(reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(to),
                         _mm_or_si128(_mm_and_si128(mask, result), _mm_andnot_si128(mask, old)));
    }
#else
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Opmsub(Vu& v, int fd, int fs, int ft) {
        const u32 *a = v.regs.vf[fs], *b = v.regs.vf[ft];
        const u32* acc = v.regs.vacc;
        const u32 out[3] = {lifted::Binary(lifted::kMsub, a[1], b[2], acc[0]),
                            lifted::Binary(lifted::kMsub, a[2], b[0], acc[1]),
                            lifted::Binary(lifted::kMsub, a[0], b[1], acc[2])};
        if (fd == 0) {                                  // the flags' alone
            for (int lane = 0; lane < 3; ++lane) v.discarded_[lane] = out[lane];
            v.discarded_[3] = 0;
            return;
        }
        if constexpr ((Dest & 8) != 0) v.regs.vf[fd][0] = out[0];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 4) != 0) v.regs.vf[fd][1] = out[1];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 2) != 0) v.regs.vf[fd][2] = out[2];
    }
#endif
    /* ITOF0/4/12/15 (Shift 0-3), FTOI the same, ABS: into ft (VF0 stays). */
    template <u32 Dest, int Shift>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Itof(Vu& v, int ft, int fs) {
        static constexpr double kScale[4] = {1.0, 16.0, 4096.0, 32768.0};
        const u32* a = v.regs.vf[fs];
        u32 out[4];
        for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane) out[lane] = lifted::Result(double(std::int32_t(a[lane])) / kScale[Shift]);
        WriteVf<Dest>(v, ft, out);
        Wrote<Dest>(v, ft, true);
    }
    template <u32 Dest, int Shift>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Ftoi(Vu& v, int ft, int fs) {
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
        // Clean, times a power of two (exact, or an infinity past the
        // largest), truncated; cvttps2dq gives 0x80000000 for anything past
        // 32 bits, right for negatives, and turned to 0x7FFFFFFF for the
        // positives - lifted::FloatToInt's saturation.
        static constexpr float kScaleF[4] = {1.0f, 16.0f, 4096.0f, 32768.0f};
        if (ft == 0) return;
        const __m128 x = _mm_mul_ps(
            _mm_castsi128_ps(lifted::CleanLanes(_mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(v.regs.vf[fs])))),
            _mm_set1_ps(kScaleF[Shift]));
        const __m128i over = _mm_castps_si128(_mm_cmpge_ps(x, _mm_set1_ps(2147483648.0f)));
        const __m128i value = _mm_xor_si128(_mm_cvttps_epi32(x), over);
        __m128i* to = reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(v.regs.vf[ft]);
        if constexpr (Dest == 15) _mm_storeu_si128(to, value);
        else _mm_storeu_si128(to, Blend(LaneMask(Dest), value, _mm_loadu_si128(to)));
        Wrote<Dest>(v, ft, false);                      // integers
        return;
#endif
        static constexpr double kScale[4] = {1.0, 16.0, 4096.0, 32768.0};
        const u32* a = v.regs.vf[fs];
        u32 out[4];
        for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane) out[lane] = lifted::FloatToInt(lifted::Value(a[lane]) * kScale[Shift]);
        WriteVf<Dest>(v, ft, out);
        Wrote<Dest>(v, ft, false);                      // integers
    }
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Abs(Vu& v, int ft, int fs) {
        const u32* a = v.regs.vf[fs];
        u32 out[4];
        for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane) out[lane] = lifted::Clean(a[lane]) & ~lifted::kSign;
        WriteVf<Dest>(v, ft, out);
        Wrote<Dest>(v, ft, true);
    }
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void WriteVf(Vu& v, int reg, const u32 out[4]) {
        if (reg == 0) return;
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
        __m128i* to = reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(v.regs.vf[reg]);
        const __m128i value = _mm_set_epi32(int(out[3]), int(out[2]), int(out[1]), int(out[0]));
        if constexpr (Dest == 15) _mm_storeu_si128(to, value);
        else _mm_storeu_si128(to, Blend(LaneMask(Dest), value, _mm_loadu_si128(to)));
#else
        if constexpr ((Dest & 8) != 0) v.regs.vf[reg][0] = out[0];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 4) != 0) v.regs.vf[reg][1] = out[1];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 2) != 0) v.regs.vf[reg][2] = out[2];
        if constexpr ((Dest & 1) != 0) v.regs.vf[reg][3] = out[3];
#endif
    }
    /* Any other upper operation, as macro mode's COP2 runs it. */
    static void Cop2(Vu& v, u32 word) {
        lifted::Cop2(v.regs, 0x4A000000u | (word & 0x01FFFFFF));
        // Whatever it wrote is not known clean: fd's and ft's fields, ACC.
        v.unclean_ |= ((1u << ((word >> 6) & 31)) | (1u << ((word >> 16) & 31))) & ~1u;
        v.acc_unclean_ = true;
    }
    /* CLIP: fs.xyz against |ft.w| - compared as Clean leaves them: the
       magnitudes of clean floats are in the order of their bits (a
       denormal's is zero, an infinity's or NaN's the largest), and x > |w|
       (x < -|w|) is x positive (negative) with the larger magnitude. */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE u32 CleanMagnitude(u32 bits) {
        const u32 exponent = bits & 0x7F800000u;
        return exponent == 0 ? 0 : exponent == 0x7F800000u ? lifted::kMax : bits & 0x7FFFFFFFu;
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void ClipJudge(Vu& v, int fs, int ft) {
        const u32* f = v.regs.vf[fs];
        const u32 w = CleanMagnitude(v.regs.vf[ft][3]);
        u32 judgement = 0;
        for (int lane = 0; lane < 3; ++lane)
            if (CleanMagnitude(f[lane]) > w) judgement |= (f[lane] >> 31 ? 2u : 1u) << (2 * lane);
        v.clip_latest_ = ((v.clip_latest_ << 6) | judgement) & 0xFFFFFF;
    }
    /* MAC: zero (bits 3-0) and sign (7-4) of each written field, x highest;
       `out` the register the upper wrote (Target: -1 ACC, 0 VF0 - the result
       itself, which VF0 does not keep). */
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
    /* The four lanes at once: which are zero and which negative, lane x
       the highest bit as the MAC flag has it (the lanes turned round before
       the mask is taken). No Clean, as the interpreter has: every operation
       that sets the flags leaves its fields clean (the FMAC through
       LanesSse, the rest through lifted::Result) - Clean would hand back the
       same bits. */
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void FlagsOf(Vu& v, __m128i bits) {
        bits = _mm_shuffle_epi32(bits, _MM_SHUFFLE(0, 1, 2, 3));
        const __m128i magnitude = _mm_and_si128(bits, _mm_set1_epi32(0x7FFFFFFF));
        const u32 zero = u32(_mm_movemask_ps(_mm_castsi128_ps(_mm_cmpeq_epi32(magnitude, _mm_setzero_si128()))));
        const u32 sign = u32(_mm_movemask_ps(_mm_castsi128_ps(bits)));
        const u32 m = (zero & Dest) | (sign & Dest) << 4;
        const u32 low = ((m & 0xF) ? 1u : 0u) | ((m & 0xF0) ? 2u : 0u);
        v.mac_latest_ = m;
        v.status_latest_ = (v.status_latest_ & ~0x3u) | low | low << 6;
    }
    template <u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void StickyFlagsOf(Vu& v, __m128i bits) {
        const __m128i magnitude = _mm_and_si128(bits, _mm_set1_epi32(0x7FFFFFFF));
        constexpr u32 kLanes = ((Dest & 8) ? 1u : 0u) | ((Dest & 4) ? 2u : 0u) | ((Dest & 2) ? 4u : 0u) |
                               ((Dest & 1) ? 8u : 0u);
        const u32 zero = u32(_mm_movemask_ps(_mm_castsi128_ps(_mm_cmpeq_epi32(magnitude, _mm_setzero_si128())))) & kLanes;
        const u32 sign = u32(_mm_movemask_ps(_mm_castsi128_ps(bits))) & kLanes;
        v.status_latest_ |= ((zero ? 1u : 0u) | (sign ? 2u : 0u)) << 6;
    }
#endif
    template <int Target, u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Flags(Vu& v) {
        const u32* out = Target > 0 ? v.regs.vf[Target] : Target == 0 ? v.discarded_ : v.regs.vacc;
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
        FlagsOf<Dest>(v, _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(out)));
#else
        u32 m = 0;
        for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane) {
            if (!(Dest & (8u >> lane))) continue;
            const u32 bits = lifted::Clean(out[lane]);
            if ((bits & 0x7FFFFFFFu) == 0) m |= 8u >> lane;
            if (bits & 0x80000000u) m |= 0x80u >> lane;
        }
        v.mac_latest_ = m;
        v.status_latest_ = (v.status_latest_ & ~0x3u) | ((m & 0xF) ? 1u : 0u) | ((m & 0xF0) ? 2u : 0u);
        v.status_latest_ |= (v.status_latest_ & 3u) << 6;
#endif
    }

    /* Flags no one can see (vurecomp.py, dead_flags): a later FMAC of the
       block sets them over these before any flag instruction or the block's
       end - but STATUS's sticky bits (6, 7) gather every result's, so those
       are kept. */
    template <int Target, u32 Dest>
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void StickyFlags(Vu& v) {
        const u32* out = Target > 0 ? v.regs.vf[Target] : Target == 0 ? v.discarded_ : v.regs.vacc;
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
        StickyFlagsOf<Dest>(v, _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(out)));
#else
        u32 zero = 0, sign = 0;
        for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane) {
            if (!(Dest & (8u >> lane))) continue;
            if ((out[lane] & 0x7FFFFFFFu) == 0) zero = 1;
            if (out[lane] & 0x80000000u) sign = 1;
        }
        v.status_latest_ |= ((zero ? 1u : 0u) | (sign ? 2u : 0u)) << 6;
#endif
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ the pair's end
    /* As Run after the two halves: the lower's held writes (giving way to the
       upper's fields), when the fields land, the flags on their way, Q and P. */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Finish(Vu& v, u64& cycle, Vu::Pending& pending, int written, u32 lanes,
                                         bool set_flags, bool sets_mac, bool sets_clip, bool vi0 = true) {
        const u64 ready = cycle + kFmacLatency;
        if (pending.vf > 0) {
            const u32 landing = pending.lanes & ~(written == pending.vf ? lanes : 0u);
#if PS2RT_VU_SSE
            __m128i* to = reinterpret_cast<__m128i*>(v.regs.vf[pending.vf]);
            _mm_storeu_si128(to, Blend(LaneMask(landing),
                                       _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<const __m128i*>(pending.value)),
                                       _mm_loadu_si128(to)));
#endif
            for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane) {
                if (landing & (8u >> lane)) {
#if !PS2RT_VU_SSE
                    v.regs.vf[pending.vf][lane] = pending.value[lane];
#endif
                    v.vf_ready_[pending.vf][lane] = ready;
                }
            }
            // Clean only if what lands is, and either it is all of the
            // register or the rest was clean; with the upper writing the same
            // register too, not known.
            const u32 reg = 1u << pending.vf;
            if (pending.clean && written != pending.vf && (pending.lanes == 15 || !(v.unclean_ & reg)))
                v.unclean_ &= ~reg;
            else
                v.unclean_ |= reg;
        }
        FinishUpper(v, cycle, written, lanes, set_flags, sets_mac, sets_clip);
        if (pending.q_latency) {
            v.q_next_ = pending.q_set ? pending.q_value
                      : pending.vc    ? pending.vc_after[lifted::kRegQ] : v.regs.vc[lifted::kRegQ];
            v.q_ready_ = cycle + u64(pending.q_latency);
            v.q_busy_ = true;
            v.qp_due_ = std::min(v.qp_due_, v.q_ready_);
            if (pending.vc) pending.vc_after[lifted::kRegQ] = v.regs.vc[lifted::kRegQ];
        }
        if (pending.vc) std::memcpy(v.regs.vc, pending.vc_after, sizeof pending.vc_after);
        if (pending.p) {
            v.p_next_ = pending.p_value;
            v.p_ready_ = cycle + u64(pending.p_latency ? pending.p_latency : 1);
            v.p_busy_ = true;
            v.qp_due_ = std::min(v.qp_due_, v.p_ready_);
        }
        if (vi0) End(v, cycle);
        else Next(cycle);
    }
    /* The same for a pair whose lower left nothing (FinishUpper, then End). */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void FinishUpper(Vu& v, u64 cycle, int written, u32 lanes, bool set_flags,
                                              bool sets_mac, bool sets_clip) {
        const u64 ready = cycle + kFmacLatency;
#if defined(__AVX2__)
        if (written > 0 && lanes == 15)         // all four in a store
            _mm256_storeu_si256(reinterpret_cast<__m256i*>(v.vf_ready_[written]), _mm256_set1_epi64x(long long(ready)));
        else
#endif
        if (written > 0)
            for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; ++lane)
                if (lanes & (8u >> lane)) v.vf_ready_[written][lane] = ready;
        if (set_flags && v.flag_count_ == 8) LandFlags(v, cycle);   // as eager landing would have, at this issue
        if (set_flags && v.flag_count_ < 8) {
            // Straight into the queue's slot (PushFlags, without the copy).
            Vu::FlagWrite& f = v.flag_queue_[(v.flag_head_ + v.flag_count_++) & 7];
            f.ready = ready;
            f.mac = v.mac_latest_;
            f.status = v.status_latest_;
            f.clip = v.clip_latest_;
            f.sets_mac = sets_mac;
            f.sets_clip = sets_clip;
        }
    }
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void End(Vu& v, u64& cycle) {
        v.regs.vc[0] = 0;
        ++cycle;
    }
    /* End where VI0 is known 0 still: a pair after a block's first (which
       ends with End) whose lower is not one of macro mode's COP2 operations
       - nothing else writes VI0 (SetVi leaves it out, Mtir copies it). */
    static PS2HOST_VU_INLINE void Next(u64& cycle) { ++cycle; }
};

}  // namespace ps2host

#endif  /* PS2HOST_VU_CORE_H */

```

`host/src/audio.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * The port's sound (--audio): the SPU2's mixed output (spu2.cpp) played through
 * the system's audio engine (WASAPI, shared mode), or its wave device (waveOut)
 * where that cannot open.
 *
 * The SPU2 produces samples as the IOP runs, in bursts (a frame's worth, or a
 * half-buffer's), by the emulated clock; the device takes them at its own,
 * steadily. Between the two is a ring: AudioFrames puts the samples in, an
 * audio thread takes them out as the device asks. The ring is kept near a
 * target fill (kTargetMs: enough to ride out a burst and a late frame) by
 * playing it a little faster or slower than it came - at most half a percent,
 * a pitch no one hears - so neither a clock's drift nor a hitch builds into
 * lag: the old queue only ever grew after each hitch, until every buffer was
 * full and samples were dropped (crackling, and a picture 170 ms ahead of its
 * sound). An empty ring plays silence, faded out over a few samples rather
 * than cut off, and fills to the target again before it plays on.
 *
 * --audio-wav records the SPU2's output itself to a WAV file, instead of (or as
 * well as) playing it: how sound is checked without anyone listening
 * (tools/audiocheck.py).
 *
 * PS2HOST_AUDIO_LOG=1: every two seconds, how the sound came and went.
 * PS2HOST_AUDIO_MUTE=1: played (the device measured) but silent.
 * PS2HOST_AUDIO_LATENCY_MS=n: the ring's target, 20 to 250 ms.
 * PS2HOST_AUDIO_WAVEOUT=1: the wave device even where WASAPI would open.
 */

#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <windows.h>
#include <mmsystem.h>
#include <mmreg.h>
#include <audioclient.h>
#include <mmdeviceapi.h>
#undef small            // rpcndr.h's, through the COM headers; run.h names a parameter so

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#include "ps2host/run.h"
#include "ps2host/timeline.h"

#pragma comment(lib, "winmm.lib")
#pragma comment(lib, "ole32.lib")

namespace ps2host {

namespace {

constexpr int kRate = 48000;
constexpr unsigned kRingFrames = 1u << 15;      // 683 ms: room for a long hitch's catch-up
constexpr double kMaxStretch = 0.005;           // the rate control's reach: +-0.5%
constexpr unsigned kFadeFrames = 96;            // 2 ms: into and out of silence

// The ring between the SPU2 (one writer) and the audio thread (one reader):
// interleaved stereo floats; positions count frames and only ever grow.
struct Ring {
    std::vector<float> data = std::vector<float>(kRingFrames * 2);
    std::atomic<unsigned long long> written{0}, read{0};
    unsigned long long Filled() const { return written.load(std::memory_order_acquire) - read.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
};

struct Stats {
    std::atomic<unsigned> batches{0}, ran_dry{0};
    std::atomic<unsigned long long> dropped{0};
    std::atomic<double> longest_ms{0};
    std::atomic<int> fewest_ms{1 << 30}, most_ms{0};
```
