```cpp
    std::atomic<double> stretch_min{1}, stretch_max{1};
};

struct Device {
    Ring ring;
    Stats stats;
    unsigned target_frames = kRate * 60 / 1000;
    bool mute = false;
    bool log = false;
    std::atomic<bool> open{false}, stop{false};
    std::atomic<int> opened{0};         // the audio thread's answer: 1 a device, -1 none
    std::thread thread;
    std::FILE* wav = nullptr;
    unsigned long long wav_frames = 0;
    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point last_batch{};

    // The reader's state (the audio thread's alone).
    double phase = 0;                   // between the frame `read` and the next, 0-1
    double smoothed_fill = 0;           // the ring's fill, averaged over ~100 ms
    bool buffering = true;              // filling to the target before playing on
    float last[2] = {0, 0};             // the last frame played: faded out from
    unsigned fade = 0;                  // frames left of a fade in

    ~Device() { Close(); }
    void Close() {
        stop = true;
        if (thread.joinable()) thread.join();
        open = false;
        if (!wav) return;
        WriteHeader(unsigned(wav_frames * 4));
        std::fclose(wav);
        wav = nullptr;
    }
    void WriteHeader(unsigned data) {
        unsigned char h[44] = {'R', 'I', 'F', 'F', 0, 0, 0, 0, 'W', 'A', 'V', 'E', 'f', 'm', 't', ' ',
                               16, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 0x80, 0xBB, 0, 0, 0, 0xEE, 2, 0,
                               4, 0, 16, 0, 'd', 'a', 't', 'a', 0, 0, 0, 0};
        const unsigned riff = 36 + data;
        std::memcpy(h + 4, &riff, 4);
        std::memcpy(h + 40, &data, 4);
        std::fseek(wav, 0, SEEK_SET);
        std::fwrite(h, 1, 44, wav);
        std::fseek(wav, 0, SEEK_END);
    }

    // `frames` stereo frames for the device, taken from the ring at the
    // controlled rate. Called by the audio thread only.
    void Render(float* out, unsigned frames);
};

Device& D() {
    static Device device;
    return device;
}

template <typename T>
void AtomicMax(std::atomic<T>& a, T v) {
    T now = a.load();
    while (v > now && !a.compare_exchange_weak(now, v)) {
    }
}
template <typename T>
void AtomicMin(std::atomic<T>& a, T v) {
    T now = a.load();
    while (v < now && !a.compare_exchange_weak(now, v)) {
    }
}

// Catmull-Rom through four frames, at t (0-1) between the middle two.
inline float Cubic(float a, float b, float c, float d, float t) {
    return b + 0.5f * t * (c - a + t * (2.0f * a - 5.0f * b + 4.0f * c - d + t * (3.0f * (b - c) + d - a)));
}

void Device::Render(float* out, unsigned frames) {
    const unsigned long long available = ring.Filled();
    // The fill the rate control steers by: the ring's, smoothed - it jumps by a
    // whole batch each time the SPU2 delivers one.
    smoothed_fill += (double(available) - smoothed_fill) * 0.05;
    if (buffering) {
        if (available < target_frames) {
            std::fill(out, out + 2 * frames, 0.0f);
            return;
        }
        buffering = false;
        fade = kFadeFrames;
        smoothed_fill = double(available);
    }
    // Faster when fuller than the target, slower when emptier: the step, in
    // ring frames per device frame.
    const double error = (smoothed_fill - double(target_frames)) / double(target_frames);
    const double step = 1.0 + std::clamp(error * kMaxStretch * 2.0, -kMaxStretch, kMaxStretch);
    if (log) {
        AtomicMin(stats.stretch_min, step);
        AtomicMax(stats.stretch_max, step);
    }
    const float* data = ring.data.data();
    unsigned long long at = ring.read.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const unsigned long long end = ring.written.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    auto frame = [&](unsigned long long n, int ch) { return data[2 * (n % kRingFrames) + ch]; };
    unsigned k = 0;
    for (; k < frames; ++k) {
        // Four frames around the position: at-1, at, at+1, at+2.
        if (at + 2 >= end) break;
        const float t = float(phase);
        for (int ch = 0; ch < 2; ++ch) {
            const float before = at ? frame(at - 1, ch) : frame(at, ch);
            float v = Cubic(before, frame(at, ch), frame(at + 1, ch), frame(at + 2, ch), t);
            if (fade) v *= float(kFadeFrames - fade) / float(kFadeFrames);
            out[2 * k + ch] = v;
        }
        if (fade) --fade;
        last[0] = out[2 * k];
        last[1] = out[2 * k + 1];
        phase += step;
        const double whole = std::floor(phase);
        at += (unsigned long long)whole;
        phase -= whole;
    }
    ring.read.store(at, std::memory_order_release);
    if (k < frames) {
        // Ran dry: what was playing fades to silence, and the ring fills to
        // the target before it plays again.
        if (log) ++stats.ran_dry;
        for (unsigned n = 0; k < frames; ++k, ++n) {
            const float g = n < kFadeFrames ? float(kFadeFrames - n) / float(kFadeFrames) : 0.0f;
            out[2 * k] = last[0] * g;
            out[2 * k + 1] = last[1] * g;
        }
        last[0] = last[1] = 0;
        buffering = true;
    }
    if (mute) std::fill(out, out + 2 * frames, 0.0f);
    if (log) {
        const int ms = int(available * 1000 / kRate);
        AtomicMin(stats.fewest_ms, ms);
        AtomicMax(stats.most_ms, ms);
    }
}

// PS2HOST_AUDIO_LOG: every two seconds, from the writer's side.
void LogStats(Device& d) {
    static auto since = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    if (now - since < std::chrono::seconds(2)) return;
    since = now;
    Stats& s = d.stats;
    const int fewest = s.fewest_ms.exchange(1 << 30);
    std::fprintf(stderr, "[audio] %u batches, longest wait %.1f ms; ring %d-%d ms (target %u), ran dry %u times, "
                         "%llu frames dropped, rate %.4f-%.4f\n",
                 s.batches.exchange(0), s.longest_ms.exchange(0), fewest == (1 << 30) ? 0 : fewest, s.most_ms.exchange(0), d.target_frames * 1000 / kRate, s.ran_dry.exchange(0), s.dropped.exchange(0),
                 s.stretch_min.exchange(1), s.stretch_max.exchange(1));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- WASAPI

// KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_IEEE_FLOAT, without ksuser.lib.
const GUID kFloatFormat = {0x00000003, 0x0000, 0x0010, {0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0xAA, 0x00, 0x38, 0x9B, 0x71}};

template <typename T>
void Release(T*& p) {
    if (p) p->Release();
    p = nullptr;
}

// Plays until stopped; false if the device could not be opened at all (the
// caller falls back to waveOut). A device that goes away (headphones pulled)
// is opened again - the default one, whatever it now is.
bool RunWasapi(Device& d) {
    if (FAILED(CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_MULTITHREADED))) return false;
    HANDLE event = CreateEventW(nullptr, FALSE, FALSE, nullptr);
    bool ever = false;
    while (!d.stop) {
        IMMDeviceEnumerator* enumerator = nullptr;
        IMMDevice* device = nullptr;
        IAudioClient* client = nullptr;
        IAudioRenderClient* render = nullptr;
        ISimpleAudioVolume* volume = nullptr;
        bool ok = SUCCEEDED(CoCreateInstance(__uuidof(MMDeviceEnumerator), nullptr, CLSCTX_ALL,
                                             __uuidof(IMMDeviceEnumerator), reinterpret_cast<void**>(&enumerator))) &&
                  SUCCEEDED(enumerator->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eConsole, &device)) &&
                  SUCCEEDED(device->Activate(__uuidof(IAudioClient), CLSCTX_ALL, nullptr,
                                             reinterpret_cast<void**>(&client)));
        UINT32 buffer_frames = 0;
        if (ok) {
            // 48 kHz float stereo, the system converting to its mix format
            // (another rate, more channels) where that differs.
            WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE f = {};
            f.Format.wFormatTag = WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE;
            f.Format.nChannels = 2;
            f.Format.nSamplesPerSec = kRate;
            f.Format.wBitsPerSample = 32;
            f.Format.nBlockAlign = 8;
            f.Format.nAvgBytesPerSec = kRate * 8;
            f.Format.cbSize = sizeof f - sizeof f.Format;
            f.Samples.wValidBitsPerSample = 32;
            f.dwChannelMask = SPEAKER_FRONT_LEFT | SPEAKER_FRONT_RIGHT;
            f.SubFormat = kFloatFormat;
            const DWORD flags = AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_EVENTCALLBACK | AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_AUTOCONVERTPCM |
                                AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY;
            ok = SUCCEEDED(client->Initialize(AUDCLNT_SHAREMODE_SHARED, flags, 200000 /* 20 ms */, 0,
                                              &f.Format, nullptr)) &&
                 SUCCEEDED(client->SetEventHandle(event)) && SUCCEEDED(client->GetBufferSize(&buffer_frames)) &&
                 SUCCEEDED(client->GetService(__uuidof(IAudioRenderClient), reinterpret_cast<void**>(&render)));
        }
        if (ok) {
            if (SUCCEEDED(client->GetService(__uuidof(ISimpleAudioVolume), reinterpret_cast<void**>(&volume)))) {
                // PS2HOST_AUDIO_RESET_VOLUME=1: this program's volume in the
                // mixer back to full (an earlier build's mute set it to
                // nothing, and the mixer keeps it).
                if (std::getenv("PS2HOST_AUDIO_RESET_VOLUME")) volume->SetMasterVolume(1.0f, nullptr);
                float level = 1;
                volume->GetMasterVolume(&level);
                if (!ever)
                    std::fprintf(stderr, "[audio] playing (WASAPI, %.0f ms buffer, %u ms target); this program's "
                                         "volume in the system's mixer %.0f%%\n",
                                 1000.0 * buffer_frames / kRate, d.target_frames * 1000 / kRate, 100.0 * level);
            }
            ever = true;
            d.opened.store(1);
            BYTE* out = nullptr;
            if (SUCCEEDED(render->GetBuffer(buffer_frames, &out)))
                render->ReleaseBuffer(buffer_frames, AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_SILENT);
            ok = SUCCEEDED(client->Start());
        }
        while (ok && !d.stop) {
            WaitForSingleObject(event, 100);
            UINT32 padding = 0;
            if (FAILED(client->GetCurrentPadding(&padding))) break;      // the device went away
            const UINT32 room = buffer_frames - padding;
            if (!room) continue;
            BYTE* out = nullptr;
            if (FAILED(render->GetBuffer(room, &out))) break;
            d.Render(reinterpret_cast<float*>(out), room);
            render->ReleaseBuffer(room, 0);
        }
        if (client) client->Stop();
        Release(volume);
        Release(render);
        Release(client);
        Release(device);
        Release(enumerator);
        if (!ever) break;                   // never opened: waveOut instead
        if (!d.stop) std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(500));   // a new default device
    }
    CloseHandle(event);
    CoUninitialize();
    return ever;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- waveOut

void RunWaveOut(Device& d) {
    constexpr int kBuffers = 4;
    constexpr unsigned kFrames = 480;           // 10 ms each
    WAVEFORMATEX format = {};
    format.wFormatTag = WAVE_FORMAT_PCM;
    format.nChannels = 2;
    format.nSamplesPerSec = kRate;
    format.wBitsPerSample = 16;
    format.nBlockAlign = 4;
    format.nAvgBytesPerSec = kRate * 4;
    HANDLE event = CreateEventW(nullptr, FALSE, FALSE, nullptr);
    HWAVEOUT out = nullptr;
    if (waveOutOpen(&out, WAVE_MAPPER, &format, DWORD_PTR(event), 0, CALLBACK_EVENT) != MMSYSERR_NOERROR) {
        CloseHandle(event);
        d.opened.store(-1);
        return;
    }
    std::fprintf(stderr, "[audio] playing (waveOut, %u ms target)\n", d.target_frames * 1000 / kRate);
    d.opened.store(1);
    WAVEHDR headers[kBuffers] = {};
    std::vector<short> data[kBuffers];
    std::vector<float> scratch(kFrames * 2);
    for (int i = 0; i < kBuffers; ++i) {
        data[i].assign(kFrames * 2, 0);
        headers[i].lpData = reinterpret_cast<LPSTR>(data[i].data());
        headers[i].dwBufferLength = kFrames * 4;
        headers[i].dwFlags = WHDR_DONE;
    }
    while (!d.stop) {
        for (int i = 0; i < kBuffers; ++i) {
            WAVEHDR& h = headers[i];
            if (!(h.dwFlags & WHDR_DONE)) continue;
            if (h.dwFlags & WHDR_PREPARED) waveOutUnprepareHeader(out, &h, sizeof h);
            d.Render(scratch.data(), kFrames);
            for (unsigned k = 0; k < kFrames * 2; ++k)
                data[i][k] = short(std::lrint(std::clamp(scratch[k], -1.0f, 1.0f) * 32767.0f));
            h.dwFlags = 0;
            waveOutPrepareHeader(out, &h, sizeof h);
            waveOutWrite(out, &h, sizeof h);
        }
        WaitForSingleObject(event, 20);
    }
    waveOutReset(out);
    for (WAVEHDR& h : headers)
        if (h.dwFlags & WHDR_PREPARED) waveOutUnprepareHeader(out, &h, sizeof h);
    waveOutClose(out);
    CloseHandle(event);
}

}  // namespace

void CloseAudio() { D().Close(); }

bool OpenAudio() {
    Device& d = D();
    d.mute = std::getenv("PS2HOST_AUDIO_MUTE") != nullptr;
    d.log = std::getenv("PS2HOST_AUDIO_LOG") != nullptr;
    if (const char* ms = std::getenv("PS2HOST_AUDIO_LATENCY_MS"))
        d.target_frames = unsigned(kRate * std::clamp(std::atoi(ms), 20, 250) / 1000);
    const bool wave_only = std::getenv("PS2HOST_AUDIO_WAVEOUT") != nullptr;
    d.thread = std::thread([&d, wave_only] {
        timeline::NameThread("audio");
        SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL);
        if (wave_only || !RunWasapi(d)) RunWaveOut(d);
    });
    // Until the thread says whether a device opened.
    while (d.opened.load() == 0) std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
    if (d.opened.load() < 0) {
        d.stop = true;
        d.thread.join();
        return false;
    }
    d.open = true;
    return true;
}

bool OpenWavDump(const std::string& path) {
    Device& d = D();
    d.wav = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "wb");
    if (!d.wav) return false;
    d.WriteHeader(0);
    return true;
}

void AudioFrames(const short* frames, unsigned count) {
    Device& d = D();
    if (d.wav) {
        std::fwrite(frames, 4, count, d.wav);
        d.wav_frames += count;
    }
    if (!d.open) return;
    if (d.log) {
        const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        if (d.last_batch.time_since_epoch().count())
            AtomicMax(d.stats.longest_ms, std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(now - d.last_batch).count());
        d.last_batch = now;
        ++d.stats.batches;
        LogStats(d);
    }
    Ring& r = d.ring;
    const unsigned long long w = r.written.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const unsigned long long room = kRingFrames - 4 - (w - r.read.load(std::memory_order_acquire));
    if (count > room) {
        // A burst the ring cannot hold (the emulation far ahead of the device:
        // virtual time, a catch-up): the newest are dropped.
        if (d.log) d.stats.dropped += count - room;
        count = unsigned(room);
    }
    float* data = r.data.data();
    for (unsigned k = 0; k < count; ++k) {
        const unsigned long long at = (w + k) % kRingFrames;
        data[2 * at] = frames[2 * k] * (1.0f / 32768.0f);
        data[2 * at + 1] = frames[2 * k + 1] * (1.0f / 32768.0f);
    }
    r.written.store(w + count, std::memory_order_release);
}

}  // namespace ps2host

```

`host/src/cdvd.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * The CD/DVD services the IOP's file system module (cdvdfsv) provides to the EE,
 * as host RPC servers reading the user's disc image (disc.cpp).
 *
 * Each server's protocol is read from the game's own EE-side library, which
 * builds the request and reads the answer: Burnout 3's copy of the SDK's
 * libcdvd is at 0x0011E9A8-0x0011FD00. The servers are added one at a time, as
 * a game is seen to reach them.
 */

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <ctime>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "ps2host/disc.h"
#include "ps2host/host.h"
#include "ps2host/memory.h"
#include "ps2host/run.h"

namespace ps2host {

namespace {

std::vector<u8> Word(u32 value) {
    return {u8(value), u8(value >> 8), u8(value >> 16), u8(value >> 24)};
}

u32 At(const std::vector<u8>& data, std::size_t offset) {
    u32 value = 0;
    if (offset + 4 <= data.size()) std::memcpy(&value, &data[offset], 4);
    return value;
}

// sceCdDiskReady (server 0x8000059C, procedure 0): sent the wait mode, answers
// the drive's state in one word - 2, SCECdComplete, when a disc is ready, and 6,
// SCECdNotReady, when there is none.
std::vector<u8> DiskReady(u32 /*procedure*/, const std::vector<u8>& /*data*/) {
    return Word(GuestDisc().IsOpen() ? 2 : 6);
}

// sceCdSearchFile (server 0x80000597, procedure 0). The request (0x12C bytes):
//   0x000  sceCdlFILE { u32 lsn; u32 size; char name[16]; u8 date[8]; }
//   0x024  the path, 256 bytes, NUL-terminated: "\\DATA\\CARS.BIN;1"
//   0x124  the EE address of this buffer, where the answer's file record goes
// The answer word is 1 when the file was found, 0 when not; the library then
// copies the record from the buffer to its caller.
std::vector<u8> SearchFile(u32 /*procedure*/, const std::vector<u8>& data) {
    if (data.size() < 0x128) return Word(0);
    const char* begin = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&data[0x24]);
    const std::string path(begin, strnlen(begin, 256));
    Disc::File file;
    const bool found = GuestDisc().IsOpen() && GuestDisc().Find(path, &file);
    Note("cd search " + path, "CD: search " + path + (found ? "" : " (not found)"));
    if (!found) return Word(0);
    const u32 record = At(data, 0x124);
    Memory& m = GuestMemory();
    m.Write(record, file.lsn, 4);
    m.Write(record + 4, file.size, 4);
    // The name, as the directory has it: the path's last part.
    const std::size_t slash = path.find_last_of("\\/");
    const std::string name = path.substr(slash == std::string::npos ? 0 : slash + 1);
    for (u32 i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
        m.Write(record + 8 + i, i < name.size() ? u8(name[i]) : 0, 1);
    for (u32 i = 0; i < 8; ++i) m.Write(record + 24 + i, 0, 1);
    return Word(1);
}

u8 Bcd(int value) { return u8(((value / 10) << 4) | (value % 10)); }

// S-commands (server 0x80000593): the procedure is the command; each answers a
// result word, 1 for success, and the command's data after it. Read from the
// game's wrappers, each of which names its command and reply size.
std::vector<u8> SCommand(u32 procedure, const std::vector<u8>& /*data*/) {
    switch (procedure) {
        case 0x01: {                                    // sceCdReadClock: result, sceCdCLOCK
            // With --virtual-time the clock starts at a fixed date and follows
            // the virtual clock: games seed their random choices from it
            // (Burnout 3 its EA Trax playlist), and a scripted run must repeat.
            std::tm local{};
            if (VirtualClock()) {
                const std::time_t start = 1094558400;   // 2004-09-07 12:00:00 UTC, Burnout 3's release
                const std::time_t now = start + std::time_t(ClockNs() / 1000000000ull);
                gmtime_s(&local, &now);
            } else {
                const std::time_t now = std::time(nullptr);
                localtime_s(&local, &now);
            }
            std::vector<u8> reply = Word(1);
            // sceCdCLOCK { stat, second, minute, hour, pad, day, month, year }, BCD
            const u8 clock[8] = {0, Bcd(local.tm_sec), Bcd(local.tm_min), Bcd(local.tm_hour), 0,
                                 Bcd(local.tm_mday), Bcd(local.tm_mon + 1),
                                 Bcd(local.tm_year % 100)};
            reply.insert(reply.end(), clock, clock + 8);
            return reply;
        }
        case 0x03:                                      // sceCdGetDiskType
            return Word(!GuestDisc().IsOpen() ? 0x00 : GuestDisc().IsCd() ? 0x12 : 0x14);  // none, SCECdPS2CD, SCECdPS2DVD
        case 0x05: {                                    // sceCdTrayReq: result, tray state
            std::vector<u8> reply = Word(1);
            const std::vector<u8> closed = Word(0);
            reply.insert(reply.end(), closed.begin(), closed.end());
            return reply;
        }
        case 0x22:                                      // sceCdMmode: the media mode is set
            return Word(1);
        case 0x04:                                      // sceCdGetError: SCECdErNO
            // SDK 2.3's library reads one word, the error (Mister Mosquito,
            // 0x0010D9E0); every read here succeeds.
            return Word(0);
        default:
            Note("cd scmd " + std::to_string(procedure),
                 "CD: S-command " + std::to_string(procedure) + " (answered with zeros)");
            return {};
    }
}

// sceCdInit (server 0x80000592, procedure 0): sent the init mode; the drive is
// ready at once.
std::vector<u8> CdInit(u32 /*procedure*/, const std::vector<u8>& /*data*/) { return Word(1); }

// N-commands (server 0x80000595): the procedure is the command. Reads finish at
// once - the sectors are in EE memory when the call's end arrives.
//   1  sceCdRead: { u32 lsn, sectors, EE buffer, mode (trycount, spindlctrl,
//      datapattern, -), u32 EE address of the library's unaligned-ends record,
//      - }. cdvdfsv sends a buffer's 64-byte-aligned middle by DMA and its
//      ragged ends through that record { u32 length1, length2, dest1, dest2,
//      u8 bytes1[64], bytes2[64] }, which the library's completion copies out:
//      here every byte goes straight to the buffer and the record says none.
//  14  sceCdDiskReady (N): 2, SCECdComplete.
// How long a read takes the drive: a 24x CD's 3.6 MB/s, after a seek. Games
// time things by it - Mister Mosquito's stage loader moves a sound bank a
// jingle still plays from, which the seconds its reads take let end first.
// Fast (FastDisc): an SSD's - the image is read in the time the RPC takes.
// PS2HOST_DISC_SPEED=n: the drive n times as fast, for measuring what the
// drive's time costs a loading screen.
u64 ReadTimeNs(std::size_t bytes) {
    constexpr u64 kSeekNs = 2000000, kBytesPerSecond = 3686400;
    static const double speed = [] {
        const char* text = std::getenv("PS2HOST_DISC_SPEED");
        return text ? std::max(1.0, std::atof(text)) : 1.0;
    }();
    if (FastDisc()) return 50000 + u64(bytes) * 1000000000ull / (400ull << 20);
    return u64(double(kSeekNs + u64(bytes) * 1000000000ull / kBytesPerSecond) / speed);
}



std::vector<u8> NCommand(u32 procedure, const std::vector<u8>& data) {
    Memory& m = GuestMemory();
    switch (procedure) {
        case 1: {
            if (data.size() < 20) return Word(0);
            const u32 lsn = At(data, 0), sectors = At(data, 4), buffer = At(data, 8);
            const u32 pattern = (At(data, 12) >> 16) & 0xFF, ends = At(data, 16);
            std::vector<u8> bytes(std::size_t(sectors) * Disc::PatternSize(pattern));
            const bool ok = GuestDisc().IsOpen() &&
                            GuestDisc().ReadPattern(lsn, sectors, pattern, bytes.data());
            char text[160];
            std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "CD: read %u sectors at %u to 0x%08X (pattern %u, ends 0x%08X)%s",
                          sectors, lsn, buffer, pattern, ends, ok ? "" : " - past the disc's end");
            Note("cd read " + std::to_string(lsn) + " " + std::to_string(buffer), text);
            if (!ok) return Word(0);
            m.WriteBytes(buffer, bytes.data(), bytes.size());
            if (ends)
                for (u32 k = 0; k < 16; ++k) m.Write(ends + k, 0, 1);
            DelayRpcReply(ReadTimeNs(bytes.size()));
            return Word(1);
        }
        case 13: {
            // sceCdReadIOPMem: { lsn, sectors, IOP buffer, mode }: the sectors
            // into IOP memory, for a module there.
            if (data.size() < 12) return Word(0);
            const u32 lsn = At(data, 0), sectors = At(data, 4), buffer = At(data, 8) & 0x1FFFFF;
            const u32 pattern = data.size() >= 16 ? (At(data, 12) >> 16) & 0xFF : 0;
            const u32 size = sectors * Disc::PatternSize(pattern);
            std::vector<u8> bytes(size);
            const bool ok = buffer + size <= kIopRamSize && GuestDisc().IsOpen() &&
                            GuestDisc().ReadPattern(lsn, sectors, pattern, bytes.data());
            char text[160];
            std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "CD: read %u sectors at %u into IOP memory at 0x%06X%s",
                          sectors, lsn, buffer, ok ? "" : " - failed");
            Note("cd read iop " + std::to_string(lsn), text);
            if (!ok) return Word(0);
            m.WriteBytes(kIopRamBase + buffer, bytes.data(), size);
            DelayRpcReply(ReadTimeNs(size));
            return Word(1);
        }
        case 14:
            return Word(2);
        default:
            Note("cd ncmd " + std::to_string(procedure),
                 "CD: N-command " + std::to_string(procedure) + " (answered with zeros)");
            return {};
    }
}

}  // namespace

void InstallIopServers() {
    InstallFileIo();
    InstallLoadFile();
    InstallDbc();
    InstallIopHeap();
    InstallMcserv();
    RegisterRpcServer(0x8000059Cu, DiskReady);
    RegisterRpcServer(0x8000059Au, DiskReady);      // the same, as SDK 2.3's libcdvd binds it
    RegisterRpcServer(0x80000592u, CdInit);
    RegisterRpcServer(0x80000595u, NCommand);
    RegisterRpcServer(0x80000597u, SearchFile);
    RegisterRpcServer(0x80000593u, SCommand);
}

}  // namespace ps2host
```

`host/src/cpu_check.cpp`:

```cpp
// The game executable's entry (ps2_add_port links it as /ENTRY), before the
// C runtime starts: whether this processor can run this build.
//
// A port is built for AVX2 by default (engine/host/CMakeLists.txt,
// PS2HOST_AVX2) - and so is everything in it, the runtime's start and the
// static constructors included: on a processor without AVX2 (Intel's
// Pentium and Celeron of before 2021: Pentium Silver, Celeron N) the first
// of its instructions would stop the program with no word said. So this file
// is built without AVX, and runs first: on such a processor it starts the
// build for it beside this one (<name>-sse4.exe: PS2HOST_AVX2=OFF), with the
// same command line, or says what is needed. The SSE4 build checks for
// SSE4.1 in turn (its intrinsics: the VU's lanes, the IPU).
//
// Only the Windows API here: nothing of the C runtime is up yet.

#if defined(_WIN32) && defined(_MSC_VER)

#if defined(__AVX__)
#error "cpu_check.cpp must be built without AVX (it runs on processors without it)"
#endif

#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <windows.h>
#include <intrin.h>

extern "C" DWORD mainCRTStartup(LPVOID);   // the runtime's start: main

namespace {

bool HasAvx2() {
    int info[4];
    __cpuid(info, 0);
    if (info[0] < 7) return false;
    __cpuid(info, 1);
    const bool osxsave = (info[2] >> 27) & 1, avx = (info[2] >> 28) & 1;
    if (!osxsave || !avx) return false;
    if ((_xgetbv(0) & 6) != 6) return false;        // the OS saves the YMM registers
    __cpuidex(info, 7, 0);
    return (info[1] >> 5) & 1;
}

bool HasSse41() {
    int info[4];
    __cpuid(info, 1);
    return (info[2] >> 19) & 1;
}

/* PS2HOST_TEST_NO_AVX2=1: as on a processor without AVX2 (to test the way to
   the SSE4 build on one with it). */
bool TestNoAvx2() {
    wchar_t value[8];
    return GetEnvironmentVariableW(L"PS2HOST_TEST_NO_AVX2", value, 8) > 0;
}

/* The SSE4 build beside this executable: its own path with "-sse4" before
   ".exe", or "" when there is none. */
bool SiblingPath(wchar_t* out, DWORD size) {
    wchar_t self[MAX_PATH];
    const DWORD n = GetModuleFileNameW(nullptr, self, MAX_PATH);
    if (n == 0 || n >= MAX_PATH || n < 4) return false;
    DWORD stem = n;
    if (self[n - 4] == L'.') stem = n - 4;         // before ".exe"
    const wchar_t suffix[] = L"-sse4.exe";
    if (stem + (sizeof suffix / sizeof suffix[0]) > size) return false;
    for (DWORD i = 0; i < stem; ++i) out[i] = self[i];
    for (DWORD i = 0; i < sizeof suffix / sizeof suffix[0]; ++i) out[stem + i] = suffix[i];
    return GetFileAttributesW(out) != INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES;
}

/* The other build, with this one's command line; its exit code is this one's. */
DWORD RunSibling(const wchar_t* path) {
    const wchar_t* line = GetCommandLineW();
    DWORD length = 0;
    while (line[length]) ++length;
    HANDLE heap = GetProcessHeap();
    wchar_t* copy = static_cast<wchar_t*>(HeapAlloc(heap, 0, (length + 1) * sizeof(wchar_t)));
    if (!copy) return 71;
    for (DWORD i = 0; i <= length; ++i) copy[i] = line[i];
    // Its output where this one's goes (a terminal, a pipe: a scripted run's).
    STARTUPINFOW si{};
    si.cb = sizeof si;
    si.dwFlags = STARTF_USESTDHANDLES;
    si.hStdInput = GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE);
    si.hStdOutput = GetStdHandle(STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE);
    si.hStdError = GetStdHandle(STD_ERROR_HANDLE);
    PROCESS_INFORMATION pi{};
    if (!CreateProcessW(path, copy, nullptr, nullptr, TRUE, 0, nullptr, nullptr, &si, &pi)) return 71;
    WaitForSingleObject(pi.hProcess, INFINITE);
    DWORD code = 71;
    GetExitCodeProcess(pi.hProcess, &code);
    CloseHandle(pi.hThread);
    CloseHandle(pi.hProcess);
    return code;
}

}  // namespace

extern "C" DWORD Ps2CheckedStart(LPVOID peb) {
#if defined(PS2HOST_BUILT_FOR_AVX2)
    if (HasAvx2() && !TestNoAvx2()) return mainCRTStartup(peb);
    wchar_t sibling[MAX_PATH];
    if (SiblingPath(sibling, MAX_PATH)) ExitProcess(RunSibling(sibling));
    MessageBoxW(nullptr,
                L"This build needs a processor with AVX2 (Intel Haswell or AMD Excavator, 2013-2015, or later).\n\n"
                L"For a processor without it (Intel Pentium or Celeron before 2021), use the \"-sse4\" "
                L"executable that comes with it, in the same folder.",
                L"Processor not supported", MB_OK | MB_ICONERROR);
    ExitProcess(70);
#else
    if (HasSse41()) return mainCRTStartup(peb);
    MessageBoxW(nullptr, L"This build needs a processor with SSE4.1 (2008 or later).",
                L"Processor not supported", MB_OK | MB_ICONERROR);
    ExitProcess(70);
#endif
}

#endif

```

`host/src/dbc.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * The IOP's controller manager, dbcman (server 0x80001300), on the host: the
 * devices behind the SDK's libdbc and, above it, libpad2. A DualShock 2 is
 * attached on port 0, driven by every device - the window's game controllers
 * (SDL3, any SDL knows) and the keyboard while the window has focus - and
 * none on port 1, until a game gives each port its players' devices
 * (SetPortDevices): then port 1 has a DualShock 2 too, driven by its own.
 *
 * The protocol, as Burnout 3's copies of libdbc (0x00215F18-0x00216D20) and
 * libpad2 (0x00215620-0x00215EE0) speak it:
 *
 *   0x80001363  version: answer word 0 = major << 8 | minor (libdbc 3.0 needs 3)
 *   0x80001304  sceDbcSetWorkAddr: +4 the EE work area; its first 16 words are
 *               each socket's status, 1 when a device is there
 *   0x80001301  sceDbcCreateSocket: +8 the port, +0x28 and +0x2C the EE
 *               addresses of the socket's two 0x80-byte data blocks; answer
 *               +0x24 the socket (-1: none)
 *   0x80001302  sceDbcDeleteSocket: +0 the socket
 *   0x80001303  sceDbcGetDepNumber: +0 the socket; answer +4 (0: present)
 *   0x8000131B  sceDbcSendData2: +0 the socket, +4 a header, +8 the length,
 *               +0xC the data: a command's length (word), its data's length
 *               (word), the data, the command. Command 3 with two bytes of
 *               data sets a DualShock 2's motors (Burnout 3's 0x00217070):
 *               the small motor in bit 0, the large one's 0-255 above it.
 *
 * The device writes its state into the socket's blocks, the newer one
 * marked by the larger counter at +0x7C. A block:
 *   +0 state (1: connected)   +2 data length   +3 profile length
 *   +4 status (non-zero: valid)   +0x1C the data, then the profile
 * The profile is a bitmask of 40 inputs; libpad2 lays the data out by it
 * (0x00215E30): inputs 16-31 and 35-38 are a byte each (analog), the others
 * a bit each, in input order. A DualShock 2 has inputs 0-31: 16 buttons
 * (active low: a pressed button's bit is 0), the four stick bytes, then 12
 * pressures - 18 bytes,
 * profile FF FF FF FF 00.
 */

#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <windows.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cctype>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "ps2host/host.h"
#include "ps2host/memory.h"
#include "ps2host/run.h"

namespace ps2host {

namespace {

constexpr u32 kVersion = 0x0300;    // dbcman 3.0, as libdbc 3.0 expects
constexpr u32 kDataBytes = 18, kProfileBytes = 5;

struct Socket {
    u32 port = 0, block[2] = {0, 0};
    u32 counter = 0;
};

struct Dbc {
    u32 work = 0;
    std::map<s32, Socket> sockets;
};

// Ports 0 and 1 are the controller ports, 2 and 3 the memory card slots. A
// socket opens on any of them; what is plugged in shows in its blocks. There is
// a DualShock 2 on port 0, one on port 1 while it has devices of its own
// (SetPortDevices), and no memory card.
constexpr u32 kPorts = 4, kPadPorts = 2;
bool g_assigned = false;                        // SetPortDevices: each port its devices
bool g_split = false;                           // SetPortsSplit: ... and they drive them now
std::vector<u32> g_port_devices[kPadPorts];
bool Present(u32 port) { return port == 0 || (port == 1 && g_assigned && !g_port_devices[1].empty()); }
// Whether a port is player 1's, every device's: port 0 - and port 1 too
// while seated and not split (a game's menus: its screens for player 2 then
// work from any device).
bool Split() { return g_assigned && g_split; }
bool Everyones(u32 port) { return port == 0 || (port == 1 && Present(1) && !g_split); }
// Whether a device drives a port: split, its seat's; otherwise everyone's.
bool Drives(u32 port, u32 device) {
    if (!Split()) return Everyones(port);
    if (port >= kPadPorts) return false;
    const auto& d = g_port_devices[port];
    return std::find(d.begin(), d.end(), device) != d.end();
}

Dbc& D() {
    static Dbc dbc;
    return dbc;
}

u32 At(const std::vector<u8>& data, std::size_t offset) {
    u32 value = 0;
    if (offset + 4 <= data.size()) std::memcpy(&value, &data[offset], 4);
    return value;
}

void Put(std::vector<u8>& data, std::size_t offset, u32 value) {
    if (offset + 4 <= data.size()) std::memcpy(&data[offset], &value, 4);
}

// The keyboard as a DualShock 2: (input, key). Inputs 0-15 are the buttons in
// libpad's order: Select, L3, R3, Start, Up, Right, Down, Left, L2, R2, L1, R1,
// Triangle, Circle, Cross, Square.
const std::pair<int, int> kKeys[] = {
    {0, VK_BACK}, {3, VK_RETURN}, {4, VK_UP}, {5, VK_RIGHT}, {6, VK_DOWN}, {7, VK_LEFT},
    {8, '1'}, {9, '3'}, {10, 'Q'}, {11, 'E'}, {12, 'V'}, {13, 'C'}, {14, 'X'}, {15, 'Z'},
};

// Scripted presses (--press): (input, first frame, last frame, pressure), and
// the scripted controller pressing it (--press padN:..., N from 1), or 0: the
// player's own presses, on port 0 whoever drives it.
struct Press { int input; u64 from, to; u8 pressure; u32 device; };
std::vector<Press>& Script() {
    static std::vector<Press> presses;
    return presses;
}
// Scripted keys (--key): (virtual key, first frame, last frame).
struct KeyPress { int key; u64 from, to; };
std::vector<KeyPress>& KeyScript() {
    static std::vector<KeyPress> keys;
    return keys;
}
u64 g_frame = 0;

bool Pressed(int key) { return (WindowFocused() || KeysScripted()) && HostKeyDown(key); }
u16 g_held = 0;                     // PadButtonsHeld: port 0's
u16 (*g_pad_hook)() = nullptr;      // SetPadHook
void (*g_controller_filter)(HostPadState*) = nullptr;     // SetControllerFilter
u16 (*g_keyboard_mapper)() = nullptr;                       // SetKeyboardMapper
// LastInputDevice: the device of the last press, and when; what each held.
InputDevice g_last_device = InputDevice::kNone;
u64 g_last_input_frame = 0;
struct Before {                     // each port's, the read before
    u16 keys = 0, controller = 0;
    bool sticks = false;
};
Before g_before[kPadPorts];

// A scripted controller (--press padN:...) as a controller reads now.
HostPadState ScriptedPad(u32 n) {
    HostPadState pad;
    for (const Press& p : Script())
        if (p.device == n && g_frame >= p.from && g_frame <= p.to) {
            pad.buttons |= u16(1u << p.input);
            if (p.input == 8) pad.l2 = p.pressure;
            if (p.input == 9) pad.r2 = p.pressure;
        }
    return pad;
}
std::vector<u32> ScriptedDevices() {
    std::vector<u32> n;
    for (const Press& p : Script())
        if (p.device && std::find(n.begin(), n.end(), p.device) == n.end()) n.push_back(p.device);
    std::sort(n.begin(), n.end());
    return n;
}

// --record-input and --replay-input (RecordInput, ReplayInput): the reports,
// by the frame each starts at.
std::FILE* g_record = nullptr;
u8 g_recorded[kDataBytes] = {};
bool g_recorded_any = false;
struct Report { u64 frame; u8 data[kDataBytes]; };
std::vector<Report> g_replay;
std::size_t g_replay_next = 0;
bool g_replaying = false;

// The report as recorded or replayed: a replay's replaces the pad's whole.
void RecordOrReplay(u8* data) {
    if (g_replaying) {
        while (g_replay_next < g_replay.size() && g_replay[g_replay_next].frame <= g_frame) ++g_replay_next;
        if (g_replay_next) std::memcpy(data, g_replay[g_replay_next - 1].data, kDataBytes);
        else for (u32 i = 0; i < kDataBytes; ++i) data[i] = i < 2 ? 0xFF : i < 6 ? 0x80 : 0;
        g_held = u16(~(u32(data[0]) | u32(data[1]) << 8));
    }
    if (g_record && (!g_recorded_any || std::memcmp(data, g_recorded, kDataBytes) != 0)) {
        std::fprintf(g_record, "%llu", (unsigned long long)g_frame);
        for (u32 i = 0; i < kDataBytes; ++i) std::fprintf(g_record, " %02X", data[i]);
        std::fputc('\n', g_record);
        std::fflush(g_record);
        std::memcpy(g_recorded, data, kDataBytes);
        g_recorded_any = true;
    }
}

void PadData(u32 port, u8* data) {
    u16 buttons = 0xFFFF;                                   // active low: nothing pressed
    u8 pressure[16] = {};                                   // each input's, the most any source gives
    u16 keys = 0;
    if (Drives(port, kKeyboardDevice)) {
        if (g_keyboard_mapper) {
            keys = g_keyboard_mapper();
            for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
                if (keys & (1u << i)) pressure[i] = 0xFF;
        } else {
            for (const auto& [input, key] : kKeys)
                if (Pressed(key)) keys |= u16(1u << input), pressure[input] = 0xFF;
        }
    }
    buttons &= u16(~keys);
    // PS2HOST_SCRIPT_CONTROLLER=1: scripted presses as a controller's (a
    // game's controller filter sees them; L2's and R2's pressure the
    // triggers' travel) - to test a game's own controls in a scripted run.
    // The player's own presses (--press without padN:) are player 1's.
    static const bool script_controller = std::getenv("PS2HOST_SCRIPT_CONTROLLER") != nullptr;
    HostPadState scripted;
    if (Everyones(port))
        for (const Press& p : Script())
            if (!p.device && g_frame >= p.from && g_frame <= p.to) {
                if (script_controller) {
                    scripted.buttons |= u16(1u << p.input);
                    if (p.input == 8) scripted.l2 = p.pressure;
                    if (p.input == 9) scripted.r2 = p.pressure;
                    continue;
                }
                buttons &= u16(~(1u << p.input));
                pressure[p.input] = std::max(pressure[p.input], p.pressure);
            }
    // The port's controllers, each as the player pressed it, then through a
    // game's own controls (SetControllerFilter), together: the buttons any
    // holds, the most pressure, the sticks of the first pushed off centre.
    std::vector<HostPadState> pads;
    for (const HostDevice& d : WindowControllers()) {
        HostPadState pad;
        if (Drives(port, d.id) && WindowControllerPad(d.id, &pad)) pads.push_back(pad);
    }
    if (script_controller && Everyones(port) && pads.empty()) pads.push_back(scripted);
    for (u32 n : ScriptedDevices())
        if (Drives(port, kScriptedDevice + n)) pads.push_back(ScriptedPad(n));
    const bool controller = !pads.empty();
    HostPadState pad;
    u16 controller_held = 0;
    bool sticks = false;
    for (std::size_t n = 0; n < pads.size(); ++n) {
        HostPadState& p = pads[n];
        p.port = u8(port);
        controller_held |= p.buttons;
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) sticks = sticks || std::abs(int(p.sticks[i]) - 0x80) > 0x50;
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
            if (p.buttons & (1u << i)) p.pressure[i] = 0xFF;
        if (p.buttons & (1u << 8)) p.pressure[8] = std::max<u8>(p.l2, 1);
        if (p.buttons & (1u << 9)) p.pressure[9] = std::max<u8>(p.r2, 1);
        // A game's own controls (SetControllerFilter): the controller's alone.
        if (g_controller_filter) g_controller_filter(&p);
        if (n == 0) {
            pad = p;
            continue;
        }
        pad.buttons |= p.buttons;
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) pad.pressure[i] = std::max(pad.pressure[i], p.pressure[i]);
        pad.l2 = std::max(pad.l2, p.l2);
        pad.r2 = std::max(pad.r2, p.r2);
        bool centred = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) centred = centred && std::abs(int(pad.sticks[i]) - 0x80) <= 0x10;
        if (centred) std::copy(std::begin(p.sticks), std::end(p.sticks), std::begin(pad.sticks));
    }
    if (controller) {
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
            if (pad.buttons & (1u << i)) pressure[i] = std::max(pressure[i], pad.pressure[i]);
        buttons &= u16(~pad.buttons);
    }
    // A key or a controller's button newly down, or a stick pushed well off
    // its centre: that device the player's now.
    Before& before = g_before[port < kPadPorts ? port : 0];
    if (keys & ~before.keys) g_last_device = InputDevice::kKeyboard, g_last_input_frame = g_frame;
    if (controller && ((controller_held & ~before.controller) || (sticks && !before.sticks)))
        g_last_device = InputDevice::kController, g_last_input_frame = g_frame;
    before.keys = keys;
    before.controller = controller_held;
    before.sticks = sticks;
    if (g_pad_hook && Everyones(port)) {
        // (asked once a frame: both ports' the same)
        static u64 hook_frame = ~0ull;
        static u16 hook_buttons = 0;
        if (hook_frame != g_frame) hook_buttons = g_pad_hook(), hook_frame = g_frame;
        const u16 hooked = hook_buttons;
        buttons &= u16(~hooked);
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
            if (hooked & (1u << i)) pressure[i] = 0xFF;
    }
    if (PcMenuOpen()) {                     // the PC settings panel has the keys
        buttons = 0xFFFF;
        pad = HostPadState{};
        std::fill(std::begin(pressure), std::end(pressure), u8(0));
    }
    if (port == 0) g_held = u16(~buttons);
    data[0] = u8(buttons);
    data[1] = u8(buttons >> 8);
    // Then, as libpad's DualShock 2 report has them: the sticks (right X, Y,
    // left X, Y), centred without a controller, and the pressure of the
    // pressure-sensitive buttons - right, left, up, down, triangle, circle,
    // cross, square, L1, R1, L2, R2 - full when pressed, the triggers' own
    // travel for L2 and R2 (or wherever a controller filter puts it), a
    // scripted press's its own. (Sticks read as 0 are pushed fully up and
    // left: with them there, the frontend saw input held and never a press.)
    for (u32 i = 2; i < 6; ++i) data[i] = controller ? pad.sticks[i - 2] : 0x80;
    static const int kPressure[12] = {5, 7, 4, 6, 12, 13, 14, 15, 10, 11, 8, 9};
    for (u32 i = 0; i < 12; ++i) data[6 + i] = (buttons >> kPressure[i]) & 1 ? 0 : pressure[kPressure[i]];
    if (port == 0) RecordOrReplay(data);    // (port 0's alone: one player's session)
}

// A port's motors: its controllers' - every controller's while port 0 has them all.
void PortRumble(u32 port, u8 large, u8 small) {
    if (!Split()) {
        if (port == 0) HostRumble(large, small);
        return;
    }
    for (const HostDevice& d : WindowControllers())
        if (Drives(port, d.id)) HostRumbleOf(d.id, large, small);
}

std::vector<u8> Server(u32 procedure, const std::vector<u8>& request) {
    Dbc& d = D();
    std::vector<u8> answer(request.size() < 0x30 ? 0x30 : request.size(), 0);
    std::copy(request.begin(), request.end(), answer.begin());
    switch (procedure) {
        case 0x80001363u:
            Put(answer, 0, kVersion);
            return answer;
        case 0x80001304u:
            d.work = At(request, 4);
            return answer;
        case 0x80001301u: {
            Socket s;
            s.port = At(request, 8);
            s.block[0] = At(request, 0x28);
            s.block[1] = At(request, 0x2C);
            s32 id = -1;
            if (s.port < kPorts)
                for (s32 n = 0; n < 16 && id < 0; ++n)
                    if (!d.sockets.count(n)) id = n;
            if (id >= 0) d.sockets[id] = s;
            char text[128];
            std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "DBC: socket %d on port %u (blocks 0x%08X, 0x%08X)%s",
                          int(id), unsigned(s.port), unsigned(s.block[0]), unsigned(s.block[1]),
                          id < 0 ? ": no such port" : Present(s.port) ? "" : ": nothing plugged in");
            Note("dbc socket " + std::to_string(s.port), text);
            Put(answer, 0x24, u32(id));
            return answer;
        }
        case 0x80001302u:
            d.sockets.erase(s32(At(request, 0)));
            return answer;
        case 0x80001303u: {
            const auto found = d.sockets.find(s32(At(request, 0)));
            Put(answer, 4, found != d.sockets.end() && Present(found->second.port) ? 0 : u32(-1));
            return answer;
        }
        case 0x8000131Bu: {
            const u32 command_bytes = At(request, 0xC), data_bytes = At(request, 0x10);
            if (data_bytes == 2 && command_bytes == 1 && request.size() > 0x16 && request[0x16] == 3) {
                const u32 value = u32(request[0x14]) | u32(request[0x15]) << 8;
                const u8 small = (value & 1) ? 255 : 0, large = u8(std::min(255u, value >> 1));
                if (std::getenv("PS2HOST_RUMBLE_LOG"))
                    std::fprintf(stderr, "[pad] motors: large %u small %u (0x%04X)\n", unsigned(large),
                                 unsigned(small), unsigned(value));
                const auto socket = d.sockets.find(s32(At(request, 0)));
                PortRumble(socket != d.sockets.end() ? socket->second.port : 0, large, small);
            } else {
                char text[128];
                std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "DBC: SendData2 command length %u, data length %u (ignored)",
                              unsigned(command_bytes), unsigned(data_bytes));
                Note("dbc senddata2 " + std::to_string(command_bytes) + "/" + std::to_string(data_bytes), text);
            }
            return answer;
        }
        case 0x8000131Au: {
            // sceDbcReceiveData: +0 socket, +4 command, +8 room. Answer: +0x20C
            // the result (< 0: failed), +8 the length, +0xC the data - whose
            // first byte libpad2 reads as the device's state (1: connected).
            if (answer.size() < 0x210) answer.resize(0x210, 0);
            const auto found = d.sockets.find(s32(At(request, 0)));
            const bool there = found != d.sockets.end() && Present(found->second.port);
            Put(answer, 0x20C, there ? 0 : u32(-1));
            Put(answer, 8, there ? 1 : 0);
            answer[0xC] = there ? 1 : 0;
            return answer;
        }
        default: {
            char text[96];
            std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "IOP: dbcman procedure 0x%08X is not implemented (zeros)",
                          unsigned(procedure));
            Note("dbcman " + std::to_string(procedure), text);
            std::fill(answer.begin(), answer.end(), 0);
            return answer;
        }
    }
}

/*
 * The older controller module, padman (servers 0x80000100 and 0x80000101),
 * behind libpad 2.x - as Mister Mosquito's copy (0x0010AF50-0x0010C100,
 * "PsIIlibpad  2300", padman 4.x) speaks it. A call is procedure 1 with a
 * 0x80-byte buffer: +0 the command, then its arguments; the answer's result
 * is at +0xC.
 *
 *   0x12  version: +0xC = major << 8 | minor (the library needs major 4)
 *   0x10  init      0x0F  end
 *   0x01  scePadPortOpen: +4 port, +8 slot, +0x10 the EE pad area (two
 *         0x80-byte frames); answer +0x14 the IOP address libpad DMAs its
 *         actuator settings to
 *   0x0E  scePadPortClose: +4 port, +8 slot
 *
 * The module writes the pad's state into the older of the two frames each
 * frame, numbering it past the other:
 *   +0x00 the report: 0 (ok), the mode ID (0x73: DualShock, analog), the
 *         buttons (active low), the sticks; its length at +0x60
 *   +0x58 u32 frame number (libpad reads the frame with the larger)
 *   +0x50 u16 mode table (pad types: 4 digital, 7 DualShock), +0x64 2 (a
 *         controller with modes), +0x65 the mode ID, +0x68 modes, +0x69 the
 *         current mode, +0x6A actuators
 *   +0x70 state (6: stable), +0x71 request state (0: done, 2: busy),
 *   +0x72 1 (a controller is there)
 */
struct PadArea {
    u32 port = 0, slot = 0, area = 0;
    u32 frame = 0;
};
std::map<u64, PadArea>& PadAreas() {
    static std::map<u64, PadArea> areas;
    return areas;
}
constexpr u8 kPadmanMode = 0x73;                // DualShock, analog: 3 halfwords after the header

std::vector<u8> Padman(u32 /*procedure*/, const std::vector<u8>& request) {
    std::vector<u8> answer(request.size() < 0x80 ? 0x80 : request.size(), 0);
    std::copy(request.begin(), request.end(), answer.begin());
    const u32 command = At(request, 0);
    switch (command) {
        case 0x12:
            Put(answer, 0xC, 0x0400);
            return answer;
        case 0x10: case 0x0F:
            Put(answer, 0xC, 1);
            return answer;
        case 0x01: {
            PadArea p;
            p.port = At(request, 4);
            p.slot = At(request, 8);
            p.area = At(request, 0x10);
            PadAreas()[u64(p.port) << 32 | p.slot] = p;
            char text[96];
            std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "PAD: port %u slot %u open (pad area 0x%08X)%s",
                          unsigned(p.port), unsigned(p.slot), unsigned(p.area),
                          Present(p.port) && p.slot == 0 ? "" : ": nothing plugged in");
            Note("padman open " + std::to_string(p.port), text);
            Put(answer, 0xC, 1);
            Put(answer, 0x14, 0x001F0000u + 0x100 * (p.port * 4 + p.slot));
            return answer;
        }
        case 0x0E:
            PadAreas().erase(u64(At(request, 4)) << 32 | At(request, 8));
            Put(answer, 0xC, 1);
            return answer;
        default: {
            char text[96];
            std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "PAD: padman command 0x%X (answered done)", unsigned(command));
            Note("padman " + std::to_string(command), text);
            Put(answer, 0xC, 1);
            return answer;
        }
    }
}

void PadmanFrame() {
    Memory& m = GuestMemory();
    for (auto& [key, p] : PadAreas()) {
        const u32 f = p.area + 0x80 * ((p.frame + 1) & 1);
        ++p.frame;
        const bool present = Present(p.port) && p.slot == 0;
        for (u32 i = 0; i < 0x80; i += 4) m.Write(f + i, 0, 4);
        m.Write(f + 0x58, p.frame, 4);
        m.Write(f + 0x70, present ? 6 : 0, 1);           // stable, or disconnected
        m.Write(f + 0x71, 0, 1);
        if (!present) continue;
        u8 data[kDataBytes];
        PadData(p.port, data);
        static const bool pad_log = std::getenv("PS2HOST_PAD_LOG") != nullptr;
        if (pad_log && (data[0] != 0xFF || data[1] != 0xFF))
            std::fprintf(stderr, "[pad] frame %llu port %u area 0x%08X frame# %u buttons %02X%02X\n",
                         (unsigned long long)g_frame, unsigned(p.port), unsigned(f), unsigned(p.frame), data[1], data[0]);
        const u32 length = 2 + 2 * (kPadmanMode & 0xF);
        m.Write(f + 0, 0, 1);
        m.Write(f + 1, kPadmanMode, 1);
        for (u32 i = 0; i + 2 < length; ++i) m.Write(f + 2 + i, data[i], 1);
        m.Write(f + 0x60, length, 4);
        m.Write(f + 0x50, 4, 2);                         // digital,
        m.Write(f + 0x52, 7, 2);                         // DualShock
        m.Write(f + 0x64, 2, 1);
        m.Write(f + 0x65, kPadmanMode, 1);
        m.Write(f + 0x68, 2, 1);
        m.Write(f + 0x69, 1, 1);
        m.Write(f + 0x6A, 2, 1);
        m.Write(f + 0x72, 1, 1);
    }
}

}  // namespace

bool ScriptPress(const std::string& spec, u64 from, u64 to, u8 pressure) {
    static const char* const kNames[16] = {"select", "l3", "r3", "start", "up", "right", "down", "left",
                                           "l2", "r2", "l1", "r1", "triangle", "circle", "cross", "square"};
    // padN:BUTTON - scripted controller N's (from 1).
    std::string button = spec;
    u32 device = 0;
    if (spec.compare(0, 3, "pad") == 0 && spec.find(':') != std::string::npos) {
        device = u32(std::strtoul(spec.c_str() + 3, nullptr, 10));
        if (!device || device > 0xFFFF) return false;
        button = spec.substr(spec.find(':') + 1);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
        if (button == kNames[i]) {
            Script().push_back({i, from, to, pressure, device});
            return true;
        }
    return false;
}

std::vector<HostDevice> HostDevices() {
    std::vector<HostDevice> list;
    list.push_back({kKeyboardDevice, "Keyboard", ControllerFamily::kOther});
    for (const HostDevice& d : WindowControllers()) list.push_back(d);
    for (u32 n : ScriptedDevices())
        list.push_back({kScriptedDevice + n, "Scripted controller " + std::to_string(n), ControllerFamily::kOther});
    return list;
}

bool HostDevicePad(u32 id, HostPadState* state) {
    if (id > kScriptedDevice && id <= kScriptedDevice + 0xFFFF) {
        *state = ScriptedPad(id - kScriptedDevice);
        return true;
    }
    return id != kKeyboardDevice && WindowControllerPad(id, state);
}

void SplitChanged();

void SetPortDevices(u32 port, const std::vector<u32>& devices) {
    if (port >= kPadPorts) return;
    if (!g_assigned) {
        g_assigned = true;
        for (auto& d : g_port_devices) d.clear();
    }
    const bool was = Split();
    g_port_devices[port] = devices;
    if (Split() || was) SplitChanged();
    std::string text = "players: port " + std::to_string(port) + " has";
    for (u32 id : devices) text += " " + std::to_string(id);
    std::fprintf(stderr, "[pad] %s\n", text.c_str());
}

// The ports split or joined: motors stopped (their controllers change), and
// the trigger effects follow port 0's controllers while split (the
// keyboard's id, no controller's, when it has none: none has them).
void SplitChanged() {
    for (const HostDevice& d : WindowControllers()) HostRumbleOf(d.id, 0, 0);
    std::vector<u32> targets;
    if (Split()) {
        for (u32 id : g_port_devices[0])
            if (id != kKeyboardDevice) targets.push_back(id);
        if (targets.empty()) targets.push_back(kKeyboardDevice);
    }
    HostTriggerTargets(targets);
}

void ResetPortDevices() {
    if (!g_assigned) return;
    const bool was = Split();
    g_assigned = false;
    for (auto& d : g_port_devices) d.clear();
    if (was) SplitChanged();
    std::fprintf(stderr, "[pad] players: every device on port 0 again\n");
}

void SetPortsSplit(bool on) {
    const bool was = Split();
    g_split = on;
    if (Split() != was) SplitChanged();
}

bool PortsAssigned() { return g_assigned; }

bool ScriptKey(const std::string& key, u64 from, u64 to) {
    static const std::pair<const char*, int> kNames[] = {
        {"enter", VK_RETURN}, {"escape", VK_ESCAPE}, {"space", VK_SPACE}, {"backspace", VK_BACK},
        {"tab", VK_TAB},      {"up", VK_UP},         {"down", VK_DOWN},   {"left", VK_LEFT},
        {"right", VK_RIGHT},  {"lshift", VK_LSHIFT}, {"rshift", VK_RSHIFT}, {"lctrl", VK_LCONTROL},
        {"rctrl", VK_RCONTROL}};
    int vk = 0;
    if (key.size() == 1 && std::isalnum(static_cast<unsigned char>(key[0])))
        vk = std::toupper(static_cast<unsigned char>(key[0]));
    else if (key.size() > 2 && key[0] == '0' && (key[1] == 'x' || key[1] == 'X'))
        vk = int(std::strtol(key.c_str() + 2, nullptr, 16));
    else
        for (const auto& [name, code] : kNames)
            if (key == name) vk = code;
    if (vk <= 0 || vk > 0xFE) return false;
    KeyScript().push_back({vk, from, to});
    return true;
}

bool ScriptedKeyDown(int key) {
    for (const KeyPress& k : KeyScript())
        if (k.key == key && g_frame >= k.from && g_frame <= k.to) return true;
    return false;
}

bool KeysScripted() { return !KeyScript().empty(); }

bool RecordInput(const std::string& path) {
    g_record = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "w");
    return g_record != nullptr;
}

bool ReplayInput(const std::string& path) {
    std::FILE* file = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "r");
    if (!file) return false;
    char line[256];
    while (std::fgets(line, sizeof line, file)) {
        Report r{};
        char* at = line;
        r.frame = std::strtoull(at, &at, 10);
        u32 i = 0;
        for (; i < kDataBytes; ++i) {
            char* end = nullptr;
            const unsigned long value = std::strtoul(at, &end, 16);
            if (end == at) break;
            r.data[i] = u8(value);
            at = end;
        }
        if (i == kDataBytes) g_replay.push_back(r);
    }
    std::fclose(file);
    g_replaying = true;
    return !g_replay.empty();
}

// Each frame: every socket's device writes its state into the next block.
void DbcFrame() {
    ++g_frame;
    PadmanFrame();
    Dbc& d = D();
    Memory& m = GuestMemory();
    for (auto& [id, s] : d.sockets) {
        const bool present = Present(s.port);
        if (d.work) m.Write(d.work + 4 * u32(id), present ? 1 : 0, 4);
        const u32 b = s.block[(s.counter + 1) & 1];
        if (!b) continue;
        if (!present) {                                 // an empty port: disconnected
            m.Write(b + 0, 0, 1);
            m.Write(b + 4, 0, 4);
            m.Write(b + 0x7C, ++s.counter, 4);
            continue;
        }
        u8 data[kDataBytes];
        PadData(s.port, data);
        m.Write(b + 0, 1, 1);                           // connected
        m.Write(b + 1, 0, 1);
        m.Write(b + 2, kDataBytes, 1);
        m.Write(b + 3, kProfileBytes, 1);
        m.Write(b + 4, 1, 4);                           // valid
        for (u32 i = 0; i < kDataBytes; ++i) m.Write(b + 0x1C + i, data[i], 1);
        const u8 profile[kProfileBytes] = {0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00};
        for (u32 i = 0; i < kProfileBytes; ++i) m.Write(b + 0x1C + kDataBytes + i, profile[i], 1);
        m.Write(b + 0x7C, ++s.counter, 4);
    }
}

void InstallDbc() {
    RegisterRpcServer(0x80001300u, Server);
    // libdbc binds a client of its own to each send (SendData2, SendData3):
    // their servers' ids are the procedures', and dbcman answers them alike.
    RegisterRpcServer(0x8000131Bu, Server);
    RegisterRpcServer(0x8000131Cu, Server);
    RegisterRpcServer(0x80000100u, Padman);
    RegisterRpcServer(0x80000101u, Padman);
}

u16 PadButtonsHeld() { return g_held; }

InputDevice LastInputDevice(u64* frame) {
    if (frame) *frame = g_last_input_frame;
    return g_last_device;
}

void SetPadHook(u16 (*hook)()) { g_pad_hook = hook; }

void SetControllerFilter(void (*filter)(HostPadState* pad)) { g_controller_filter = filter; }
void SetKeyboardMapper(u16 (*mapper)()) { g_keyboard_mapper = mapper; }

namespace {
struct MouseStep {
    u64 frame;
    float x, y;
    char action;            // 'L', 'R', 'U', 'D' or 0
};
std::vector<MouseStep>& MouseScript() {
    static std::vector<MouseStep> steps;
    return steps;
}
}  // namespace

bool ScriptMouse(const std::string& spec) {
    MouseStep step{};
    char action[2] = {};
    const int n = std::sscanf(spec.c_str(), "%llu:%f,%f,%1[LRUD]", reinterpret_cast<unsigned long long*>(&step.frame),
                              &step.x, &step.y, action);
    if (n < 3) return false;
    step.action = action[0];
    MouseScript().push_back(step);
    std::sort(MouseScript().begin(), MouseScript().end(),
              [](const MouseStep& a, const MouseStep& b) { return a.frame < b.frame; });
    return true;
}

bool ScriptedMouse(HostMouseState* state) {
    if (MouseScript().empty()) return false;
    *state = HostMouseState{};
    for (const MouseStep& s : MouseScript()) {
        if (s.frame > g_frame) break;
        state->over = true;
        state->x = s.x;
        state->y = s.y;
        if (s.frame == g_frame) {
            state->moved = true;
            if (s.action == 'L') state->pressed |= 1;
            if (s.action == 'R') state->pressed |= 4;
            if (s.action == 'U') state->wheel += 1.0f;
            if (s.action == 'D') state->wheel -= 1.0f;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

}  // namespace ps2host
```

`host/src/devices.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * Device registers with hardware meaning, stage one: just enough for code that
 * starts a transfer and waits for it, or waits for a vertical blank, to go on.
 *
 * DMA: setting a channel's STR bit starts a transfer; here it completes at once
 *      - the bit clears and the channel's interrupt status is raised. VIF0, VIF1
 *      and GIF transfers are walked (dma.cpp), chains included: VIF1's data
 *      goes to its VIFcode decoder, the rest is counted. Nothing reaches a GS
 *      yet.
 * GIF: while PATH3 is masked, a PATH3 transfer's data waits in the GIF FIFO
 *      (16 quadwords deep), and GIF_STAT's FQC counts it - code handing PATH3
 *      over to VIF1 waits for the GIF to have taken its data before letting VIF1
 *      go. Unmasking drains it.
 * GS:  CSR reports a vertical blank on every read, its field bit alternating, so
 *      a wait for the next frame ends.
 * Timers: in host time, with their interrupts (timers.cpp).
 * VIF1: quadwords stored to its FIFO are decoded as VIFcodes (vif.cpp);
 *      MSKPATH3 shows in GIF_STAT's M3P bit, which code that hands PATH3 over
 *      waits on.
 *
 * Every register the game touches is counted for the report, so the next device
 * to implement is the one the game leans on.
 */

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdio>
#include <ctime>
#include <filesystem>
#include <functional>
#include <cstring>
#include <deque>
#include <mutex>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "ps2host/dma.h"
#include "ps2host/timeline.h"
#ifdef PS2HOST_VULKAN
#include "ps2gpu/display.h"
#endif
#include "ps2host/gs.h"
#include "ps2host/ipu.h"
#include "ps2host/memory.h"
#include "ps2host/path3.h"
#include "ps2host/run.h"
#include "ps2host/settings.h"
#include "ps2host/vif.h"
#include "ps2host/vu.h"
#include "ps2host/profile.h"

namespace ps2host {

namespace {

struct Channel {
    u32 base;
    const char* name;
    u32 status_bit;                 // its bit in D_STAT
    bool walked;                    // its transfers are followed (dma.cpp)
};

const Channel kChannels[] = {
    {0x10008000u, "VIF0", 0, true}, {0x10009000u, "VIF1", 1, true},
    {0x1000A000u, "GIF", 2, true}, {0x1000B000u, "IPU_FROM", 3, false},
    {0x1000B400u, "IPU_TO", 4, false}, {0x1000C000u, "SIF0", 5, false},
    {0x1000C400u, "SIF1", 6, false}, {0x1000C800u, "SIF2", 7, false},
    {0x1000D000u, "SPR_FROM", 8, true}, {0x1000D400u, "SPR_TO", 9, true},
};

// Register offsets within a channel.
constexpr u32 kMadr = 0x10, kQwc = 0x20, kTadr = 0x30, kAsr0 = 0x40, kAsr1 = 0x50;
constexpr u32 kGifFifoDepth = 16;

constexpr u32 kDStat = 0x1000E010u;

// D_STAT: writing 1 clears a status bit (0-15) and flips a mask bit (16-31), so
// what a store leaves is computed from what was there, kept here.
u32 d_stat = 0;

void SetDStat(u32 value) {
    d_stat = value;
    *reinterpret_cast<u32*>(GuestMemory().Translate(kDStat, 4)) = value;
}
constexpr u32 kGsCsr = 0x12001000u;
constexpr u32 kGifStat = 0x10003020u;
constexpr u32 kGifStatM3P = 1u << 1;
constexpr u32 kGifStatFqcShift = 24, kGifStatFqc = 0x1Fu << kGifStatFqcShift;

// PATH3: GIF DMA data to the GS, held while VIF1 has PATH3 masked - it goes
// after the PATH2 data VIF1 sends meanwhile, as the GIF arbitrates.
//
// A mask takes effect only at the end of the GIF packet PATH3 is in - the one
// whose tag has EOP set - so unmasking and masking again at once lets exactly
// one EOP-ended group through. Burnout 3 queues a picture's texture uploads
// (161,280 words at the car select) on PATH3 while it is masked and opens a
// window like that before each group of draws: five groups, five windows,
// each texture slot refilled between the draws that use its contents.
// Releasing everything at the first window refilled every slot early, and the
// garage was drawn with whatever was uploaded last into its slots (the font).
Path3Queue g_path3_held;
bool g_path3_masked = false;

void Path3(const u32* words, u32 count, u32 from) {
    // Behind what is still held, even unmasked: the GIF keeps PATH3 in order.
    if (g_path3_masked || !g_path3_held.empty()) g_path3_held.Push(words, count);
    else GsWords(3, words, count, from);
}

void ReleasePath3(bool all) {
    g_path3_held.ReleaseBlock(all, [](const u32* words, std::size_t count) {
        GsWords(3, words, u32(count));
    });
}

u32* Register(u32 address) { return reinterpret_cast<u32*>(GuestMemory().Translate(address, 4)); }

// The scratchpad channels: SADR (base + 0x80) is the scratchpad address.
// SPR_FROM copies QWC quadwords from it to MADR; SPR_TO copies from memory
// (normal or a source chain) into it.
constexpr u32 kSadr = 0x80;

// Main RAM or the scratchpad, with nothing watching stores: no hooks to run,
// so a copy may go through pointers.
bool Plain(const Memory& m, u32 address) {
    return !m.watching() && ((address & 0x1FFFFFFFu) < 0x10000000u || (address >> 28) == 0x7);
}

std::string Scratchpad(const Channel& ch, u32 chcr, bool describe) {
    Memory& m = GuestMemory();
    u32 sadr = u32(m.Read(ch.base + kSadr, 4)) & 0x3FF0u;
    const u32 madr = u32(m.Read(ch.base + kMadr, 4)), qwc = u32(m.Read(ch.base + kQwc, 4));
    char text[160];
    if (ch.base == 0x1000D000u) {                       // SPR_FROM
        if ((chcr >> 2) & 3) return "chain mode is not modelled (nothing copied)";
        for (u32 i = 0; i < 16 * qwc; i += 16) {           // a quadword at a time (SADR is aligned)
            const u32 from = kScratchpadBase + ((sadr + i) & 0x3FF0u);
            u8* to = Plain(m, madr + i) ? m.Translate(madr + i, 16) : nullptr;
            if (const u8* source = to ? m.Translate(from, 16) : nullptr) {
                std::memcpy(to, source, 16);
                continue;
            }
            for (u32 k = 0; k < 16; k += 4) m.Write(madr + i + k, m.Read(from + k, 4), 4);
        }
        *Register(ch.base + kMadr) = madr + 16 * qwc;
        *Register(ch.base + kQwc) = 0;
        *Register(ch.base + kSadr) = (sadr + 16 * qwc) & 0x3FF0u;
        if (!describe) return {};
        std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "%u quadwords from scratchpad 0x%04X", unsigned(qwc), unsigned(sadr));
        return text;
    }
    DmaChannelState state{chcr, madr, qwc, u32(m.Read(ch.base + kTadr, 4)),
                          u32(m.Read(ch.base + kAsr0, 4)), u32(m.Read(ch.base + kAsr1, 4))};
    u8* scratchpad = Plain(m, kScratchpadBase) ? m.Translate(kScratchpadBase, kScratchpadSize) : nullptr;
    const DmaOutcome outcome = SendDmaBlocks(state, [&sadr, scratchpad](const u32* words, u32 count, u32 from) {
        for (u32 i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
            g_dma_source = from + 4 * i;
            if (scratchpad) std::memcpy(scratchpad + (sadr & 0x3FFCu), &words[i], 4);
            else GuestMemory().Write(kScratchpadBase + (sadr & 0x3FFCu), words[i], 4);
            sadr = (sadr + 4) & 0x3FFFu;
        }
    });
    *Register(ch.base + kMadr) = state.madr;
    *Register(ch.base + kQwc) = state.qwc;
    *Register(ch.base + kTadr) = state.tadr;
    *Register(ch.base + kSadr) = sadr & 0x3FF0u;
    *Register(ch.base) = state.chcr;
    if (!describe) return {};
    std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "%llu quadwords to scratchpad", static_cast<unsigned long long>(outcome.quadwords));
    return text;
}

// GIF_STAT as VIF1's worker will leave it, worked out on the EE's thread, so
// a read need not wait for the worker (Vif1Guess). Burnout 3 starts each
// display-list packet by waiting for VIF1, VU1 and the GIF to be idle; with
// its transfers ending as they start, every wait was the EE waiting for all
// the worker had - ~15% of the EE's time at a race's start, the pictures it
// missed. Only the worker changes GIF_STAT: VIF1's MSKPATH3 (from the FIFO or
// a transfer) and a GIF transfer held behind the mask filling the FIFO. The
// EE follows the FIFO's commands and the GIF transfers itself, and takes a
// VIF1 transfer to leave GIF_STAT as the one before it left it. Each guess
// is checked on the worker, in turn; a wrong one ends guessing.
struct GifShadow {
    bool known = false;
    u32 value = 0;
};
GifShadow g_gif_shadow;                         // the EE's
std::atomic<u32> g_gif_after_vif1{0};           // the worker's: GIF_STAT as the last VIF1 transfer left it
std::atomic<bool> g_gif_after_known{false};
// The EE's: the register last answered by a guess, nothing it follows
// queued since - read again, the game is waiting for it to change.
u32 g_guessed_last = 0;
std::atomic<u64> g_guesses{0}, g_wrong{0};
std::atomic<bool> g_guessing_off{false};
bool g_check_guesses = false;

bool Shadowing() { return g_check_guesses || Vif1Async(); }

// With nothing queued, GIF_STAT is what memory holds (a check takes the
// worker to be always behind: only its guesses count).
void GifShadowFromMemory() {
    if (!g_check_guesses && !Vif1Busy()) g_gif_shadow = {true, *Register(kGifStat)};
}

void ShadowMask(bool masked) {
    u32& v = g_gif_shadow.value;
    v = masked ? (v | kGifStatM3P) : (v & ~(kGifStatM3P | kGifStatFqc));
}

u32 HeldInFifo(u64 quadwords) { return quadwords < kGifFifoDepth ? u32(quadwords) : kGifFifoDepth; }

// A VIF1 or GIF chain's words as the EE walked it, for VIF1's worker (Walk).
// Kept in a pool: a race walks a hundred chains a frame, and a vector made
// for each grew by reallocating for each of its runs - a sixth of the EE's
// time went to copying them about.
struct ChainCopy {
    std::vector<u32> words;
    std::vector<std::pair<u32, u32>> runs;      // (count, from) each, in order
};
std::mutex g_chain_pool_lock;
std::vector<ChainCopy*> g_chain_pool;

std::shared_ptr<ChainCopy> NewChainCopy() {
    ChainCopy* copy = nullptr;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> hold(g_chain_pool_lock);
        if (!g_chain_pool.empty()) {
            copy = g_chain_pool.back();
            g_chain_pool.pop_back();
        }
    }
    if (!copy) {
        copy = new ChainCopy;
        copy->words.reserve(1u << 16);
        copy->runs.reserve(1024);
    }
    copy->words.clear();            // (the capacity stays)
    copy->runs.clear();
    return std::shared_ptr<ChainCopy>(copy, [](ChainCopy* done) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> hold(g_chain_pool_lock);
        if (g_chain_pool.size() < 16) g_chain_pool.push_back(done);
        else delete done;
    });
}

// Walks a started transfer and leaves the registers as it would; returns a
// note (when `describe`: a transfer is noted only the first time).
std::string Walk(const Channel& ch, u32 chcr, bool describe) {
    Memory& m = GuestMemory();
    if (ch.base == 0x1000D000u || ch.base == 0x1000D400u) return Scratchpad(ch, chcr, describe);
    DmaChannelState state{chcr, u32(m.Read(ch.base + kMadr, 4)), u32(m.Read(ch.base + kQwc, 4)),
                          u32(m.Read(ch.base + kTadr, 4)), u32(m.Read(ch.base + kAsr0, 4)),
                          u32(m.Read(ch.base + kAsr1, 4))};
    // A run of words at a time, each handed on directly.
    auto to_vif = [](VifStream& vif) {
        return [&vif](const u32* words, u32 count, u32 from) { vif.Words(words, count, from); };
    };
    DmaBlockSink sink = [](const u32*, u32, u32) {};
    if (ch.base == 0x10008000u) sink = to_vif(Vif0());
    if (ch.base == 0x10009000u) sink = to_vif(Vif1());
    if (ch.base == 0x1000A000u) sink = Path3;
    // With VIF1's worker, VIF1's and the GIF's words are copied as the chain
    // is walked and handed to it in a command (the transfer ends here, as on
    // the console its data is taken).
    const bool queued = Vif1Async() && (ch.base == 0x10009000u || ch.base == 0x1000A000u);
    auto copy = queued ? NewChainCopy() : nullptr;
    if (queued)
        sink = [copy](const u32* words, u32 count, u32 from) {
            copy->words.insert(copy->words.end(), words, words + count);
            copy->runs.emplace_back(count, from);
        };
    char text[160] = "";
    try {
        Timed timed(Section::Dma);      // (VU1 and the GS, which it drives, timed apart)
        // The GIF takes no chain tags (TTE): dma.h.
        const bool tags = ch.base != 0x1000A000u;
        const DmaOutcome outcome = SendDmaBlocks(state, sink, 1u << 16, tags);
        if (describe)
            std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "%llu quadwords, %u tags%s",
                      static_cast<unsigned long long>(outcome.quadwords), outcome.tags,
                      outcome.ended ? "" : ", stopped: the chain does not end");
        const bool gif = ch.base == 0x1000A000u, vif1 = ch.base == 0x10009000u;
        const u64 quadwords = outcome.quadwords;
        auto fifo = [gif, quadwords] {
            if (gif && (*Register(kGifStat) & kGifStatM3P))
                *Register(kGifStat) = (*Register(kGifStat) & ~kGifStatFqc) | (HeldInFifo(quadwords) << kGifStatFqcShift);
        };
        auto learn = [vif1] {
            if (!vif1) return;
            g_gif_after_vif1 = *Register(kGifStat);
            g_gif_after_known = true;
        };
        if (Shadowing() && (gif || vif1)) {
            GifShadowFromMemory();
            g_guessed_last = 0;             // a read from here on asks again
            if (vif1) {
                g_gif_shadow = {g_gif_after_known.load(), g_gif_after_vif1.load()};
            } else if (g_gif_shadow.known && (g_gif_shadow.value & kGifStatM3P)) {
                g_gif_shadow.value = (g_gif_shadow.value & ~kGifStatFqc) | (HeldInFifo(quadwords) << kGifStatFqcShift);
            }
        }
        if (queued) {
            Vif1Run([copy, gif, fifo, learn] {
                const u32* at = copy->words.data();
                for (const auto& [count, from] : copy->runs) {
                    if (gif) Path3(at, count, from);
                    else Vif1().Words(at, count, from);
                    at += count;
                }
                fifo();
                learn();
            });
        } else {
            fifo();
            learn();
        }
    } catch (const MemoryFault& fault) {
        std::snprintf(text, sizeof text, "stopped: read outside memory at 0x%08X", unsigned(fault.address));
    }
    *Register(ch.base + kMadr) = state.madr;
    *Register(ch.base + kQwc) = state.qwc;
    *Register(ch.base + kTadr) = state.tadr;
    *Register(ch.base + kAsr0) = state.asr0;
    *Register(ch.base + kAsr1) = state.asr1;
    *Register(ch.base) = state.chcr;
    return text;
}
constexpr u32 kVif1Fifo = 0x10005000u;

    g_frames_dir = dir;
    g_frames_every = every > 0 ? every : 1;
    g_frames_limit = limit;
    g_frames_from = from;
}
```
