```cpp
                const u32 amount = u32(value());
                u64 lo1, hi1, lo2, hi2;
                lifted::ShiftLanes(lo1, hi1, blo, bhi, width, kind, amount);
                lifted::ShiftLanesScalar(lo2, hi2, blo, bhi, width, kind, amount);
                ++checked;
                if (lo1 != lo2 || hi1 != hi2) ++wrong;
            }
    char what[128];
    std::snprintf(what, sizeof what, "MMI lanes in SSE2 are the model's (%u of %u differ)", wrong, checked);
    Check(wrong == 0, what);
}

void VuMaxKeepsADenormal() {
    ps2host::Vu vu(0);
    const std::uint32_t kNopU = 0x000002FF, kNopL = 0x8000033C, kI = 0x80000000, kEnd = 0x40000000;
    const std::uint32_t program[] = {
        0x00000412, kI | kNopU,         // loi 0x412
        kNopL, 0x0040005D,              //                          maxi.z vf1, vf0, I
        0x00000412, kI | kNopU,         // loi 0x412
        kNopL, 0x0040009F,              //                          minii.z vf2, vf0, I
        kNopL, kEnd | kNopU,
        kNopL, kNopU};
    std::memcpy(vu.micro.data(), program, sizeof program);
    vu.Run(0);
    Check(vu.regs.vf[1][2] == 0x412 && vu.regs.vf[2][2] == 0, "VU: MAXI and MINII compare and keep the bits");
}

// The IOP interpreter against emu.py, the verified R5900 interpreter: one MIPS I
// instruction per vector (engine/tools/iop_vectors.py).
struct CpuVector {
    const char* name;
    u32 word;
    u32 regs[32];
    u8 data[64];
    u32 out[32];
    u32 hi, lo;
    u8 data_out[64];
};

const CpuVector kCpuVectors[] = {
#include "iop_cpu_vectors.inc"
};

void IopInstructionsMatchTheR5900() {
    using namespace ps2host::iop;
    Vm& vm = TheVm();
    int failures = 0;
    for (const CpuVector& v : kCpuVectors) {
        vm.Write(0x00100000u, v.word, 4);
        for (u32 i = 0; i < 64; ++i) vm.Write(0x00100100u + i, v.data[i], 1);
        Context c;
        for (u32 i = 1; i < 32; ++i) c.r[i] = v.regs[i];
        c.hi = v.regs[0];
        c.lo = v.regs[0] ^ 0x5A5A5A5Au;
        c.pc = 0x00100000u;
        c.npc = 0x00100004u;
        vm.Step(c, 1);
        bool ok = c.hi == v.hi && c.lo == v.lo;
        for (u32 i = 1; i < 32; ++i) ok = ok && c.r[i] == v.out[i];
        for (u32 i = 0; i < 64; ++i) ok = ok && vm.Read(0x00100100u + i, 1) == v.data_out[i];
        if (!ok && failures++ < 5) {
            char what[96];
            std::snprintf(what, sizeof what, "IOP %s (0x%08X) matches the R5900", v.name, unsigned(v.word));
            Check(false, what);
        }
    }
    Check(failures == 0, "every IOP instruction vector matches");
}

}  // namespace

// A core's sound-data input (a block transfer's PCM): heard at its BVOL in the
// dry mix MMIX lets it into; silent at BVOL 0, and once stopped.
void SpuPlaysItsSoundDataInput() {
    using ps2host::iop::Spu2;
    std::vector<Spu2::u8> pcm(0x800);
    for (int block = 0; block < 2; ++block)
        for (int i = 0; i < 256; ++i) {
            const Spu2::s16 left = 8192, right = -8192;
            std::memcpy(&pcm[block * 0x400 + i * 2], &left, 2);
            std::memcpy(&pcm[block * 0x400 + 0x200 + i * 2], &right, 2);
        }
    auto play = [&](Spu2::u32 bvol, bool stop) {
        Spu2 spu;
        std::vector<Spu2::s16> heard;
        spu.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16* frames, Spu2::u32 count) { heard.assign(frames, frames + 2 * count); });
        spu.SetParam(0x0801, 0x00C0);                   // MMIX, core 1: the input, dry
        spu.SetParam(0x0F01, bvol);                     // BVOLL
        spu.SetParam(0x1001, bvol);                     // BVOLR
        spu.SetInput(1, pcm.data(), Spu2::u32(pcm.size()));
        if (stop) spu.SetInput(1, nullptr, 0);
        spu.Advance(1000, [](Spu2::u32) {});
        spu.Advance(11000, [](Spu2::u32) {});           // 10 ms: 480 samples
        return heard;
    };
    const std::vector<Spu2::s16> loud = play(0x7FFF, false);
    Check(loud.size() >= 2 && loud[loud.size() - 2] > 1000 && loud.back() < -1000,
          "SPU2: the sound-data input, left and right");
    const std::vector<Spu2::s16> muted = play(0, false), stopped = play(0x7FFF, true);
    Check(!muted.empty() && muted[muted.size() - 2] == 0 && muted.back() == 0,
          "SPU2: the sound-data input at BVOL 0 is silent");
    Check(!stopped.empty() && stopped.back() == 0, "SPU2: a stopped input is silent");
}

// The cores' routing (PCSX2's mixer): core 0's output is core 1's external
// input, heard at core 1's AVOL (silent at 0); MMIX's external bits (0-3) do
// not let the sound-data input in - its own are 4-7.
void SpuRoutesCore0ThroughCore1() {
    using ps2host::iop::Spu2;
    auto play = [](Spu2::u32 avol) {
        Spu2 spu;
        Spu2::u8 loop[16] = {0x00, 0x07};
        for (int i = 2; i < 16; ++i) loop[i] = 0x11;
        spu.Write(0x5000, loop, 16);
        std::vector<Spu2::s16> heard;
        spu.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16* frames, Spu2::u32 count) { heard.assign(frames, frames + 2 * count); });
        spu.SetAddr(0x2000, 0x5000);                // voice 0 of core 0
        spu.SetParam(0x0000, 0x3FFF);
        spu.SetParam(0x0100, 0x3FFF);
        spu.SetParam(0x0200, 0x1000);
        spu.SetParam(0x0300, 0x000F);
        spu.SetParam(0x0400, 0x1FC0);
        spu.SetParam(0x0D01, avol);                 // AVOLL, core 1
        spu.SetParam(0x0E01, avol);
        spu.SetSwitch(0x1800, 1);
        spu.SetSwitch(0x1A00, 1);
        spu.SetSwitch(0x1500, 1);
        spu.Advance(1000, [](Spu2::u32) {});
        spu.Advance(2000, [](Spu2::u32) {});
        return heard.size() == 96 ? int(heard[90]) : -1;
    };
    Check(play(0x7FFF) > 3500, "SPU2: core 0 heard through core 1");
    Check(play(0) == 0, "SPU2: core 0 silent at core 1's AVOL 0");
    std::vector<Spu2::u8> pcm(0x800, 0x40);
    Spu2 spu;
    std::vector<Spu2::s16> heard;
    spu.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16* frames, Spu2::u32 count) { heard.assign(frames, frames + 2 * count); });
    spu.SetParam(0x0801, 0x000F);                   // MMIX, core 1: the external input only
    spu.SetInput(1, pcm.data(), Spu2::u32(pcm.size()));
    spu.Advance(1000, [](Spu2::u32) {});
    spu.Advance(2000, [](Spu2::u32) {});
    Check(!heard.empty() && heard.back() == 0, "SPU2: the external bits keep the sound-data input out");
}

// A voice's samples go through the hardware's Gaussian interpolation, whose
// four taps sum to 0x7F80, not 0x8000: a block of 4096s plays as ~4080 (4095
// through linear interpolation, as before).
void SpuInterpolatesAsTheHardware() {
    using ps2host::iop::Spu2;
    Spu2 spu;
    Spu2::u8 loop[16] = {0x00, 0x07};
    for (int i = 2; i < 16; ++i) loop[i] = 0x11;
    spu.Write(0x5000, loop, 16);
    std::vector<Spu2::s16> heard;
    spu.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16* frames, Spu2::u32 count) { heard.assign(frames, frames + 2 * count); });
    spu.SetAddr(0x2000, 0x5000);
    spu.SetParam(0x0000, 0x3FFF);
    spu.SetParam(0x0100, 0x3FFF);
    spu.SetParam(0x0200, 0x1000);
    spu.SetParam(0x0300, 0x000F);
    spu.SetParam(0x0400, 0x1FC0);
    spu.SetSwitch(0x1800, 1);
    spu.SetSwitch(0x1A00, 1);
    spu.SetSwitch(0x1500, 1);
    spu.Advance(1000, [](Spu2::u32) {});
    spu.Advance(2000, [](Spu2::u32) {});
    Check(heard.size() == 96 && heard[90] >= 4070 && heard[90] <= 4088,
          "SPU2: a voice's samples through the Gaussian table");
}

// The reverb runs at 24 kHz, its input and output resampled by the hardware's
// half-band FIR: a 1.5 kHz tone through it, its 24 kHz image (22.5 kHz) below
// -40 dB of the tone. A step's output held for two samples left it at -20 dB.
void SpuReverbHasNoImage() {
    using ps2host::iop::Spu2;
    std::vector<Spu2::u8> pcm(0x1000);              // 1,024 samples: 32 periods of 1.5 kHz
    for (int block = 0; block < 4; ++block)
        for (int i = 0; i < 256; ++i) {
            const double t = double(block * 256 + i) / 48000.0;
            const Spu2::s16 s = Spu2::s16(8000.0 * std::sin(2.0 * 3.14159265358979 * 1500.0 * t));
            std::memcpy(&pcm[block * 0x400 + i * 2], &s, 2);
            std::memcpy(&pcm[block * 0x400 + 0x200 + i * 2], &s, 2);
        }
    Spu2 spu;
    std::vector<Spu2::s16> heard;
    spu.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16* frames, Spu2::u32 count) { heard.insert(heard.end(), frames, frames + 2 * count); });
    spu.SetParam(0x0801, 0x0030);                   // MMIX, core 1: the input, wet only
    spu.SetParam(0x0F01, 0x7FFF);
    spu.SetParam(0x1001, 0x7FFF);
    Check(spu.SetEffectAttr(1, 0x101, 0x3FFF, 0x3FFF, 0, 0) == 0, "SPU2: the Room preset on core 1");
    spu.SetCoreAttr(0x3, 1);                        // SD_CORE_EFFECT_ENABLE, core 1
    spu.SetInput(1, pcm.data(), Spu2::u32(pcm.size()));
    spu.Advance(1000, [](Spu2::u32) {});
    spu.Advance(1000 + 300000, [](Spu2::u32) {});   // 300 ms
    auto bin = [&](double hz) {
        double re = 0, im = 0;
        const std::size_t from = heard.size() / 2 - 9600;
        for (std::size_t k = 0; k < 9600; ++k) {
            const double w = 2.0 * 3.14159265358979 * hz * double(k) / 48000.0;
            re += heard[2 * (from + k)] * std::cos(w);
            im += heard[2 * (from + k)] * std::sin(w);
        }
        return std::sqrt(re * re + im * im);
    };
    const double tone = bin(1500), image = bin(22500);
    Check(tone > 1e5, "SPU2: the reverb passes the tone");
    Check(image < tone * 0.01, "SPU2: the reverb's output has no 24 kHz image");
}

// The input's half-buffer interrupt comes from where the SPU2 plays: each half
// begun stops the Advance there (the IOP refills the half before it is read
// again), InputHalf says which half plays, and PlayedUs where it stopped.
void SpuInputInterruptsAtEachHalf() {
    using ps2host::iop::Spu2;
    std::vector<Spu2::u8> pcm(0x1000);              // two halves of 512 samples
    Spu2 spu;
    Spu2::u32 played = 0;
    spu.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16*, Spu2::u32 count) { played += count; });
    spu.SetInput(1, pcm.data(), Spu2::u32(pcm.size()));
    std::vector<Spu2::u32> halves;
    auto half = [&](Spu2::u32 core) { halves.push_back(spu.InputHalf(core)); };
    spu.Advance(1000, [](Spu2::u32) {}, half);
    spu.Advance(1000 + 30000, [](Spu2::u32) {}, half);  // 30 ms: 1,440 samples due
    Check(played == 512 && halves.size() == 1 && halves[0] == 1, "SPU2: the input stops at its second half");
    Check(spu.PlayedUs() < 1000 + 30000, "SPU2: an input's stop leaves the rest owed");
    spu.Advance(1000 + 30000, [](Spu2::u32) {}, half);
    spu.Advance(1000 + 30000, [](Spu2::u32) {}, half);
    Check(played == 1440 && halves.size() == 2 && halves[1] == 0, "SPU2: the rest played, a half at a time");
}

void SpuDecodesAdpcmAndPlaysAVoice() {
    using ps2host::iop::Spu2;
    // Shift 0, filter 0: a nibble is the sample's top four bits.
    Spu2::u8 block[16] = {0x00, 0x00, 0x81};
    Spu2::s32 out[28], older = 0, old = 0;
    Spu2::DecodeBlock(block, out, &older, &old);
    Check(out[0] == 4096 && out[1] == -32768 && out[2] == 0, "ADPCM: shift 0, filter 0");
    // Filter 1 predicts 60/64 of the previous sample.
    Spu2::u8 predicted[16] = {0x1C};
    older = 0;
    old = 64;
    Spu2::DecodeBlock(predicted, out, &older, &old);
    Check(out[0] == 60, "ADPCM: filter 1 predicts from the previous sample");

    // A voice looping one block of 4096s, at full volume once its attack is done.
    Spu2 spu;
    Spu2::u8 loop[16] = {0x00, 0x07};
    for (int i = 2; i < 16; ++i) loop[i] = 0x11;
    spu.Write(0x5000, loop, 16);
    std::vector<Spu2::s16> heard;
    spu.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16* frames, Spu2::u32 count) { heard.assign(frames, frames + 2 * count); });
    spu.SetAddr(0x2000, 0x5000);                    // SSA, voice 0 of core 0
    spu.SetParam(0x0000, 0x3FFF);                   // VOLL
    spu.SetParam(0x0100, 0x3FFF);                   // VOLR
    spu.SetParam(0x0200, 0x1000);                   // pitch: 48 kHz
    spu.SetParam(0x0300, 0x000F);                   // ADSR1: fastest attack, full sustain
    spu.SetParam(0x0400, 0x1FC0);                   // ADSR2: sustain holds
    spu.SetSwitch(0x1800, 1);                       // VMIXL
    spu.SetSwitch(0x1A00, 1);                       // VMIXR
    spu.SetSwitch(0x1500, 1);                       // KON
    auto none = [](Spu2::u32) {};
    spu.Advance(1000, none);
    spu.Advance(2000, none);                        // 48 samples
    Check(heard.size() == 96, "SPU2: a millisecond is 48 stereo frames");
    Check(heard.size() == 96 && heard[90] > 3500 && heard[90] < 4200 && heard[91] == heard[90],
          "SPU2: a voice sounds at its volume");
    Check(spu.GetSwitch(0x1700) & 1, "SPU2: ENDX after the loop's end");
    Check(spu.GetParam(0x0500) == 0x7FFF, "SPU2: ENVX after the attack");
    // A sweep: VOLL 0xA020 (linear, decreasing, rate 0x20 - a step of 64 a
    // sample) fades the voice from where it was to nothing in about 512
    // samples; VOLR stays. Burnout 3 quiets the voices it leaves running so:
    // played at full volume instead, a race's twenty of them clipped.
    spu.SetParam(0x0000, 0xA020);
    spu.Advance(3000, none);                        // 48 samples on
    const int fading = heard[90];
    spu.Advance(15000, none);                       // 576 more
    Check(fading > 2500 && fading < heard[91], "SPU2: a decreasing sweep lowers the volume from where it was");
    Check(heard[2 * 575] == 0 && heard[2 * 575 + 1] > 3500, "SPU2: the sweep reaches silence, the other side plays on");
    Check(spu.GetParam(0x0600) == 0, "SPU2: VOLXL, the current volume, is the sweep's");

    // Wet-only voices need their capture buffers even with reverb disabled.
    // Burnout 3 DMA-reads this mix to process the player's engine sound.
    Spu2 captured;
    captured.Write(0x5000, loop, 16);
    std::vector<Spu2::s16> capture_output;
    captured.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16* frames, Spu2::u32 count) { capture_output.assign(frames, frames + 2 * count); });
    captured.SetAddr(0x2000, 0x5000);
    captured.SetParam(0x0000, 0x3FFF);
    captured.SetParam(0x0100, 0x3FFF);
    captured.SetParam(0x0200, 0x1000);
    captured.SetParam(0x0300, 0x000F);
    captured.SetParam(0x0400, 0x1FC0);
    captured.SetSwitch(0x1900, 1);
    captured.SetSwitch(0x1B00, 1);
    captured.SetSwitch(0x1500, 1);
    captured.SetAddr(0x1F00, 0x2820);
    captured.SetAddr(0x1F01, 0x2820);
    captured.SetCoreAttr(0x04, 1);
    captured.SetCoreAttr(0x05, 1);
    unsigned capture_irqs = 0;
    auto capture_irq = [&](Spu2::u32 core) { capture_irqs |= 1u << core; };
    captured.Advance(1000, capture_irq);
    captured.Advance(2000, capture_irq);
    auto capture_sample = [&](unsigned address) {
        Spu2::u8 bytes[2]; captured.Read(address, bytes, 2);
        return int(Spu2::s16(unsigned(bytes[0]) | unsigned(bytes[1]) << 8));
    };
    Check(capture_sample(0x2800 + 94) > 3500 && capture_sample(0x2C00 + 94) > 3500,
          "SPU2: wet capture is written at 48 kHz without audible reverb");
    Check(capture_sample(0x2000 + 94) == 0 && capture_sample(0x2400 + 94) == 0 &&
          capture_output.back() == 0, "SPU2: a wet-only voice does not leak into the dry output");
    Check(capture_irqs == 3, "SPU2: both cores see a capture-buffer write at their IRQA");
    captured.Advance(12000, none);                  // Fill the complete ring before fading.
    captured.SetParam(0x0000, 0);
    captured.SetParam(0x0100, 0);
    captured.Advance(14000, none);                  // 624 samples total: wrapped at 512
    Check(capture_sample(0x2800 + 94) == 0 && capture_sample(0x2C00 + 94) == 0 &&
          capture_sample(0x2800 + 400) > 3500,
          "SPU2: 512-sample captures wrap and retain the unoverwritten part");
    // Voice 1 and 3 taps are before voice volume and mix routing.
    captured.SetAddr(0x2002, 0x5000);
    captured.SetParam(0x0202, 0x1000);
    captured.SetParam(0x0302, 0x000F);
    captured.SetParam(0x0402, 0x1FC0);
    captured.SetSwitch(0x1500, 2);
    captured.Advance(15000, none);
    Check(capture_sample(0x0800 + 300) > 3500,
          "SPU2: the raw voice-1 tap captures post-envelope audio at zero volume");

    // B3ROUTE returns planar, signed PCM to core 1's input RAM. BVOL is
    // signed 16-bit (unlike a voice volume's signed 15-bit fixed mode).
    Spu2 pcm;
    std::vector<Spu2::s16> pcm_output;
    pcm.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16* frames, Spu2::u32 count) { pcm_output.assign(frames, frames + 2 * count); });
    std::vector<Spu2::u8> pcm_data(0x800);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 512; ++i) {
        pcm_data[i*2] = 0x10; pcm_data[i*2+1] = 0x27;     // left: +10000
        pcm_data[0x400+i*2] = 0xF0; pcm_data[0x401+i*2] = 0xD8; // right: -10000
    }
    pcm.Write(0x4800, pcm_data.data(), unsigned(pcm_data.size()));
    pcm.SetParam(0x0801, 0x0C0);                   // PCM directly to both speakers
    pcm.SetParam(0x0F81, 0x7FFF);
    pcm.SetParam(0x1081, 0x4000);
    pcm.Advance(1000, none); pcm.Advance(2000, none);
    Check(pcm_output[90] > 9900 && pcm_output[90] < 10000 &&
          pcm_output[91] >= -5000 && pcm_output[91] < -4900,
          "SPU2: planar PCM input plays at independent signed 16-bit volumes");
    Check(pcm.GetParam(0x0801) == 0x0C0 && pcm.GetParam(0x0F81) == 0x7FFF &&
          pcm.GetParam(0x1081) == 0x4000, "SPU2: input parameters read back");
    pcm.SetParam(0x0801, 0x040);                   // gate off only the left input
    pcm.Advance(3000, none);
    Check(pcm_output[90] == 0 && pcm_output[91] < -4900,
          "SPU2: MMIX gates PCM separately on each side");
    pcm.SetParam(0x0801, 0x0C0);
    pcm.SetParam(0x0F81, 0x8000);                  // negative unity, not a sweep
    pcm.SetParam(0x1081, 0);
    pcm.Advance(4000, none);
    Check(pcm_output[90] < -9900 && pcm_output[91] == 0,
          "SPU2: signed PCM volume can invert or silence the input");
    pcm.Advance(15000, none);                     // crosses the 512-sample ring
    Check(pcm_output[900] < -9900 && pcm_output[901] == 0,
          "SPU2: PCM input wraps at 512 samples");

    // Host engine gain changes only returned PCM, with a 5 ms ramp. The
    // guest's samples and volume registers remain untouched.
    pcm.SetParam(0x0F81, 0x7FFF);
    pcm.SetParam(0x1081, 0x7FFF);
    pcm.Advance(16000, none);
    const int unity_left = pcm_output[90], unity_right = pcm_output[91];
    pcm.SetInputVolume(1, 50);
    pcm.Advance(25000, none);
    Check(pcm_output[700] >= 4990 && pcm_output[700] <= 5000 &&
          pcm_output[701] >= -5000 && pcm_output[701] <= -4990,
          "SPU2: host PCM gain halves both channels after the ramp");
    pcm.SetInputVolume(1, 0);
    pcm.Advance(35000, none);
    Check(pcm_output[0] > 0 && pcm_output[700] == 0 && pcm_output[701] == 0,
          "SPU2: gain fades smoothly to silence");
    pcm.SetInputVolume(1, 200);
    pcm.Advance(45000, none);
    Check(pcm_output[700] >= 19980 && pcm_output[700] <= 20000,
          "SPU2: host PCM gain can boost to 200 percent");
    pcm.SetInputVolume(1, 100);
    pcm.Advance(55000, none);
    Check(pcm_output[700] == unity_left && pcm_output[701] == unity_right,
          "SPU2: 100 percent preserves the original PCM exactly");
    Spu2::u8 retained[2] = {};
    pcm.Read(0x4800, retained, 2);
    Check(retained[0] == 0x10 && retained[1] == 0x27 &&
          pcm.GetParam(0x0F81) == 0x7FFF,
          "SPU2: host gain preserves guest input RAM and BVOL");

    // Voices (traffic/effects/music) remain audible with player PCM muted.
    Spu2::u8 traffic[16] = {0x00, 0x07};
    for (int i = 2; i < 16; ++i) traffic[i] = 0x11;
    pcm.Write(0x5000, traffic, 16);
    pcm.SetAddr(0x2001, 0x5000);
    pcm.SetParam(0x0001, 0x3FFF);
    pcm.SetParam(0x0101, 0x3FFF);
    pcm.SetParam(0x0201, 0x1000);
    pcm.SetParam(0x0301, 0x000F);
    pcm.SetParam(0x0401, 0x1FC0);
    pcm.SetParam(0x0801, 0x0CC0);
    pcm.SetSwitch(0x1801, 1);
    pcm.SetSwitch(0x1A01, 1);
    pcm.SetSwitch(0x1501, 1);
    pcm.SetInputVolume(1, 0);
    pcm.Advance(70000, none);
    Check(pcm_output[1000] > 3500 && pcm_output[1001] > 3500,
          "SPU2: PCM mute does not mute the other ADPCM voices");

    // The reverb: one loud sample sent only to it (VMIXEL/VMIXER, not the dry
    // mix) comes out later, and keeps coming out after the voice has ended.
    Spu2 wet;
    Spu2::u8 burst[16] = {0x00, 0x01};              // loop end, no repeat: one block, then silence
    for (int i = 2; i < 16; ++i) burst[i] = 0x77;   // 28 loud samples (the envelope rises through them)
    wet.Write(0x5000, burst, 16);
    std::vector<Spu2::s16> tail;
    wet.SetOutput([&](const Spu2::s16* frames, Spu2::u32 count) { tail.assign(frames, frames + 2 * count); });
    wet.SetAddr(0x2000, 0x5000);
    wet.SetParam(0x0000, 0x3FFF);
    wet.SetParam(0x0100, 0x3FFF);
    wet.SetParam(0x0200, 0x1000);
    wet.SetParam(0x0300, 0x000F);
    wet.SetParam(0x0400, 0x1FC0);
    wet.SetSwitch(0x1900, 1);                       // VMIXEL
    wet.SetSwitch(0x1B00, 1);                       // VMIXER
    Check(wet.SetEffectAttr(0, 0x101, 0x3FFF, 0x3FFF, 0, 0) == 0, "SPU2: the Room preset, its work area cleared");
    wet.SetCoreAttr(0x2, 1);                        // SD_CORE_EFFECT_ENABLE
    wet.SetSwitch(0x1500, 1);
    wet.Advance(1000, none);
    wet.Advance(201000, none);                      // 200 ms
    int loud_late = 0;
    for (std::size_t i = 2 * 4800; i < tail.size(); ++i) loud_late += std::abs(int(tail[i])) > 8;
    Check(tail.size() == 2 * 9600 && tail[0] == 0, "SPU2: nothing dry");
    Check(loud_late > 100, "SPU2: the reverb's tail, long after the sound ended");
    Check(wet.SetEffectAttr(0, 10, 0, 0, 0, 0) == -1, "SPU2: no eleventh preset");
}

// Two overlays loaded at the same address: a call runs the function of the one
// whose code is in memory, and FlushCache makes a call look again.
int g_overlay_ran = 0;
void OverlayA(lifted::Context&) { g_overlay_ran = 1; }
void OverlayB(lifted::Context&) { g_overlay_ran = 2; }

void OverlaysRunWhatIsLoaded() {
    static const ps2host::FunctionEntry a[] = {{0x00500000u, OverlayA, "a", 16u}};
    static const ps2host::FunctionEntry b[] = {{0x00500000u, OverlayB, "b", 16u}};
    static const u32 a_checks[] = {0x11111111u, 0x22222222u, 0x33333333u, 0x44444444u};
    static const u32 b_checks[] = {0x55555555u, 0x66666666u, 0x77777777u, 0x88888888u};
    static const ps2host::OverlayEntry overlays[] = {
        {"a", 0x00500000u, 0x00500100u, a, 1, a_checks},
        {"b", 0x00500000u, 0x00500100u, b, 1, b_checks},
    };
    ps2host::RegisterOverlays(overlays, 2);
    ps2host::Memory& m = ps2host::GuestMemory();
    lifted::Context c{};
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) m.Write(0x00500000u + 4 * i, b_checks[i], 4);
    ps2host::CodeChanged();
    ps2host::Dispatch(c, 0x00500000u);
    Check(g_overlay_ran == 2, "overlays: the loaded one's function runs");
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) m.Write(0x00500000u + 4 * i, a_checks[i], 4);
    ps2host::CodeChanged();
    ps2host::Dispatch(c, 0x00500000u);
    Check(g_overlay_ran == 1, "overlays: another loaded over it, and flushed: its function runs");
    m.Write(0x00500000u, 0u, 4);
    ps2host::CodeChanged();
    bool refused = false;
    try {
        ps2host::Dispatch(c, 0x00500000u);
    } catch (const ps2host::Unimplemented&) {
        refused = true;
    }
    Check(refused, "overlays: code neither overlay's is not run as either");
    ps2host::RegisterOverlays(nullptr, 0);
}

int main() {
    OverlaysRunWhatIsLoaded();
    MirrorsReachTheSameRam();
    LoadsExtendAsTheEeDoes();
    OutsideMemoryFaults();
    ScratchpadAndHooks();
    BiosIsReadOnly();
    Kseg1ReachesDeviceRegisters();
    DiscFindsFilesByPath();
    WideWritesReachEveryWordsHook();
    VifSkipsDataAndAppliesMaskPath3();
    DmaChainsAreWalked();
    GsLayoutsArePermutations();
    GsDrawsASprite();
    GsFogsTowardsFogcol();
    GsLoadsACsm2Clut();
    Path3GoesOneGroupPerWindow();
    GsKeepsAFlatDepthExact();
    GsFillsTopLeft();
    GsTakesImagesInBlocks();
    GsTakesRegisterPacketsInBlocks();
    TexturePackNamesAsPcsx2();
#if PS2HOST_VULKAN
    GpuMemorySwizzlesAsTheGs();
    GpuScaledColourTransfersAsTheGs();
    GpuDecodesTexturesAsTheGs();
#endif
    VifRunsMicroprogramsOnAVu();
    MemoryCardKeepsSaves();
    VuLanesAreTheModel();
    VuCompiledIsTheInterpreter();
    VuFastIsTheExactButFlags();
    VuTimingIsVisible();
    VuFlagsOfAResultIntoVf0();
    VuMaxKeepsADenormal();
    MmiLanesAreScalar();
    IpuDecodesAndRetriesCleanly();
    IopInstructionsMatchTheR5900();
    SpuDecodesAdpcmAndPlaysAVoice();
    SpuPlaysItsSoundDataInput();
    SpuInputInterruptsAtEachHalf();
    SpuReverbHasNoImage();
    SpuInterpolatesAsTheHardware();
    SpuRoutesCore0ThroughCore1();
    std::printf(g_failures ? "host tests: %d failed\n" : "host tests: all passed\n", g_failures);
    return g_failures ? EXIT_FAILURE : EXIT_SUCCESS;
}
```

`ps2decomp/analysis.py`:

```py
"""Code discovery for a stripped PS2 executable.

The retail Burnout 3 binary is one flat PROGBITS blob: no symbol table, and no
section headers marking where code stops and read-only data begins.  Everything
about the layout therefore has to be recovered by analysis.

The approach here is deliberately conservative, in the order that produces the
fewest false positives:

1. **Call-target harvesting.**  Every `jal` in the image names a function entry
   directly.  A `jal` that lands inside the image is near-proof of a function,
   because the compiler only emits it for real call sites.
2. **Recursive traversal.**  Starting from the ELF entry point and every
   harvested call target, walk the control-flow graph, following branches and
   jumps, and stop at returns.  This marks bytes that are *provably* reachable
   code rather than bytes that merely decode as code.
3. **Prologue scanning.**  In the gaps, look for the conventional frame setup
   (`addiu $sp, $sp, -N`) to catch functions only reached through function
   pointers - vtables, jump tables, and callback tables, which a 2004 C++ game
   uses heavily.
4. **Data classification.**  Whatever is left is scored: runs that decode poorly,
   or that look like pointers, floats, or strings, are recorded as data.

Each stage records *why* an address was classified, so the results stay
auditable instead of being an opaque guess.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
import collections
import dataclasses
import struct

from .r5900 import DISASM, Flags, GPR

# Confidence levels attached to each discovered function.
CONF_ENTRY = "entry"          # the ELF entry point
CONF_CALLED = "called"        # at least one direct jal targets it
CONF_PROLOGUE = "prologue"    # found by frame-setup pattern
CONF_POINTER = "pointer"      # referenced by a plausible pointer word


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Function:
    """A discovered function: a half-open address range plus provenance."""

    start: int
    end: int = 0
    confidence: str = CONF_PROLOGUE
    callers: set = dataclasses.field(default_factory=set)
    calls: set = dataclasses.field(default_factory=set)
    instruction_count: int = 0
    has_return: bool = False
    uses_vu: bool = False
    name: str = ""

    @property
    def size(self) -> int:
        return max(0, self.end - self.start)

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        return self.name or ("func_%08X" % self.start)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Region:
    """A classified span of the image."""

    start: int
    end: int
    kind: str  # "code" | "data" | "unknown"

    @property
    def size(self) -> int:
        return self.end - self.start


class ImageAnalyzer:
    """Recovers functions and code/data boundaries from a flat loaded image."""

    def __init__(self, data: bytes, base_addr: int, entry_point: int = 0) -> None:
        self.data = data
        self.base = base_addr
        self.end = base_addr + len(data)
        self.entry_point = entry_point
        self.words = struct.unpack("<%dI" % (len(data) // 4), data[: (len(data) // 4) * 4])
        self.functions: dict = {}
        self.code_bytes = bytearray(len(data))  # 1 where traversal proved code
        self.call_sites: dict = collections.defaultdict(set)
        self.case_targets: set = set()    # labels reached through switch jump tables
        self.stats = collections.Counter()

    # -- address helpers ----------------------------------------------

    def contains(self, addr: int) -> bool:
        return self.base <= addr < self.end

    def word_at(self, addr: int) -> int:
        if not self.contains(addr) or (addr - self.base) % 4:
            return 0
        return self.words[(addr - self.base) // 4]

    def _index(self, addr: int) -> int:
        return addr - self.base

    # -- stage 1: harvest direct call targets --------------------------

    def harvest_call_targets(self) -> int:
        """Scan every aligned word for `jal` and record its target.

        This deliberately scans the whole image rather than only known code: a
        `jal` encoding appearing inside genuine data is rare, and the traversal
        stage discards targets that do not hold sane code.
        """
        found = 0
        for i, word in enumerate(self.words):
            if (word >> 26) != 0x03:  # jal
                continue
            addr = self.base + i * 4
            target = ((addr + 4) & 0xF0000000) | ((word & 0x03FFFFFF) << 2)
            if not self.contains(target):
                continue
            self.call_sites[target].add(addr)
            found += 1
        return found

    # -- stage 2: recursive control-flow traversal ---------------------

    def _looks_like_code(self, addr: int, probe: int = 8, called: bool = False) -> bool:
        """Cheap sanity check that `addr` begins a decodable instruction run.

        Decoding successfully is not enough on its own: a zero word decodes as a
        perfectly valid `nop`, so a run of zeroes in read-only data passes any
        test that only asks "does this decode?".  Real code therefore also has to
        carry some actual work - at least two non-`nop` instructions, and not be
        mostly padding.
        """
        valid = 0
        meaningful = 0
        for k in range(probe):
            a = addr + k * 4
            if not self.contains(a):
                break
            ins = DISASM.decode(self.word_at(a), a)
            if not ins.is_valid:
                return False
            valid += 1
            if not ins.is_nop:
                meaningful += 1
            if ins.ends_block:
                # The delay slot executes too, and is often the whole body: a getter
                # is `jr $ra; lw $v0, 8($a0)`. Not counting it rejected 424 call
                # targets - one of them called from 866 sites - as "not code".
                # An empty delay slot counts for nothing either way: it is neither
                # work nor padding, and counting it as padding tipped 37 real
                # entries over the padding ratio.
                slot = a + 4
                if ins.has_delay_slot and self.contains(slot):
                    slot_ins = DISASM.decode(self.word_at(slot), slot)
                    if not slot_ins.is_valid:
                        return False
                    if not slot_ins.is_nop:
                        valid += 1
                        meaningful += 1
                break
        if called and valid == 1 and meaningful == 1:
            # A `jal` target that is just `jr $ra; nop` or `j elsewhere; nop` is an
            # empty function or a thunk. Data that happens to decode that way is
            # not what a call instruction points at.
            first = DISASM.decode(self.word_at(addr), addr)
            if first.is_return or first.mnemonic in ("j", "b"):
                return True
        if valid < 2 or meaningful < 2:
            return False
        # Padding-dominated windows are data, not a function body.
        return meaningful * 2 > valid

    def traverse(self, start: int, func: Function) -> set:
        """Walk one function's control-flow graph, marking reachable bytes.

        Returns the set of addresses proven to belong to this function, which the
        caller turns into an extent.  The traversal itself must not decide the
        extent: a tail jump or a shared epilogue can land far away, and treating
        the furthest address reached as the end merges everything in between into
        one enormous bogus function.
        """
        queue = collections.deque([start])
        seen = set()
        max_addr = start
        while queue:
            addr = queue.popleft()
            while True:
                if not self.contains(addr) or addr in seen:
                    break
                seen.add(addr)
                idx = self._index(addr)
                ins = DISASM.decode(self.words[idx // 4], addr)
                if not ins.is_valid:
                    break
                self.code_bytes[idx : idx + 4] = b"\x01\x01\x01\x01"
                func.instruction_count += 1
                if addr > max_addr:
                    max_addr = addr
                if ins.mnemonic.startswith("v") or ins.mnemonic in ("qmfc2", "qmtc2"):
                    func.uses_vu = True

                # The delay slot always executes, so claim it before branching.
                if ins.has_delay_slot:
                    slot = addr + 4
                    if self.contains(slot):
                        self.code_bytes[self._index(slot) : self._index(slot) + 4] = b"\x01\x01\x01\x01"
                        seen.add(slot)
                        if slot > max_addr:
                            max_addr = slot

                if ins.is_call:
                    if ins.target >= 0 and self.contains(ins.target):
                        func.calls.add(ins.target)
                elif ins.target >= 0 and self.contains(ins.target):
                    # Intra-function branch or tail jump: queue the target.
                    queue.append(ins.target)

                if ins.mnemonic == "jr" and ins.rs != 31:
                    # A switch: its cases are this function's own code.
                    targets = self.jump_table(addr, ins.rs)
                    if targets:
                        queue.extend(targets)
                        self.case_targets.update(targets)
                        self.stats["jump_tables"] += 1

                if ins.is_return:
                    func.has_return = True
                    break
                if ins.ends_block:
                    break

                addr += 8 if ins.has_delay_slot else 4
        return seen

    # How far back from a `jr` its table and bound are looked for.
    JUMP_TABLE_WINDOW = 32
    MAX_CASES = 1024

    def jump_table(self, jr_addr: int, register: int):
        """The targets of the switch that ends in `jr register`, or None.

        GCC's switch on the R5900 bounds the index, then loads the case's
        address from a table and jumps to it:

            sltiu $at, $i, N;  beq $at, $zero, default; ...
            lui $t, %hi(T);  sll $i, $i, 2;  addiu $t, $t, %lo(T)
            addu $i, $i, $t;  lw $r, 0($i);  jr $r

        Walking back from the `jr` finds the load, the sum, the table's two
        halves and the bound; the table's N words are the cases. Without the
        bound the table's length is unknown, and nothing is claimed.
        """
        load = index = low = table = bound = None
        register_of_sum = register
        addr = jr_addr - 4
        for _ in range(self.JUMP_TABLE_WINDOW):
            if not self.contains(addr):
                break
            ins = DISASM.decode(self.word_at(addr), addr)
            if not ins.is_valid or ins.is_call:
                break
            m = ins.mnemonic
            if load is None:
                if m == "lw" and ins.rt == register_of_sum:
                    load = ins
                    register_of_sum = ins.rs
            elif table is None:
                if index is None and m in ("addu", "daddu") and ins.rd == register_of_sum:
                    index = (ins.rs, ins.rt)
                elif index and low is None and m == "addiu" and ins.rt in index:
                    # The lui is the addiu's source: GCC adds in place
                    # (`addiu $t, $t, lo`), CodeWarrior into another register
                    # (`lui $v0, hi; addiu $v1, $v0, lo; sll $v0, $i, 2`).
                    low = (ins.rs, ins.imm)
                elif m == "lui" and ((low and ins.rt == low[0]) or (index and not low and ins.rt in index)):
                    # The table's low half is in the addiu, or else in the load's
                    # own offset: `lui $t, hi; addu $t, $t, $i; lw $r, lo($t)`.
                    table = ((ins.imm << 16) + (low[1] if low else 0) + load.imm) & 0xFFFFFFFF
            elif m == "sltiu":
                bound = ins.imm
                break
            addr -= 4
        if table is None or not bound or bound > self.MAX_CASES:
            return None
        targets = []
        for i in range(bound):
            target = self.word_at(table + 4 * i)
            if not self.contains(target) or target % 4:
                return None             # not a table of code addresses after all
            targets.append(target)
        return targets

    # A function's pieces outside its range add up to no more than this; more is
    # a closure that leaked into other code. Burnout 3's largest, 0x00186850,
    # has 54 KB of them (a state machine's cases).
    MAX_CHUNK_BYTES = 0x10000

    def chunks(self, start: int, end: int, entries) -> list:
        """The function's out-of-line pieces: [(start, end)] outside [start, end).

        The compiler places a function's cold blocks after the hot code, among
        other functions' cold blocks, and reaches them by branch. Following the
        function's branches - conditional, `b` and switch tables, but not `j`,
        which is how it tail-calls, and stopping at the entries of other
        functions - gives every block that is its own. Those outside its range
        are its chunks, each ending in a transfer.
        """
        seen = self.closure(start, entries)
        if seen is None:
            return []                           # not code after all: claim nothing
        runs = []
        for a in sorted(x for x in seen if not (start <= x < end)):
            if runs and a == runs[-1][1]:
                runs[-1][1] = a + 4
            else:
                runs.append([a, a + 4])
        if sum(e - s for s, e in runs) > self.MAX_CHUNK_BYTES:
            return []
        return [(s, e) for s, e in runs]

    def closure(self, start: int, entries):
        """Every instruction a function reaches by its own branches (as
        `chunks` follows them), or None when that runs into what is not code."""
        seen = set()
        queue = [start]
        while queue:
            addr = queue.pop()
            while self.contains(addr) and addr not in seen:
                if addr != start and addr in entries:
                    break
                ins = DISASM.decode(self.word_at(addr), addr)
                if not ins.is_valid:
                    return None
                seen.add(addr)
                if ins.has_delay_slot:
                    seen.add(addr + 4)
                    if not ins.is_call and ins.mnemonic not in ("jr", "jalr", "j") and ins.target >= 0:
                        queue.append(ins.target)
                    if ins.mnemonic == "jr" and ins.rs != 31:
                        queue.extend(self.jump_table(addr, ins.rs) or [])
                if ins.is_return or ins.ends_block:
                    break
                addr += 8 if ins.has_delay_slot else 4
        return seen

    # -- stage 2b: pointer-table targets -------------------------------

    def _is_prologue(self, addr: int) -> bool:
        """True when `addr` holds `addiu $sp, $sp, -N`, or the large frame's
        `lui $at, 0xFFFF; ori $at, $at, lo; addu $sp, $sp, $at` (CodeWarrior's,
        past 32 KB: Mister Mosquito's task entries)."""
        word = self.word_at(addr)
        if (word & self._PROLOGUE_MASK) == self._PROLOGUE_MATCH and bool(word & 0x8000):
            return True
        return self._is_large_prologue(addr)

    def _is_large_prologue(self, addr: int) -> bool:
        if not (self.contains(addr) and self.contains(addr + 8)):
            return False
        return (self.word_at(addr) == 0x3C01FFFF and (self.word_at(addr + 4) >> 16) == 0x3421
                and self.word_at(addr + 8) in (0x03A1E821, 0x03A1E82D))

    def _follows_terminator(self, addr: int) -> bool:
        """True when the instruction two slots back ends a function.

        A function entry is normally preceded by the previous function's final
        delay slot, so the terminating `jr`/`j` sits two words back.
        """
        # Alignment padding (a few `nop`s) may come between: Burnout 3's
        # 0x002A6B80, a leaf reached only through a pointer, follows two, and was
        # missed - its switch's cases taken for functions instead.
        for padding in range(0, self.MAX_PADDING_WORDS + 1):
            terminator = addr - 8 - 4 * padding
            if not self.contains(terminator):
                return False
            if padding and self.word_at(addr - 4 * padding) != 0:
                return False                    # not padding: something else is there
            if DISASM.decode(self.word_at(terminator), terminator).ends_block:
                return True
        return False

    def harvest_pointer_targets(self) -> list:
        """Find function entries referenced only by pointer tables.

        Virtual calls and callback tables never produce a `jal`, so those targets
        are invisible to call-target harvesting.  Every aligned word that points
        at a plausible entry inside the image is considered, then filtered hard -
        a word has to land on a stack prologue or just past another function's
        terminator to be accepted, which is what keeps ordinary data from
        registering as code.
        """
        candidates = set()
        for word in self.words:
            if not self.contains(word) or word % 4:
                continue
            candidates.add(word)

        accepted = []
        for addr in sorted(candidates):
            if addr in self.functions:
                continue
            if not (self._is_prologue(addr) or self._follows_terminator(addr)):
                continue
            if not self._looks_like_code(addr):
                continue
            accepted.append(addr)
        return accepted

    # Alignment padding between functions is a short run of `nop`; bridging that
    # much keeps a function whole without letting a real gap merge two of them.
    MAX_PADDING_WORDS = 4

    def extent_from(self, start: int, visited: set) -> int:
        """Turn a traversal's visited set into a contiguous end address.

        The body of a function is the unbroken run of its own instructions. A gap
        means the run has ended - the next bytes belong to something else - except
        when the gap is only `nop` padding inserted for alignment.
        """
        addr = start
        end = start
        while self.contains(addr):
            if addr in visited:
                addr += 4
                end = addr
                continue
            # Look past a short run of nops for more of this function.
            probe = addr
            padding = 0
            while (
                self.contains(probe)
                and padding < self.MAX_PADDING_WORDS
                and self.word_at(probe) == 0
                and probe not in visited
            ):
                probe += 4
                padding += 1
            if padding and self.contains(probe) and probe in visited:
                addr = probe
                continue
            break
        return max(end, start + 4)

    # -- stage 3: prologue scan ----------------------------------------

    _PROLOGUE_MASK = 0xFFFF0000
    # addiu $sp, $sp, -N  ->  op=0x09 rs=29 rt=29, negative immediate
    _PROLOGUE_MATCH = (0x09 << 26) | (29 << 21) | (29 << 16)

    def scan_prologues(self) -> list:
        """Find `addiu $sp, $sp, -N` in spans not already proven to be code."""
        candidates = []
        # Skip only what lies inside a known function. Bytes merely *reached* by
        # another function's traversal - the target of a tail jump or a shared
        # epilogue - can still begin a function of their own; skipping every
        # visited byte lost 37 functions, one of them already verified, when
        # better call-target discovery made more traversals reach them.
        extents = sorted((f.start, f.end) for f in self.functions.values())
        starts = [start for start, _end in extents]

        def inside_function(addr):
            index = bisect.bisect_right(starts, addr) - 1
            return index >= 0 and extents[index][0] <= addr < extents[index][1]

        for i, word in enumerate(self.words):
            if word == 0x3C01FFFF:              # lui $at, 0xFFFF: perhaps a large frame
                if not self._is_large_prologue(self.base + i * 4):
                    continue
            elif (word & self._PROLOGUE_MASK) != self._PROLOGUE_MATCH:
                continue
            elif not (word & 0x8000):  # immediate must be negative
                continue
            addr = self.base + i * 4
            if inside_function(addr):
                continue
            if not self._looks_like_code(addr):
                continue
            candidates.append(self._scheduled_entry(addr, inside_function))
        return candidates

    # How far back from a frame's setup the entry is looked for. The walk stops
    # at the first branch, jump or padding anyway; four left out 0x001ADF00 of
    # Resident Evil Outbreak, five instructions above its `addiu $sp`, called
    # only from an overlay - whose port stopped there entering a room.
    MAX_SCHEDULED = 16

    def _scheduled_entry(self, addr: int, inside_function) -> int:
        """The entry of a function whose frame is set up at `addr`.

        CodeWarrior schedules an instruction or two above the `addiu $sp`: a
        `lui` of a global's address (`lui $v0, 0x21; addiu $sp, $sp, -0x30;
        lw $v1, -0x6208($v0)`, Resident Evil Outbreak's 0x0011B920), an `srl`.
        Taking the frame setup for the entry left them out, and the function
        read a register it never set. Plain instructions between the previous
        function's last delay slot and the setup are reachable only as this
        function's start, so it begins there; anything else - a branch, a
        jump, padding, another function's code - and it begins at `addr`.
        """
        entry = addr
        for _step in range(self.MAX_SCHEDULED + 1):
            # After a terminator's delay slot, or the padding after it (0x00106880:
            # `lui $v0, 0x21` after a `nop`, the `addiu $sp` at 0x00106884).
            if self._follows_terminator(entry):
                return entry
            before = entry - 4
            if not self.contains(before) or inside_function(before):
                return addr
            word = self.word_at(before)
            ins = DISASM.decode(word, before)
            if word == 0 or ins.is_branch or ins.is_jump or ins.is_return or ins.has_delay_slot:
                return addr
            entry = before
        return addr

    # -- driver ---------------------------------------------------------

    def run(self) -> None:
        self.stats["jal_sites"] = self.harvest_call_targets()
        self.stats["call_targets"] = len(self.call_sites)

        # Seed with the entry point and every direct call target.
        seeds = []
        if self.contains(self.entry_point):
            seeds.append((self.entry_point, CONF_ENTRY))
        for target in sorted(self.call_sites):
            seeds.append((target, CONF_CALLED))

        for addr, confidence in seeds:
            if addr in self.functions:
                continue
            if confidence != CONF_ENTRY and not self._looks_like_code(addr, called=True):
                self.stats["rejected_call_targets"] += 1
                continue
            func = Function(start=addr, confidence=confidence)
            func.callers = set(self.call_sites.get(addr, ()))
            self.functions[addr] = func
            visited = self.traverse(addr, func)
            func.end = self.extent_from(addr, visited)
            func.instruction_count = sum(
                1 for a in visited if func.start <= a < func.end
            )

        # Functions reached only through pointer tables emit no jal at all, so
        # harvest plausible pointer targets before falling back to a blind scan.
        for addr in self.harvest_pointer_targets():
            if addr in self.functions:
                continue
            func = Function(start=addr, confidence=CONF_POINTER)
            visited = self.traverse(addr, func)
            # A pointer-table entry is a real function - a virtual method or a
            # callback - so it has to return. Without a `jr $ra` the candidate is
            # almost always data that merely decodes: tables of small integers
            # read as instructions on $zero, or pointer arrays pointing at
            # themselves. Requiring a return discards those without needing a
            # hand-maintained list of data ranges.
            # One that opens a stack frame is code all the same: a task's entry
            # never returns (it kills itself, or loops forever).
            if not func.has_return and not self._is_prologue(addr):
                self.stats["pointer_rejected_no_return"] += 1
                continue
            self.functions[addr] = func
            func.end = self.extent_from(addr, visited)
            func.instruction_count = sum(
                1 for a in visited if func.start <= a < func.end
            )
            self.stats["pointer_found"] += 1

        # A final pass catches anything still missing.
        for addr in self.scan_prologues():
            if addr in self.functions:
                continue
            func = Function(start=addr, confidence=CONF_PROLOGUE)
            self.functions[addr] = func
            visited = self.traverse(addr, func)
            func.end = self.extent_from(addr, visited)
            func.instruction_count = sum(
                1 for a in visited if func.start <= a < func.end
            )
            self.stats["prologue_found"] += 1

        # A switch's cases are labels of the function that jumps to them. Their
        # table's words point at code just past a `jr` or `b`, which is what the
        # pointer harvest looks for; 2,258 of Burnout 3's 2,986 pointer-found
        # "functions" were cases. Called ones stay: a `jal` is evidence enough.
        for addr in sorted(self.case_targets):
            func = self.functions.get(addr)
            if func is not None and func.confidence in (CONF_POINTER, CONF_PROLOGUE) and not func.callers:
                del self.functions[addr]
                self.stats["switch_cases_not_functions"] += 1

        self._tighten_bounds()
        self._compute_stats()

    def _tighten_bounds(self) -> None:
        """Clamp each function to end no later than the next function start."""
        starts = sorted(self.functions)
        for i, addr in enumerate(starts):
            func = self.functions[addr]
            limit = starts[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(starts) else self.end
            # Clamp only. The extent already reflects the function's own
            # contiguous code, so growing it here would reintroduce the merging
            # this pass exists to prevent.
            if func.end > limit:
                func.end = limit
            if func.end <= func.start:
                func.end = min(func.start + 4, limit)

    def _compute_stats(self) -> None:
        self.stats["functions"] = len(self.functions)
        self.stats["code_bytes"] = sum(self.code_bytes)
        self.stats["image_bytes"] = len(self.data)
        self.stats["with_return"] = sum(1 for f in self.functions.values() if f.has_return)
        self.stats["uses_vu"] = sum(1 for f in self.functions.values() if f.uses_vu)
        for f in self.functions.values():
            self.stats["conf_" + f.confidence] += 1

    # -- reporting -------------------------------------------------------

    def regions(self) -> list:
        """Collapse the code bitmap into contiguous code/unknown regions."""
        out = []
        start = 0
        current = self.code_bytes[0] if self.code_bytes else 0
        for i in range(1, len(self.code_bytes)):
            if self.code_bytes[i] != current:
                out.append(Region(self.base + start, self.base + i, "code" if current else "unknown"))
                start = i
                current = self.code_bytes[i]
        out.append(
            Region(self.base + start, self.base + len(self.code_bytes), "code" if current else "unknown")
        )
        return out

    def coverage(self) -> float:
        total = len(self.data)
        return (sum(self.code_bytes) / total * 100.0) if total else 0.0

```

`ps2decomp/calls.py`:

```py
"""Which arguments each function reads, for calling it without deriving it.

A derived function that calls one that has not been derived passes it the values
in the argument registers. Only the ones the callee actually reads are part of
the call: a register that merely still holds something is not an argument, and
passing it would make every call site's signature different.

Integer arguments come from structs.argument_use. Float arguments ($f12..$f19)
get the same treatment here: a function reads one if an instruction reads the
register before anything writes it, or passes it on to a callee that reads it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import re
import struct

from .r5900 import DISASM
from .structs import argument_use
from .symexec import FLOAT_ARG_BASE, FLOAT_ARG_REGS

_FLOAT_REGISTER = re.compile(r"\$f(\d+)")


def _float_operands(ins):
    """(read, written) float registers of one instruction."""
    m = ins.mnemonic
    names = [int(n) for op in ins.operands for n in _FLOAT_REGISTER.findall(str(op))]
    if not names:
        return set(), set()
    if m in ("swc1", "mfc1") or m.startswith("c."):
        return set(names), set()
    if m in ("lwc1", "mtc1", "ctc1"):
        return set(), set(names)
    if m.startswith(("adda.", "suba.", "mula.", "madda.", "msuba.")):
        return set(names), set()          # these write the accumulator, not an FPR
    # Arithmetic, moves and conversions: the first operand is the destination.
    return set(names[1:]), {names[0]}


def float_argument_use(database, image, base) -> set:
    """(function, vector index) for every float argument a function reads."""
    functions = {f["addr"]: f for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}
    used = set()
    passes = collections.defaultdict(set)
    for func in functions.values():
        start, end = func["addr"], func["end"]
        original = {reg: FLOAT_ARG_BASE + k for k, reg in enumerate(FLOAT_ARG_REGS)}
        address = start
        while address < end:
            ins = DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, address - base)[0], address)
            sequence = [ins]
            if ins.has_delay_slot and address + 4 < end:
                sequence.insert(0, DISASM.decode(
                    struct.unpack_from("<I", image, address + 4 - base)[0], address + 4))
            for step in sequence:
                if step.is_call or (step.is_jump and step.mnemonic == "j"):
                    target = step.target
                    if target in functions and not (start <= target < end):
                        for reg, index in original.items():
                            passes[(target, index)].add((start, index))
                    if step.is_call:
                        original = {}          # $f0..$f19 are caller-saved
                    continue
                read, written = _float_operands(step)
                for reg in read:
                    if reg in original:
                        used.add((start, original[reg]))
                for reg in written:
                    original.pop(reg, None)
            address += 8 if len(sequence) == 2 else 4
    work = list(used)
    while work:
        slot = work.pop()
        for caller in passes.get(slot, ()):
            if caller not in used:
                used.add(caller)
                work.append(caller)
    return used


class Parameters(dict):
    """{function: argument-vector indices it reads}, plus `preserves_v0`: the
    functions after a call to which $v0 still holds the caller's value, and
    `returns_float`: the functions whose callers read their result from $f0;
    `returns_int`: those whose callers read $v0 after calling them;
    `address_taken`: those a pointer can reach; `preserved`: {function: the
    caller-saved registers it leaves untouched}."""

    preserves_v0 = frozenset()
    returns_float = frozenset()
    returns_int = frozenset()
    address_taken = frozenset()
    preserved = {}
    stack_readers = frozenset()
    sets_v0 = frozenset()


def parameters(database, image, base) -> dict:
    """{function: argument-vector indices it reads}, for every known function.

    Live-in analysis over each function's control flow, to a fixed point over the
    call graph (see live_parameters).
    """
    # An overlay's callees in the executable and the other overlays resident
    # with it (analyze.py's `external_functions`) are analysed with its own:
    # a call to one is a call to a known function.
    if database.get("external_functions"):
        database = dict(database, functions=database["functions"] + database["external_functions"])
    found = Parameters(live_parameters(database, image, base))
    found.preserves_v0 = v0_preserving(database, image, base)
    found.returns_float = float_returning(database, image, base)
    found.returns_int = int_returning(database, image, base)
    found.address_taken = address_taken(database, image, base)
    found.preserved = preserved_registers(database, image, base)
    found.stack_readers = stack_readers(database, image, base)
    found.sets_v0 = v0_setting(database, image, base)
    return found


def address_taken(database, image, base) -> frozenset:
    """Functions whose address a word of the image holds or code builds (the
    analysis's xrefs): reached through a pointer, by callers no scan of call
    sites sees - so int_returning's silence says nothing about them."""
    starts = {f["addr"] for f in database["functions"]}
    words = struct.unpack_from("<%dI" % (len(image) // 4), image, 0)
    taken = {word for word in words if word in starts}
    taken |= {x["to"] for x in database.get("xrefs", ()) if x["to"] in starts}
    return frozenset(taken)


# How far after a call a read of $f0 still counts as reading its result.
_RESULT_WINDOW = 24


def float_returning(database, image, base) -> frozenset:
    """Functions that return a float: some caller reads $f0 after calling them,
    before anything writes it.

    What a function computes into $f0 says nothing on its own - $f0 is also
    every float computation's scratch register - so the evidence is taken where
    the result is used. The scan after a call is straight-line: it stops at a
    branch, a jump, another call or the window's end, which can only miss
    evidence, never invent it. A function that ends by jumping to another hands
    that one's result to its own callers, so the evidence passes down tail calls.
    """
    functions = {f["addr"]: f for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}

    def decode(pc):
        return DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, pc - base)[0], pc)

    found, tails = set(), collections.defaultdict(set)
    for func in functions.values():
        start, end = func["addr"], func["end"]
        for pc in range(start, end, 4):
            ins = decode(pc)
            if ins.is_jump and ins.mnemonic == "j" and ins.target in functions                     and not (start <= ins.target < end):
                tails[start].add(ins.target)
            if not ins.is_call or ins.target not in functions:
                continue
            for after in range(pc + 8, min(end, pc + 8 + 4 * _RESULT_WINDOW), 4):
                step = decode(after)
                if step.is_branch or step.is_jump or step.is_call:
                    break
                read, written = _float_operands(step)
                if 0 in read:
                    found.add(ins.target)
                    break
                if 0 in written:
                    break
    work = list(found)
    while work:
        for target in tails.get(work.pop(), ()):
            if target not in found:
                found.add(target)
                work.append(target)
    return frozenset(found)


def int_returning(database, image, base) -> frozenset:
    """Functions some caller reads $v0 after calling, before anything writes
    it: evidence of a result in $v0, found as float_returning finds a result
    in $f0 (straight-line after the call; it can miss evidence, never invent
    it). Passed down tail calls the same way."""
    from .structs import _read_registers, _written_register

    functions = {f["addr"]: f for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}

    def decode(pc):
        return DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, pc - base)[0], pc)

    found, tails = set(), collections.defaultdict(set)
    for func in functions.values():
        start, end = func["addr"], func["end"]
        for pc in range(start, end, 4):
            ins = decode(pc)
            if ins.is_jump and ins.mnemonic == "j" and ins.target in functions \
                    and not (start <= ins.target < end):
                tails[start].add(ins.target)
            if not ins.is_call or ins.target not in functions:
                continue
            for after in range(pc + 8, min(end, pc + 8 + 4 * _RESULT_WINDOW), 4):
                step = decode(after)
                if 2 in _read_registers(step):
                    found.add(ins.target)
                    break
                if step.is_branch or step.is_jump or step.is_call or _written_register(step) == 2:
                    break
    work = list(found)
    while work:
        for target in tails.get(work.pop(), ()):
            if target not in found:
                found.add(target)
                work.append(target)
    return frozenset(found)


def v0_preserving(database, image, base) -> frozenset:
    """Functions that leave $v0 exactly as the caller had it.

    A function that never writes $v0, and calls only functions that never write it
    either, returns with the caller's $v0 still in place - and callers do rely on
    that, returning a value they set before the call. Treating such a call's $v0 as
    the callee's result made the model return whatever the callee happened to start
    with. A call through a register or a kernel call (which returns in $v0) rules
    a function out; the rest is a fixed point over the call graph.
    """
    from .structs import _written_register

    functions = {f["addr"]: f for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}
    candidates, needs = set(), {}
    for address, func in functions.items():
        writes, callees = False, set()
        for pc in range(func["addr"], func["end"], 4):
            ins = DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, pc - base)[0], pc)
            if _written_register(ins) == 2 or ins.mnemonic in ("syscall", "jalr"):
                writes = True
                break
            if ins.is_call or (ins.is_jump and not ins.is_return and ins.mnemonic != "jr"):
                if not (func["addr"] <= ins.target < func["end"]):
                    callees.add(ins.target)
            elif ins.mnemonic == "jr" and not ins.is_return:
                writes = True                     # a jump table: unknown targets
                break
        if not writes:
            candidates.add(address)
            needs[address] = callees
    preserving = set(candidates)
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for address in list(preserving):
            if not needs[address] <= preserving:
                preserving.discard(address)
                changed = True
    return frozenset(preserving)


def v0_setting(database, image, base) -> frozenset:
    """Functions that write $v0 on every path to their return.

    Any other may hand back the $v0 it was called with - a handler returning a
    value on one path and nothing on another - so a call to it passes the
    caller's $v0 along (paths.Call.v0). A path is followed from the entry
    while $v0 is unwritten: a write ends it (a conditional move does not
    write for sure), as does a call or tail call to a function in the set or a
    kernel call (which returns in $v0); a return, a call through a register, a
    jump table, a branch or jump out of the function to anything else, or
    running off its end means $v0 may come back as it was. Recursion is
    resolved as a greatest fixed point: a path that only returns through
    itself returns through one of its other paths.
    """
    from .structs import _written_register

    functions = {f["addr"]: f for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}

    def decode(pc):
        return DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, pc - base)[0], pc)

    def writes(ins):
        return _written_register(ins) == 2 and ins.mnemonic not in ("movz", "movn")

    def sets(func, setting) -> bool:
        start, end = func["addr"], func["end"]
        seen, work = set(), [start]
        while work:
            pc = work.pop()
            if pc in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(pc)
            if not (start <= pc < end) or pc + 4 > base + len(image):
                return False
            ins = decode(pc)
            if not ins.has_delay_slot:
                if ins.mnemonic == "syscall" or writes(ins):
                    continue
                if ins.is_jump or ins.is_branch:
                    return False
                work.append(pc + 4)
                continue
            if pc + 8 > end:
                return False
            slot = decode(pc + 4)
            slot_writes = writes(slot)
            if ins.is_call:
                if slot_writes:
                    continue
                if ins.mnemonic == "jal" and ins.target in setting:
                    continue
                if ins.mnemonic != "jal":
                    return False                  # through a register
                work.append(pc + 8)
                continue
            if ins.is_return:
                if not slot_writes:
                    return False
                continue
            targets = []
            if ins.is_branch:
                if not slot_writes:
                    targets.append(ins.target)    # taken: the slot runs
                if ins.is_likely or not slot_writes:
                    work.append(pc + 8)           # not taken: a likely one skips it
            elif ins.mnemonic in ("j", "b") or (ins.is_jump and ins.target >= 0):
                if slot_writes:
                    continue
                targets.append(ins.target)
            else:
                return False                      # a jump table
            for target in targets:
                if start <= target < end:
                    work.append(target)
                elif target not in setting:
                    return False                  # a tail call or a chunk
        return True

    setting = set(functions)
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for address in sorted(setting):
            if not sets(functions[address], setting):
                setting.discard(address)
                changed = True
    return frozenset(setting)


# Caller-saved general registers a callee may leave as they were: $v1, $a0-$t7,
# $t8, $t9 ($v0 is v0_preserving's).
PRESERVABLE = (3,) + tuple(range(4, 16)) + (24, 25)

# Instructions that name a general register first and only read it.
_READS_FIRST = frozenset({
    "sb", "sh", "sw", "sd", "sq", "swl", "swr", "sdl", "sdr", "swc1", "sdc1", "sqc2",
    "mtc0", "mtc1", "ctc1", "qmtc2", "ctc2", "mthi", "mtlo", "mthi1", "mtlo1",
    "mtsa", "mtsab", "mtsah", "pmthi", "pmtlo", "pmthl", "jr", "cache", "pref", "sync",
})


def _may_write(ins):
    """The general register an instruction may write, or None. Over-reports
    rather than under: whatever names a register first, other than a store, a
    branch or a move to another unit, is taken to write it."""
    if ins.is_call:
        return 31
    if ins.is_branch or ins.is_jump or ins.mnemonic in _READS_FIRST:
        return None
    from .structs import _NUMBER, _REGISTER
    for operand in ins.operands:
        for name in _REGISTER.findall(str(operand)):
            if name in _NUMBER:
                return _NUMBER[name]
    return None


def preserved_registers(database, image, base) -> dict:
    """{function: the PRESERVABLE registers it leaves as the caller had them}.

    CodeWarrior keeps a value in a caller-saved register across a call to a
    function that never touches it (Resident Evil Outbreak's 0x00190100 holds
    its argument in $t1 across a call to 0x0018F570, and reads it after).
    A register is preserved by a function that writes it nowhere - not in its
    body, its cold chunks, or any function it calls or jumps to. A call through
    a register, a kernel call, a jump table, a branch or a fall-through out of
    the function's known code, or a call into the middle of something, and
    nothing is: a fixed point over the call graph, from the conservative side.
    """
    functions = {f["addr"]: f for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}
    every = frozenset(PRESERVABLE)
    kept, needs = {}, {}
    for address, func in functions.items():
        ranges = [(func["addr"], func["end"])] + [tuple(c) for c in func.get("chunks") or ()]

        def inside(target):
            return any(low <= target < high for low, high in ranges)

        written, callees, unknown = set(), set(), False
        for low, high in ranges:
            last = DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, high - 8 - base)[0], high - 8)
            if not last.ends_block:
                unknown = True                       # runs on past what is known
            for pc in range(low, high, 4):
                ins = DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, pc - base)[0], pc)
                if ins.mnemonic in ("syscall", "jalr") or (ins.mnemonic == "jr" and not ins.is_return):
                    unknown = True
                    break
                register = _may_write(ins)
                if register is not None:
                    written.add(register)
                if (ins.is_call or ins.is_jump or ins.is_branch) and not ins.is_return:
                    if ins.target is None or ins.target < 0:
                        unknown = True
                    elif ins.is_call or not inside(ins.target):
                        if ins.is_branch and not ins.is_call:
                            unknown = True           # a branch out of the function
                        elif ins.target in functions:
                            callees.add(ins.target)
                        else:
                            unknown = True
            if unknown:
                break
        kept[address] = frozenset() if unknown else every - written
        needs[address] = callees
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for address, callees in needs.items():
            value = kept[address]
            for callee in callees:
                value &= kept[callee]
            if value != kept[address]:
                kept[address] = value
                changed = True
    return {address: value for address, value in kept.items() if value}


_LOADS = frozenset({"lb", "lbu", "lh", "lhu", "lw", "lwu", "ld", "lq", "lwl", "lwr", "ldl",
                    "ldr", "lwc1", "ldc1", "lqc2"})


def stack_readers(database, image, base) -> frozenset:
    """Functions that read their caller's frame: arguments past the eighth, which
    EABI passes at 0($sp) and up.

    A load from `$sp` at an offset of at least the function's own frame (its
    `addiu $sp, $sp, -F`), or such an address taken (a va_list), reads above
    it. A function with no frame reads its caller's too through what it calls
    or jumps to. The model keeps a caller's frame symbolic, so a callee reading
    its arguments there read nothing (Resident Evil Outbreak's 0x00135078
    passes a pointer at 0($sp) to 0x00127FC8, which wrote through null).
    """
    functions = {f["addr"]: f for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}
    readers, frameless_calls = set(), {}
    for address, func in functions.items():
        frame, reads, callees = 0, False, set()
        for pc in range(func["addr"], func["end"], 4):
            ins = DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, pc - base)[0], pc)
            if ins.mnemonic in ("addiu", "daddiu") and ins.rs == 29:
                if ins.rt == 29:
                    if ins.imm < 0 and not frame:
                        frame = -ins.imm
                    continue
                if ins.imm >= frame:
                    reads = True
            elif ins.mnemonic in _LOADS and ins.rs == 29 and ins.imm >= frame:
                reads = True
            elif ins.mnemonic in ("daddu", "addu", "or") and 29 in (ins.rs, ins.rt) and not frame:
                if ins.rd != 29:
                    reads = True                 # $sp copied with no frame: its caller's
            if (ins.is_call or ins.is_jump) and ins.target is not None and ins.target >= 0:
                if not func["addr"] <= ins.target < func["end"]:
                    callees.add(ins.target)
        if reads:
            readers.add(address)
        elif not frame:
            frameless_calls[address] = callees
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for address, callees in frameless_calls.items():
            if address not in readers and callees & readers:
                readers.add(address)
                changed = True
    return frozenset(readers)


def scanned_parameters(database, image, base) -> dict:
    """{function: sorted argument-vector indices it reads}, for every known function.

    A function that reads no argument maps to (), so that "takes nothing" and "not
    a function anyone found" stay distinguishable - a jump into the middle of
    some other code is not a call that can be made with no arguments.
    """
    found = {f["addr"]: set() for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}
    for function, index in argument_use(database, image, base):
        found.setdefault(function, set()).add(index)
    for function, index in float_argument_use(database, image, base):
        found.setdefault(function, set()).add(index)
    return {function: tuple(sorted(indices)) for function, indices in found.items()}


# -- liveness ------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The scans above follow each function in address order, so a register written on
# one branch and read after the paths rejoin looks written-before-read, although
# on the other path it is read first. That missed real arguments - a caller set
# $t1 and $t2 for a callee whose analysis said it took five - and every miss
# surfaced as a disagreement, since the call then passed nothing in those
# registers. Live-in analysis over the control-flow graph has no such blind spot.

ALL_ARGUMENTS = (1 << 16) - 1
_INT_INDEX = {reg: index for index, reg in enumerate((4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11))}
_FLOAT_INDEX = {reg: FLOAT_ARG_BASE + k for k, reg in enumerate(FLOAT_ARG_REGS)}


def _effects(ins) -> tuple:
    """(uses, defs) of one instruction, as bitmasks over argument-vector indices."""
    from .structs import _read_registers, _written_register

    uses = defs = 0
    if ins.mnemonic == "syscall":
        # The kernel takes its arguments where a function does: a stub of
        # `addiu $v1, N; syscall; jr $ra` reads them though no instruction
        # names them. Read as none, a caller passing a local's address to
        # ReferThreadStatus or SetOsdConfigParam kept its frame symbolic and
        # read back a slot the kernel had filled (Resident Evil Outbreak, 14
        # functions). How many a service takes is not recorded, so all eight.
        uses |= (1 << FLOAT_ARG_BASE) - 1
    for reg in _read_registers(ins):
        if reg in _INT_INDEX:
            uses |= 1 << _INT_INDEX[reg]
    written = _written_register(ins)
    if ins.mnemonic in ("movz", "movn"):
        # A conditional move keeps the old value when its condition fails: it
        # reads its destination, and kills nothing (Resident Evil Outbreak's
        # 0x00197900 passes on $t0 untouched when its `movz` does not move).
        if written in _INT_INDEX:
            uses |= 1 << _INT_INDEX[written]
        written = None
    if written in _INT_INDEX:
        defs |= 1 << _INT_INDEX[written]
    read, wrote = _float_operands(ins)
    for reg in read:
        if reg in _FLOAT_INDEX:
            uses |= 1 << _FLOAT_INDEX[reg]
    for reg in wrote:
        if reg in _FLOAT_INDEX:
            defs |= 1 << _FLOAT_INDEX[reg]
    return uses, defs


def _graph(func, image, base, functions) -> list:
    """The function as nodes (uses, defs, successors, call target) in address order.

    A call is its own node after its delay slot: it uses whatever the callee reads
    and defines every argument register, all of which are caller-saved. A call
    target of None means "reads everything" - a call through a register, a jump
    table, a jump to somewhere that is not a known function.
    """
    start, end = func["addr"], func["end"]
    nodes = {}
    slots = set()

    def decode(address):
        return DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, address - base)[0], address)

    address = start
    while address < end:
        if address in slots:
            address += 4
            continue
        ins = decode(address)
        uses, defs = _effects(ins)
        if not ins.has_delay_slot or address + 4 >= end:
            successors = [address + 4] if address + 4 < end else []
            if ins.has_delay_slot or (ins.is_jump and not ins.is_call):
                successors = []
            nodes[address] = (uses, defs, successors, False)
            address += 4
            continue

        slot = address + 4
        slots.add(slot)
        slot_uses, slot_defs = _effects(decode(slot))
        after = address + 8
        target = ins.target
        inside = start <= target < end

        if ins.is_call:
            callee = target if ins.mnemonic == "jal" and target in functions else None
            nodes[address] = (uses, defs, [slot], False)
            nodes[slot] = (slot_uses, slot_defs, [("call", address)], False)
            nodes[("call", address)] = (callee, ALL_ARGUMENTS, [after], True)
        elif ins.is_return:
            nodes[address] = (uses, defs, [slot], False)
            nodes[slot] = (slot_uses, slot_defs, [], False)
        elif ins.is_branch:
            branch_targets = [target] if inside else [("tail", address)]
            nodes[address] = (uses, defs, [slot] + ([after] if ins.is_likely else []), False)
            nodes[slot] = (slot_uses, slot_defs,
                           branch_targets + ([] if ins.is_likely else [after]), False)
            if not inside:
                nodes[("tail", address)] = (None, 0, [], True)
```
