```py
            if ins.is_likely:
                successors[address] = [slot, after]
                successors[slot] = to_target
                branches[address] = address
            else:
                successors[address] = [slot]
                successors[slot] = to_target + [after]
                branches[address] = slot
        else:
            successors[address], successors[slot] = [slot], [after]
    for node, targets in successors.items():
        successors[node] = [t if (t == EXIT or start <= t < end) else EXIT for t in targets]
    nodes = sorted(successors) + [EXIT]
    index = {node: i for i, node in enumerate(nodes)}
    full = (1 << len(nodes)) - 1
    pdom = {node: full for node in nodes}
    pdom[EXIT] = 1 << index[EXIT]
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for node in reversed(nodes[:-1]):
            meet = full
            for successor in successors[node]:
                meet &= pdom.get(successor, 1 << index[EXIT])
            value = meet | (1 << index[node])
            if value != pdom[node]:
                pdom[node] = value
                changed = True
    joins = {}
    for branch, parting in branches.items():
        strict = pdom[parting] & ~(1 << index[parting])
        for candidate in nodes:
            if strict >> index[candidate] & 1 and pdom[candidate] == strict:
                if candidate != EXIT:
                    joins[branch] = candidate
                break
    return joins


def _returned_values(paths):
    """Every value the function can return, from inside loop bodies too."""
    for path in paths:
        if path.leaf is None:
            yield path.expression
        for _count, kind, obj in path.marks:
            if kind == "loop":
                yield from _tree_returns(obj.body)


def _tree_returns(statements):
    for statement in statements:
        if statement[0] == "return":
            yield statement[1]
        elif statement[0] == "if":
            yield from _tree_returns(statement[2])
            yield from _tree_returns(statement[3])
        elif statement[0] == "loop":
            yield from _tree_returns(statement[1].body)


def tree_expressions(statements):
    """Every expression in a statement tree, loop bodies included."""
    for statement in statements:
        kind = statement[0]
        if kind == "store":
            yield statement[1].address
            yield statement[1].value
        elif kind == "call":
            for _index, expr in statement[1].arguments:
                yield expr
            if statement[1].pointer is not None:
                yield statement[1].pointer
        elif kind == "if":
            yield statement[1]
            yield from tree_expressions(statement[2])
            yield from tree_expressions(statement[3])
        elif kind == "loop":
            for _register, expr in statement[1].init:
                yield expr
            yield from tree_expressions(statement[1].body)
        elif kind == "continue":
            for _register, expr in statement[2]:
                yield expr
        elif kind == "return" and statement[1] is not None:
            yield statement[1]


def _loop_info(image, base, start, end) -> dict:
    """{head: (body addresses, carried registers, moves sp)} for each loop.

    A loop is found by its back edge - a branch or jump to an address at or
    before itself - and taken to span from the head to the last back edge's
    delay slot, which is how compiled loops are laid out. The carried registers
    are every register the body can write; a body containing a call also
    clobbers everything a call does.
    """
    from .calls import _float_operands
    from .structs import _written_register

    def decode(address):
        return DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, address - base)[0], address)

    last = {}
    for address in range(start, end, 4):
        ins = decode(address)
        if (ins.is_branch or (ins.is_jump and not ins.is_call)) \
                and start <= ins.target <= address:
            last[ins.target] = max(last.get(ins.target, 0), address)
    info = {}
    for head, back in last.items():
        body = frozenset(range(head, min(back + 8, end), 4))
        carried, moves_sp, calls = set(), False, False
        uses_vu = False
        for address in body:
            ins = decode(address)
            written = _written_register(ins)
            if written:
                carried.add(written)
                moves_sp |= written == 29
            _read, wrote = _float_operands(ins)
            carried |= {fpr(r) for r in wrote}
            if ins.raw >> 26 in (0x12, 0x36, 0x3E):
                uses_vu = True
            carried |= vu_written(ins)
            field = QUAD_WRITERS.get(ins.mnemonic)
            if field is not None and getattr(ins, field):
                carried.add(upper(getattr(ins, field)))
            if ins.mnemonic.startswith(("mult", "div", "madd", "mthi", "mtlo")):
                carried |= {REG_HI, REG_LO}
            if ins.mnemonic.startswith("c."):
                carried.add(FP_COND)
            calls |= ins.is_call
        if calls and uses_vu:
            # A call clobbers all VU0 state, and carrying every lane through the
            # loop as a variable is not worth it for what is rare.
            raise Unsupported("a loop calls and uses VU0")
        if calls:
            carried |= set(CALLER_SAVED) | {fpr(i) for i in range(20)}
            carried |= {upper(i) for i in CALLER_SAVED}
            carried |= {REG_HI, REG_LO, FP_COND, 31}
        carried.discard(0)
        info[head] = (body, tuple(sorted(carried)), moves_sp)
    return info


def _touches_frame_memory(derivation) -> bool:
    roots = []
    for path in derivation.paths:
        roots += list(path.conditions)
        if path.expression is not None:
            roots.append(path.expression)
        for store in path.stores:
            if _is_frame_address(store.address):
                return True
            roots += [store.address, store.value]
    seen, stack = set(), roots
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        if id(node) in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(id(node))
        if isinstance(node, Load) and _is_frame_address(node.address):
            return True
        stack.extend(children(node))
    return False

```

`ps2decomp/r5900.py`:

```py
"""Disassembler for the Emotion Engine CPU (MIPS R5900), as used by the PS2.

The R5900 is a MIPS III core with Sony/Toshiba extensions, so a stock MIPS
disassembler mis-decodes a meaningful fraction of a real PS2 binary.  The pieces
that matter here and that generic decoders get wrong are:

* the MMI opcode space (opcode 0x1C) - 128-bit integer SIMD, with four nested
  sub-tables MMI0..MMI3 plus PMFHL/PMTHL and the shift group;
* 128-bit LQ/SQ load/store (opcodes 0x1E/0x1F);
* COP2, which on the EE is the VU0 macro-mode interface rather than a normal
  MIPS coprocessor 2;
* MIPS III 64-bit arithmetic, which the EE fully implements.

Everything decodes into a small `Instruction` value that records enough control
flow information (branch targets, call/return classification, delay slots) for
the function-discovery and splitting passes to work off.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import struct

# -- register names ------------------------------------------------------

GPR = [
    "$zero", "$at", "$v0", "$v1", "$a0", "$a1", "$a2", "$a3",
    "$t0", "$t1", "$t2", "$t3", "$t4", "$t5", "$t6", "$t7",
    "$s0", "$s1", "$s2", "$s3", "$s4", "$s5", "$s6", "$s7",
    "$t8", "$t9", "$k0", "$k1", "$gp", "$sp", "$fp", "$ra",
]

FPR = ["$f%d" % i for i in range(32)]
VF = ["$vf%d" % i for i in range(32)]
VI = ["$vi%d" % i for i in range(32)]

COP0_REG = {
    0: "Index", 1: "Random", 2: "EntryLo0", 3: "EntryLo1", 4: "Context",
    5: "PageMask", 6: "Wired", 8: "BadVAddr", 9: "Count", 10: "EntryHi",
    11: "Compare", 12: "Status", 13: "Cause", 14: "EPC", 15: "PRId",
    16: "Config", 23: "BadPAddr", 24: "Debug", 25: "Perf", 28: "TagLo",
    29: "TagHi", 30: "ErrorEPC",
}

# Register indices that carry meaning for control flow.
REG_ZERO = 0
REG_RA = 31
REG_SP = 29


# -- instruction classification -----------------------------------------

class Flags:
    """Bit flags describing what an instruction does, for the analysis passes."""

    NONE = 0
    BRANCH = 1 << 0        # PC-relative conditional branch
    JUMP = 1 << 1          # unconditional transfer (j, jr, b)
    CALL = 1 << 2          # jal / jalr / bgezal etc - writes $ra
    RETURN = 1 << 3        # jr $ra
    LIKELY = 1 << 4        # ...L branch: delay slot nullified when not taken
    LOAD = 1 << 5
    STORE = 1 << 6
    FLOAT = 1 << 7
    HAS_DELAY_SLOT = 1 << 8
    TRAP = 1 << 9
    INVALID = 1 << 10


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Instruction:
    """One decoded machine instruction."""

    addr: int
    raw: int
    mnemonic: str
    operands: tuple = ()
    flags: int = Flags.NONE
    target: int = -1        # resolved branch/jump target, or -1
    # Decoded field values, kept for analysis passes that need raw registers.
    rs: int = 0
    rt: int = 0
    rd: int = 0
    imm: int = 0

    # -- predicates ---------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def is_branch(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.flags & Flags.BRANCH)

    @property
    def is_jump(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.flags & Flags.JUMP)

    @property
    def is_call(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.flags & Flags.CALL)

    @property
    def is_return(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.flags & Flags.RETURN)

    @property
    def is_likely(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.flags & Flags.LIKELY)

    @property
    def has_delay_slot(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.flags & Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT)

    @property
    def is_valid(self) -> bool:
        return not self.flags & Flags.INVALID

    @property
    def is_nop(self) -> bool:
        return self.raw == 0

    @property
    def ends_block(self) -> bool:
        """True when control does not fall through past the delay slot."""
        if self.is_return:
            return True
        if self.is_jump and not self.is_call:
            return True
        return False

    def format(self, symbolizer=None) -> str:
        """Render as assembly text; `symbolizer(addr)` may supply a label."""
        if not self.operands:
            return self.mnemonic
        ops = list(self.operands)
        if self.target >= 0 and symbolizer is not None:
            label = symbolizer(self.target)
            if label:
                ops[-1] = label
        return "%-10s %s" % (self.mnemonic, ", ".join(str(o) for o in ops))

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.format()


# -- field helpers -------------------------------------------------------

def _op(w):     return (w >> 26) & 0x3F
def _rs(w):     return (w >> 21) & 0x1F
def _rt(w):     return (w >> 16) & 0x1F
def _rd(w):     return (w >> 11) & 0x1F
def _sa(w):     return (w >> 6) & 0x1F
def _funct(w):  return w & 0x3F
def _imm(w):    return w & 0xFFFF
def _simm(w):
    v = w & 0xFFFF
    return v - 0x10000 if v & 0x8000 else v
def _target(w): return w & 0x03FFFFFF


def _hex(value: int) -> str:
    """Format an immediate the way the EE assembler conventionally shows it."""
    if value < 0:
        return "-0x%x" % (-value)
    return "0x%x" % value

class Disassembler:
    """Decodes R5900 instructions.

    Stateless by design: `decode` is a pure function of (word, address) so the
    analysis passes can decode the same address repeatedly without bookkeeping.
    """

    # -- public API ---------------------------------------------------

    def decode(self, word: int, addr: int = 0) -> Instruction:
        word &= 0xFFFFFFFF
        if word == 0:
            return Instruction(addr, word, "nop")
        op = _op(word)
        handler = getattr(self, "_op_%02x" % op, None)
        if handler is not None:
            result = handler(word, addr)
            if result is not None:
                return result
        if op in _ITYPE:
            return self._itype(word, addr, *_ITYPE[op])
        if op in _MEM:
            return self._mem(word, addr, *_MEM[op])
        return self._invalid(word, addr)

    def decode_bytes(self, data: bytes, base_addr: int = 0):
        """Decode a little-endian instruction stream into a list."""
        count = len(data) // 4
        words = struct.unpack("<%dI" % count, data[: count * 4])
        return [self.decode(w, base_addr + i * 4) for i, w in enumerate(words)]

    # -- helpers ------------------------------------------------------

    def _invalid(self, word: int, addr: int) -> Instruction:
        return Instruction(addr, word, ".word", ("0x%08x" % word,), Flags.INVALID)

    def _branch_target(self, word: int, addr: int) -> int:
        return addr + 4 + (_simm(word) << 2)

    def _jump_target(self, word: int, addr: int) -> int:
        return ((addr + 4) & 0xF0000000) | (_target(word) << 2)

    def _format_operands(self, word: int, form: str, regs=GPR, cop1: bool = False):
        """Build operand tuple from a compact form string.

        COP1 R-format packs its register fields differently from the integer
        unit: fd sits in the shift-amount field and fs in the rd field, so the
        `cop1` flag switches to that mapping.
        """
        pick_d = _sa if cop1 else _rd
        pick_s = _rd if cop1 else _rs
        out = []
        for part in form.split(","):
            if part == "d":
                out.append(regs[pick_d(word)])
            elif part == "s":
                out.append(regs[pick_s(word)])
            elif part == "t":
                out.append(regs[_rt(word)])
            elif part == "a":
                out.append(_sa(word))
            elif part == "i":
                out.append(_hex(_simm(word)))
            elif part == "u":
                out.append(_hex(_imm(word)))
        return tuple(out)

    # -- opcode 0x00: SPECIAL -----------------------------------------

    def _op_00(self, word: int, addr: int):
        funct = _funct(word)
        entry = _SPECIAL.get(funct)
        if entry is None:
            return self._invalid(word, addr)
        mnem, form = entry
        rs, rt, rd = _rs(word), _rt(word), _rd(word)

        if funct == 0x08:  # jr
            flags = Flags.JUMP | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT
            if rs == REG_RA:
                flags |= Flags.RETURN
            return Instruction(addr, word, "jr", (GPR[rs],), flags, rs=rs)

        if funct == 0x09:  # jalr
            # The two-operand form is only printed when rd is not the default $ra.
            ops = (GPR[rd], GPR[rs]) if rd != REG_RA else (GPR[rs],)
            return Instruction(
                addr, word, "jalr", ops,
                Flags.JUMP | Flags.CALL | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT, rs=rs, rd=rd,
            )

        if funct in (0x18, 0x19):  # mult/multu: rd is optional on the EE
            if rd:
                ops = (GPR[rd], GPR[rs], GPR[rt])
            else:
                ops = (GPR[rs], GPR[rt])
            return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, ops, rs=rs, rt=rt, rd=rd)

        if funct in (0x0C, 0x0D, 0x0F):  # syscall/break/sync
            return Instruction(addr, word, mnem)

        # `sll $zero, $zero, 0` is canonical nop and was handled earlier; treat
        # the remaining shift-by-zero encodings normally.
        flags = Flags.TRAP if 0x30 <= funct <= 0x36 else Flags.NONE
        return Instruction(
            addr, word, mnem, self._format_operands(word, form),
            flags, rs=rs, rt=rt, rd=rd, imm=_sa(word),
        )

    # -- opcode 0x01: REGIMM ------------------------------------------

    def _op_01(self, word: int, addr: int):
        rt = _rt(word)
        mnem = _REGIMM.get(rt)
        if mnem is None:
            return self._invalid(word, addr)
        rs = _rs(word)
        if mnem in ("mtsab", "mtsah"):
            return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rs], _hex(_imm(word))), rs=rs, imm=_imm(word))
        if mnem.startswith("t"):  # trap immediate
            return Instruction(
                addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rs], _hex(_simm(word))), Flags.TRAP, rs=rs
            )
        target = self._branch_target(word, addr)
        flags = Flags.BRANCH | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT
        if mnem.endswith("l"):
            flags |= Flags.LIKELY
        if "al" in mnem:
            flags |= Flags.CALL
        return Instruction(
            addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rs], "0x%08x" % target), flags, target, rs=rs
        )

    # -- opcodes 0x02/0x03: J / JAL -----------------------------------

    def _op_02(self, word: int, addr: int):
        target = self._jump_target(word, addr)
        return Instruction(
            addr, word, "j", ("0x%08x" % target,),
            Flags.JUMP | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT, target,
        )

    def _op_03(self, word: int, addr: int):
        target = self._jump_target(word, addr)
        return Instruction(
            addr, word, "jal", ("0x%08x" % target,),
            Flags.JUMP | Flags.CALL | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT, target,
        )

    # -- opcodes 0x04..0x07, 0x14..0x17: branches ---------------------

    def _branch(self, word: int, addr: int, mnem: str, two_reg: bool):
        target = self._branch_target(word, addr)
        rs, rt = _rs(word), _rt(word)
        flags = Flags.BRANCH | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT
        if mnem.endswith("l"):
            flags |= Flags.LIKELY
        # `beq $zero, $zero, x` is an unconditional branch; the assembler spells
        # it `b`, and treating it as a jump keeps block splitting accurate.
        if mnem == "beq" and rs == REG_ZERO and rt == REG_ZERO:
            return Instruction(
                addr, word, "b", ("0x%08x" % target,),
                Flags.JUMP | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT, target,
            )
        ops = (GPR[rs], GPR[rt], "0x%08x" % target) if two_reg else (GPR[rs], "0x%08x" % target)
        return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, ops, flags, target, rs=rs, rt=rt)

    def _op_04(self, word, addr): return self._branch(word, addr, "beq", True)
    def _op_05(self, word, addr): return self._branch(word, addr, "bne", True)
    def _op_06(self, word, addr): return self._branch(word, addr, "blez", False)
    def _op_07(self, word, addr): return self._branch(word, addr, "bgtz", False)
    def _op_14(self, word, addr): return self._branch(word, addr, "beql", True)
    def _op_15(self, word, addr): return self._branch(word, addr, "bnel", True)
    def _op_16(self, word, addr): return self._branch(word, addr, "blezl", False)
    def _op_17(self, word, addr): return self._branch(word, addr, "bgtzl", False)

    # -- opcode 0x0F: LUI ---------------------------------------------

    def _op_0f(self, word: int, addr: int):
        rt = _rt(word)
        return Instruction(
            addr, word, "lui", (GPR[rt], _hex(_imm(word))), rt=rt, imm=_imm(word)
        )

    # -- opcode 0x10: COP0 --------------------------------------------

    def _op_10(self, word: int, addr: int):
        rs, rt, rd = _rs(word), _rt(word), _rd(word)
        if rs == 0x00:
            return Instruction(addr, word, "mfc0", (GPR[rt], COP0_REG.get(rd, "$%d" % rd)), rt=rt, rd=rd)
        if rs == 0x04:
            return Instruction(addr, word, "mtc0", (GPR[rt], COP0_REG.get(rd, "$%d" % rd)), rt=rt, rd=rd)
        if rs == 0x08:  # BC0
            target = self._branch_target(word, addr)
            mnem = {0: "bc0f", 1: "bc0t", 2: "bc0fl", 3: "bc0tl"}.get(rt, "bc0?")
            return Instruction(
                addr, word, mnem, ("0x%08x" % target,),
                Flags.BRANCH | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT, target,
            )
        if rs == 0x10:
            mnem = {0x01: "tlbr", 0x02: "tlbwi", 0x06: "tlbwr", 0x08: "tlbp",
                    0x18: "eret", 0x38: "ei", 0x39: "di"}.get(_funct(word))
            if mnem:
                flags = Flags.JUMP if mnem == "eret" else Flags.NONE
                return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, (), flags)
        return self._invalid(word, addr)

    # -- opcode 0x11: COP1 (FPU) --------------------------------------

    def _op_11(self, word: int, addr: int):
        rs, rt, rd = _rs(word), _rt(word), _rd(word)
        if rs == 0x00:
            return Instruction(addr, word, "mfc1", (GPR[rt], FPR[rd]), Flags.FLOAT, rt=rt, rd=rd)
        if rs == 0x02:
            return Instruction(addr, word, "cfc1", (GPR[rt], "$%d" % rd), Flags.FLOAT, rt=rt, rd=rd)
        if rs == 0x04:
            return Instruction(addr, word, "mtc1", (GPR[rt], FPR[rd]), Flags.FLOAT, rt=rt, rd=rd)
        if rs == 0x06:
            return Instruction(addr, word, "ctc1", (GPR[rt], "$%d" % rd), Flags.FLOAT, rt=rt, rd=rd)
        if rs == 0x08:  # BC1
            target = self._branch_target(word, addr)
            mnem = {0: "bc1f", 1: "bc1t", 2: "bc1fl", 3: "bc1tl"}.get(rt, "bc1?")
            flags = Flags.BRANCH | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT | Flags.FLOAT
            if rt >= 2:
                flags |= Flags.LIKELY
            return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, ("0x%08x" % target,), flags, target)
        if rs == 0x10:  # single precision
            entry = _COP1_S.get(_funct(word))
            if entry is None:
                return self._invalid(word, addr)
            mnem, form = entry
            return Instruction(
                addr, word, mnem,
                self._format_operands(word, form, FPR, cop1=True), Flags.FLOAT,
            )
        if rs == 0x14:  # fixed point -> single
            if _funct(word) == 0x20:
                return Instruction(
                    addr, word, "cvt.s.w", (FPR[_sa(word)], FPR[_rd(word)]), Flags.FLOAT
                )
        return self._invalid(word, addr)

    # -- opcode 0x12: COP2 (VU0 macro mode) ---------------------------

    def _op_12(self, word: int, addr: int):
        rs, rt, rd = _rs(word), _rt(word), _rd(word)
        # Data movement between the EE core and VU0.
        simple = {0x01: "qmfc2", 0x02: "cfc2", 0x05: "qmtc2", 0x06: "ctc2"}
        if rs in simple:
            reg = VF[rd] if rs in (0x01, 0x05) else VI[rd]
            return Instruction(addr, word, simple[rs], (GPR[rt], reg), rt=rt, rd=rd)
        if rs == 0x08:  # BC2
            target = self._branch_target(word, addr)
            mnem = {0: "bc2f", 1: "bc2t", 2: "bc2fl", 3: "bc2tl"}.get(rt, "bc2?")
            return Instruction(
                addr, word, mnem, ("0x%08x" % target,),
                Flags.BRANCH | Flags.HAS_DELAY_SLOT, target,
            )
        if rs & 0x10:
            return self._cop2_special(word, addr)
        return self._invalid(word, addr)

    def _cop2_special(self, word: int, addr: int):
        """Decode VU0 macro-mode operations.

        Special1 (funct below 0x3C) is the FMAC group, named with their
        destination mask: `vaddx.xyz`. Special2 (funct 0x3C..0x3F) indexes a
        second table by bits 10..6 and 1..0, where the accumulator forms,
        conversions, moves and the divide unit live. Every field is read from the
        raw word by whatever executes the instruction; the operands here are for
        reading.
        """
        funct = _funct(word)
        dest = (word >> 21) & 0xF
        mask = "".join(c for c, bit in zip("xyzw", (8, 4, 2, 1)) if dest & bit) or "xyzw"
        fd, fs, ft = _sa(word), _rd(word), _rt(word)
        if funct >= 0x3C:
            index = (word & 0x3) | ((word >> 4) & 0x7C)
            base = _COP2_SPECIAL2.get(index)
            if base is None:
                return Instruction(addr, word, "cop2", ("0x%07x" % (word & 0x1FFFFFF),))
            if base in _COP2_UNMASKED:
                return Instruction(addr, word, base, (VF[fs], VF[ft]))
            return Instruction(addr, word, "%s.%s" % (base, mask), (VF[fs], VF[ft]))
        base = _COP2_SPECIAL1.get(funct)
        if base is None:
            return Instruction(addr, word, "cop2", ("0x%07x" % (word & 0x1FFFFFF),))
        if base in ("viadd", "visub", "viaddi", "viand", "vior", "vcallms", "vcallmsr"):
            return Instruction(addr, word, base, (VI[fd], VI[fs], VI[ft]))
        return Instruction(
            addr, word, "%s.%s" % (base, mask), (VF[fd], VF[fs], VF[ft])
        )

    # -- opcode 0x1C: MMI ---------------------------------------------

    def _op_1c(self, word: int, addr: int):
        funct = _funct(word)
        sub = _sa(word)
        rs, rt, rd = _rs(word), _rt(word), _rd(word)

        if funct == 0x08:  # MMI0
            mnem = _MMI0.get(sub)
            return (
                Instruction(addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rd], GPR[rs], GPR[rt]), rs=rs, rt=rt, rd=rd)
                if mnem else self._invalid(word, addr)
            )
        if funct == 0x28:  # MMI1
            mnem = _MMI1.get(sub)
            return (
                Instruction(addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rd], GPR[rs], GPR[rt]), rs=rs, rt=rt, rd=rd)
                if mnem else self._invalid(word, addr)
            )
        if funct == 0x09:  # MMI2
            mnem = _MMI2.get(sub)
            if mnem is None:
                return self._invalid(word, addr)
            if mnem in ("pmfhi", "pmflo"):
                return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rd],), rd=rd)
            return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rd], GPR[rs], GPR[rt]), rs=rs, rt=rt, rd=rd)
        if funct == 0x29:  # MMI3
            mnem = _MMI3.get(sub)
            if mnem is None:
                return self._invalid(word, addr)
            if mnem in ("pmthi", "pmtlo"):
                return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rs],), rs=rs)
            if mnem == "pcpyh":
                return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rd], GPR[rt]), rt=rt, rd=rd)
            return Instruction(addr, word, mnem, (GPR[rd], GPR[rs], GPR[rt]), rs=rs, rt=rt, rd=rd)

        entry = _MMI.get(funct)
        if entry is None:
            return self._invalid(word, addr)
        mnem, form = entry
        if form == "pmfhl":
            name = _PMFHL.get(sub)
            return (
                Instruction(addr, word, name, (GPR[rd],), rd=rd)
                if name else self._invalid(word, addr)
            )
        if form == "pmthl":
            return Instruction(addr, word, "pmthl.lw", (GPR[rs],), rs=rs)
        return Instruction(
            addr, word, mnem, self._format_operands(word, form),
            rs=rs, rt=rt, rd=rd, imm=_sa(word),
        )

    # -- generic I-type and memory forms -------------------------------

    def _itype(self, word: int, addr: int, mnem: str, form: str):
        rs, rt = _rs(word), _rt(word)
        # `addiu $rt, $zero, imm` is the canonical li; keeping the real mnemonic
        # avoids surprises when the output is fed back to an assembler.
        return Instruction(
            addr, word, mnem, self._format_operands(word, form),
            rs=rs, rt=rt, imm=_simm(word),
        )

    def _mem(self, word: int, addr: int, mnem: str, is_store: bool, is_float: bool):
        rs, rt = _rs(word), _rt(word)
        if is_float:
            reg = FPR[rt]
        elif mnem in ("lqc2", "sqc2"):
            reg = VF[rt]
        elif mnem in ("pref", "cache"):
            # These encode an operation selector in `rt`, not a register.
            reg = str(rt) if mnem == "pref" else _hex(rt)
        else:
            reg = GPR[rt]
        flags = Flags.STORE if is_store else Flags.LOAD
        if is_float:
            flags |= Flags.FLOAT
        offset = _simm(word)
        return Instruction(
            addr, word, mnem, (reg, "%s(%s)" % (_hex(offset), GPR[rs])),
            flags, rs=rs, rt=rt, imm=offset,
        )


# A module-level instance is convenient and safe because the class is stateless.
DISASM = Disassembler()


def decode(word: int, addr: int = 0) -> Instruction:
    return DISASM.decode(word, addr)


def decode_bytes(data: bytes, base_addr: int = 0):
    return DISASM.decode_bytes(data, base_addr)

```

`ps2decomp/signatures.py`:

```py
"""Function signatures that survive relinking, for recognising code across games.

Games built against the same SDK or middleware contain the same library code: the
EE kernel stubs, Sony's libraries, the C runtime, RenderWare. Linked into a
different executable, that code keeps its instructions but not its addresses. Call
targets, the halves of absolute addresses and $gp-relative offsets all change,
while the rest stays the same.

A signature is a hash of the function's words with exactly those fields masked:

* `j`/`jal` targets (26 bits);
* `lui` immediates, the high half of an absolute address;
* the immediate of an instruction whose base register still holds a `lui` result,
  the low half of the same address;
* the immediate of an instruction based on $gp (small data).

Branch offsets are relative and stay in. Masking depends only on the instruction
stream and never on the values masked, so the same code always masks the same way.
The register tracking is a linear scan with no control flow, which is enough for
determinism.

Short functions collide: every `jr $ra; nop` looks alike. So the instruction count
is part of the signature, and a library entry carrying more than one name is never
used to name anything.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import struct

# Opcodes whose 16-bit immediate is added to the rs register: arithmetic and
# logical immediates, then every load and store form.
_BASED = ({0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x0E, 0x18, 0x19, 0x1A, 0x1B, 0x1E, 0x1F}
          | set(range(0x20, 0x30)) | {0x31, 0x33, 0x36, 0x37, 0x39, 0x3E, 0x3F})
_STORES = set(range(0x28, 0x30)) | {0x1F, 0x39, 0x3E, 0x3F}
_COP_STORES_AND_LOADS = {0x31, 0x33, 0x36, 0x39, 0x3E}   # write no general register
_GP = 28
_IMM = 0xFFFF
_TARGET = 0x03FFFFFF


def written_register(word: int):
    """The general register an instruction writes, as far as tracking needs it."""
    op = word >> 26
    rt = (word >> 16) & 31
    rd = (word >> 11) & 31
    if op == 3:                                   # jal
        return 31
    if op in (0x00, 0x1C):                        # SPECIAL, MMI
        return rd or None
    if op == 0x11 and ((word >> 21) & 31) in (0, 1, 2):   # mfc1, dmfc1, cfc1
        return rt
    if op == 0x12 and ((word >> 21) & 31) in (1, 2):      # qmfc2, cfc2
        return rt
    if op in _BASED and op not in _STORES and op not in _COP_STORES_AND_LOADS:
        return rt
    if op == 0x0F:
        return rt
    return None


def masked_words(words) -> list:
    """The words with every relocation-dependent field cleared."""
    high = set()                 # registers holding a lui result
    out = []
    for word in words:
        op = word >> 26
        rs = (word >> 21) & 31
        if op in (2, 3):
            word &= ~_TARGET
        elif op == 0x0F:
            word &= ~_IMM
        elif op in _BASED and (rs in high or rs == _GP):
            word &= ~_IMM
        out.append(word)
        written = written_register(word)
        if op == 0x0F:
            high.add(written)
        elif written is not None:
            high.discard(written)
    return out


def function_words(image: bytes, base: int, start: int, end: int) -> list:
    count = (end - start) // 4
    return list(struct.unpack_from("<%dI" % count, image, start - base))


def signature(image: bytes, base: int, start: int, end: int) -> str:
    words = masked_words(function_words(image, base, start, end))
    digest = hashlib.sha1(struct.pack("<%dI" % len(words), *words)).hexdigest()
    return "%d:%s" % (len(words), digest[:16])


def compute(database: dict, image: bytes, base: int) -> dict:
    """{function address: signature} for every function with a body."""
    return {func["addr"]: signature(image, base, func["addr"], func["end"])
            for func in database["functions"] if func["end"] > func["addr"]}


LIBRARY_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
                            "signatures", "library.json")


class Library:
    """Named signatures gathered from every game: signature -> {name: [executables]}.

    Each name records the executables that gave it. Two games naming the same code
    differently leaves the entry ambiguous, and an ambiguous entry names nothing.
    Re-exporting a game first withdraws everything it contributed before, so a
    corrected name replaces the old one instead of joining it.
    """

    def __init__(self, entries=None):
        self.entries = entries or {}

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str = LIBRARY_PATH) -> "Library":
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            return cls()
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            return cls(json.load(handle)["functions"])

    def save(self, path: str = LIBRARY_PATH) -> None:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
        ordered = {key: {name: sorted(sources) for name, sources in sorted(entry.items())}
                   for key, entry in sorted(self.entries.items())}
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            json.dump({"format": 2, "functions": ordered}, handle, indent=1)
            handle.write("\n")

    def withdraw(self, source: str) -> None:
        """Remove every name this executable contributed."""
        for key in list(self.entries):
            entry = self.entries[key]
            for name in list(entry):
                if source in entry[name]:
                    entry[name].remove(source)
                if not entry[name]:
                    del entry[name]
            if not entry:
                del self.entries[key]

    def add(self, key: str, name: str, source: str) -> None:
        sources = self.entries.setdefault(key, {}).setdefault(name, [])
        if source not in sources:
            sources.append(source)

    def sources(self, key: str) -> list:
        return sorted({s for sources in self.entries.get(key, {}).values() for s in sources})

    def name_for(self, key: str):
        """The one name this signature carries, or None if it has none or several."""
        entry = self.entries.get(key)
        if entry and len(entry) == 1:
            return next(iter(entry))
        return None

```

`ps2decomp/structs.py`:

```py
"""Recover structure types from how the code uses pointers.

The method is type unification in the style of Steensgaard's points-to analysis,
extended with field offsets:

* Every value that is dereferenced gets a *type node*: the arguments of each
  function, each function's return value, and the contents of pointer fields -
  if `lw $t0, 4($a0)` is followed by a dereference of `$t0`, then field 4 of
  whatever `$a0` points to is itself a pointer, to a type of its own.
* A node collects the offsets it is accessed at, with their widths.
* Evidence that two nodes are the same type joins them: an argument passed
  unchanged into a call, a value returned, a pointer stored into a field. Joining
  two types joins whatever their common pointer fields point to as well.

Unification is only as good as its links, and one generic routine - a memcpy, a
list helper - links every type it is ever handed. The measurement in
engine/tools/fields.py showed that cutting links into widely-called functions trades one
error for another: too strict a cutoff discards real links to central objects,
too loose a one fuses unrelated types into one 700-function blob. So instead of a
cutoff, each join is *checked*: two types are joined only if they agree on the
width of every offset both use, recursively through their pointer fields. A
generic routine is refused at the first type it disagrees with. Links are applied
in order of how specific the callee is - functions with fewer callers first - so
that generic routines meet already-established types and are refused, rather
than establishing a fused type first.

Because the guard uses widths, width agreement is no longer evidence of quality.
Two properties the guard never looks at are: whether an offset is used as float
or integer, and whether it is loaded signed or unsigned. `quality()` reports
agreement on those as the independent check.

The scan is flow-aware rather than linear. A register's meaning is carried along
each path, and where paths join only the meanings all of them agree on survive;
at the head of a loop, anything the loop body overwrites is dropped. Imprecision
therefore loses links rather than inventing them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
import collections
import struct

import re

from . import layout
from .r5900 import DISASM, GPR

# mnemonic -> (width, kind, signed); signed is None for stores
ACCESSES = {
    "lb": (1, "int", True), "lbu": (1, "int", False),
    "lh": (2, "int", True), "lhu": (2, "int", False),
    "lw": (4, "int", True), "lwu": (4, "int", False),
    "ld": (8, "int", False), "lq": (16, "int", False),
    "lwc1": (4, "float", None),
    "sb": (1, "int", None), "sh": (2, "int", None), "sw": (4, "int", None),
    "sd": (8, "int", None), "sq": (16, "int", None), "swc1": (4, "float", None),
}
STORES = {"sb", "sh", "sw", "sd", "sq", "swc1"}
MOVES = {"daddu", "addu", "or", "dadd"}
# All eight integer argument registers: $a0..$a3, then $t0..$t3.
ARG_REGS = (4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11)
CALLER_SAVED = set(range(1, 16)) | {24, 25, 31}
# 16-byte accesses are block copies (`lq`/`sq` move a struct 16 bytes at a time),
# not fields; they say nothing about the layout inside the block.
BLOCK_WIDTH = 16
MAX_TERM_DEPTH = 4
# Interior pointers further than this from their base are not followed; real
# structures here span up to ~0x7000 bytes.
MAX_DISPLACEMENT = 0x8000

# The whole global address space, as one type node. A register holding a
# constant address holds (GLOBALS, address), so the same machinery that records
# fields of a struct records global variables: an access through it is a field of
# GLOBALS at an absolute address, a pointer loaded from one gets a type of its
# own, and a global's address passed into a function is an embedded object.
GLOBALS = ("globals",)
GP = 28


def _written_register(ins):
    """The general register an instruction writes, or None."""
    m = ins.mnemonic
    if ins.is_call:
        return 31
    if m in STORES or ins.is_branch or (ins.is_jump and not ins.is_call):
        return None
    if m in ("lwc1", "mtc1", "ctc1") or m.startswith(("add.", "sub.", "mul.", "div.", "c.")):
        return None
    if m in ACCESSES or m in ("lui", "addiu", "addi", "daddiu", "daddi", "andi", "ori",
                              "xori", "slti", "sltiu", "mfc1", "qmfc2", "cfc1"):
        return ins.rt
    if ins.rd:
        return ins.rd
    return None


_REGISTER = re.compile(r"\$[a-z0-9]+")
_NUMBER = {name: index for index, name in enumerate(GPR)}


def _read_registers(ins) -> set:
    """General registers an instruction reads.

    Taken from the operand text: every register named, less the destination when
    it is named only once as the first operand. `addu $a0, $a0, $t0` names $a0
    twice and so reads it.
    """
    names = [_NUMBER[n] for op in ins.operands for n in _REGISTER.findall(str(op))
             if n in _NUMBER]
    written = _written_register(ins)
    if written is not None and names and names[0] == written and names.count(written) == 1:
        names = names[1:]
    return set(names)


def argument_use(database, image, base) -> set:
    """(function, index) for every argument a function actually reads.

    An argument register that still holds the caller's value at a call is only
    evidence if the callee looks at it. Without this, a wrapper's untouched
    `$a1..$a3` were linked into every callee it made, which joined the arguments
    of unrelated functions into one type.

    A function reads an argument if an instruction reads the register before it
    is overwritten, or passes it to a callee that reads it - so this is solved to
    a fixed point over the call graph.
    """
    functions = {f["addr"]: f for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}
    used = set()
    passes = collections.defaultdict(set)    # (callee, i) -> {(caller, i)}
    for func in functions.values():
        start, end = func["addr"], func["end"]
        original = {reg: index for index, reg in enumerate(ARG_REGS)}
        address = start
        while address < end:
            ins = DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, address - base)[0], address)
            sequence = [ins]
            if ins.has_delay_slot and address + 4 < end:
                sequence.insert(0, DISASM.decode(
                    struct.unpack_from("<I", image, address + 4 - base)[0], address + 4))
            for step in sequence:
                if step.is_call or (step.is_jump and step.mnemonic == "j"):
                    target = step.target
                    if target in functions and not (start <= target < end):
                        for reg, index in original.items():
                            passes[(target, ARG_REGS.index(reg))].add((start, index))
                    if step.is_call:
                        for reg in CALLER_SAVED:
                            original.pop(reg, None)
                    continue
                for reg in _read_registers(step):
                    if reg in original:
                        used.add((start, original[reg]))
                written = _written_register(step)
                if written is not None:
                    original.pop(written, None)
            address += 8 if len(sequence) == 2 else 4
    # Propagate: passing an argument to a callee that reads it is a read.
    work = list(used)
    while work:
        slot = work.pop()
        for caller in passes.get(slot, ()):
            if caller not in used:
                used.add(caller)
                work.append(caller)
    return used


def _sign32(value: int) -> int:
    value &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return value - (1 << 32) if value & 0x80000000 else value


def _depth(term) -> int:
    depth = 0
    while term[0] == "field":
        term = term[1]
        depth += 1
    return depth


def _intersect(states):
    """Register meanings every incoming path agrees on."""
    first = states[0]
    return {reg: term for reg, term in first.items()
            if all(state.get(reg) == term for state in states[1:])}


def scan(func, image, base, functions, used):
    """Return the type events one function produces.

    Events are ("access", term, offset, width, kind, signed, is_store) and
    ("link", term_a, term_b, callee) where callee is the function whose slot the
    link leads into (None for links within this function). A term names a value:
    ("arg", f, i), ("ret", f) or ("field", term, offset).
    """
    start, end = func["addr"], func["end"]
    address = start

    def decode(addr):
        return DISASM.decode(struct.unpack_from("<I", image, addr - base)[0], addr)

    # Registers written inside each loop, dropped at the loop head: the state there
    # was computed from the entry path alone and the back edge may disagree.
    loop_kill = collections.defaultdict(set)
    addr = start
    while addr < end:
        ins = decode(addr)
        if (ins.is_branch or ins.is_jump) and start <= ins.target <= addr:
            for inner in range(ins.target, min(addr + 8, end), 4):
                reg = _written_register(decode(inner))
                if reg is not None:
                    loop_kill[ins.target].add(reg)
        addr += 4

    events = []
    pending = collections.defaultdict(list)
    has_jump_table = any(
        ins.mnemonic == "jr" and ins.rs != 31
        for ins in (decode(a) for a in range(start, end, 4))
    )
    state = {reg: (("arg", start, index), 0) for index, reg in enumerate(ARG_REGS)}
    # $gp is fixed for the whole program, so small-data accesses are globals too.
    state[GP] = (GLOBALS, layout.CURRENT.gp)
    reachable = True

    # A register holds (term, displacement): the value `term` plus a constant. The
    # displacement is what makes interior pointers work - code that does
    # `addiu $v1, $a0, 0x1E4` and then stores at 0($v1), 4($v1)... is writing fields
    # 0x1E4 and 0x1E8 of $a0's type, and dropping $v1 lost them.
    def apply(ins, state):
        m = ins.mnemonic
        if m in ACCESSES:
            width, kind, signed = ACCESSES[m]
            is_store = m in STORES
            held = state.get(ins.rs)
            offset = None
            if held is not None:
                base_term, displacement = held
                offset = displacement + ins.imm
                # Storing $zero clears a field of any kind - an int, a float, a
                # pointer - so it is evidence of width but not of kind.
                stored_kind = "zero" if is_store and ins.rt == 0 else kind
                events.append(
                    ("access", base_term, offset, width, stored_kind, signed, is_store)
                )
            if is_store:
                value = state.get(ins.rt)
                if (held is not None and value is not None and value[1] == 0
                        and width == 4 and kind == "int" and ins.rt != 0
                        and _depth(held[0]) < MAX_TERM_DEPTH):
                    events.append(("link", ("field", held[0], offset), value[0], None))
                return
            if kind == "float":
                return
            if held is not None and width == 4 and _depth(held[0]) < MAX_TERM_DEPTH:
                state[ins.rt] = (("field", held[0], offset), 0)
            else:
                state.pop(ins.rt, None)
            return
        if m in MOVES and ins.rd:
            if ins.rt == 0 and ins.rs in state:
                state[ins.rd] = state[ins.rs]
                return
            if ins.rs == 0 and ins.rt in state:
                state[ins.rd] = state[ins.rt]
                return
        if m in ("addiu", "daddiu") and ins.rs in state:
            term, displacement = state[ins.rs]
            if term == GLOBALS or abs(displacement + ins.imm) <= MAX_DISPLACEMENT:
                state[ins.rt] = (term, _sign32(displacement + ins.imm))
                return
        if m == "lui":
            state[ins.rt] = (GLOBALS, _sign32(ins.imm << 16))
            return
        if m == "ori" and state.get(ins.rs, (None,))[0] == GLOBALS:
            state[ins.rt] = (GLOBALS, _sign32(state[ins.rs][1] | ins.imm))
            return
        reg = _written_register(ins)
        if reg is not None:
            state.pop(reg, None)

    def link_call(target, state):
        for index, reg in enumerate(ARG_REGS):
            held = state.get(reg)
            # Only an undisplaced pointer is the object itself; base+8 passed to a
            # callee is a pointer to something embedded at offset 8.
            if held is None or (target, index) not in used:
                continue
            if held[1] == 0:
                events.append(("link", held[0], ("arg", target, index), target))
            elif held[1] > 0:
                # base+d handed to a callee: the callee's argument type is
                # embedded in this one at offset d.
                events.append(("embed", held[0], held[1], ("arg", target, index), target))

    while address < end:
        if address in pending or address in loop_kill or not reachable:
            incoming = pending.pop(address, [])
            if reachable:
                incoming.append(state)
            state = _intersect(incoming) if incoming else {}
            for reg in loop_kill.get(address, ()):
                state.pop(reg, None)
            # Code after a return or a jump is reached only by a recorded branch.
            # Treating it as reachable with an empty state - padding after `jr $ra`,
            # say - then intersected that emptiness into the real branch target
            # and lost everything the branch carried. A jump table's targets are
            # unknown, though, so in a function with one everything stays
            # reachable, conservatively empty.
            reachable = bool(incoming) or has_jump_table

        ins = decode(address)
        if not ins.has_delay_slot or address + 4 >= end:
            apply(ins, state)
            address += 4
            continue
        delay = decode(address + 4)

        if ins.is_call:
            apply(delay, state)
            target = ins.target if ins.mnemonic == "jal" else -1
            if target in functions:
                link_call(target, state)
            for reg in CALLER_SAVED:
                state.pop(reg, None)
            if target in functions:
                state[2] = (("ret", target), 0)
        elif ins.is_return:
            apply(delay, state)
            if 2 in state and state[2][1] == 0:
                events.append(("link", state[2][0], ("ret", start), None))
            reachable = False
        elif ins.is_branch:
            taken = dict(state)
            apply(delay, taken)
            if address < ins.target < end:
                pending[ins.target].append(taken)
            # A likely branch nullifies its delay slot when not taken, so the
            # fall-through path may or may not have run it.
            state = _intersect([state, taken]) if ins.is_likely else taken
        else:   # unconditional jump
            apply(delay, state)
            target = ins.target
            if address < target < end:
                pending[target].append(state)
            elif ins.mnemonic == "j" and target in functions:
                # A tail call: the callee's arguments and result are this
                # function's own.
                link_call(target, state)
                events.append(("link", ("ret", target), ("ret", start), target))
            reachable = False
        address += 8
    return events


class Field:
    __slots__ = ("uses", "functions", "target", "strides")

    def __init__(self):
        self.uses = collections.Counter()    # (width, kind, signed, is_store) -> count
        self.functions = set()
        self.target = None
        # Strides this field was seen indexed with: the field is element 0 of an
        # array whose elements are that many bytes apart.
        self.strides = collections.Counter()

    def widths(self) -> set:
        return {use[0] for use in self.uses if use[0] != BLOCK_WIDTH}


class TypeGraph:
    """Union-find over type nodes, each with a map of fields."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.parent = []
        self.fields = []
        self.slots = []          # the argument/return terms each node stands for
        self.embeds = []         # node -> {offset: node of the embedded type}
        self.ids = {}            # term -> node, for arg and ret terms
        self.refused = 0
        self.joined = 0

    def new(self) -> int:
        self.parent.append(len(self.parent))
        self.fields.append({})
        self.slots.append(set())
        self.embeds.append({})
        return len(self.parent) - 1

    def find(self, node: int) -> int:
        root = node
        while self.parent[root] != root:
            root = self.parent[root]
        while self.parent[node] != root:
            self.parent[node], node = root, self.parent[node]
        return root

    def node(self, term) -> int:
        if term[0] == "field":
            return self.target(self.node(term[1]), term[2])
        if term not in self.ids:
            self.ids[term] = self.new()
            self.slots[self.ids[term]].add(term)
        return self.ids[term]

    def field(self, node: int, offset: int) -> Field:
        fields = self.fields[self.find(node)]
        if offset not in fields:
            fields[offset] = Field()
        return fields[offset]

    def target(self, node: int, offset: int) -> int:
        field = self.field(node, offset)
        if field.target is None:
            field.target = self.new()
        return field.target

    def compatible(self, a: int, b: int) -> bool:
        """Whether joining a and b keeps every shared offset at one width set."""
        stack, seen = [(a, b)], set()
        while stack:
            x, y = stack.pop()
            x, y = self.find(x), self.find(y)
            if x == y or (x, y) in seen:
                continue
            seen.add((x, y))
            fx, fy = self.fields[x], self.fields[y]
            ex, ey = self.embeds[x], self.embeds[y]
            for offset in ex.keys() & ey.keys():
                stack.append((ex[offset], ey[offset]))
            for offset in fx.keys() & fy.keys():
                wx, wy = fx[offset].widths(), fy[offset].widths()
                # Identical, not merely overlapping: a node that already mixes
                # widths at an offset is a generic pointer (memcpy's argument),
                # and a subset rule let it absorb every type it touched.
                if wx and wy and wx != wy:
                    return False
                if fx[offset].target is not None and fy[offset].target is not None:
                    stack.append((fx[offset].target, fy[offset].target))
        return True

    def embed(self, outer: int, offset: int, inner: int) -> bool:
        """Record that `outer` contains an `inner` at `offset`."""
        embeds = self.embeds[self.find(outer)]
        if offset in embeds:
            return self.join(embeds[offset], inner)
        embeds[offset] = inner
        return True

    def join(self, a: int, b: int) -> bool:
        if self.find(a) == self.find(b):
            return True
        if not self.compatible(a, b):
            self.refused += 1
            return False
        self.joined += 1
        work = [(a, b)]
        while work:
            x, y = work.pop()
            x, y = self.find(x), self.find(y)
            if x == y:
                continue
            # Keep the node with more fields as the root, so merging stays cheap.
            if len(self.fields[x]) > len(self.fields[y]):
                x, y = y, x
            self.parent[x] = y
            self.slots[y] |= self.slots[x]
            self.slots[x] = set()
            into = self.fields[y]
            for offset, field in self.fields[x].items():
                if offset not in into:
                    into[offset] = field
                    continue
                other = into[offset]
                other.uses.update(field.uses)
                other.functions |= field.functions
                other.strides.update(field.strides)
                if field.target is not None:
                    if other.target is None:
                        other.target = field.target
                    else:
                        work.append((field.target, other.target))
            self.fields[x] = {}
            for offset, inner in self.embeds[x].items():
                if offset in self.embeds[y]:
                    work.append((inner, self.embeds[y][offset]))
                else:
                    self.embeds[y][offset] = inner
            self.embeds[x] = {}
        return True


def recover(database, image, base):
    """Scan every function and unify; returns the TypeGraph."""
    functions = {f["addr"] for f in database["functions"] if f["size"]}
    used = argument_use(database, image, base)
    callers = collections.defaultdict(set)
    events = []
    for func in database["functions"]:
        if not func["size"]:
            continue
        for event in scan(func, image, base, functions, used):
            events.append((func["addr"], event))
            if event[0] in ("link", "embed") and event[-1] is not None:
                callers[event[-1]].add(func["addr"])

    graph = TypeGraph()
    for owner, event in events:
        if event[0] == "access":
            _kind, term, offset, width, kind, signed, is_store = event
            field = graph.field(graph.node(term), offset)
            field.uses[(width, kind, signed, is_store)] += 1
            field.functions.add(owner)
    # Specific links first, so a generic routine meets established types and is
    # refused instead of fusing them before their own evidence arrives.
    links = [event for _owner, event in events if event[0] in ("link", "embed")]
    links.sort(key=lambda event: len(callers.get(event[-1], ())) if event[-1] else 0)
    for event in links:
        if event[0] == "link":
            graph.join(graph.node(event[1]), graph.node(event[2]))
        else:
            graph.embed(graph.node(event[1]), event[2], graph.node(event[3]))
    return graph


def types(graph):
    """Roots that have fields, as {root: fields}."""
    found = {}
    for node in range(len(graph.parent)):
        if graph.find(node) == node and graph.fields[node]:
            found[node] = graph.fields[node]
    return found


def quality(graph) -> dict:
    """Agreement on what the join guard never checks, at shared offsets."""
    shared = kind_agree = kind_total = sign_agree = sign_total = 0
    for fields in types(graph).values():
        for field in fields.values():
            if len(field.functions) < 2:
                continue
            shared += 1
            kinds = {use[1] for use in field.uses
                     if use[0] == 4 and use[1] not in ("zero", "derived")}
            if kinds:
                kind_total += 1
                kind_agree += len(kinds) == 1
            signs = {use[2] for use in field.uses if use[2] is not None and use[0] < 4}
            if signs:
                sign_total += 1
                sign_agree += len(signs) == 1
    return {
        "shared offsets": shared,
        "float/int agreement": kind_agree / max(1, kind_total),
        "signedness agreement": sign_agree / max(1, sign_total),
    }


class Catalog:
    """Recovered types, named and queryable by the code emitter.

    Names are placeholders, like the function names, and are derived from the
    evidence so they stay stable between runs: a type is named after the
    lowest-addressed function that takes it as an argument (`S_0035F0A0_a0` is
    the type of argument 0 of func_0035F0A0), or that returns it; a type known
    only as the target of a pointer field is named after that field
    (`S_0035F0A0_a0_p1C`).
    """

    def __init__(self, graph: TypeGraph) -> None:
        self.graph = graph
        self.roots = types(graph)
        self.names = {}
        self.globals = None
        self._arrays = {}
        if GLOBALS in graph.ids:
            # Kept even with no direct fields: a program whose globals are only
            # ever reached as objects passed to functions still has them.
            root = graph.find(graph.ids[GLOBALS])
            self.roots.setdefault(root, graph.fields[root])
            self.globals = root
            self.names[root] = "globals"
        named = []
        for root in self.roots:
            terms = sorted(t for t in graph.slots[root] if t[0] in ("arg", "ret"))
            if terms:
                term = terms[0]
                suffix = "a%d" % term[2] if term[0] == "arg" else "r"
                named.append(("S_%08X_%s" % (term[1], suffix), root))
        for name, root in sorted(named):
            self.names[root] = name
        # Name pointer-only types after the field that leads to them, breadth
        # first from the named ones so the shortest description wins.
        frontier = [root for root, _name in sorted(self.names.items(), key=lambda i: i[1])]
        while frontier:
            following = []
            for root in frontier:
                for offset in sorted(self.roots[root]):
                    target = self.pointee(root, offset)
                    if target is not None and target not in self.names:
                        if root == self.globals:
                            # What global variable 0x4876E8 points to.
                            self.names[target] = "S_g%08X" % (offset & 0xFFFFFFFF)
                        else:
                            self.names[target] = "%s_p%s" % (
                                self.names[root], _offset_name(offset))
                        following.append(target)
                for offset, inner in sorted(self.embedded(root).items()):
                    if inner not in self.names:
                        if root == self.globals:
                            self.names[inner] = "S_g%08X_obj" % (offset & 0xFFFFFFFF)
                        else:
                            self.names[inner] = "%s_e%s" % (
                                self.names[root], _offset_name(offset))
                        following.append(inner)
            frontier = following
        for root in sorted(self.roots):
            self.names.setdefault(root, "S_node%d" % root)

    def slot(self, function: int, index: int):
        node = self.graph.ids.get(("arg", function, index))
        if node is None:
            return None
        root = self.graph.find(node)
        return root if root in self.roots else None

    def field(self, root: int, offset: int):
        return self.roots.get(root, {}).get(offset)

    def pointee(self, root: int, offset: int):
        field = self.field(root, offset)
        if field is None or field.target is None:
            return None
        target = self.graph.find(field.target)
        return target if target in self.roots else None

    # The catalog is read-only once built, so these are computed once per type.
    # Recomputing them on every lookup was most of emission's time - eleven minutes
    # of a run - because the global address space embeds thousands of objects and
    # each typed access scanned all of them.

    def embedded(self, root: int):
        """{offset: root} for the types embedded in this one that have fields."""
        cache = self.__dict__.setdefault("_embedded_cache", {})
        if root not in cache:
            found = {}
            for offset, node in self.graph.embeds[root].items():
                inner = self.graph.find(node)
                if inner in self.roots and inner != root:
                    found[offset] = inner
            cache[root] = found
        return cache[root]

    def extent(self, root: int) -> int:
        """One past the last byte any field of the type is known to occupy."""
        cache = self.__dict__.setdefault("_extent_cache", {})
        if root not in cache:
            cache[root] = max(offset + max(field.widths() or {4}) for offset, field
                              in self.roots[root].items())
        return cache[root]

    def covering(self, root: int, offset: int) -> list:
        """(at, inner) for each embedded type whose extent covers `offset`,
        nearest first."""
        cache = self.__dict__.setdefault("_covering_cache", {})
        if root not in cache:
            items = sorted(self.embedded(root).items())
            starts = [at for at, _inner in items]
            spans = [self.extent(inner) for _at, inner in items]
            cache[root] = (starts, items, spans, max(spans, default=0))
        starts, items, spans, widest = cache[root]
        found = []
        index = bisect.bisect_right(starts, offset) - 1
        while index >= 0 and offset - starts[index] < widest:
            if offset < starts[index] + spans[index]:
                found.append(items[index])
            index -= 1
        return found

    def locate(self, root: int, offset: int):
        """Where a field at `offset` of `root` is: [(embed offset, inner root)...], field.

        A direct field wins. Otherwise the field is looked for in an embedded type
        whose extent covers the offset, recursively. Returns None if neither has it.
        """
        field = self.field(root, offset)
        if field is not None:
            return [], root, offset, field
        for at, inner in self.covering(root, offset):
            found = self.locate(inner, offset - at)
            if found is not None:
                path, owner, local, field = found
                return [(at, inner)] + path, owner, local, field
        return None

    def arrays(self, root: int) -> dict:
        """{start: (stride, count)} for the arrays in a type; count None if unbounded.

        Two kinds of evidence. A field the code indexes with a variable is element 0
        of an array of that stride - its length is not known. And a run of fields
        with the same access flavour at a fixed spacing is an array the code walked
        with an unrolled loop; there the run gives the length.

        Runs need to be long to count. A struct of eight consecutive ints looks
        exactly like an int array of eight, and calling a real struct an array
        would misdescribe it, so contiguous runs need 16 elements; a run with gaps
        between elements - records, each with several fields - needs 6. Global
        memory gets no run detection at all: neighbouring globals are usually
        separate variables.
        """
        if root in self._arrays:
            return self._arrays[root]
        fields = self.roots.get(root, {})
        found = {}
        for offset, field in fields.items():
            if field.strides:
                stride = max(sorted(field.strides), key=lambda s: field.strides[s])
                found[offset] = (stride, None)
        if root != self.globals:
            found.update(self._runs(fields, found))
        self._arrays[root] = found
        return found

    def _runs(self, fields, taken) -> dict:
        by_shape = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for offset, field in fields.items():
            shape = (self.read_flavour(field), self.write_width(field))
            by_shape[shape].append(offset)
        runs = {}
        for shape, offsets in by_shape.items():
            width = (shape[0] or (shape[1], None))[0]
            if not width:
                continue
            offsets.sort()
            members = set(offsets)
            claimed = set()
            for position, start in enumerate(offsets):
                if start in claimed or start in taken:
                    continue
                best = (0, 0)
                for following in offsets[position + 1:position + 9]:
                    stride = following - start
                    if stride < width or stride > 0x10000:
                        continue
                    count = 1
                    while start + count * stride in members:
                        count += 1
                    best = max(best, (count, -stride))
                count, stride = best[0], -best[1]
                needed = 16 if stride == width else 6
                if count >= needed:
                    runs[start] = (stride, count)
                    claimed.update(start + i * stride for i in range(count))
        return runs

    def element(self, root: int, offset: int):
        """(start, index) if a constant offset falls on an element of a known run."""
        for start, (stride, count) in self.arrays(root).items():
            if count is None or offset < start:
                continue
            index, remainder = divmod(offset - start, stride)
            if remainder == 0 and index < count:
                return start, index
        return None

    def candidates(self, root: int, offset: int):
        """Every way to reach a field at `offset`, best first.

        For an ordinary type the direct field comes first, as in `locate`. For the
        global address space it comes last: a global object's fields read as
        `g_0049A278_obj.f_4()`, and the same object's first field should not read
        as an unrelated-looking `g_0049A278()` just because the scan also saw it
        accessed directly.
        """
        direct = self.field(root, offset)
        nested = []
        for at, inner in self.covering(root, offset):
            for path, owner, local, field in self.candidates(inner, offset - at):
                nested.append(([(at, inner)] + path, owner, local, field))
        found = [([], root, offset, direct)] if direct is not None else []
        return nested + found if root == self.globals else found + nested

    @staticmethod
    def read_flavour(field):
        """The (width, signed) the field is most often loaded with, or None."""
        loads = collections.Counter()
        for (width, kind, signed, is_store), count in field.uses.items():
            if is_store or width == BLOCK_WIDTH:
                continue
            # lwc1 reads a raw 32-bit pattern; the expression model treats it as
            # an unsigned word load, so it shares that flavour.
            loads[(width, bool(signed))] += count
        if not loads:
            return None
        return max(sorted(loads), key=lambda key: loads[key])

    @staticmethod
    def write_width(field):
        widths = collections.Counter()
        for (width, _kind, _signed, is_store), count in field.uses.items():
            if is_store and width != BLOCK_WIDTH:
                widths[width] += count
        if not widths:
            return None
        return max(sorted(widths), key=lambda key: widths[key])

    @staticmethod
    def kind(field) -> str:
        kinds = {kind for (width, kind, _s, _st) in field.uses
                 if kind not in ("zero", "derived") and width != BLOCK_WIDTH}
        if kinds == {"float"}:
            return "float"
        if kinds == {"int"}:
            return "int"
        return "mixed" if kinds else "unknown"

    def functions(self, root: int) -> set:
        found = set()
        for field in self.roots[root].values():
            found |= field.functions
        return found


def _offset_name(offset: int) -> str:
    return "%X" % offset if offset >= 0 else "m%X" % -offset

```

`ps2decomp/structure.py`:

```py
"""Structured C++ from machine code: loops and ifs instead of gotos, locals for registers.

Lifted code (lift.py) is one statement per instruction over the register context,
with gotos for control flow: correct and complete, and hard to read. This renders
the same statements in a form a person can follow:

* Control flow is structured. Natural loops become `for (;;)` with `continue` and
  `break`; a two-way branch whose arms meet again at its immediate post-dominator
  becomes `if`/`else`. Whatever does not fit - irreducible flow, jumps into the
  middle of another construct - stays a `goto`, so the result is always faithful.
* Registers are named locals (`a0`, `v0`, `f12`, `hi`), copied from the context on
  entry and back to it around anything that takes the context: calls, syscalls,
  the moves to and from VU0, returns. `out()` and `in()` do the copying.

The output keeps lift.py's interface - `void F_xxxxxxxx(lifted::Context& c)` - so
it is verified exactly as lifted code is, comparing the whole register file and
memory against the original. Functions with jump tables or linking branches are
left to the plain lifted form.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import struct

from . import lift
from .r5900 import DISASM

GPR_NAMES = ("zero", "at", "v0", "v1", "a0", "a1", "a2", "a3",
             "t0", "t1", "t2", "t3", "t4", "t5", "t6", "t7",
             "s0", "s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s5", "s6", "s7",
             "t8", "t9", "k0", "k1", "gp", "sp", "fp", "ra")
SCALARS = ("hi", "lo", "hi1", "lo1", "acc", "fcc", "sa")

# Callee-saved registers. A function saves them on entry and restores them before
# it returns, so to its caller they never change; here they are plain locals that
# are never written back, and the save and restore - stack traffic the caller
# cannot observe - are left out. A function that breaks the convention fails its
# verification and keeps the plain lifted form.
CALLEE_SAVED = (16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 30)
_SAVED = r"(?P<reg>s[0-7]|fp|ra)"
_OFFSET = r"(?: \+ (?P<off>0x[0-9A-F]+)u)?"
_SLOT = r"\(\(u32\)sp%s\)" % _OFFSET
_SPILLS = [
    re.compile(r"^\s*\{ u32 q = %s & ~0xFu; Write64\(q, %s\); Write64\(q \+ 8, c\.rh\[\d+\]\); \}$"
               % (_SLOT, _SAVED)),
    re.compile(r"^\s*Write64\(\(u32\)sp%s, %s\);$" % (_OFFSET, _SAVED)),
    re.compile(r"^\s*\{ u32 q = %s & ~0xFu; u64 lo = Read64\(q\); u64 hi = Read64\(q \+ 8\); "
               r"%s = lo; c\.rh\[\d+\] = hi; \}$" % (_SLOT, _SAVED)),
    re.compile(r"^\s*%s = ReadU64\(\(u32\)sp%s\);$" % (_SAVED, _OFFSET)),
]


def _save_slots(code, start: int):
    """{(register name, stack offset)} the prologue saves callee-saved registers
    in: the stores of them to the stack before the first branch, jump or call.
    None when the function writes a callee-saved register it never saves - its
    callers would see the change, so nothing about its saves can be elided.
    A store of one the function has already set is not a save but data - in
    0x00817820 (Resident Evil Outbreak) `daddu $s3, $a3` then `sd $s3,
    8($sp)` passed a callee an argument on the stack, and dropping it as a
    save left the slot's old value (1.0f) to be read as a pointer."""
    slots, saved, written = set(), set(), set()
    in_prologue = True
    for ins in code:
        if in_prologue and ins.mnemonic in ("sd", "sq", "sw") and ins.rs == 29 \
                and (ins.rt in CALLEE_SAVED or ins.rt == 31) and ins.rt not in written:
            slots.add((GPR_NAMES[ins.rt], ins.imm & 0xFFFF))
            saved.add(ins.rt)
        if ins.is_branch or ins.is_jump or ins.is_call:
            in_prologue = False
        # Eliding keeps a saved register in a local, and only its low 64 bits:
        # a COP2 move reaches it through the context, and a 128-bit write sets
        # its upper half there - both of which the caller would then see. In
        # 0x002284B0 `qmfc2 $s0` left a VU0 value in its caller's $s0.
        if ins.mnemonic in ("qmfc2", "qmtc2", "cfc2", "ctc2") and ins.rt in CALLEE_SAVED:
            return None
        rd = _written_gpr(ins)
        if rd in CALLEE_SAVED:
            written.add(rd)
            wide = ins.mnemonic == "lq" or (ins.mnemonic.startswith("p") and ins.mnemonic != "pref")
            if wide and not (ins.mnemonic == "lq" and ins.rs == 29
                             and (GPR_NAMES[rd], ins.imm & 0xFFFF) in slots):
                return None
    return slots if written <= saved else None


def _written_gpr(ins):
    """The general register an instruction writes, or None (from the analysis)."""
    from .structs import _written_register
    return _written_register(ins)


def _is_spill(text: str, slots) -> bool:
    """Whether `text` saves or restores a callee-saved register in its own save
    slot - bookkeeping no caller can see. A load of one from any other stack slot
    is data (a local the code keeps in a saved register) and is kept: dropping
    such a load once made software double multiplication loop forever."""
    if not slots:
        return False
    for pattern in _SPILLS:
        match = pattern.match(text)
        if match and (match.group("reg"), int(match.group("off") or "0", 16)) in slots:
            return True
    return False


class Unstructurable(lift.Refused):
    """This function is left in the plain lifted form."""


class Block:
    def __init__(self, start):
        self.start = start
        self.code = []           # statements before the terminator
        self.kind = "fall"       # fall, jump, cond, return, tail
        self.condition = None
        self.slot = ""           # the delay slot's statement
        self.likely = False
        self.taken = None        # address
        self.next = None         # fallthrough or jump target address
        self.tail = None         # address of a tail transfer
        self.succs = []


def _blocks(code, start, end, ranges=None):
    """Basic blocks keyed by start address, with terminators decoded. `ranges`
    are the function's pieces, the body first (see lift.lift_function)."""
    ranges = ranges or [(start, end)]
    inside = lambda address: any(first <= address < last for first, last in ranges)
    by_address = {ins.addr: ins for ins in code}
    leaders = {start} | {first for first, _last in ranges}
    for ins in code:
        if ins.has_delay_slot:
            if ins.mnemonic == "jr" and ins.rs != 31:
                raise Unstructurable("jump table")
            if ins.mnemonic in ("bltzal", "bgezal", "bltzall", "bgezall"):
                raise Unstructurable("linking branch")
            if not ins.is_call and ins.mnemonic not in ("jr", "jalr") and inside(ins.target):
                leaders.add(ins.target)
            if not ins.is_call:
                leaders.add(ins.addr + 8)
    slots = {ins.addr + 4 for ins in code if ins.has_delay_slot}
    if leaders & slots:
        raise Unstructurable("a jump lands in a delay slot")
    leaders = sorted(a for a in leaders if inside(a))
    blocks = {}
    for i, first in enumerate(leaders):
        block = Block(first)
        # A block ends at the next leader or its piece's end, whichever is first:
        # pieces are not contiguous, and one does not fall into the next.
        piece_end = next(last for f, last in ranges if f <= first < last)
        limit = min(leaders[i + 1], piece_end) if i + 1 < len(leaders) else piece_end
        address = first
        while address < limit:
            ins = by_address[address]
            if not ins.has_delay_slot:
                block.code.append(lift.statement(ins))
                address += 4
                continue
            slot = lift.statement(by_address[address + 4])
            m = ins.mnemonic
            after = address + 8
            link = "c.r[31] = 0x%08Xull;" % after
            if m == "jal":
                block.code += [slot, link, "lifted::Call(c, 0x%08Xu);" % ins.target]
                address = after
                continue
            if m == "jalr":
                block.code += ["{ u32 target = (u32)%s;" % lift._r(ins.rs), slot, link,
                               "lifted::Call(c, target); }"]
                address = after
                continue
            block.slot = slot
            if m == "jr":
                block.kind = "return"
            elif m in ("j", "b"):
                if inside(ins.target):
                    block.kind, block.next = "jump", ins.target
                else:
                    block.kind, block.tail = "tail", ins.target
            else:
                block.kind = "cond"
                block.condition = lift._CONDITIONS[m] % {"a": lift._r(ins.rs), "b": lift._r(ins.rt)}
                block.likely = m.endswith("l")
                block.taken = ins.target
                block.next = after
            address = after
            break
        else:
            block.next = limit           # falls into the next block, or off the end
        blocks[first] = block
    return blocks


def _successors(block, blocks):
    out = []
    for target in (block.taken, block.next):
        if target is not None and target in blocks and target not in out:
            out.append(target)
    return out


def _dominators(order, preds, entry):
    """Immediate dominators (Cooper, Harvey and Kennedy)."""
    index = {node: i for i, node in enumerate(order)}
    idom = {entry: entry}

    def intersect(a, b):
        while a != b:
            while index[a] > index[b]:
                a = idom[a]
            while index[b] > index[a]:
                b = idom[b]
        return a

    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for node in order[1:]:
            known = [p for p in preds[node] if p in idom]
            if not known:
                continue
            new = known[0]
            for p in known[1:]:
                new = intersect(p, new)
            if idom.get(node) != new:
                idom[node] = new
                changed = True
    return idom


def _reverse_postorder(entry, succs):
    seen, order = set(), []

    def visit(node):
        stack = [(node, iter(succs[node]))]
        seen.add(node)
        while stack:
```
