```py
            current, children = stack[-1]
            child = next(children, None)
            if child is None:
                order.append(current)
                stack.pop()
            elif child not in seen:
                seen.add(child)
                stack.append((child, iter(succs[child])))

    visit(entry)
    return list(reversed(order))


class _Emitter:
    def __init__(self, blocks, start, end):
        self.blocks = blocks
        self.end = end
        self.succs = {a: _successors(b, blocks) for a, b in blocks.items()}
        self.order = _reverse_postorder(start, self.succs)
        reachable = set(self.order)
        preds = {a: [] for a in reachable}
        for a in reachable:
            for s in self.succs[a]:
                preds[s].append(a)
        self.idom = _dominators(self.order, preds, start)
        # Post-dominators: dominators of the reversed graph from a virtual exit.
        exit_node = "exit"
        rsuccs = {exit_node: []}
        rpreds = {a: [] for a in reachable}
        rpreds[exit_node] = []
        for a in reachable:
            rsuccs.setdefault(a, [])
            outs = [s for s in self.succs[a]]
            if not outs or blocks[a].kind in ("return", "tail") or (
                    blocks[a].kind in ("fall", "cond") and blocks[a].next not in blocks):
                outs = outs + [exit_node]
            for s in outs:
                rsuccs.setdefault(s, []).append(a)
        rorder = _reverse_postorder(exit_node, rsuccs)
        rpred = {n: [] for n in rorder}
        for n in rorder:
            for s in rsuccs.get(n, []):
                if s in rpred:
                    rpred[s].append(n)
        self.ipdom = _dominators(rorder, rpred, exit_node)
        # Loops: a back edge goes to a block that dominates its source.
        self.headers = set()
        self.loops = {}
        for a in reachable:
            for s in self.succs[a]:
                if self._dominates(s, a):
                    self.headers.add(s)
                    self.loops.setdefault(s, set()).add(a)
        self.body = {h: self._natural_loop(h, sources, preds) for h, sources in self.loops.items()}
        self.emitted = set()
        self.labels = set()
        # Small blocks reached a second time are emitted again rather than jumped
        # to - a shared error path, the tail of an `a || b` - up to this many.
        self.copies_left = 64

    def _duplicable(self, node):
        """Whether a jump to this already-emitted block may be a copy of it instead."""
        block = self.blocks.get(node)
        if block is None or node in self.headers or self.copies_left <= 0:
            return False
        if len([s for s in block.code if s]) > 6 or block.kind == "cond":
            return False
        self.copies_left -= 1
        return True

    def _returns_soon(self, node, budget=6):
        """A short run of blocks that ends the function: emitting it at a loop exit
        costs less than a goto past the loop to it."""
        block = self.blocks.get(node)
        if block is None or node in self.headers:
            return False
        size = len([x for x in block.code if x]) + (1 if block.slot else 0)
        if size > budget:
            return False
        if block.kind in ("return", "tail"):
            return True
        if block.kind in ("fall", "jump") and block.next in self.blocks:
            return self._returns_soon(block.next, budget - size)
        return False

    def _dominates(self, a, b):
        while True:
            if a == b:
                return True
            parent = self.idom.get(b)
            if parent is None or parent == b:
                return False
            b = parent

    def _natural_loop(self, header, sources, preds):
        body, work = {header}, list(sources)
        while work:
            node = work.pop()
            if node not in body:
                body.add(node)
                work.extend(preds[node])
        return body

    def _follow(self, header):
        """The single block a loop exits to, or None."""
        exits = {s for n in self.body[header] for s in self.succs[n] if s not in self.body[header]}
        return next(iter(exits)) if len(exits) == 1 else None

    def emit(self, node, stop, loops, depth):
        lines = []
        pad = "    " * depth
        while node is not None and node != stop:
            if node not in self.blocks:
                lines.append(pad + "out(); lifted::TailCall(c, 0x%08Xu, entry_ra, entry_sp); return;" % node)
                return lines
            if loops and node not in self.body[loops[-1][0]]:
                # Leaving the loop: break, a goto to wherever it goes, or - for a
                # small block that returns - that block, right here.
                jump = self._transfer(node, loops, depth)
                if jump is not None:
                    lines.append(jump)
                    return lines
            if node in self.emitted:
                if self._duplicable(node):
                    body, node = self._chain(node, stop, loops, depth, copy=True)
                    lines += body
                    continue
                lines.append(pad + "goto L_%08X;" % node)
                self.labels.add(node)
                return lines
            if node in self.headers and (not loops or loops[-1][0] != node):
                follow = self._follow(node)
                lines.append(pad + "for (;;) {")
                lines.append(pad + "    lifted::Tick(c, 0x%08Xu);" % node)
                inner = self._block(node, None, loops + [(node, follow)], depth + 1)
                lines += inner
                lines.append(pad + "}")
                node = follow
                continue
            body, node = self._chain(node, stop, loops, depth)
            lines += body
        return lines

    def _block(self, node, stop, loops, depth):
        """The header's code then the rest of the loop body (`node` already marked)."""
        lines, nxt = self._chain(node, stop, loops, depth)
        if nxt is not None:
            lines += self.emit(nxt, stop, loops, depth)
        return lines

    def _transfer(self, target, loops, depth):
        """The statement for an edge to `target`, or None to fall into it."""
        pad = "    " * depth
        if target is not None and target not in self.blocks:
            return pad + "out(); lifted::TailCall(c, 0x%08Xu, entry_ra, entry_sp); return;" % target
        if loops:
            header, follow = loops[-1]
            if target == header:
                return pad + "continue;"
            if target == follow:
                return pad + "break;"
            if target not in self.body[header]:
                if self._returns_soon(target):
                    return None
                self.labels.add(target)
                return pad + "goto L_%08X;" % target
        if target in self.emitted and not self._duplicable(target):
            self.labels.add(target)
            return pad + "goto L_%08X;" % target
        return None

    def _chain(self, node, stop, loops, depth, copy=False):
        """Emit one block; returns (lines, the block to continue with or None).

        A copy - a second emission of a small block - carries no label: the label
        stays with the first.
        """
        pad = "    " * depth
        block = self.blocks[node]
        self.emitted.add(node)
        lines = [] if copy else ["@L_%08X" % node]   # a label placeholder, kept if targeted
        lines += [pad + s for s in block.code if s]
        if block.kind == "return":
            lines += [pad + s for s in (block.slot,) if s]
            lines.append(pad + "out(); return;")
            return lines, None
        if block.kind == "tail":
            lines += [pad + s for s in (block.slot,) if s]
            lines.append(pad + "out(); lifted::TailCall(c, 0x%08Xu, entry_ra, entry_sp); return;" % block.tail)
            return lines, None
        if block.kind in ("fall", "jump"):
            if block.slot:
                lines.append(pad + block.slot)
            target = block.next
            if target is not None and target not in self.blocks:
                lines.append(pad + "out(); lifted::TailCall(c, 0x%08Xu, entry_ra, entry_sp); "
                             "return;  /* runs off the end */" % target)
                return lines, None
            jump = self._transfer(target, loops, depth)
            if jump is not None:
                lines.append(jump)
                return lines, None
            return lines, target
        # A two-way branch.
        taken, fall = block.taken, block.next
        plain = not block.likely and not block.slot
        if block.likely:
            lines.append(pad + "if (%s) {" % block.condition)
            if block.slot:
                lines.append(pad + "    " + block.slot)
        elif plain:
            # Nothing runs between the test and the branch: no temporary needed.
            lines.append(pad + "if (%s) {" % block.condition)
        else:
            lines.append(pad + "{ const bool t = %s;" % block.condition)
            if block.slot:
                lines.append(pad + "  " + block.slot)
            lines.append(pad + "  if (t) {")
        join = self.ipdom.get(node)
        if join == "exit" or (loops and join not in self.body[loops[-1][0]]):
            join = None
        inner = depth + (1 if block.likely else 1)
        lines += self._arm(taken, join, loops, inner + (0 if block.likely else 0))
        lines.append(pad + ("} else {" if block.likely or plain else "  } else {"))
        lines += self._arm(fall, join, loops, inner)
        lines.append(pad + ("}" if block.likely or plain else "  } }"))
        if join is None:
            return lines, None
        jump = self._transfer(join, loops, depth)
        if jump is not None:
            lines.append(jump)
            return lines, None
        return lines, join

    def _arm(self, target, join, loops, depth):
        if target == join:
            return []
        jump = self._transfer(target, loops, depth + 1)
        if jump is not None:
            return [jump]
        return self.emit(target, join, loops, depth + 1)


_ATOM = r"(?:[A-Za-z_]\w*|0x[0-9A-F]+u(?:ll)?|\d+u(?:ll)?)"


def tidy(line: str) -> str:
    """Rewrites that cannot change a value, for reading. The structured function is
    verified after them, so a wrong one would show as a disagreement."""
    line = line.replace("lifted::", "").replace("generated::", "")
    # Sx32 keeps the low 32 bits, which a (u32) on an addend or a left shift
    # cannot change.
    line = re.sub(r"Sx32\(\(u32\)(%s) ([+-]|<<) \(u32\)(%s)\)" % (_ATOM, _ATOM),
                  r"Sx32(\1 \2 \3)", line)
    line = re.sub(r"Sx32\(\(u32\)(%s) ([+-]|<<) (%s)\)" % (_ATOM, _ATOM), r"Sx32(\1 \2 \3)", line)
    # Adding or or-ing zero: how MIPS spells a move.
    line = re.sub(r"= (%s) [+|] 0ull;" % _ATOM, r"= \1;", line)
    line = re.sub(r"= 0ull [+|] (%s);" % _ATOM, r"= \1;", line)
    line = re.sub(r"Sx32\((%s) \+ 0x0u\)" % _ATOM, r"Sx32(\1)", line)
    line = re.sub(r"Sx32\(0ull \+ (%s)\)" % _ATOM, r"Sx32(\1)", line)
    line = re.sub(r"\(u32\)(%s) \+ 0x0u\b" % _ATOM, r"(u32)\1", line)
    # A sign-extended literal below 2^31 is that literal; small ones read better
    # in decimal where they are compared.
    line = re.sub(r"Sx32\(0x([0-7]?[0-9A-F]{1,7})u\)", r"0x\1ull", line)
    line = re.sub(r"\(s64\)0x([0-9A-F]{1,4})ull\b", lambda m: str(int(m.group(1), 16)), line)
    line = re.sub(r"\(u(32|64)\)\((0x[0-9A-F]+ull)\)", r"(u\1)\2", line)
    # A comparison's 0 or 1, widened and tested against zero, is the comparison.
    operand = r"(?:\(s64\))?(?:%s|\d+)" % _ATOM
    line = re.sub(r"\(\(u64\)\((%s (?:<|==|!=) %s)\)\) != 0ull" % (operand, operand),
                  r"\1", line)
    line = re.sub(r"\(\(u64\)\((%s (?:<|==|!=) %s)\)\) == 0ull" % (operand, operand),
                  r"!(\1)", line)
    return _inner_sign_extensions(line)


def _closing(text, open_at):
    """The index of the parenthesis closing the one at `open_at`, or None."""
    depth = 0
    for i in range(open_at, len(text)):
        if text[i] == "(":
            depth += 1
        elif text[i] == ")":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return i
    return None


def _inner_sign_extensions(line):
    """`Sx32(a + (Sx32(b)))` is `Sx32(a + (b))`: the outer Sx32 keeps only the low
    32 bits of the sum, which depend only on the low 32 bits of each addend - and
    those Sx32 does not change. Likewise for subtraction."""
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for outer in re.finditer(r"Sx32\(", line):
            open_at = outer.end() - 1
            close = _closing(line, open_at)
            if close is None:
                continue
            argument = line[open_at + 1:close]
            for inner in re.finditer(r"(?<= [+-] )\(Sx32\(|^\(Sx32\(", argument):
                start = inner.start()
                end = _closing(argument, start)
                if end is None:
                    continue
                # Only a direct addend: `(Sx32(...))` with nothing else inside.
                if _closing(argument, start + 5) != end - 1:
                    continue
                # And the outer argument is a plain sum or difference at top level.
                depth, top = 0, []
                for i, ch in enumerate(argument):
                    depth += ch == "("
                    depth -= ch == ")"
                    if depth == 0 and ch in "*/&|^<>?%":
                        top.append(ch)
                if top:
                    continue
                argument = argument[:start] + "(" + argument[start + 6:end - 1] + ")" + argument[end + 1:]
                line = line[:open_at + 1] + argument + line[close:]
                changed = True
                break
            if changed:
                break
    # (u32)(Sx32(x)) is (u32)(x): the low 32 bits are what Sx32 keeps.
    while True:
        match = re.search(r"\(u32\)\(Sx32\(", line)
        if not match:
            return line
        open_at = match.start() + 5
        end = _closing(line, open_at)
        if end is None or _closing(line, open_at + 5) != end - 1:
            return line
        line = line[:open_at] + "(" + line[open_at + 6:end - 1] + ")" + line[end + 1:]


def _loop_test(lines, k):
    """At lines[k], `if (C) { continue; } else { break; }` (or the reverse):
    (the condition to repeat on, the number of lines it takes), or None."""
    shapes = ((("continue;", "} else {", "break;", "}"), False),
              (("break;", "} else {", "continue;", "}"), True),
              (("continue;", "}", "break;"), False),
              (("break;", "}", "continue;"), True))
    head = lines[k].strip()
    if not (head.startswith("if (") and head.endswith(") {")):
        return None
    condition = head[4:-3]
    for shape, negate in shapes:
        rest = [line.strip() for line in lines[k + 1:k + 1 + len(shape)]]
        if tuple(rest) == shape:
            return ("!(%s)" % condition if negate else condition), 1 + len(shape)
    return None


_FLIP = {"==": "!=", "!=": "==", "<": ">=", ">=": "<", ">": "<=", "<=": ">"}


def negate(condition: str) -> str:
    """The opposite condition, spelled as plainly as it safely can be."""
    match = re.match(r"^([^ ()]*(?:\([us]64\)[^ ()]+)?) (==|!=|<|>=|>|<=) ([^ ()]+)$", condition)
    if match:
        return "%s %s %s" % (match.group(1), _FLIP[match.group(2)], match.group(3))
    if condition.startswith("!(") and _closing(condition, 1) == len(condition) - 1:
        return condition[2:-1]
    return "!(%s)" % condition


def _close_of(lines, k, texts):
    """The first line after k that is exactly one of `texts`, or None."""
    return next((j for j in range(k + 1, len(lines)) if lines[j] in texts), None)


_PLAIN_SLOT = re.compile(r"^([a-z][a-z0-9]*) = [^;]*;$")


def hoist_delay_slots(lines):
    """`{ const bool t = C; S; if (t) {...} else {...} }` is `S; if (C) {...}
    else {...}` when S cannot change C: S is a plain assignment to a name C does
    not mention, writing no memory and calling nothing. With the slot elided, it
    is just `if (C)`."""
    lines = list(lines)
    k = 0
    while k + 1 < len(lines):
        head = lines[k].strip()
        if not (head.startswith("{ const bool t = ") and head.endswith(";")):
            k += 1
            continue
        pad = lines[k][:len(lines[k]) - len(lines[k].lstrip())]
        condition = head[len("{ const bool t = "):-1]
        if lines[k + 1] == pad + "  if (t) {":
            slot, test = None, k + 1
        else:
            slot, test = lines[k + 1].strip(), k + 2
            match = _PLAIN_SLOT.match(slot)
            if (test >= len(lines) or lines[test] != pad + "  if (t) {" or not match
                    or re.search(r"\b%s\b" % match.group(1), condition)
                    or any(word in slot for word in ("Write", "Call", "(c"))
                    or "(c" in condition):
                k += 1
                continue
        middle = _close_of(lines, test, (pad + "  } else {", pad + "  } }"))
        if middle is None:
            k += 1
            continue
        end = middle if lines[middle] == pad + "  } }" else _close_of(lines, middle, (pad + "  } }",))
        if end is None:
            k += 1
            continue
        lines[end] = pad + "}"
        if middle != end:
            lines[middle] = pad + "} else {"
        lines[k:test + 1] = ([pad + slot] if slot else []) + [pad + "if (%s) {" % condition]
        k += 1
    return lines


def invert_empty_then(lines):
    """`if (C) { } else { A }` is `if (!C) { A }`."""
    out = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if (out and stripped == "} else {" and out[-1].strip().startswith("if (")
                and out[-1].strip().endswith(") {")
                and out[-1][:len(out[-1]) - len(out[-1].lstrip())]
                == line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]):
            pad = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
            out[-1] = pad + "if (%s) {" % negate(out[-1].strip()[4:-3])
            continue
        out.append(line)
    return out


_LABEL = re.compile(r"^L_([0-9A-F]{8}):;$")
_GOTO = re.compile(r"goto L_([0-9A-F]{8});")


def tick_backward_gotos(lines):
    """A goto to a label above it is another turn of a loop, and spends budget
    as one: `{ Tick(c, X); goto L_X; }` - unless the label is a loop header's,
    with its Tick straight after. Without it a loop the structuring left as
    gotos never gives the host control: Resident Evil Outbreak's 0x001A9AC0
    polls a loader for ever, its head a one-instruction block copied onto every
    edge into it (so no header with a Tick is ever emitted)."""
    lines = list(lines)
    seen, ticked = set(), set()
    for k, line in enumerate(lines):
        label = _LABEL.match(line.strip())
        if label:
            seen.add(label.group(1))
            following = next((l.strip() for l in lines[k + 1:] if l.strip()), "")
            if following.endswith("Tick(c, 0x%su);" % label.group(1)):
                ticked.add(label.group(1))
            continue

        def guarded(match):
            target = match.group(1)
            if target not in seen or target in ticked:
                return match.group(0)
            return "{ Tick(c, 0x%su); goto L_%s; }" % (target, target)

        lines[k] = _GOTO.sub(guarded, line)
    return lines


def loop_guards(lines):
    """A loop ending in `if (C) { A continue; } else { break; }` is `if (!C)
    break; A`; and a loop whose first test that is - `for (;;) { Tick; if (!C)
    break; ...}` - is `while (C) { Tick; ... }`."""
    lines = list(lines)
    k = 0
    while k < len(lines):
        if lines[k].strip() != "for (;;) {":
            k += 1
            continue
        pad = lines[k][:len(lines[k]) - len(lines[k].lstrip())]
        close = _close_of(lines, k, (pad + "}",))
        if close is None:
            k += 1
            continue
        inner = pad + "    "
        arm = inner + "        "
        if (lines[close - 1] == inner + "}" and lines[close - 2] == arm + "break;"
                and lines[close - 3] == inner + "} else {" and lines[close - 4] == arm + "continue;"):
            start = next((j for j in range(close - 5, k, -1)
                          if lines[j].startswith(inner + "if (") and lines[j].endswith(") {")
                          and not lines[j].startswith(inner + " ")), None)
            body = lines[start + 1:close - 4] if start is not None else None
            if body is not None and all(line.startswith(arm) or line.startswith("L_")
                                        or not line.strip() for line in body):
                condition = lines[start].strip()[4:-3]
                lines[start:close] = ([inner + "if (%s) break;" % negate(condition)]
                                      + [line[8:] if line.startswith(arm) else line for line in body])
                close = _close_of(lines, k, (pad + "}",))
        # The guard straight after the tick: a while loop.
        if (k + 2 < close and lines[k + 1].strip().startswith("Tick(c, ")
                and re.match(r"^if \((.*)\) break;$", lines[k + 2].strip())
                and lines[k + 2].startswith(inner + "if (")):
            condition = lines[k + 2].strip()[4:-len(") break;")]
            lines[k:k + 3] = [pad + "while (%s) {" % negate(condition), lines[k + 1]]
        k += 1
    return lines


_LINK = re.compile(r"^(\s*)ra = 0x(00[0-7][0-9A-F]{5})ull;$")
_PLAIN_CALL = re.compile(r"^(\s*)out\(\); Call\(c, (0x[0-9A-F]{8}u)\); in\(\);$")


def fold_links(lines):
    """`ra = R; out(); Call(c, T); in();` is `out(); Call(c, T, R); in();` - the
    link a jal sets, given to the call that uses it."""
    out = []
    for line in lines:
        call = _PLAIN_CALL.match(line)
        link = _LINK.match(out[-1]) if out else None
        if call and link and link.group(1) == call.group(1):
            out[-1] = "%sout(); Call(c, %s, 0x%su); in();" % (call.group(1), call.group(2),
                                                         link.group(2))
            continue
        out.append(line)
    return out


def loops_to_do_while(lines):
    """`for (;;) { ...; if (C) continue; else break; }` is `do { ... } while (C);`
    when nothing else in the body continues - a `continue` in a do-while goes to
    the test, not the top."""
    lines = list(lines)
    k = 0
    while k < len(lines):
        if lines[k].strip() != "for (;;) {":
            k += 1
            continue
        pad = lines[k][:len(lines[k]) - len(lines[k].lstrip())]
        close = next((j for j in range(k + 1, len(lines)) if lines[j] == pad + "}"), None)
        if close is None:
            k += 1
            continue
        found = None
        for start in (close - 5, close - 4):
            test = _loop_test(lines, start) if start > k else None
            if test is not None and start + test[1] == close:
                found = (start, test[0])
        if found is None:
            k += 1
            continue
        start, condition = found
        body = lines[k + 1:start]
        if any("continue;" in line for line in body) or any(
                line.lstrip().startswith("L_") for line in lines[start:close]):
            k += 1
            continue
        lines[k:close + 1] = [pad + "do {"] + body + [pad + "} while (%s);" % condition]
        k += 1
    return lines


_SET_CONSTANT = re.compile(r"^(\s*)([a-z][a-z0-9]*) = (0x[0-9A-F]+)ull;$")
_ADD_CONSTANT = re.compile(r"^(\s*)([a-z][a-z0-9]*) = Sx32\(([a-z][a-z0-9]*) \+ (0x[0-9A-F]+)u\);$")


def drop_empty_else(lines):
    """`} else {` straight before the arm's closing brace: an empty else arm."""
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        following = lines[i + 1].strip() if i + 1 < len(lines) else None
        if line.strip() == "} else {" and following == "}":
            out.append(line.replace("} else {", "}"))
            i += 2
            continue
        if line.strip() == "} else {" and following == "} }":
            out.append(line.replace("} else {", "} }"))
            i += 2
            continue
        out.append(line)
        i += 1
    return out


def fold_constants(lines, strings=None):
    """Join `x = 0x520000; x = Sx32(x + 0xFFFFC220u)` into one constant: how MIPS
    builds a 32-bit address in two steps. Only within straight-line code - any
    line that is not a plain assignment forgets what is known. A constant that
    is the address of a known string says so."""
    strings = strings or {}
    known, out = {}, []
    for line in lines:
        match = _ADD_CONSTANT.match(line)
        if match and match.group(3) in known:
            pad, target, source, addend = match.groups()
            value = (known[source] + int(addend, 16)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
            value = (value - (1 << 32) if value & 0x80000000 else value) & ((1 << 64) - 1)
            line = "%s%s = 0x%08Xull;" % (pad, target, value)
        match = _SET_CONSTANT.match(line)
        if match:
            pad, target, literal = match.groups()
            known[target] = int(literal, 16)
            # Not lui's value alone (its low half zero): the upper half of an
            # address still to be added to, wherever a string begins.
            if known[target] & 0xFFFF:
                line += _string_note(known[target], strings)
            out.append(line)
            continue
        assigned = re.match(r"^\s*([a-z][a-z0-9]*) = ", line)
        if assigned and ";" in line and "{" not in line and "}" not in line:
            known.pop(assigned.group(1), None)
        else:
            known = {}
        out.append(line)
    return out


# A split address once its base register is folded away (liveness.fold puts
# `lui`'s constant in place of the register): the whole address of a memory
# access, or the whole argument of a sign extension. Only there - as a whole
# argument, nothing around it binds tighter than the sum.
_SPLIT_ADDRESS = re.compile(r"((?:Read|Write)(?:U|S)?(?:8|16|32|64)\()\(u32\)(0x[0-9A-F]+)ull \+ (0x[0-9A-F]+)u(?=[),])")
_SPLIT_SIGN_EXTENDED = re.compile(r"\bSx32\(\((0x[0-9A-F]+)ull\) \+ (0x[0-9A-F]+)u\)")
_ASSIGNED_CONSTANT = re.compile(r"^\s*[a-z][a-z0-9]* = (0x[0-9A-F]+)ull;$")


def _string_note(value, strings):
    text = strings.get(value & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    if text is None:
        return ""
    shown = text if len(text) <= 48 else text[:45] + "..."
    return '  /* "%s" */' % shown.encode("unicode_escape").decode("ascii").replace("*/", "*\\/")


def fold_addresses(lines, strings=None):
    """`ReadS32((u32)0x4A0000ull + 0xFFFFB0A0u)` is `ReadS32(0x0049B0A0u)`, and
    `Sx32((0x4C0000ull) + 0xFFFF9AD0u)` the constant it sign-extends: a 32-bit
    address MIPS builds in two steps, whose first step folding put in place of
    its register. A plain assignment of an address of a known string says so."""
    strings = strings or {}
    out = []
    for line in lines:
        line = _SPLIT_ADDRESS.sub(
            lambda m: "%s0x%08Xu" % (m.group(1), (int(m.group(2), 16) + int(m.group(3), 16)) & 0xFFFFFFFF), line)

        def extended(m):
            value = (int(m.group(1), 16) + int(m.group(2), 16)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
            if value & 0x80000000:
                value |= 0xFFFFFFFF00000000
            return "0x%08Xull" % value
        line = _SPLIT_SIGN_EXTENDED.sub(extended, line)
        # Not a value lui made alone (its low half zero): that is the upper
        # half of an address still to be added to, wherever a string begins.
        assigned = _ASSIGNED_CONSTANT.match(line)
        if assigned and "/*" not in line and int(assigned.group(1), 16) & 0xFFFF:
            line += _string_note(int(assigned.group(1), 16), strings)
        out.append(line)
    return out


def _localize(text, gprs, fprs, scalars):
    text = re.sub(r"c\.r\[(\d+)\]", lambda m: _gpr(int(m.group(1)), gprs), text)
    text = re.sub(r"c\.f\[(\d+)\]", lambda m: _fpr(int(m.group(1)), fprs), text)
    for name in SCALARS:
        if re.search(r"\bc\.%s\b" % name, text):
            scalars.add(name)
            text = re.sub(r"\bc\.%s\b" % name, name, text)
    return text


def _gpr(index, used):
    used.add(index)
    return GPR_NAMES[index] if index else "0ull"


def _fpr(index, used):
    used.add(index)
    return "f%d" % index


# Statements that hand the context to something else; registers are synchronised
# around them.
_TAKES_CONTEXT = re.compile(r"\b(?:lifted::)?(Call|TailCall|Syscall|Cop2Move|Vcallms)\(c")


# What a caller can see of a function's registers after it returns, under the
# calling convention: the results, the stack and global pointers, and the
# callee-saved registers (kept as locals that are never written back).
ABI_RETURNED = ("v0", "v1", "sp", "gp", "f0", "f1")
# What a caller relies on finding as it left it: the callee-saved registers,
# integer and float. A structured function keeps them in locals; any it hands
# to its callees through the context (out(), before each call) it must hand
# back as it returns - its epilogue having restored the locals - or its caller
# sees the values it worked with. 0x0042DAE0 used $f20 and $f21 that way,
# restored them into its locals and returned without them: the car select's
# cars were not drawn. Its tests never took a path with a call.
ABI_PRESERVED = ("s0", "s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s5", "s6", "s7", "fp") + tuple("f%d" % i for i in range(20, 32))


def _prepare_readable(blocks, elide, slots=None):
    """Localise every block's statements, then fold single-use temporaries.

    Returns the names to synchronise around calls. Folding needs the statements
    in their final form - locals, tidied, saves elided, calls wrapped - so that is
    done here, per block, and the later per-line pass finds nothing left to do.
    """
    from . import liveness

    gprs, fprs, scalars = set(), set(), set()

    def finish(text):
        text = tidy(_localize(text, gprs, fprs, scalars))
        if _TAKES_CONTEXT.search(text) and "out();" not in text:
            text = "out(); %s in();" % text.strip()
        return text

    for block in blocks.values():
        code = [finish(s) for s in block.code if s]
        if elide:
            code = [s for s in code if not _is_spill(s, slots)]
        block.code = code
        block.slot = finish(block.slot) if block.slot else block.slot
        if block.slot and elide and _is_spill(block.slot, slots):
            block.slot = ""
        if block.condition:
            block.condition = finish(block.condition)
    gprs.discard(0)
    synced = {GPR_NAMES[i] for i in gprs if not (elide and i in CALLEE_SAVED)}
    synced |= {"f%d" % i for i in fprs} | set(scalars)
    returned = (set(ABI_RETURNED) | set(ABI_PRESERVED)) & synced
    succs = {a: _successors(b, blocks) for a, b in blocks.items()}
    live = liveness.live_out(blocks, succs, synced, returned,
                             lambda b: b.condition, lambda b: b.slot)
    for address, block in blocks.items():
        later = [block.slot] if block.slot else []
        block.code, condition = liveness.fold(block.code, block.condition, live[address],
                                              synced, returned, later)
        block.condition = condition
    gprs.add(0)
    return gprs, fprs, scalars


def structure_function(image: bytes, base: int, start: int, end: int,
                       elide: bool = True, strings=None, readable: bool = False,
                       chunks=()) -> str:
    """Structured C++ for one function; raises lift.Refused if it cannot be.

    `elide` drops the saves and restores of callee-saved registers (see
    CALLEE_SAVED); a function that does not keep the convention needs it off.

    `readable` also folds single-use temporaries into their uses (liveness.py)
    and gives back on return only what the calling convention returns. That
    changes registers no caller may rely on, so it is verified at that level:
    results, stack and global pointers, callee-saved registers and memory.
    """
    lift.lift_function(image, base, start, end, chunks)    # the same refusals as lifting
    ranges = [(start, end)] + sorted((s, e) for s, e in chunks if e > s)
    code = []
    for first, last in ranges:
        words = struct.unpack_from("<%dI" % ((last - first) // 4), image, first - base)
        code += [DISASM.decode(word, first + 4 * i) for i, word in enumerate(words)]
    blocks = _blocks(code, start, end, ranges)
    slots = _save_slots(code, start)
    elide = elide and slots is not None
    if readable:
        has_tail = any(b.kind == "tail"
                       or (b.taken is not None and b.taken not in blocks)
                       or (b.next is not None and b.next not in blocks and b.kind != "return")
                       for b in blocks.values())
        elide = elide and not has_tail
        seen = _prepare_readable(blocks, elide, slots)
    emitter = _Emitter(blocks, start, end)
    body = emitter.emit(start, None, [], 1)
    # Blocks only reachable by a goto - from inside a loop, say - follow the main
    # body, each under its label.
    for node in emitter.order:
        if node not in emitter.emitted:
            body += emitter.emit(node, None, [], 1)
    # The registers the function names, gathered as statements become locals -
    # already, in the readable form, which localises before structuring.
    gprs, fprs, scalars = (set(x) for x in seen) if readable else (set(), set(), set())
    out_lines = []
    # A tail transfer can reach a shared epilogue that restores the saved registers
    # from the stack, so those functions keep their saves.
    elide = elide and not any("TailCall(c" in line for line in body)
    for line in body:
        if line.startswith("@L_"):
            address = int(line[3:], 16)
            if address in emitter.labels:
                # A loop header's label goes before its Tick: a goto back to the
                # header is another iteration, and has to spend budget like one.
                # After it, 0x0029CCC0 looped forever on the equivalence check.
                tick = "Tick(c, 0x%08Xu);" % address
                if out_lines and out_lines[-1].strip().endswith(tick):
                    out_lines.insert(len(out_lines) - 1, "L_%08X:;" % address)
                else:
                    out_lines.append("L_%08X:;" % address)
            continue
        localized = tidy(_localize(line, gprs, fprs, scalars))
        if elide:
            if _is_spill(localized, slots):
                continue
            localized = localized.replace("out(); return;", "leave(); return;")
        if _TAKES_CONTEXT.search(localized) and "out();" not in localized:
            indent = localized[:len(localized) - len(localized.lstrip())]
            localized = "%sout(); %s in();" % (indent, localized.strip())
        out_lines.append(localized)
    gprs.discard(0)
    names = [(GPR_NAMES[i], "c.r[%d]" % i) for i in sorted(gprs)]
    locals_only = [(GPR_NAMES[i], "c.r[%d]" % i) for i in sorted(gprs)
                   if i in CALLEE_SAVED and elide]
    names += [("f%d" % i, "c.f[%d]" % i) for i in sorted(fprs)]
    names += [(n, "c.%s" % n) for n in SCALARS if n in scalars]
    types = {"fcc": "u32", "acc": "u32", "sa": "u32"}
    lines = ["void %s(lifted::Context& c) {" % lift.name_of(start),
             "    using namespace generated;",
             "    using namespace lifted;",
             "    const u32 entry_ra = (u32)c.r[31], entry_sp = (u32)c.r[29];",
             "    (void)entry_ra; (void)entry_sp;"]
    for name, source in names:
        kind = "u32" if name.startswith("f") and name[1:].isdigit() else types.get(name, "u64")
        lines.append("    %s %s = %s;" % (kind, name, source))
    synced = [(n, src) for n, src in names if (n, src) not in locals_only]
    returned = [(n, src) for n, src in synced if n != "ra"]
    if readable:
        returned = [(n, src) for n, src in returned if n in ABI_RETURNED or n in ABI_PRESERVED]
    lines.append("    auto out = [&] { %s };" % " ".join("%s = %s;" % (s, n) for n, s in synced))
    # On return the caller sees its own $ra again, whatever links calls left in it.
    lines.append("    auto leave = [&] { %s c.r[31] = entry_ra; };"
                 % " ".join("%s = %s;" % (s, n) for n, s in returned))
    # The context is lifted::Context; everything else reads without the prefixes.
    lines.append("    auto in = [&] { %s };" % " ".join("%s = %s;" % (n, s) for n, s in synced))
    lines.append("    (void)out; (void)in; (void)leave;")
    body = drop_empty_else(hoist_delay_slots(fold_links(fold_addresses(fold_constants(out_lines, strings),
                                                                       strings))))
    lines += tick_backward_gotos(loop_guards(loops_to_do_while(invert_empty_then(body))))
    lines.append("}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

```

`ps2decomp/symbols.py`:

```py
"""Symbol and cross-reference recovery for a stripped image.

A stripped binary still leaks a surprising amount of naming information, and this
module extracts the three kinds that are actually reliable:

* **String cross-references.**  MIPS materialises a 32-bit address with a
  `lui` / `addiu` pair (or `lui` plus a load offset).  Reassembling those pairs
  recovers the constant, and when the constant lands in a string the call site
  gains a very strong human-readable hint.
* **RenderWare provenance.**  The binary keeps RCS `$Id:` tags naming the exact
  middleware source files linked in.  Those tags sit in the read-only data next
  to the code they belong to, so they identify which regions are RenderWare
  rather than game code.
* **Indirect call tables.**  Runs of aligned words pointing at known function
  starts are vtables or jump tables, which both name-adjacent functions and
  reveal C++ class layout.

Everything here is a *hint generator*.  Nothing renames a function without a
recorded reason, so a wrong guess stays auditable rather than silently
poisoning the database.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import dataclasses
import re
import struct

from .r5900 import DISASM
from .signatures import written_register

# A printable run this long is almost certainly a real string rather than noise.
MIN_STRING_LEN = 4

_RW_ID = re.compile(rb"\$Id:\s*//([^\s$]+)")
_IDENT = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$")


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class StringEntry:
    addr: int
    text: str

    @property
    def is_identifier_like(self) -> bool:
        return bool(_IDENT.match(self.text))


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Xref:
    """A recovered constant address and the instruction pair that built it."""

    from_addr: int
    target: int
    kind: str  # "lui+addiu" | "lui+load" | "lui+store"


_ADDRESSED = {"lw", "lh", "lb", "lbu", "lhu", "lwu", "ld", "lq", "sw", "sh", "sb", "sd",
              "sq", "lwc1", "swc1"}
_CALLEE_SAVED = set(range(16, 24)) | {30}     # $s0-$s7, $fp


class SymbolRecovery:
    def __init__(self, data: bytes, base_addr: int) -> None:
        self.data = data
        self.base = base_addr
        self.end = base_addr + len(data)
        self.strings: dict = {}
        self.xrefs: list = []
        self.xrefs_by_target: dict = collections.defaultdict(list)
        self.renderware_files: list = []

    def contains(self, addr: int) -> bool:
        return self.base <= addr < self.end

    # -- strings --------------------------------------------------------

    def find_strings(self, min_len: int = MIN_STRING_LEN) -> int:
        """Index every NUL-terminated printable run in the image."""
        data = self.data
        start = None
        for i, byte in enumerate(data):
            printable = 0x20 <= byte <= 0x7E or byte in (9, 10, 13)
            if printable:
                if start is None:
                    start = i
                continue
            if start is not None:
                # Only accept runs that actually terminate with NUL, which is
                # what distinguishes a C string from incidental printable bytes.
                if byte == 0 and i - start >= min_len:
                    text = data[start:i].decode("ascii", "replace")
                    self.strings[self.base + start] = StringEntry(self.base + start, text)
                start = None
        return len(self.strings)

    def find_renderware_tags(self) -> list:
        """Recover the RenderWare SDK source paths embedded as RCS tags."""
        out = []
        for match in _RW_ID.finditer(self.data):
            path = match.group(1).decode("ascii", "replace")
            out.append((self.base + match.start(), path))
        self.renderware_files = out
        return out

    # -- address materialisation ----------------------------------------

    def find_xrefs(self, code_ranges) -> int:
        """Reassemble `lui`+offset pairs into absolute addresses.

        `code_ranges` is an iterable of (start, end) spans to scan. Tracking is per
        register and kept conservative, so a pair is never matched across a write
        that replaced the upper half:

        * any other write to a register drops its pending upper half;
        * a branch or jump's delay slot is processed before the transfer, because
          it executes first - `lui $a0` before a `jal` and `addiu $a0` in its delay
          slot is how a string argument is usually passed;
        * a call keeps only the callee-saved registers, which the callee preserves;
        * any other control transfer drops everything.
        """
        count = 0

        def record(addr, upper, ins, kind):
            nonlocal count
            target = (upper + ins.imm) & 0xFFFFFFFF
            if self.contains(target):
                xref = Xref(addr, target, kind)
                self.xrefs.append(xref)
                self.xrefs_by_target[target].append(xref)
                count += 1

        def step(addr, pending):
            word = struct.unpack_from("<I", self.data, addr - self.base)[0]
            ins = DISASM.decode(word, addr)
            if ins.mnemonic == "lui":
                pending[ins.rt] = (ins.imm & 0xFFFF) << 16
                return ins
            if ins.mnemonic in ("addiu", "addi", "daddiu") and ins.rs in pending:
                record(addr, pending[ins.rs], ins, "lui+addiu")
            elif ins.mnemonic in _ADDRESSED and ins.rs in pending:
                kind = "lui+store" if ins.mnemonic.startswith("s") else "lui+load"
                record(addr, pending[ins.rs], ins, kind)
            written = written_register(word)
            if written is not None:
                pending.pop(written, None)
            return ins

        for start, end in code_ranges:
            pending = {}  # register -> upper immediate of the lui that set it
            addr = start
            while addr < end and self.contains(addr):
                ins = step(addr, pending)
                if ins.is_branch or ins.is_jump:
                    if addr + 4 < end and self.contains(addr + 4):
                        step(addr + 4, pending)
                    if ins.is_call:
                        for reg in [r for r in pending if r not in _CALLEE_SAVED]:
                            del pending[reg]
                    else:
                        pending.clear()
                    addr += 8
                    continue
                addr += 4
        return count

    # -- pointer tables --------------------------------------------------

    def find_pointer_tables(self, function_starts, min_entries: int = 3) -> list:
        """Locate runs of words pointing at known function entries.

        These are vtables and switch jump tables.  Requiring several consecutive
        valid entries keeps random data from registering as a table.
        """
        starts = set(function_starts)
        tables = []
        words = struct.unpack("<%dI" % (len(self.data) // 4), self.data[: (len(self.data) // 4) * 4])
        run_start = None
        run_len = 0
        for i, word in enumerate(words):
            if word in starts:
                if run_start is None:
                    run_start = i
                run_len += 1
                continue
            if run_start is not None and run_len >= min_entries:
                tables.append(
                    (self.base + run_start * 4, run_len,
                     [words[run_start + k] for k in range(run_len)])
                )
            run_start = None
            run_len = 0
        if run_start is not None and run_len >= min_entries:
            tables.append(
                (self.base + run_start * 4, run_len,
                 [words[run_start + k] for k in range(run_len)])
            )
        return tables

    # -- naming ----------------------------------------------------------

    def string_for(self, addr: int):
        return self.strings.get(addr)

    def annotate(self, addr: int):
        """Return a short human-readable note for a referenced address."""
        entry = self.strings.get(addr)
        if entry is not None:
            text = entry.text
            if len(text) > 48:
                text = text[:45] + "..."
            return '"%s"' % text.replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\r", "\\r")
        return None

```

`ps2decomp/symexec.py`:

```py
"""Symbolic execution of straight-line functions, to derive their semantics.

A large number of the discovered functions are tiny read-only accessors - load a
pointer from a structure, index it, return a field.  Reading each one by hand works
but does not scale, and the result is mechanical enough that it can be derived
instead.

This walks a branch-free function with *expressions* in the registers rather than
values, and reports whatever ends up in `$v0` as a tree.  That tree does two jobs:
it renders as C for a human to read, and it evaluates against concrete arguments so
the derivation can be differential-tested against the real machine code.  A
derivation that cannot be tested is worth little, so both come from the same tree.

Scope is deliberately narrow.  Anything with a branch, a store, or an instruction
outside the supported set is refused with `Unsupported` rather than approximated -
a plausible but wrong formula presented as a derivation would be worse than no
derivation at all.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import struct

from .r5900 import DISASM

MASK32 = 0xFFFFFFFF
MASK64 = (1 << 64) - 1


class Unsupported(Exception):
    """Raised when a function is outside what can be derived symbolically."""


def _cached(name):
    """Memoise a function of one expression on the (immutable) node itself.

    Unrolled loops build expressions that share subtrees, so a plain recursive
    walk is exponential in the tree's depth - the first version of these turned a
    15-second derivation run into one that did not finish in ten minutes.
    """
    def wrap(function):
        def cached(expr):
            try:
                return object.__getattribute__(expr, name)
            except AttributeError:
                result = function(expr)
                object.__setattr__(expr, name, result)
                return result
        cached.__doc__ = function.__doc__
        cached.__name__ = function.__name__
        return cached
    return wrap


# -- expression tree -----------------------------------------------------

class Expr:
    """Base class for symbolic values."""

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # Record the node's size *as a tree* - the size its rendering would have -
        # at construction, from the children's already-recorded sizes. That makes the
        # size free to query, which matters because unrolled loops build expressions
        # that share subtrees: a value used twice per iteration doubles the tree each
        # time round while the underlying graph grows only linearly. Anything that
        # walks such a value as a tree is exponential, and the deriver has to be able
        # to notice that before it walks it. Defined here so every dataclass subclass
        # inherits it; dataclasses call an inherited __post_init__.
        #
        # Named `tree_size`, not `size`: Load already has a field called `size` (the
        # access width), and a base-class `size` attribute becomes that field's
        # default value, which breaks every dataclass declared after it.
        object.__setattr__(
            self,
            "_tree_size",
            min(1 + sum(child.tree_size for child in children(self)), 1 << 30),
        )

    @property
    def tree_size(self) -> int:
        """Node count as a tree, i.e. the size of this expression when printed."""
        return getattr(self, "_tree_size", 1)

    def render(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.render()


# The EE calling convention passes eight integer arguments in registers - $a0..$a3
# and then $t0..$t3 - and eight float arguments in $f12..$f19. The model numbers
# them as one vector: 0..7 are the integer arguments, 8..15 the float ones.
INT_ARG_REGS = (4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11)
FLOAT_ARG_BASE = 8
FLOAT_ARG_REGS = tuple(range(12, 20))
ARG_COUNT = 16
# $v0 as the function was entered with it: what a path that never sets $v0
# returns. CodeWarrior leaves it so in a void function, or one returning a value
# on some paths only - a state handler in a table, whose callers through the
# table may read it. Entry 16 of the vector, after the arguments.
V0_IN = ARG_COUNT


def arg_name(index: int) -> str:
    """`arg0`..`arg7` for integer arguments, `farg0`..`farg7` for float ones,
    `v0_in` for the incoming $v0."""
    if index == V0_IN:
        return "v0_in"
    if index >= FLOAT_ARG_BASE:
        return "farg%d" % (index - FLOAT_ARG_BASE)
    return "arg%d" % index


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Arg(Expr):
    index: int  # see INT_ARG_REGS and FLOAT_ARG_REGS

    def render(self) -> str:
        if _ARG_RENDERER is not None:
            return _ARG_RENDERER(self)
        return arg_name(self.index)

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        # A vector without the incoming $v0 has it 0, as the interpreter's call.
        return (args[self.index] if self.index < len(args) else 0) & MASK64


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Const(Expr):
    value: int

    def render(self) -> str:
        v = self.value
        if -256 < _signed(v) < 256:
            return str(_signed(v))
        return "0x%X" % (v & MASK64)

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        return self.value & MASK64


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Load(Expr):
    address: Expr
    size: int
    signed: bool
    # Which memory the load reads: 0 is memory as the function was entered, and
    # epoch k is memory as it stood when the k-th call to a function that has not
    # been derived returned. Such a callee can change anything, so a load after it
    # is a different value from the same load before it, and must compare unequal.
    epoch: int = 0

    def render(self) -> str:
        if _LOAD_RENDERER is not None:
            return _LOAD_RENDERER(self, lambda node: node.render())
        kind = {1: "s8" if self.signed else "u8",
                2: "s16" if self.signed else "u16",
                4: "s32" if self.signed else "u32",
                8: "u64", 16: "u128"}[self.size]
        return "*(%s*)(%s)" % (kind, self.address.render())

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        address = self.address.evaluate(args, read) & MASK32
        if self.epoch:
            return read(address, self.size, self.signed, self.epoch)
        return read(address, self.size, self.signed)


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class CallResult(Expr):
    """What `$v0` - or, for a float result, `$f0` - held when the `index`-th
    opaque call on a path returned.

    An opaque call is one into a function that has not been derived: rather than
    inlining it, the derived code calls it. Evaluating this needs the call to have
    been made, so it is only meaningful inside a sequential evaluation that makes
    the calls (see paths.Execution).
    """

    index: int
    target: int
    # 2 for $v0; FLOAT_RESULT for $f0, as its 32 bits.
    register: int = 2

    def render(self) -> str:
        return ("r%d" if self.register == 2 else "rf%d") % self.index

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        if self.register == 2:
            return read.result(self.index) & MASK64
        return read.float_result(self.index) & 0xFFFFFFFF


_REGISTER_NAMES = ["zero", "at", "v0", "v1", "a0", "a1", "a2", "a3",
                   "t0", "t1", "t2", "t3", "t4", "t5", "t6", "t7",
                   "s0", "s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s5", "s6", "s7",
                   "t8", "t9", "k0", "k1", "gp", "sp", "fp", "ra"]


def register_name(index: int) -> str:
    """A register's name for a C++ identifier: `s0`, `f20`, `hi`, `fcc`."""
    if index < 32:
        return _REGISTER_NAMES[index]
    if index == REG_HI:
        return "hi"
    if index == REG_LO:
        return "lo"
    if index == FP_COND:
        return "fcc"
    if index == FP_ACC:
        return "facc"
    if UPPER_BASE <= index < UPPER_BASE + 32:
        return "%s_hi" % _REGISTER_NAMES[index - UPPER_BASE]
    if VF_BASE <= index < VC_BASE:
        return "vf%d%s" % ((index - VF_BASE) // 4, "xyzw"[(index - VF_BASE) % 4])
    if VC_BASE <= index < VACC_BASE:
        return "vc%d" % (index - VC_BASE)
    if VACC_BASE <= index < VACC_BASE + 4:
        return "vacc%s" % "xyzw"[index - VACC_BASE]
    if index >= FPR_BASE:
        return "f%d" % (index - FPR_BASE)
    return "r%d" % index


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Var(Expr):
    """A register's value at the start of the current iteration of a loop.

    A loop whose trip count depends on its input cannot be unrolled into one
    expression, so its body is derived once over variables: every register the
    body writes is a Var, given its value before the loop on entry and the body's
    new value on each `continue`.
    """

    loop: int
    register: int

    def render(self) -> str:
        return "l%d_%s" % (self.loop, register_name(self.register))

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        return read.var(self.loop, self.register) & MASK64


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class LoopExit(Expr):
    """True when a loop was left by its `index`-th exit."""

    loop: int
    index: int

    def render(self) -> str:
        return "l%d_exit == %d" % (self.loop, self.index)

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        return read.exit_taken(self.loop) == self.index

    def negate(self) -> Expr:
        return Not1(self)


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Temp(Expr):
    """A named value the emitter has already captured into a local.

    Exists only during rendering: the emitter replaces a subexpression with one of
    these once it has been stored in a `const` local, so later statements refer to
    the local instead of re-reading memory that may have changed since.
    """

    name: str

    def render(self) -> str:
        return self.name

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        raise Unsupported("a rendering temporary has no value of its own")


# C operator precedence, tighter binding first. Rendering *must* respect this:
# `arg1 << 2 + arg0` is not `(arg1 << 2) + arg0` in C, it is `arg1 << (2 + arg0)`.
# Emitting unparenthesised text would produce source that disagrees with the tree
# it was derived from, which is the one failure mode this module exists to avoid.
PRECEDENCE = {
    "mul": 10,
    "add": 9, "sub": 9,
    "shl": 8, "shr": 8, "sar": 8,
    "dshl": 8, "dshr": 8, "dsar": 8,
    "ltu": 6, "lt": 6, "geu": 6,
    # Relational and equality operators, for branch conditions.
    "eq": 5, "ne": 5, "le": 6, "gt": 6, "ge": 6,
    "and": 4,
    "xor": 3,
    "or": 2,
}
ATOM_PRECEDENCE = 12


def _precedence(expr: "Expr") -> int:
    # Arithmetic shifts render as a parenthesised cast expression, which is an atom.
    if isinstance(expr, Binary) and expr.op in ("sar", "dsar"):
        return ATOM_PRECEDENCE
    if isinstance(expr, (Binary, Compare, Predicate)):
        return PRECEDENCE[expr.op]
    if isinstance(expr, Select):
        return 1
    return ATOM_PRECEDENCE


# -- C++ value semantics -------------------------------------------------
#
# The rendered text is C++, and it has to mean what the tree means, not merely
# look like it. The tree computes on 64-bit register values, so the rendering
# makes every value a `u64`: arguments are declared `u64`, the Read* helpers
# return the register image of the loaded value (sign- or zero-extended), and
# the operators whose meaning depends on width or signedness carry explicit
# casts. Left to C++'s own promotion rules, `ReadU8(p) << 24` is an `int` shift
# and a signed compare of two `u64`s is unsigned - an earlier version emitted
# exactly that, and only compiling and running the output exposed it.

def fits_u32(expr: "Expr") -> bool:
    """True when the value is provably below 2**32."""
    if isinstance(expr, Const):
        return (expr.value & MASK64) <= MASK32
    if isinstance(expr, Load):
        return not expr.signed and expr.size <= 4
    if isinstance(expr, (Compare, Predicate, FloatPredicate, Not1, FloatOp, VuOp,
                         IntToFloat, FloatToInt)):
        return True
    if isinstance(expr, Binary):
        if expr.op == "shr":
            return True
        if expr.op == "and":
            return fits_u32(expr.left) or fits_u32(expr.right)
        if expr.op in ("or", "xor"):
            return fits_u32(expr.left) and fits_u32(expr.right)
        if expr.op == "dshr" and isinstance(expr.right, Const):
            return (expr.right.value & 0x3F) >= 32
    if isinstance(expr, Select):
        return fits_u32(expr.when_true) and fits_u32(expr.when_false)
    return False


def nonnegative(expr: "Expr") -> bool:
    """True when the value is below 2**63, so signed and unsigned order agree."""
    if fits_u32(expr):
        return True
    if isinstance(expr, Const):
        return _signed(expr.value) >= 0
    if isinstance(expr, Binary):
        if expr.op == "dshr" and isinstance(expr.right, Const):
            return (expr.right.value & 0x3F) >= 1
        if expr.op == "and":
            return nonnegative(expr.left) or nonnegative(expr.right)
        if expr.op in ("or", "xor"):
            return nonnegative(expr.left) and nonnegative(expr.right)
    return False


def _signed_literal(value: int) -> str:
    """A constant spelled so C++ gives it its signed 64-bit value.

    Negative values are written in decimal on purpose: `-0x80000000` is unsigned
    in C++ (the hex literal is an `unsigned int` and negating it wraps), whereas
    the decimal literal 2147483648 is a `long long`.
    """
    s = _signed(value)
    if s == -(1 << 63):
        return "INT64_MIN"
    if s < 0:
        return "-%d" % -s if s <= -256 else str(s)
    return Const(value).render()


def _signed_operand(expr: "Expr", limit: int) -> str:
    """Render an operand of a signed 64-bit comparison."""
    if isinstance(expr, Const):
        return _signed_literal(expr.value)
    if isinstance(expr, SignExtend32):
        # (s32) already yields the right signed value; widening it to u64 and back
        # would only add noise.
        return "(s32)%s" % _wrap(expr.value, ATOM_PRECEDENCE)
    return "(s64)%s" % _wrap(expr, ATOM_PRECEDENCE)


def _render_order(op: str, left: "Expr", right: "Expr", symbol: str, level: int) -> str:
    """Render a relational comparison with the signedness the tree specifies."""
    if op in ("eq", "ne", "ltu", "geu") or (nonnegative(left) and nonnegative(right)):
        return "%s %s %s" % (_wrap(left, level), symbol, _wrap(right, level + 1))
    return "%s %s %s" % (
        _signed_operand(left, level), symbol, _signed_operand(right, level + 1)
    )


def _shift_amount(amount: "Expr", bits: int) -> str:
    """The shift count, masked as the hardware masks it.

    A C++ shift by the operand width or more is undefined, while the R5900 simply
    uses the low 5 (word) or 6 (doubleword) bits, so a variable count is masked
    explicitly and a constant one is reduced before printing.
    """
    mask = bits - 1
    if isinstance(amount, Const):
        return str(amount.value & mask)
    return "(%s & %d)" % (amount.render(), mask)


# How a Load is rendered varies by consumer: the default prints a pointer cast,
# while the C++ emitter prints a Read* helper call. Everything *else* about
# rendering - precedence, parenthesisation - must not vary, so it lives here once
# and the Load form is the only hook. An earlier version duplicated the whole
# renderer in the emitter, and the two drifted: a clarity rule added here never
# reached the generated source.
_LOAD_RENDERER = None


def set_load_renderer(renderer):
    """Install a custom Load renderer; returns the previous one.

    `renderer(node, render_child)` returns the text for a Load node, where
    `render_child(expr)` renders a subexpression at lowest precedence.
    """
    global _LOAD_RENDERER
    previous = _LOAD_RENDERER
    _LOAD_RENDERER = renderer
    return previous


# The second and last hook: how an argument prints. A typed argument is a view
# object in the emitted C++, so in a value context it has to read `arg0.address`.
_ARG_RENDERER = None


class arg_renderer:
    """Install a renderer for `Arg` nodes for the duration of a block."""

    def __init__(self, renderer):
        self._renderer = renderer
        self._previous = None

    def __enter__(self):
        global _ARG_RENDERER
        self._previous, _ARG_RENDERER = _ARG_RENDERER, self._renderer
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        global _ARG_RENDERER
        _ARG_RENDERER = self._previous
        return False


class load_renderer:
    """Context manager form of `set_load_renderer`."""

    def __init__(self, renderer):
        self._renderer = renderer
        self._previous = None

    def __enter__(self):
        self._previous = set_load_renderer(self._renderer)
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        set_load_renderer(self._previous)
        return False


def _wrap(child: "Expr", limit: int) -> str:
    """Render `child`, parenthesising it when its binding is looser than `limit`."""
    text = child.render()
    return "(%s)" % text if _precedence(child) < limit else text


def _narrow_in_cpp(expr) -> bool:
    """Whether an expression's rendered C++ may have a 32-bit type: the float and
    VU helpers return u32, and a bitwise combination of such values and literals
    stays u32. Everything else - loads, arguments, arithmetic - is u64."""
    if isinstance(expr, Const):
        return True
    if type(expr).__name__ in ("FloatOp", "VuOp", "IntToFloat", "FloatToInt"):
        return True
    if isinstance(expr, Binary) and expr.op in ("and", "or", "xor"):
        return _narrow_in_cpp(expr.left) and _narrow_in_cpp(expr.right)
    return False


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Binary(Expr):
    op: str
    left: Expr
    right: Expr

    _SYMBOL = {
        "add": "+", "sub": "-", "mul": "*", "shl": "<<",
        "shr": ">>", "sar": ">>", "and": "&", "or": "|", "xor": "^",
        "dshl": "<<", "dshr": ">>", "dsar": ">>",
    }

    def render(self) -> str:
        level = PRECEDENCE[self.op]
        if self.op in ("sar", "dsar"):
            # An arithmetic shift needs a signed operand of the right width: `sra`
            # shifts the low word as an s32, `dsra` the whole register as an s64.
            # The result is widened back to the u64 every value is.
            cast, bits = ("s32", 32) if self.op == "sar" else ("s64", 64)
            return "(u64)((%s)%s >> %s)" % (
                cast, _wrap(self.left, ATOM_PRECEDENCE), _shift_amount(self.right, bits)
            )
        if self.op in ("shl", "shr", "dshl", "dshr"):
            bits = 32 if self.op in ("shl", "shr") else 64
            left = _wrap(self.left, level)
            if isinstance(self.left, Const):
                # A bare literal is an `int`, and `1 << 31` on an int overflows.
                left = "%sull" % Const(self.left.value & MASK64).render().lstrip("-")
                if _signed(self.left.value) < 0:
                    left = "0x%Xull" % (self.left.value & MASK64)
            if isinstance(self.left, Binary) and self.left.op in ("add", "sub"):
                left = "(%s)" % left
            if self.op == "shr" and not fits_u32(self.left):
                # `srl` shifts the low word only; the upper half must not shift in.
                left = "(%s & 0xFFFFFFFF)" % self.left.render()
            if self.op in ("dshl", "dshr") and _narrow_in_cpp(self.left):
                # A float or VU helper returns u32, and so does a mask of one: a
                # 64-bit shift of it in C++ would shift at 32 bits and lose it.
                left = "(u64)%s" % _wrap(self.left, ATOM_PRECEDENCE)
            return "%s %s %s" % (left, self._SYMBOL[self.op], _shift_amount(self.right, bits))
        left = _wrap(self.left, level)
        # `a - b << 4` is valid C and means `(a - b) << 4`, but almost nobody reads
        # it that way, so an arithmetic operand of a shift gets parenthesised even
        # though precedence does not require it. Redundant parentheses cannot change
        # meaning; a misread can.
        # `_wrap` leaves an add/sub unparenthesised here because precedence allows
        # it, so wrapping unconditionally cannot double up. Testing the rendered
        # text for a leading "(" would be wrong: `(a << 3) - b` starts with one
        # without being parenthesised as a whole.
        if self.op in ("shl", "shr", "sar", "dshl", "dshr", "dsar") and isinstance(self.left, Binary):
            if self.left.op in ("add", "sub"):
                left = "(%s)" % left
        # The right operand of a left-associative operator needs a parenthesis at
        # equal precedence too, or `a - (b - c)` would print as `a - b - c`.
        return "%s %s %s" % (left, self._SYMBOL[self.op], _wrap(self.right, level + 1))

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        a = self.left.evaluate(args, read)
        b = self.right.evaluate(args, read)
        if self.op == "add":
            return (a + b) & MASK64
        if self.op == "sub":
            return (a - b) & MASK64
        if self.op == "mul":
            return (a * b) & MASK64
        # Word shifts mask the amount to 5 bits, doubleword shifts to 6. Using the
        # 5-bit mask for both silently turns a shift of 32 into a shift of zero,
        # which is how `dsll32`/`dsra32` and the HI half of a multiply came out
        # wrong - caught by the differential tests rather than by reading.
        if self.op == "shl":
            return (a << (b & 0x1F)) & MASK64
        if self.op == "shr":
            return (a & MASK32) >> (b & 0x1F)
        if self.op == "sar":
            return (_sign32(a) >> (b & 0x1F)) & MASK64
        if self.op == "dshl":
            return (a << (b & 0x3F)) & MASK64
        if self.op == "dshr":
            return (a & MASK64) >> (b & 0x3F)
        if self.op == "dsar":
            return (_signed(a) >> (b & 0x3F)) & MASK64
        if self.op == "and":
            return a & b
        if self.op == "or":
            return a | b
        if self.op == "xor":
            return a ^ b
        raise Unsupported("cannot evaluate %r" % self.op)


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Compare(Expr):
    op: str
    left: Expr
    right: Expr

    def render(self) -> str:
        # `slt`/`sltu` produce 0 or 1 as a register value; the cast keeps it a u64
        # so a later `<< 31` cannot become a signed int overflow.
        return "(u64)(%s)" % _render_order(
            self.op, self.left, self.right, "<", PRECEDENCE[self.op]
        )

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        a = self.left.evaluate(args, read)
        b = self.right.evaluate(args, read)
        if self.op == "ltu":
            return 1 if (a & MASK64) < (b & MASK64) else 0
        return 1 if _signed(a) < _signed(b) else 0


# -- floating point ------------------------------------------------------
#
# Every expression in this model evaluates to an integer *bit pattern*, floats
# included. That mirrors the hardware - a float register holds 32 bits, and
# `mfc1`/`swc1` move those bits around without interpreting them - and it keeps
# evaluation uniform, with reinterpretation confined to the float operations
# themselves rather than smeared across the whole tree.

def _bits_to_float(bits: int) -> float:
    return struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", bits & MASK32))[0]


# The largest finite single-precision magnitude, bit pattern 0x7F7FFFFF.
FLOAT_MAX = struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", 0x7F7FFFFF))[0]


def _float_to_bits(value: float) -> int:
    """Encode a result the way the EE's FPU would.

    That FPU is deliberately not IEEE-754: no infinities, no NaNs, and an overflow
    saturates to the largest representable magnitude. This must match `_f32` in
    emu.py exactly - the two are compared against each other on every derivation,
    so any divergence registers as a disagreement.
    """
    if value != value:
        return _float_to_bits(0.0)
    if value > FLOAT_MAX:
        value = FLOAT_MAX
    elif value < -FLOAT_MAX:
        value = -FLOAT_MAX
    return struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", value))[0]


def _float_operand(expr: "Expr") -> str:
    """Render a float operand; a constant becomes a float literal.

    `FloatBits(-1.0f)` says what `0xBF800000` means. The literal is the shortest
    decimal that converts back to exactly the same bits, so nothing is lost; a
    NaN or infinity pattern has no literal and stays hexadecimal.
    """
    if not isinstance(expr, Const):
        return expr.render()
    bits = expr.value & MASK32
    value = _bits_to_float(bits)
    if value != value or value in (float("inf"), float("-inf")):
        return "0x%08X" % bits
    for digits in range(1, 10):
        text = "%.*g" % (digits, value)
        if struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", float(text)))[0] == bits:
            break
    if not any(c in text for c in ".en"):
        text += ".0"
    return "FloatBits(%sf)" % text


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class FloatOp(Expr):
    """A single-precision arithmetic operation over bit-pattern operands.

    `madd` and `msub` take three: the accumulator (`left`) plus or minus the
    product of `right` and `third`, rounded once, as the FPU does.
    """

    op: str
    left: Expr
    right: Expr = None   # None for the unary forms
    third: Expr = None   # only for madd and msub

    _NAMES = {
        "add": "FloatAdd", "sub": "FloatSub", "mul": "FloatMul", "div": "FloatDiv",
        "min": "FloatMin", "max": "FloatMax",
        "neg": "FloatNeg", "abs": "FloatAbs", "sqrt": "FloatSqrt", "mov": "FloatMove",
        "madd": "FloatMulAdd", "msub": "FloatMulSub",
    }

    def render(self) -> str:
        name = self._NAMES[self.op]
        if self.third is not None:
            return "%s(%s, %s, %s)" % (name, _float_operand(self.left),
                                       _float_operand(self.right), _float_operand(self.third))
        if self.right is None:
            return "%s(%s)" % (name, _float_operand(self.left))
        return "%s(%s, %s)" % (name, _float_operand(self.left), _float_operand(self.right))

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        a = _bits_to_float(self.left.evaluate(args, read))
        if self.third is not None:
            product = (_bits_to_float(self.right.evaluate(args, read))
                       * _bits_to_float(self.third.evaluate(args, read)))
            return _float_to_bits(a + product if self.op == "madd" else a - product)
        if self.right is None:
            result = {
                "neg": lambda x: -x,
                "abs": abs,
                "mov": lambda x: x,
                "sqrt": lambda x: x ** 0.5 if x >= 0 else 0.0,
            }[self.op](a)
            return _float_to_bits(result)
        b = _bits_to_float(self.right.evaluate(args, read))
        if self.op == "div":
            # The FPU flags division by zero rather than trapping; the interpreter
            # yields zero, and the two must agree or every such function would
            # register as a disagreement.
            result = 0.0 if b == 0.0 else a / b
        else:
            result = {
                "add": lambda x, y: x + y,
                "sub": lambda x, y: x - y,
                "mul": lambda x, y: x * y,
                "min": min,
                "max": max,
            }[self.op](a, b)
        return _float_to_bits(result)


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class IntDiv(Expr):
    """A 32-bit quotient or remainder as the EE computes it (emu.divide), defined
    for every input, a zero divisor included. op: quot, rem, quotu, remu."""

    op: str
    left: Expr
    right: Expr

    _NAMES = {"quot": "DivQuot", "rem": "DivRem", "quotu": "DivQuotU", "remu": "DivRemU"}

    def render(self) -> str:
        return "%s(%s, %s)" % (self._NAMES[self.op], self.left.render(), self.right.render())

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        from .emu import divide

        lo, hi = divide(self.left.evaluate(args, read), self.right.evaluate(args, read),
                        not self.op.endswith("u"))
        return lo if self.op.startswith("quot") else hi


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class VuOp(Expr):
    """A VU0 arithmetic operation on one lane, over bit patterns (see vu0.py).

    `madd`/`msub`: `left` is the accumulator lane, `right` times `third` the
    product. `itof`/`ftoi` carry their fixed-point shift in `shift`. `div` and
    `rsqrt` take numerator and denominator, `abs` and `sqrt` one operand.
    """

    op: str
    left: Expr
    right: Expr = None
    third: Expr = None
    shift: int = 0

    _NAMES = {"add": "VuAdd", "sub": "VuSub", "mul": "VuMul", "max": "VuMax",
              "mini": "VuMin", "madd": "VuMadd", "msub": "VuMsub", "abs": "VuAbs",
              "itof": "VuItof", "ftoi": "VuFtoi", "div": "VuDiv", "sqrt": "VuSqrt",
              "rsqrt": "VuRsqrt"}

    def operands(self):
        return tuple(x for x in (self.left, self.right, self.third) if x is not None)

    def render(self) -> str:
        parts = [_float_operand(x) for x in self.operands()]
        if self.op in ("itof", "ftoi"):
            parts.append(str(self.shift))
        return "%s(%s)" % (self._NAMES[self.op], ", ".join(parts))

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        from . import vu0

        values = [x.evaluate(args, read) & MASK32 for x in self.operands()]
        if self.op in ("madd", "msub"):
            return vu0.vu_binary(self.op, values[1], values[2], values[0])
        if self.op in ("add", "sub", "mul", "max", "mini"):
            return vu0.vu_binary(self.op, values[0], values[1])
        if self.op == "abs":
            return vu0.vu_abs(values[0])
        if self.op == "itof":
            return vu0.vu_itof(values[0], self.shift)
        if self.op == "ftoi":
            return vu0.vu_ftoi(values[0], self.shift)
        if self.op == "div":
            return vu0.vu_div(values[0], values[1])
        if self.op == "sqrt":
            return vu0.vu_sqrt(values[0])
        return vu0.vu_rsqrt(values[0], values[1])


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class IntToFloat(Expr):
    """`cvt.s.w`: reinterpret the operand's bits as an integer, convert to float."""

    value: Expr

    def render(self) -> str:
        if isinstance(self.value, Const):
            return "FloatFromInt(%d)" % _sign32(self.value.value)
        return "FloatFromInt(%s)" % self.value.render()

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        return _float_to_bits(float(_sign32(self.value.evaluate(args, read))))


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class FloatToInt(Expr):
    """`cvt.w.s`: convert a float to an integer, truncating toward zero and
    saturating past 32 bits (emu.float_to_word)."""

    value: Expr

    def render(self) -> str:
        return "IntFromFloat(%s)" % _float_operand(self.value)

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        bits = self.value.evaluate(args, read) & MASK32
        if (bits & 0x7F800000) <= 0x4E800000:
            return int(_bits_to_float(bits)) & MASK32
        return 0x80000000 if bits & 0x80000000 else 0x7FFFFFFF


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class FloatPredicate(Expr):
    """A `c.<cond>.s` comparison, as tested later by `bc1t`/`bc1f`."""

    op: str  # eq lt le
    left: Expr
    right: Expr

    _SYMBOL = {"eq": "==", "lt": "<", "le": "<=", "false": "false"}

    def render(self) -> str:
        if self.op == "false":
            return "false"
        return "FloatValue(%s) %s FloatValue(%s)" % (
            _float_operand(self.left), self._SYMBOL[self.op], _float_operand(self.right)
        )

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        if self.op == "false":
            return False
        a = _bits_to_float(self.left.evaluate(args, read))
        b = _bits_to_float(self.right.evaluate(args, read))
        return {"eq": a == b, "lt": a < b, "le": a <= b}[self.op]

    def negate(self) -> "Expr":
        return Not1(self)


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Not1(Expr):
    """Logical negation of a condition, as distinct from a bitwise complement."""

    value: Expr

    def render(self) -> str:
        return "!(%s)" % self.value.render()

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        return not self.value.evaluate(args, read)

    def negate(self) -> Expr:
        return self.value


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class SignExtend32(Expr):
    """Narrow to 32 bits and sign-extend, as every 32-bit MIPS result is.

    Needed to model `mult` faithfully: it multiplies the low words of its operands
    as signed values, so the raw 64-bit register contents must not be used.
    """

    value: Expr

    def render(self) -> str:
        return "(u64)(s32)%s" % _wrap(self.value, ATOM_PRECEDENCE)

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        return _sign32(self.value.evaluate(args, read)) & MASK64


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Not(Expr):
    """Bitwise complement, used to express `nor` as `~(a | b)`."""

    value: Expr

    def render(self) -> str:
        return "~%s" % _wrap(self.value, ATOM_PRECEDENCE)

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        return ~self.value.evaluate(args, read) & MASK64


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Select(Expr):
    """A ternary: the shape of a conditional move.

    `movz`/`movn` write their destination only when a condition holds, so the
    result depends on what the destination already contained - which is why the
    previous value is part of the expression rather than discarded.
    """

    condition: Expr
    when_true: Expr
    when_false: Expr

    def render(self) -> str:
        return "%s ? %s : %s" % (
            _wrap(self.condition, 7),
            _wrap(self.when_true, 7),
            _wrap(self.when_false, 7),
        )

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        taken = self.condition.evaluate(args, read)
        branch = self.when_true if taken else self.when_false
        return branch.evaluate(args, read) & MASK64


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Predicate(Expr):
    """A branch condition, evaluated with signed comparison as MIPS does."""

    op: str  # eq ne lt le gt ge, plus ltu geu for an unsigned `sltu` result
    left: Expr
```
