```py
    right: Expr

    _SYMBOL = {"eq": "==", "ne": "!=", "lt": "<", "le": "<=", "gt": ">", "ge": ">=",
               "ltu": "<", "geu": ">="}

    def render(self) -> str:
        return _render_order(self.op, self.left, self.right, self._SYMBOL[self.op], 7)

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        a = self.left.evaluate(args, read)
        b = self.right.evaluate(args, read)
        if self.op == "ltu":
            return (a & MASK64) < (b & MASK64)
        if self.op == "geu":
            return (a & MASK64) >= (b & MASK64)
        a, b = _signed(a), _signed(b)
        return {
            "eq": a == b, "ne": a != b, "lt": a < b,
            "le": a <= b, "gt": a > b, "ge": a >= b,
        }[self.op]

    def negate(self) -> "Predicate":
        opposite = {"eq": "ne", "ne": "eq", "lt": "ge", "ge": "lt", "le": "gt", "gt": "le",
                    "ltu": "geu", "geu": "ltu"}
        return Predicate(opposite[self.op], self.left, self.right)


def _signed(value: int) -> int:
    value &= MASK64
    return value - (1 << 64) if value & (1 << 63) else value


def _sign32(value: int) -> int:
    value &= MASK32
    return value - (1 << 32) if value & 0x80000000 else value


def children(expr: Expr) -> tuple:
    """Every subexpression of a node.

    Deliberately fail-closed: an unrecognised node type raises rather than
    returning nothing. Every traversal in the project is built on this, and the
    silent-empty version of it caused a real bug - `Not`, `Select` and
    `SignExtend32` were added without updating the argument scan, so arguments
    nested inside them became invisible and the emitter produced functions
    referencing undeclared parameters. A traversal that cannot see a new node type
    must break loudly, not quietly skip it.
    """
    if isinstance(expr, (Arg, Const, CallResult, Temp, Var, LoopExit)):
        return ()
    if isinstance(expr, Load):
        return (expr.address,)
    if isinstance(expr, (Not, Not1, SignExtend32, IntToFloat, FloatToInt)):
        return (expr.value,)
    if isinstance(expr, Select):
        return (expr.condition, expr.when_true, expr.when_false)
    if isinstance(expr, FloatOp):
        if expr.third is not None:
            return (expr.left, expr.right, expr.third)
        return (expr.left,) if expr.right is None else (expr.left, expr.right)
    if isinstance(expr, VuOp):
        return expr.operands()
    if isinstance(expr, IntDiv):
        return (expr.left, expr.right)
    if isinstance(expr, (Binary, Compare, Predicate, FloatPredicate)):
        return (expr.left, expr.right)
    raise Unsupported("no traversal rule for %s" % type(expr).__name__)


def rebuild(expr: Expr, new_children) -> Expr:
    """Reconstruct a node with replaced subexpressions, preserving its type."""
    if isinstance(expr, (Arg, Const, CallResult, Temp, Var, LoopExit)):
        return expr
    if isinstance(expr, Load):
        return Load(new_children[0], expr.size, expr.signed, expr.epoch)
    if isinstance(expr, Not):
        return Not(new_children[0])
    if isinstance(expr, Not1):
        return Not1(new_children[0])
    if isinstance(expr, SignExtend32):
        return SignExtend32(new_children[0])
    if isinstance(expr, IntToFloat):
        return IntToFloat(new_children[0])
    if isinstance(expr, FloatToInt):
        return FloatToInt(new_children[0])
    if isinstance(expr, Select):
        return Select(*new_children)
    if isinstance(expr, FloatOp):
        if expr.right is None:
            return FloatOp(expr.op, new_children[0])
        return FloatOp(expr.op, *new_children)
    if isinstance(expr, VuOp):
        kids = list(new_children) + [None] * (3 - len(new_children))
        return VuOp(expr.op, kids[0], kids[1], kids[2], expr.shift)
    if isinstance(expr, IntDiv):
        return IntDiv(expr.op, *new_children)
    if isinstance(expr, Binary):
        return Binary(expr.op, *new_children)
    if isinstance(expr, Compare):
        return Compare(expr.op, *new_children)
    if isinstance(expr, Predicate):
        return Predicate(expr.op, *new_children)
    if isinstance(expr, FloatPredicate):
        return FloatPredicate(expr.op, *new_children)
    raise Unsupported("no rebuild rule for %s" % type(expr).__name__)


def arguments_used(expr: Expr) -> set:
    """Indices of every `Arg` anywhere in an expression."""
    if isinstance(expr, Arg):
        return {expr.index}
    found = set()
    for child in children(expr):
        found |= arguments_used(child)
    return found


def substitute(expr: Expr, arguments) -> Expr:
    """Rewrite a derivation's `Arg` nodes with the caller's actual expressions.

    This is what makes a derived callee usable at a call site: the callee's result
    is expressed in terms of `arg0..arg3`, and inlining it means replacing those
    with whatever the caller had in `$a0..$a3` at the moment of the call.

    `arguments` maps an argument index to an expression. An index with no entry is
    left as-is, which keeps the result honest: if a callee reads an argument the
    caller never set, that shows up as a stray `argN` rather than silently becoming
    zero.

    Built on `children`/`rebuild` so that a new node type cannot be silently
    skipped - the earlier hand-written version missed three and substituted nothing
    inside them.
    """
    if isinstance(expr, Arg):
        return arguments.get(expr.index, expr)
    kids = children(expr)
    if not kids:
        return expr
    return rebuild(expr, [substitute(child, arguments) for child in kids])


def simplify(expr: Expr) -> Expr:
    """Fold constants and drop identities; see `_simplify`.

    Memoised on the node, and the result is marked as its own simplification.
    Without that mark every simplified node was new and uncached, so simplifying
    it again - which `address_of` does - recomputed everything beneath it, doubling
    the work at each level of a pointer chain.
    """
    try:
        return object.__getattribute__(expr, "_simplified")
    except AttributeError:
        pass
    result = _simplify(expr)
    object.__setattr__(expr, "_simplified", result)
    try:
        object.__getattribute__(result, "_simplified")
    except AttributeError:
        object.__setattr__(result, "_simplified", result)
    return result


def _simplify(expr: Expr) -> Expr:
    """Fold constants and drop identities, so the output reads like source.

    Every rule here preserves meaning exactly.  The derived code is
    differential-tested against the original, so an over-eager rule shows up as a
    disagreement rather than as quietly wrong source - which is why it is safe to
    simplify for readability at all.
    """
    if isinstance(expr, Binary):
        left, right = simplify(expr.left), simplify(expr.right)
        if isinstance(left, Const) and isinstance(right, Const):
            folded = Binary(expr.op, left, right).evaluate((0, 0, 0, 0), None)
            return Const(folded)
        # x + 0, x | 0, x << 0 and friends add nothing.
        if isinstance(right, Const) and right.value == 0 and expr.op in (
            "add", "sub", "or", "xor", "shl", "shr", "sar"
        ):
            return left
        if isinstance(left, Const) and left.value == 0 and expr.op in ("add", "or", "xor"):
            return right
        # Collapse a chain of constant offsets: (x + c1) + c2 becomes x + (c1 + c2).
        # These arise constantly from `lui`/`addiu` pairs feeding a further offset,
        # and leaving them unfolded prints addresses as unreadable sums.
        if (
            expr.op == "add"
            and isinstance(right, Const)
            and isinstance(left, Binary)
            and left.op == "add"
            and isinstance(left.right, Const)
        ):
            return simplify(
                Binary("add", left.left, Const((left.right.value + right.value) & MASK64))
            )
        return Binary(expr.op, left, right)
    if isinstance(expr, Load):
        return Load(address_of(expr.address), expr.size, expr.signed, expr.epoch)
    if isinstance(expr, Compare):
        return Compare(expr.op, simplify(expr.left), simplify(expr.right))
    if isinstance(expr, SignExtend32):
        simplified = simplify(expr.value)
        inner = low32(simplified)
        if inner is not simplified:
            # Removing an inner extension can expose folds it was blocking: an
            # unrolled counter is sext(sext(i + 1) + 1), which must become i + 2 or
            # it grows with every iteration.
            inner = simplify(inner)
        if isinstance(inner, Const):
            return Const(_sign32(inner.value) & MASK64)
        if isinstance(inner, SignExtend32) or fits_s32(inner):
            return inner
        return SignExtend32(inner)
    if isinstance(expr, (FloatOp, VuOp, IntDiv, IntToFloat, FloatToInt, FloatPredicate,
                         Not1, Not, Select)):
        kids = children(expr)
        return rebuild(expr, [simplify(child) for child in kids]) if kids else expr
    if isinstance(expr, Predicate):
        left, right = simplify(expr.left), simplify(expr.right)
        # `slt` followed by `bne ..., $zero` is how a compiler spells a plain
        # comparison, and printing it as `(a < b) ? 1 : 0 != 0` hides that. The
        # 0/1 result of a Compare is never anything else, so testing it against
        # zero is exactly the comparison itself, or its negation.
        if isinstance(left, Compare) and isinstance(right, Const) and right.value == 0:
            # The Compare's signedness carries over. An earlier version mapped `ltu`
            # to a signed `lt` here, which the tests missed because they only ever
            # passed small positive pointers.
            inner = Predicate(left.op, left.left, left.right)
            if expr.op == "ne":
                return inner
            if expr.op == "eq":
                return inner.negate()
        return Predicate(expr.op, left, right)
    return expr


# -- sign extension ----------------------------------------------------------
#
# Word operations produce a 32-bit result sign-extended to 64 bits, modelled as a
# SignExtend32 around them. Most consumers only ever look at the low 32 bits - an
# address, a store of four bytes or fewer, a returned value, the operands of
# another word operation - and for those the extension is noise, so `low32`
# removes it. Where all 64 bits matter (a comparison, a doubleword shift) it
# stays, unless `fits_s32` shows the value is in range anyway.

# Operations whose low 32 result bits depend only on the low 32 bits of their
# operands.
_LOW_BITS_ONLY = ("add", "sub", "mul", "shl", "and", "or", "xor", "shr", "sar")
S32_MIN, S32_MAX = -(1 << 31), (1 << 31) - 1


@_cached("_low32")
def low32(expr: Expr) -> Expr:
    """`expr` with sign extensions removed where only its low 32 bits are used."""
    if isinstance(expr, SignExtend32):
        return low32(expr.value)
    if isinstance(expr, Binary) and expr.op in _LOW_BITS_ONLY:
        left = low32(expr.left)
        # A shift amount is masked by the hardware, so its low bits suffice too.
        right = low32(expr.right)
        if left is expr.left and right is expr.right:
            return expr
        return Binary(expr.op, left, right)
    if isinstance(expr, Not):
        inner = low32(expr.value)
        return expr if inner is expr.value else Not(inner)
    return expr


def address_of(expr: Expr) -> Expr:
    """An address expression in canonical form: only its low 32 bits are used."""
    return simplify(low32(simplify(expr)))


@_cached("_range")
def value_range(expr: Expr):
    """(low, high) bounds on the value as a signed 64-bit number, or None."""
    if isinstance(expr, Const):
        value = _signed(expr.value)
        return value, value
    if isinstance(expr, Load):
        bits = 8 * expr.size
        if expr.size > 4:
            return None
        if expr.signed:
            return -(1 << (bits - 1)), (1 << (bits - 1)) - 1
        return 0, (1 << bits) - 1
    if isinstance(expr, SignExtend32):
        return S32_MIN, S32_MAX
    if isinstance(expr, (Compare, Predicate, FloatPredicate, Not1)):
        return 0, 1
    if isinstance(expr, (FloatOp, VuOp, IntToFloat, FloatToInt)):
        return 0, MASK32
    if isinstance(expr, Arg) and expr.index >= FLOAT_ARG_BASE:
        return 0, MASK32
    if isinstance(expr, Select):
        a, b = value_range(expr.when_true), value_range(expr.when_false)
        if a is None or b is None:
            return None
        return min(a[0], b[0]), max(a[1], b[1])
    if isinstance(expr, Not):
        inner = value_range(expr.value)
        return None if inner is None else (-inner[1] - 1, -inner[0] - 1)
    if not isinstance(expr, Binary):
        return None
    if expr.op == "shr":
        if isinstance(expr.right, Const):
            return 0, MASK32 >> (expr.right.value & 0x1F)
        return 0, MASK32
    if expr.op == "sar":
        return S32_MIN, S32_MAX
    if expr.op == "dshr" and isinstance(expr.right, Const) and expr.right.value & 0x3F:
        return 0, ((1 << 64) - 1) >> (expr.right.value & 0x3F)
    a, b = value_range(expr.left), value_range(expr.right)
    if expr.op == "and":
        bounds = [r for r in (a, b) if r is not None and r[0] >= 0]
        if bounds:
            return 0, min(r[1] for r in bounds)
        if a is not None and b is not None and _within_s32(a) and _within_s32(b):
            return S32_MIN, S32_MAX
        return None
    if a is None or b is None:
        return None
    if expr.op in ("or", "xor"):
        if a[0] >= 0 and b[0] >= 0:
            return 0, (1 << max(a[1], b[1]).bit_length()) - 1
        if _within_s32(a) and _within_s32(b):
            return S32_MIN, S32_MAX
        return None
    if expr.op == "add":
        result = a[0] + b[0], a[1] + b[1]
    elif expr.op == "sub":
        result = a[0] - b[1], a[1] - b[0]
    elif expr.op == "mul":
        products = [a[0] * b[0], a[0] * b[1], a[1] * b[0], a[1] * b[1]]
        result = min(products), max(products)
    elif expr.op in ("shl", "dshl") and isinstance(expr.right, Const):
        factor = 1 << (expr.right.value & (0x1F if expr.op == "shl" else 0x3F))
        result = a[0] * factor, a[1] * factor
    else:
        return None
    # Outside the signed 64-bit range the value would have wrapped.
    if result[0] < -(1 << 63) or result[1] >= (1 << 63):
        return None
    return result


def _within_s32(bounds) -> bool:
    return bounds is not None and S32_MIN <= bounds[0] and bounds[1] <= S32_MAX


def fits_s32(expr: Expr) -> bool:
    """True when sign-extending the value's low 32 bits would not change it."""
    return _within_s32(value_range(expr))


# -- the symbolic machine ------------------------------------------------

_LOAD_SIZES = {
    "lb": (1, True), "lbu": (1, False),
    "lh": (2, True), "lhu": (2, False),
    "lw": (4, True), "lwu": (4, False),
    "ld": (8, False), "lq": (16, False),
}


_STORE_SIZES = {"sb": 1, "sh": 2, "sw": 4, "sd": 8, "sq": 16}

_FLOAT_BINARY = {
    "add.s": "add", "sub.s": "sub", "mul.s": "mul", "div.s": "div",
    "max.s": "max", "min.s": "min",
}
_FLOAT_UNARY = {"mov.s": "mov", "neg.s": "neg", "abs.s": "abs", "sqrt.s": "sqrt"}
# Accumulator forms: (operation, where the result goes).
_FLOAT_ACCUMULATE = {
    "adda.s": ("add", "acc"), "suba.s": ("sub", "acc"), "mula.s": ("mul", "acc"),
    "madda.s": ("madd", "acc"), "msuba.s": ("msub", "acc"),
    "madd.s": ("madd", "fd"), "msub.s": ("msub", "fd"),
}
_FLOAT_COMPARE = {"c.eq.s": "eq", "c.lt.s": "lt", "c.le.s": "le", "c.f.s": "false"}

# The multiplier result registers. They are kept in the same dict as the general
# registers under indices the hardware cannot name, which avoids threading a second
# piece of state through every caller.
REG_HI = 64
REG_LO = 65

# Float registers and the FPU condition flag share the register dict under indices
# the integer unit cannot name, so no extra state has to be threaded through every
# caller. The condition flag holds a predicate expression, which is what `bc1t` and
# `bc1f` then branch on.
FPR_BASE = 128
FP_COND = 127
# The FPU accumulator, which adda/suba/mula/madda/msuba write and madd/msub read.
FP_ACC = 126

# The upper 64 bits of each general register, which only 128-bit operations - lq,
# sq, the MMI moves and logic - read or write. Everything else leaves them alone,
# as the hardware does. An upper half the function has not written is unknown (at
# entry it is the caller's), and reading it is refused rather than taken as zero.
UPPER_BASE = 192


def upper(index: int) -> int:
    return UPPER_BASE + index


def _upper_or_zero(get, index: int):
    return Const(0) if index == 0 else get(upper(index))


# VU0 state in the register dict: VF lanes, the control registers (VI0-VI15, then
# R, I, Q), and the accumulator lanes. None is known at entry except VF0, the
# constant (0, 0, 0, 1); a call clobbers all of it, since the callee may use VU0.
VF_BASE = 256
VC_BASE = 384
VACC_BASE = 416
VU_KEYS = tuple(range(VF_BASE + 4, VACC_BASE + 4))


def vf_lane(index: int, lane: int) -> int:
    return VF_BASE + 4 * index + lane


def vu_written(ins) -> set:
    """The VU0 state an instruction writes, for the loop analysis."""
    from . import vu0

    op = ins.raw >> 26
    if op == 0x36:                                    # lqc2
        return {vf_lane(ins.rt, lane) for lane in range(4)} if ins.rt else set()
    if op != 0x12:
        return set()
    word, m = ins.raw, ins.mnemonic
    fd, ft = (word >> 6) & 0x1F, (word >> 16) & 0x1F
    index = (word >> 11) & 0x1F
    dest = (word >> 21) & 0xF
    lanes = [lane for lane, bit in enumerate((8, 4, 2, 1)) if dest & bit]
    base = m.split(".")[0]
    if m == "qmtc2":
        return {vf_lane(index, lane) for lane in range(4)} if index else set()
    if m == "ctc2":
        return {VC_BASE + index}
    if m in ("qmfc2", "cfc2"):
        return set()
    if base == "vopmula":
        return {VACC_BASE + lane for lane in lanes if lane < 3}
    if base == "vopmsub":
        return {vf_lane(fd, lane) for lane in lanes if lane < 3} if fd else set()
    operation, to_acc, _operand = vu0._split(base)
    if operation is not None:
        if to_acc:
            return {VACC_BASE + lane for lane in lanes}
        return {vf_lane(fd, lane) for lane in lanes} if fd else set()
    if base in ("vmove", "vmr32", "vabs") or base[:5] in ("vitof", "vftoi"):
        return {vf_lane(ft, lane) for lane in lanes} if ft else set()
    if base in ("vdiv", "vsqrt", "vrsqrt"):
        return {VC_BASE + vu0.REG_Q}
    return set()


# Instructions that write an upper half, for the loop analysis: (mnemonic -> field).
QUAD_WRITERS = {"lq": "rt", "pcpyld": "rd", "pcpyud": "rd", "por": "rd", "pand": "rd",
                "pxor": "rd", "pnor": "rd"}


# Where a call's float result is read from: $f0, as CallResult.register.
FLOAT_RESULT = FPR_BASE


def fpr(index: int) -> int:
    return FPR_BASE + index


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Store:
    """One memory write a function performs, as a pair of expressions."""

    address: Expr
    value: Expr
    size: int

    def render(self) -> str:
        kind = {1: "u8", 2: "u16", 4: "u32", 8: "u64", 16: "u128"}[self.size]
        return "*(%s*)(%s) = %s;" % (
            kind, simplify(self.address).render(), simplify(self.value).render()
        )


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Derivation:
    address: int
    expression: Expr
    instructions: int
    stores: tuple = ()

    def render(self) -> str:
        lines = [store.render() for store in self.stores]
        lines.append("return %s;" % simplify(self.expression).render())
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def evaluate(self, args, read) -> int:
        return _sign32(simplify(self.expression).evaluate(args, read) & MASK32)

    def evaluate_stores(self, args, read) -> list:
        """Resolve each store to a concrete (address, value, size) triple.

        Addresses and values are evaluated against the state *before* any store is
        applied, which is correct only because a derivation is refused if it ever
        loads from an address it has already written - see `derive`.
        """
        out = []
        for store in self.stores:
            address = simplify(store.address).evaluate(args, read) & MASK32
            value = simplify(store.value).evaluate(args, read)
            out.append((address, value & ((1 << (store.size * 8)) - 1), store.size))
        return out


def derive(image: bytes, base: int, start: int, end: int,
           gp_value: int = None) -> Derivation:
    """Derive the return expression and memory effects of a branch-free function.

    `$gp` is seeded with its startup value, since globals are commonly reached as
    an offset from it and refusing those would exclude a large set of otherwise
    simple functions.
    """
    if gp_value is None:
        from .layout import CURRENT

        gp_value = CURRENT.gp
    regs = {0: Const(0), 28: Const(gp_value)}
    for i, reg in enumerate(INT_ARG_REGS):
        regs[reg] = Arg(i)
    stores = []

    def get(index: int) -> Expr:
        if index == 0:
            return Const(0)
        if index not in regs:
            raise Unsupported("reads uninitialised register $%d" % index)
        return regs[index]

    addr = start
    count = 0
    while addr < end:
        word = struct.unpack_from("<I", image, addr - base)[0]
        ins = DISASM.decode(word, addr)
        count += 1
        m = ins.mnemonic

        if m == "nop" or m == "sync":
            addr += 4
            continue

        if m == "jr":
            if not ins.is_return:
                raise Unsupported("indirect jump")
            # The delay slot still executes, so fold it in before finishing.
            slot_addr = addr + 4
            if slot_addr < end:
                slot_word = struct.unpack_from("<I", image, slot_addr - base)[0]
                slot = DISASM.decode(slot_word, slot_addr)
                if slot.mnemonic in _STORE_SIZES:
                    size = _STORE_SIZES[slot.mnemonic]
                    if size == 16:
                        raise Unsupported("128-bit store")
                    target = simplify(
                        Binary("add", get(slot.rs), Const(slot.imm & MASK64))
                    )
                    stores.append(Store(target, get(slot.rt), size))
                elif slot.mnemonic not in ("nop", "sync"):
                    _apply(regs, slot, get)
            return Derivation(start, get(2), count + 1, tuple(stores))

        if ins.is_branch or ins.is_jump:
            raise Unsupported("control flow: %s" % m)

        if m in _STORE_SIZES:
            size = _STORE_SIZES[m]
            if size == 16:
                # A quadword store needs the upper half of the register, which the
                # expression model does not carry.
                raise Unsupported("128-bit store")
            target = address_of(Binary("add", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & MASK64)))
            stores.append(Store(target, get(ins.rt), size))
            addr += 4
            continue

        if ins.mnemonic in _LOAD_SIZES and stores:
            # Loading after storing would make the result depend on the order the
            # stores were applied, which `evaluate_stores` does not model. Rare
            # enough to refuse rather than complicate.
            raise Unsupported("loads after a store")

        _apply(regs, ins, get)
        addr += 4

    raise Unsupported("no return reached")


def _apply_vu0(regs: dict, ins, get) -> None:
    """VU0 macro mode over lane expressions, following vu0.execute."""
    from . import vu0

    word, m = ins.raw, ins.mnemonic
    base = m.split(".")[0]
    fd, fs, ft = (word >> 6) & 0x1F, (word >> 11) & 0x1F, (word >> 16) & 0x1F
    dest = (word >> 21) & 0xF
    lanes = [lane for lane, bit in enumerate((8, 4, 2, 1)) if dest & bit]

    def lane(index, which):
        if index == 0:
            return Const((0, 0, 0, vu0.ONE)[which])
        return get(vf_lane(index, which))

    def write(index, values):
        if index:
            for which in lanes:
                regs[vf_lane(index, which)] = values[which]

    if m == "qmtc2":
        index = (word >> 11) & 0x1F
        if index:
            low = get(ins.rt) if ins.rt else Const(0)
            try:
                high = _upper_or_zero(get, ins.rt)
            except Unsupported:
                # The upper half is the caller's: z and w are unknown, and refused
                # only if something reads them - code using x and y still derives.
                high = None
            for which, (half, shift) in enumerate(((low, 0), (low, 32), (high, 0), (high, 32))):
                if half is None:
                    regs.pop(vf_lane(index, which), None)
                    continue
                part = Binary("dshr", half, Const(shift)) if shift else half
                regs[vf_lane(index, which)] = Binary("and", part, Const(MASK32))
        return
    if m == "qmfc2":
        index = (word >> 11) & 0x1F
        if ins.rt:
            x, y, z, w = (lane(index, which) for which in range(4))
            regs[ins.rt] = Binary("or", x, Binary("dshl", y, Const(32)))
            regs[upper(ins.rt)] = Binary("or", z, Binary("dshl", w, Const(32)))
        return
    if m in ("ctc2", "cfc2"):
        index = (word >> 11) & 0x1F
        if m == "cfc2":
            if index in vu0.UNREADABLE:
                raise Unsupported("cfc2 of an unmodelled VU0 flag register")
            if ins.rt:
                regs[ins.rt] = SignExtend32(get(VC_BASE + index)) if index else Const(0)
            return
        value = get(ins.rt) if ins.rt else Const(0)
        if index < 16:
            if index:
                regs[VC_BASE + index] = Binary("and", value, Const(0xFFFF))
        elif index == vu0.REG_R:
            regs[VC_BASE + index] = Binary("or", Binary("and", value, Const(0x7FFFFF)),
                                           Const(vu0.ONE))
        else:
            regs[VC_BASE + index] = Binary("and", value, Const(MASK32))
        return

    op, to_acc, operand = vu0._split(base)
    if op is not None and base not in ("vopmula", "vopmsub"):
        # Only the lanes the mask selects are read: x/y-only maths on a register
        # whose z and w are unknown is fine.
        if operand in ("x", "y", "z", "w"):
            broadcast = lane(ft, "xyzw".index(operand))
            second = lambda which: broadcast
        elif operand in ("q", "i"):
            special = get(VC_BASE + (vu0.REG_Q if operand == "q" else vu0.REG_I))
            second = lambda which: special
        elif operand == "":
            second = lambda which: lane(ft, which)
        else:
            raise Unsupported("VU0 %s" % base)
        out = [None] * 4
        for which in lanes:
            a = lane(fs, which)
            if op in ("madd", "msub"):
                out[which] = VuOp(op, get(VACC_BASE + which), a, second(which))
            else:
                out[which] = VuOp(op, a, second(which))
        if to_acc:
            for which in lanes:
                regs[VACC_BASE + which] = out[which]
        else:
            write(fd, out)
        return
    if base == "vopmula":
        pairs = ((1, 2), (2, 0), (0, 1))
        for which in lanes:
            if which < 3:
                i, j = pairs[which]
                regs[VACC_BASE + which] = VuOp("mul", lane(fs, i), lane(ft, j))
        return
    if base == "vopmsub":
        pairs = ((1, 2), (2, 0), (0, 1))
        out = [None] * 4
        for which in lanes:
            if which < 3:
                i, j = pairs[which]
                out[which] = VuOp("msub", get(VACC_BASE + which), lane(fs, i), lane(ft, j))
        if fd:
            for which in lanes:
                if which < 3:
                    regs[vf_lane(fd, which)] = out[which]
        return
    if base in ("vmove", "vmr32"):
        rotate = 1 if base == "vmr32" else 0
        write(ft, [lane(fs, (which + rotate) % 4) for which in range(4)])
        return
    if base == "vabs":
        write(ft, [VuOp("abs", lane(fs, which)) for which in range(4)])
        return
    if base[:5] in ("vitof", "vftoi"):
        kind = "itof" if base.startswith("vitof") else "ftoi"
        write(ft, [VuOp(kind, lane(fs, which), shift=int(base[5:])) for which in range(4)])
        return
    if base in ("vnop", "vwaitq"):
        return
    fsf, ftf = (word >> 21) & 3, (word >> 23) & 3
    if base == "vdiv":
        regs[VC_BASE + vu0.REG_Q] = VuOp("div", lane(fs, fsf), lane(ft, ftf))
        return
    if base == "vsqrt":
        regs[VC_BASE + vu0.REG_Q] = VuOp("sqrt", lane(ft, ftf))
        return
    if base == "vrsqrt":
        regs[VC_BASE + vu0.REG_Q] = VuOp("rsqrt", lane(fs, fsf), lane(ft, ftf))
        return
    raise Unsupported("no symbolic rule for %s" % base)


def _apply_quad(regs: dict, ins, get) -> None:
    """The 128-bit moves and logic, over (low, upper) pairs."""
    m, rd, rs, rt = ins.mnemonic, ins.rd, ins.rs, ins.rt
    if rd == 0:
        return
    if m == "pcpyld":
        low, high = get(rt), get(rs)
    elif m == "pcpyud":
        low, high = _upper_or_zero(get, rs), _upper_or_zero(get, rt)
    else:
        op = {"por": "or", "pand": "and", "pxor": "xor", "pnor": "or"}[m]
        low = Binary(op, get(rs), get(rt))
        try:
            high = Binary(op, _upper_or_zero(get, rs), _upper_or_zero(get, rt))
        except Unsupported:
            high = None          # an upper half nobody wrote: unknown, refused if read
        if m == "pnor":
            low = Not(low)
            high = Not(high) if high is not None else None
    regs[rd] = low
    if high is None:
        regs.pop(upper(rd), None)
    else:
        regs[upper(rd)] = high


def _apply(regs: dict, ins, get, epoch: int = 0) -> None:
    """Apply one instruction to the symbolic register state."""
    m = ins.mnemonic

    if m == "lq":
        # Both halves, from the quadword the hardware aligns the address down to.
        address = address_of(Binary("and", Binary("add", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & MASK64)),
                                    Const(~0xF & MASK64)))
        if ins.rt:
            regs[ins.rt] = Load(address, 8, False, epoch)
            regs[upper(ins.rt)] = Load(address_of(Binary("add", address, Const(8))), 8, False,
                                       epoch)
        return
    if m in ("pcpyld", "pcpyud", "por", "pand", "pxor", "pnor"):
        _apply_quad(regs, ins, get)
        return
    if ins.raw >> 26 == 0x12:
        _apply_vu0(regs, ins, get)
        return
    if m in _LOAD_SIZES:
        size, signed = _LOAD_SIZES[m]
        address = address_of(Binary("add", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & MASK64)))
        regs[ins.rt] = Load(address, size, signed, epoch)
        return

    if m == "lui":
        # The result is a 32-bit value sign-extended into the 64-bit register, which
        # matters as soon as anything manipulates it 64 bits wide: `lui 0xFFFF`
        # followed by `dsrl32 ..., 32` yields 0xFFFFFFFF, not 0. Dropping the
        # sign-extension produced exactly that wrong mask.
        regs[ins.rt] = Const(_sign32((ins.imm & 0xFFFF) << 16) & MASK64)
        return
    if m in ("addiu", "addi"):
        regs[ins.rt] = SignExtend32(Binary("add", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & MASK64)))
        return
    if m in ("daddiu", "daddi"):
        regs[ins.rt] = Binary("add", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & MASK64))
        return
    if m == "andi":
        regs[ins.rt] = Binary("and", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & 0xFFFF))
        return
    if m == "ori":
        regs[ins.rt] = Binary("or", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & 0xFFFF))
        return
    if m == "xori":
        regs[ins.rt] = Binary("xor", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & 0xFFFF))
        return
    if m == "sltiu":
        regs[ins.rt] = Compare("ltu", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & MASK64))
        return
    if m == "slti":
        regs[ins.rt] = Compare("lt", get(ins.rs), Const(ins.imm & MASK64))
        return

    # Word operations sign-extend their 32-bit result into the 64-bit register;
    # the doubleword forms keep all 64 bits. The model used to give both the
    # 64-bit result, which only shows where upper bits are observed - a `slt` on
    # the result of an `sllv` - and so went unnoticed until arguments other than
    # small pointers reached the tests. `simplify` removes the extension again
    # wherever upper bits cannot matter.
    if m in ("addu", "add"):
        regs[ins.rd] = SignExtend32(Binary("add", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt)))
        return
    if m in ("daddu", "dadd"):
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("add", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt))
        return
    if m in ("subu", "sub"):
        regs[ins.rd] = SignExtend32(Binary("sub", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt)))
        return
    if m in ("dsubu", "dsub"):
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("sub", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt))
        return
    if m == "and":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("and", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt))
        return
    if m == "or":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("or", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt))
        return
    if m == "xor":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("xor", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt))
        return
    if m == "sltu":
        regs[ins.rd] = Compare("ltu", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt))
        return
    if m == "slt":
        regs[ins.rd] = Compare("lt", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt))
        return

    if m == "sll":
        regs[ins.rd] = SignExtend32(Binary("shl", get(ins.rt), Const(ins.imm)))
        return
    if m == "srl":
        regs[ins.rd] = SignExtend32(Binary("shr", get(ins.rt), Const(ins.imm)))
        return
    if m == "sra":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("sar", get(ins.rt), Const(ins.imm))
        return
    if m == "dsll":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("dshl", get(ins.rt), Const(ins.imm))
        return
    if m == "dsrl":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("dshr", get(ins.rt), Const(ins.imm))
        return
    if m == "dsra":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("dsar", get(ins.rt), Const(ins.imm))
        return
    # The 32-prefixed forms add 32 to the shift amount.
    if m == "dsll32":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("dshl", get(ins.rt), Const(ins.imm + 32))
        return
    if m == "dsrl32":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("dshr", get(ins.rt), Const(ins.imm + 32))
        return
    if m == "dsra32":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("dsar", get(ins.rt), Const(ins.imm + 32))
        return
    # Variable shifts take their amount from a register.
    if m == "sllv":
        regs[ins.rd] = SignExtend32(Binary("shl", get(ins.rt), get(ins.rs)))
        return
    if m == "srlv":
        regs[ins.rd] = SignExtend32(Binary("shr", get(ins.rt), get(ins.rs)))
        return
    if m == "srav":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("sar", get(ins.rt), get(ins.rs))
        return
    if m == "dsllv":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("dshl", get(ins.rt), get(ins.rs))
        return
    if m == "dsrlv":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("dshr", get(ins.rt), get(ins.rs))
        return
    if m == "dsrav":
        regs[ins.rd] = Binary("dsar", get(ins.rt), get(ins.rs))
        return

    if m == "nor":
        regs[ins.rd] = Not(Binary("or", get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt)))
        return

    # Conditional moves leave the destination untouched when the condition fails,
    # so the previous value is part of the result. Without it there is nothing to
    # express, hence the refusal rather than a guess.
    if m in ("movz", "movn"):
        if ins.rd not in regs:
            raise Unsupported("conditional move over an uninitialised destination")
        op = "eq" if m == "movz" else "ne"
        regs[ins.rd] = Select(
            Predicate(op, get(ins.rt), Const(0)), get(ins.rs), regs[ins.rd]
        )
        return

    # Multiply and divide deposit their results in HI/LO, which `mfhi`/`mflo` then
    # read. Modelling the pair keeps the common "multiply then mflo" sequence
    # derivable.
    if m == "mult":
        # A signed 32x32 -> 64 multiply. Multiplying the raw 64-bit register values
        # would be wrong whenever an operand has its high bits set, so both are
        # narrowed to 32 bits and sign-extended first. LO holds the low word
        # sign-extended; HI the high word.
        product = Binary("mul", SignExtend32(get(ins.rs)), SignExtend32(get(ins.rt)))
        regs[REG_LO] = SignExtend32(product)
        regs[REG_HI] = SignExtend32(Binary("dsar", product, Const(32)))
        if ins.rd:
            regs[ins.rd] = regs[REG_LO]
        return
    if m == "multu":
        # Zero-extended 32-bit operands: their 64-bit product cannot overflow.
        product = Binary("mul", Binary("and", get(ins.rs), Const(MASK32)),
                         Binary("and", get(ins.rt), Const(MASK32)))
        regs[REG_LO] = SignExtend32(product)
        regs[REG_HI] = SignExtend32(Binary("dshr", product, Const(32)))
        if ins.rd:
            regs[ins.rd] = regs[REG_LO]
        return
    if m in ("div", "divu"):
        # Defined for every input, a zero divisor included (emu.divide).
        suffix = "u" if m == "divu" else ""
        regs[REG_LO] = IntDiv("quot" + suffix, get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt))
        regs[REG_HI] = IntDiv("rem" + suffix, get(ins.rs), get(ins.rt))
        return
    # -- coprocessor 1 (single precision) ---------------------------------
    #
    # COP1 R-format packs its registers differently from the integer unit, and the
    # disassembler does not populate rs/rt/rd for those forms, so the fields come
    # straight from the encoding.
    if m in _FLOAT_BINARY:
        fd, fs, ft = (ins.raw >> 6) & 0x1F, (ins.raw >> 11) & 0x1F, (ins.raw >> 16) & 0x1F
        regs[fpr(fd)] = FloatOp(_FLOAT_BINARY[m], get(fpr(fs)), get(fpr(ft)))
        return
    if m in _FLOAT_ACCUMULATE:
        fd, fs, ft = (ins.raw >> 6) & 0x1F, (ins.raw >> 11) & 0x1F, (ins.raw >> 16) & 0x1F
        op, target = _FLOAT_ACCUMULATE[m]
        if op in ("madd", "msub"):
            value = FloatOp(op, get(FP_ACC), get(fpr(fs)), get(fpr(ft)))
        else:
            value = FloatOp(op, get(fpr(fs)), get(fpr(ft)))
        regs[FP_ACC if target == "acc" else fpr(fd)] = value
        return
    if m in _FLOAT_UNARY:
        fd, fs = (ins.raw >> 6) & 0x1F, (ins.raw >> 11) & 0x1F
        if m == "sqrt.s":
            fs = (ins.raw >> 16) & 0x1F      # sqrt.s fd, ft: the operand is in ft
        regs[fpr(fd)] = FloatOp(_FLOAT_UNARY[m], get(fpr(fs)))
        return
    if m == "cvt.s.w":
        fd, fs = (ins.raw >> 6) & 0x1F, (ins.raw >> 11) & 0x1F
        regs[fpr(fd)] = IntToFloat(get(fpr(fs)))
        return
    if m == "cvt.w.s":
        fd, fs = (ins.raw >> 6) & 0x1F, (ins.raw >> 11) & 0x1F
        regs[fpr(fd)] = FloatToInt(get(fpr(fs)))
        return
    if m in _FLOAT_COMPARE:
        fs, ft = (ins.raw >> 11) & 0x1F, (ins.raw >> 16) & 0x1F
        regs[FP_COND] = FloatPredicate(_FLOAT_COMPARE[m], get(fpr(fs)), get(fpr(ft)))
        return
    if m == "mtc1":
        regs[fpr(ins.rd)] = get(ins.rt)
        return
    if m == "mfc1":
        regs[ins.rt] = SignExtend32(get(fpr(ins.rd)))
        return

    if m == "mfhi":
        regs[ins.rd] = get(REG_HI)
        return
    if m == "mflo":
        regs[ins.rd] = get(REG_LO)
        return
    if m == "mthi":
        regs[REG_HI] = get(ins.rs)
        return
    if m == "mtlo":
        regs[REG_LO] = get(ins.rs)
        return

    raise Unsupported("no symbolic rule for %s" % m)

```

`ps2decomp/testmem.py`:

```py
"""Memory contents for differential tests.

The tests run original functions against a scratch region of fake memory, and what
that region holds decides whether a function can be tested at all.

Uniform random bytes were the original choice and turned out to be a poor one. Any
pointer a function loads from them is a wild 32-bit value, so pointer-chasing code
faults on the first dereference, and any loop count it loads is in the billions, so
counted loops exhaust the instruction budget. Measured on the functions whose only
obstacle is a loop, 117 of 330 faulted and 32 ran out of budget - not because the
interpreter lacked anything (it hit no unsupported instruction at all) but because
the inputs made no sense.

No single alternative fixes everything, because a word one function reads as a
pointer another reads as a count. So there are several shapes, and a harness tries
them in turn, keeping the first under which the original executes:

  noise     uniform random words (the old behaviour, still occasionally the only fit)
  mixed     pointers into the region in even words, small integers in odd ones
  small     small integers only, for counts, indices and flags
  pointers  pointers into the region only, for linked structures

Trying all four took the loop-only set from 181 executable functions to 247.

Three more come last, for loops the others never end:

  zero       all zeros: a search for a key stops at once (the key read is 0 as
             well), a count read from memory is 0, a null link ends a list
  zero-self  each even word its own address, odd words 0
  self       each word its own address: an intrusive circular list whose
             links point back at its head (RenderWare's) is empty

Sampled on functions untestable for running out of instructions, these let
one in eight finish.

The choice of profile changes only what the test can *reach*, never what it
concludes: the original and the derivation always read the same memory.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
import struct
import zlib

from . import layout

# The scratch region's place and size come from the game's layout (layout.py).

# Order matters: the first profile under which a function executes is the one it is
# tested with, so the most generally useful shapes come first.
# "forward" and "forward-mixed" come last: they only matter to functions no other
# shape lets finish - typically list walks, which loop forever on the cycles that
# random pointers make. Their pointers only point further on, or are null, so every
# chain followed through them ends.
PROFILES = ("mixed", "noise", "small", "pointers", "forward", "forward-mixed", "zero", "zero-self", "self")

# Small integers stay below this so a count read from memory gives a short loop.
SMALL_LIMIT = 16


# Each test case needs memory that *differs* from the previous case's, not memory
# that is unique across the whole run. Building 32K random words in Python for every
# case made the derivation run 25x slower, so buffers come from a small cached pool
# per profile instead; consecutive seeds still select different buffers.
POOL_SIZE = 16
_POOL = {}


def build(kind: str, seed: int) -> bytes:
    """One profile's contents for the scratch region, deterministic in `seed`."""
    key = (kind, seed % POOL_SIZE, layout.CURRENT.scratch, layout.CURRENT.scratch_size)
    buffer = _POOL.get(key)
    if buffer is None:
        buffer = _build(kind, key[1])
        _POOL[key] = buffer
    return buffer


def _build(kind: str, seed: int) -> bytes:
    """Fill the scratch region with one profile's contents, deterministically."""
    # zlib.crc32 rather than hash(): Python randomises string hashes per process,
    # which would give different "deterministic" memory on every run and make a
    # failing test impossible to reproduce.
    rng = random.Random((zlib.crc32(kind.encode("ascii")) << 16) ^ seed)
    SCRATCH, SCRATCH_SIZE = layout.CURRENT.scratch, layout.CURRENT.scratch_size
    count = SCRATCH_SIZE // 4

    def pointer() -> int:
        # 16-aligned and clear of the end, so a structure read through it stays in
        # range for a reasonable span of fields.
        return SCRATCH + rng.randrange(0, SCRATCH_SIZE - 0x100, 16)

    if kind == "noise":
        words = [rng.getrandbits(32) for _ in range(count)]
    elif kind == "small":
        words = [rng.randrange(SMALL_LIMIT) for _ in range(count)]
    elif kind == "pointers":
        words = [pointer() for _ in range(count)]
    elif kind == "mixed":
        words = [pointer() if i % 2 == 0 else rng.randrange(SMALL_LIMIT)
                 for i in range(count)]
    elif kind in ("forward", "forward-mixed"):
        def forward(i: int) -> int:
            address = SCRATCH + 4 * i
            if rng.random() < 0.25 or address + 0x200 >= SCRATCH + SCRATCH_SIZE - 0x100:
                return 0
            return (address + rng.randrange(16, 0x200)) & ~15
        words = [rng.randrange(SMALL_LIMIT) if kind == "forward-mixed" and i % 2
                 else forward(i) for i in range(count)]
    elif kind == "zero":
        words = [0] * count
    elif kind == "zero-self":
        words = [SCRATCH + 4 * i if i % 2 == 0 else 0 for i in range(count)]
    elif kind == "self":
        words = [SCRATCH + 4 * i for i in range(count)]
    else:
        raise ValueError("unknown memory profile %r" % kind)
    return struct.pack("<%dI" % count, *words)


def arguments(rng: random.Random) -> tuple:
    """A full register argument vector: eight integers, then eight floats.

    The integers are 16-aligned pointers into the first half of scratch. The first
    four are drawn exactly as they were when only four arguments existed, so the
    cases every earlier function was verified on are unchanged. The floats are bit
    patterns of ordinary values - a mix of small exact ones and random magnitudes -
    rather than random bits, which would be mostly NaNs and denormals.
    """
    scratch, size = layout.CURRENT.scratch, layout.CURRENT.scratch_size
    integers = [scratch + rng.randrange(0, size // 2, 16) for _ in range(8)]
    return tuple(integers) + tuple(float_bits(rng) for _ in range(8))


FLOAT_CASES = (0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 0.5, 2.0, -0.25, 100.0, 3.5)


def float_bits(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    """The bit pattern of a plausible float argument."""
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        value = rng.choice(FLOAT_CASES)
    else:
        value = rng.uniform(-1000.0, 1000.0)
    return struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", value))[0]


def seed_global_pointers(memory, addresses) -> int:
    """Point zero-valued global pointer variables at the scratch region.

    Game state - a manager object, the current race, a list head - is reached
    through global pointers that are null in the executable and only set up once
    the game is running. Any function that dereferences one faulted in every test,
    whatever the scratch memory held: 712 otherwise derivable functions could not be
    tested for that reason alone. The recovered types say which globals are
    dereferenced as pointers; each one still holding zero is given a deterministic
    address in scratch. Like the memory profiles, this decides only what a test can
    reach - the original and the derivation read the same memory - and it is
    written once, outside any test's journal.
    """
    seeded = 0
    for address in sorted(addresses):
        try:
            if memory.read_int(address, 4, False) != 0:
                continue
        except Exception:
            continue
        size = layout.CURRENT.scratch_size
        # Every word in one 16-byte block gets the same target, so a [begin, end)
        # pair of adjacent globals describes an empty range rather than one
        # running from one random place to another - a walk over it, as in the
        # SIF RPC binder, otherwise never meets its end.
        block = address & ~15
        offset = (zlib.crc32(block.to_bytes(4, "little")) % (size // 2)) & ~15
        memory.write_int(address, layout.CURRENT.scratch + offset, 4)
        seeded += 1
    return seeded


# A dereference this close to address zero is a null pointer plus a field offset.
NULL_PAGE = 0x1000


def discover_null_pointers(machine, functions, is_global, budget: int = 20_000,
                           attempts: int = 8) -> int:
    """Seed the global pointers that running the code shows to be dereferenced.

    `seed_global_pointers` covers the globals the recovered types mark as pointers,
    but not pointer fields of global *objects* - a singleton whose address is
    passed to its methods, which then follow a pointer inside it that is null until
    the game runs. Recovering those statically drowns in merged types, so they are
    found by running instead: each function is run once, and when it faults just
    above address zero, the last word it read as zero is taken to be the null
    pointer, seeded like any other global, and the function run again.

    `is_global(address)` limits seeding to the program's own data - never code,
    the stack or the scratch region. The functions are visited in the order given
    and every seed is written outside any journal, so the result is deterministic
    and the same for every test that follows. Returns the addresses seeded.
    """
    from .emu import MemoryFault

    memory = machine.memory
    scratch = layout.CURRENT.scratch
    seeded = []
    memory.watch_zero = True
    try:
        for func in functions:
            args = arguments(random.Random(func["addr"]))
            for _attempt in range(attempts):
                memory.end_journal()
                memory.write(scratch, build("pointers", func["addr"]))
                memory.begin_journal()
                memory.last_zero_read = None
                fault = None
                try:
                    machine.call(func["addr"], args, max_instructions=budget)
                except MemoryFault as exc:
                    fault = exc
                except Exception:
                    pass
                source = memory.last_zero_read
                stack_pointer = machine.get(29) & 0xFFFFFFFF
                memory.rollback()
                memory.end_journal()
                if (fault is None or fault.addr >= NULL_PAGE or source is None
                        or source >= stack_pointer or not is_global(source)):
                    break
                if seed_global_pointers(memory, {source}):
                    seeded.append(source)
    finally:
        memory.watch_zero = False
        memory.last_zero_read = None
    return seeded


def page_contents(page: int) -> bytes:
    """What a page mapped on demand holds: the "mixed" shape, seeded by its address.

    Pointers into scratch in even words and small integers in odd ones, as the
    mixed profile has, so code that faulted following a wild pointer finds the
    kind of memory the tests are built on - and its own page differs from every
    other page, deterministically.
    """
    rng = random.Random(zlib.crc32(page.to_bytes(4, "little")) ^ 0x9A6E)
    scratch, size = layout.CURRENT.scratch, layout.CURRENT.scratch_size
    words = [scratch + rng.randrange(0, size - 0x100, 16) if i % 2 == 0
             else rng.randrange(SMALL_LIMIT) for i in range(0x1000 // 4)]
    return struct.pack("<%dI" % len(words), *words)


# How much of the stack above the test stack top - the caller's frame - is filled.
CALLER_FRAME = 0x400


def fill_caller_frame(memory) -> None:
    """Fill the stack above the test stack top with the return sentinel.

    Function discovery also finds fragments: shared epilogue tails entered with a
    frame they never built. They restore $ra (and saved registers) from their
    caller's frame and return through it - to address 0, when that memory is zero,
    so every test of them failed. With the sentinel there, a fragment's return
    ends the test as a function's does, and its own work - the restores, the
    result - is compared like any other. Written once, outside any journal.
    """
    from .emu import RETURN_SENTINEL

    words = CALLER_FRAME // 4
    memory.write(layout.CURRENT.stack_top,
                 struct.pack("<%dI" % words, *([RETURN_SENTINEL] * words)))

```

`ps2decomp/testplan.py`:

```py
"""Test cases for checking a function against the original machine code.

How a function is tested - the test memory and its seeding, the arguments and
memory profile chosen, running the original and a candidate on each case, and
comparing what they did to memory - shared by derivation (engine/tools/derive.py)
and lifting (liftverify.py). It decides verdicts, so remembered lift verdicts are
keyed by it (verdicts.py); derivation itself is not part of that key.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
import hashlib
import random
import re
import time

from . import layout, structs, testmem

# Instructions one verification case may execute, callees included. Interpreting
# is slow, and a function that calls into a large original routine would otherwise
# spend minutes per case; one that needs more than this is reported untestable.
VERIFY_BUDGET = 100_000
# The callee's own frame. Writes here are not observable effects, so they are
# excluded when comparing what the original and the derivation did to memory.
# The stack, scratch memory and the rest of the layout come from the game; see
# ps2decomp/layout.py.
ARG_SETS = 8

# Why the last test that could not be run failed: (stage, exception). Set wherever
# a test run is abandoned, and read by _attempt to explain an untestable verdict.
_LAST_FAILURE = None
_HEX = re.compile(r"0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+|\b\d+\b")


def _failed(stage, exc) -> None:
    global _LAST_FAILURE
    _LAST_FAILURE = (stage, exc)


def failure_reason() -> str:
    """The last failure as a category: numbers and addresses blanked so that
    failures of one kind count together."""
    if _LAST_FAILURE is None:
        return "unknown"
    stage, exc = _LAST_FAILURE
    message = _HEX.sub("N", str(exc).splitlines()[0] if str(exc) else "")
    return "%s: %s: %s" % (stage, type(exc).__name__, message[:90])


_GRAPHS = {}


def recovered_graph(database, image, base):
    """The struct-type graph for this binary, recovered once per run.

    It is needed to seed global pointers before testing and again to type the
    emitted source; recovering it twice was a fifth of a whole run.
    """
    key = (id(database), base)
    if key not in _GRAPHS:
        _GRAPHS[key] = structs.recover(database, image, base)
    return _GRAPHS[key]


def prepare_test_memory(machine, database, image, base, functions, verbose=False,
                        seeds=None) -> list:
    """Fill scratch and seed null global pointers, identically for every tool.

    Global pointers that are null until the game runs would make every function
    using them untestable, so they are pointed at scratch: first the ones the
    recovered types mark as pointers, then the ones found by running the
    functions (see testmem.discover_null_pointers).

    Returns the addresses seeded. Passing them back as `seeds` reproduces the same
    memory without the discovery - how a worker process matches its parent.
    """
    rng = random.Random(0xB3)
    machine.memory.write(layout.CURRENT.scratch,
                         bytes(rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(layout.CURRENT.scratch_size)))
    testmem.fill_caller_frame(machine.memory)
    if seeds is not None:
        testmem.seed_global_pointers(machine.memory, seeds)
        machine.memory.page_source = testmem.page_contents
        machine.map_faults = True
        return seeds
    static = global_pointers(database, image, base)
    seeded = testmem.seed_global_pointers(machine.memory, static)
    spans = sorted((f["addr"], f["end"]) for f in database["functions"])
    starts = [start for start, _end in spans]
    scratch_low = layout.CURRENT.scratch
    scratch_high = scratch_low + layout.CURRENT.scratch_size

    def is_global(address):
        if not base <= address < machine.memory.base + machine.memory.size:
            return False
        if scratch_low <= address < scratch_high:
            return False
        index = bisect.bisect_right(starts, address) - 1
        return index < 0 or address >= spans[index][1]

    started = time.time()
    found = testmem.discover_null_pointers(machine, functions, is_global)
    if verbose:
        print("  seeded %d null global pointers for testing, and %d more found by "
              "running (%.0fs)" % (seeded, len(found), time.time() - started))
    # From here on a test that faults on unmapped memory maps the page and runs
    # again. Only after the discovery above, which finds null pointers by their
    # faults.
    machine.memory.page_source = testmem.page_contents
    machine.map_faults = True
    return sorted(set(static) | set(found))


def global_pointers(database, image, base) -> set:
    """Addresses of global variables that some code dereferences as a pointer."""
    graph = recovered_graph(database, image, base)
    if structs.GLOBALS not in graph.ids:
        return set()
    fields = graph.fields[graph.find(graph.ids[structs.GLOBALS])]
    return {address & 0xFFFFFFFF for address, field in fields.items()
            if field.target is not None and 4 in field.widths()}


def _effects_digest(memory) -> bytes:
    """A function's net memory effects, reduced to a digest for comparison.

    Only equality is ever asked of the effects in a test, and the original's are
    kept for every verified function so the compiled check can reuse them. As
    dictionaries, a function filling a large buffer cost about a hundred bytes per
    byte written, eight cases over, for every such function - enough to exhaust
    memory once seeded globals let those functions run to completion.
    """
    effects = _journal_effects(memory)
    digest = hashlib.sha1()
    for position in sorted(effects):
        digest.update((position & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, "little"))
        digest.update(bytes((effects[position],)))
    return digest.digest()


def _journal_effects(memory) -> dict:
    """Collapse a write journal into a net address -> byte map.

    Keyed by address, not by the journal's buffer positions: a page mapped on
    demand sits at a different position in every process that mapped pages in a
    different order, and effects recorded in one process are compared in another
    (the parallel derivation's compiled check).

    Comparing journals directly would be wrong: the original and the derivation may
    write the same bytes in a different order, or write one location twice. What has
    to match is the resulting memory, so the journal is reduced to final values.

    Writes into the callee's own stack frame are excluded. They are not observable
    effects - the frame is dead the moment the function returns - and the original
    makes plenty of them spilling registers while a derived expression makes none,
    so counting them would fail every function that has a prologue.
    """
    frame_low = layout.CURRENT.stack_low - memory.base
    frame_high = layout.CURRENT.stack_top + 0x10 - memory.base
    effects = {}
    for offset, previous in getattr(memory, "_journal", None) or ():
        for index in range(len(previous)):
            position = offset + index
            if frame_low <= position <= frame_high:
                continue
            effects[position] = memory.bytes[position]
    return {memory.address_at(position): value for position, value in effects.items()}


def _choose_profile(machine, func, args):
    """Return the first memory profile under which the original executes, or None.

    The profile only decides whether the test can *reach* the function; the original
    and the derivation always read the same memory, so it never changes a verdict.
    """
    for profile in testmem.PROFILES:
        # Pages a failing profile mapped are given back: they would otherwise use
        # up the mapping budget (emu.MAX_PAGES), and the functions tested later
        # would fault for want of a page - a loss that depends on the order.
        mark = machine.memory.page_mark()
        machine.memory.end_journal()
        machine.memory.write(layout.CURRENT.scratch, testmem.build(profile, func["addr"]))
        machine.memory.begin_journal()
        try:
            machine.call(func["addr"], args, max_instructions=VERIFY_BUDGET)
            ran = True
        except Exception as exc:
            _failed("original, every memory profile", exc)
            ran = False
        finally:
            machine.memory.rollback()
            machine.memory.end_journal()
        if ran:
            return profile
        machine.memory.unmap_to(mark)
    return None


def test_plan(func, machine):
    """The argument sets and memory profile a function is tested with, or None.

    Separate from the test itself so that anything else that must face exactly the
    same cases - the compiled C++ check - can ask for them.
    """
    # Seeded from the address so argument sets are stable across passes: a
    # function retried in a later pass must be tested on the same inputs, or a
    # pass-dependent result would be impossible to reproduce.
    local_rng = random.Random(func["addr"])
    arg_sets = [testmem.arguments(local_rng) for _ in range(ARG_SETS - 1)]
    arg_sets.append(tuple(layout.CURRENT.scratch + 16 * i for i in range(8))
                    + tuple(testmem.float_bits(local_rng) for _ in range(8)))
    profile = _choose_profile(machine, func, arg_sets[0])
    if profile is None:
        return _count_plan(func, machine, arg_sets)
    return arg_sets, profile


# Integer arguments tried as a count when every argument a pointer runs out of
# instructions, and the largest count drawn.
COUNT_ARGUMENTS = 4
COUNT_LIMIT = 64


def _count_plan(func, machine, arg_sets):
    """A plan with one integer argument a small count, or None.

    Every integer argument is a pointer into scratch, about 0x01800000 - as a
    length, a copy of 25 MB. A function passing its argument on to memcpy or
    memset ran past the budget on every case and every profile, and was
    untestable (Resident Evil Outbreak: 318 functions, most of them spinning
    in those two). Only then are the first few integer arguments tried as a
    count, one at a time, each case's drawn from its own seed; the first under
    which the original runs is the plan. A function that runs as it was never
    meets these, so no verdict reached before changes.
    """
    if _LAST_FAILURE is None or type(_LAST_FAILURE[1]).__name__ != "ExecutionLimit":
        return None
    for index in range(COUNT_ARGUMENTS):
        rng = random.Random("%d:count:%d" % (func["addr"], index))
        sets = [args[:index] + (rng.randrange(COUNT_LIMIT + 1),) + args[index + 1:]
                for args in arg_sets]
        profile = _choose_profile(machine, func, sets[0])
        if profile is not None:
            return sets, profile
    return None


def run_cases(func, machine, arg_sets, profile, evaluate, record=None, recorded=None,
              float_result=False):
    """Run the original and a candidate on every case; return (outcome, tested).

    `evaluate(args)` returns the candidate's (result, writes) for one case, with
    memory as the original saw it on entry; result is None for a void function and
    writes are (address, value, size) triples. The outcome is "ok", "mismatch" or
    "failed" (the case could not be run at all).

    `record`, a list, receives the original's (result, effects) for each case;
    `recorded` supplies them instead of running the original again. The compiled
    check uses the results recorded while the derivation was verified: they are
    the same runs on the same memory, and repeating them doubled its cost.
    """
    tested = 0
    for case, args in enumerate(arg_sets):
        # Fresh memory of the chosen shape for every case, so the test varies
        # memory as well as arguments. Written outside the journal on purpose:
        # the journal does not nest, and this region is rewritten before every
        # case anyway, so nothing leaks between them.
        machine.memory.end_journal()
        machine.memory.write(layout.CURRENT.scratch,
                             testmem.build(profile, func["addr"] + case))
        # A function with stores is only verified if its *memory effects* match
        # too, so let the original run under a journal, and then check that
        # applying the candidate's stores to the same starting state reproduces
        # exactly what the original produced.
        # Journalling rather than snapshotting a region: these functions write
        # to globals well outside the scratch area, and restoring only scratch
        # left those changes in place - which both corrupted later cases and
        # made correct derivations look wrong.
        if recorded is not None:
            if recorded[case] is None:
                continue                        # the original could not run it
            expected, effects = recorded[case]
        else:
            machine.memory.begin_journal()
            try:
                expected = machine.call(func["addr"], args, max_instructions=VERIFY_BUDGET)
                if float_result:
                    # A function returning a float returns it in $f0.
                    expected = machine.fpr[0] & 0xFFFFFFFF
            except Exception as exc:
                # An input the original cannot finish with - a loop that runs
                # past the budget on this memory, a trap, a fault beyond the
                # pages it may map - is no evidence either way: the case is left
                # out, not the function. Its callers decide how many must run
                # (derive: five of the eight), and a disagreement on any case
                # that did run still fails it.
                _failed("original", exc)
                machine.memory.rollback()
                machine.memory.end_journal()
                if record is not None:
                    record.append(None)
                continue
            effects = _effects_digest(machine.memory)
            machine.memory.rollback()
            if record is not None:
                record.append((expected, effects))

        # The candidate runs inside the replay journal: one that calls an underived
        # function writes memory as it goes - the callee must see the stores made
        # before it - rather than handing back a list of writes at the end.
        machine.memory.begin_journal()
        try:
            actual, writes = evaluate(args)
        except Exception as exc:
            _failed("derivation", exc)
            machine.memory.rollback()
            machine.memory.end_journal()
            return "failed", tested
        try:
            for address, value, size in writes:
                machine.memory.write_int(address, value, size)
        except Exception as exc:
            _failed("derivation's stores", exc)
            machine.memory.rollback()
            machine.memory.end_journal()
            return "failed", tested
        replayed = _effects_digest(machine.memory)
        machine.memory.rollback()
        machine.memory.end_journal()

        tested += 1
        # A void function leaves whatever the caller had in $v0, so there is no
        # return value to compare - only its memory effects carry meaning.
        # Comparing $v0 anyway registered 175 correct derivations as failures.
        if actual is not None and float_result:
            if expected != actual & 0xFFFFFFFF:
                return "mismatch", tested
        elif actual is not None and expected != actual:
            return "mismatch", tested
        if replayed != effects:
            return "mismatch", tested
    return "ok", tested


def reset_failure() -> None:
    global _LAST_FAILURE
    _LAST_FAILURE = None

```

`ps2decomp/typed.py`:

```py
"""Render derived functions against recovered struct types.

The emitted code stays address-based - that is what lets it be compiled and run
against the interpreter - but a value whose type was recovered becomes a *view*:
a thin object over a guest address with one accessor per field. A pointer field's
accessor returns the view of the type it points to, so a chain of loads reads as
a chain of field accesses:

    ReadS32(ReadS32(arg0 + 4) + 8)      becomes      arg0.f_04().f_08()

A load is shown as a field access only when it matches the field exactly - same
offset, same width and signedness as the field's recovered read. Anything else
stays a plain Read* call on the view's `.address`, so a type that is wrong or
incomplete can make the source less tidy but never different in meaning; and the
compiled-code check runs every function in this form.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from . import layout
from .paths import _split_address
from .structs import GLOBALS, Catalog, _offset_name
from .symexec import (Arg, Binary, Const, Load, address_of, arg_name, arg_renderer,
                      children,
                      load_renderer,
                      simplify)

READERS = {
    (1, True): "ReadS8", (1, False): "ReadU8",
    (2, True): "ReadS16", (2, False): "ReadU16",
    (4, True): "ReadS32", (4, False): "ReadU32",
    (8, False): "ReadU64",
}
WRITERS = {1: "Write8", 2: "Write16", 4: "Write32", 8: "Write64"}
VALUE_TYPES = {
    (1, True): "s8", (1, False): "u8", (2, True): "s16", (2, False): "u16",
    (4, True): "s32", (4, False): "u32", (8, False): "u64",
}


def _hex(value: int, signed: bool = False) -> str:
    text = "0x%X" % abs(value)
    if value < 0:
        return "-" + text
    return "+" + text if signed else text


MAX_STRIDE = 0x10000
# Global arrays live in the program's data (layout.image_start..image_end).
MASK64 = (1 << 64) - 1


def _sum_terms(expr):
    """The operands of a chain of additions."""
    if isinstance(expr, Binary) and expr.op == "add":
        yield from _sum_terms(expr.left)
        yield from _sum_terms(expr.right)
    else:
        yield expr


def _combine(a, b, sign):
    """a + sign*b for linear forms (coefficient, atom, constant); None if the
    atoms differ."""
    if a[1] is not None and b[1] is not None and a[1] != b[1]:
        return None
    return ((a[0] + sign * b[0]) & MASK64, a[1] if a[1] is not None else b[1],
            (a[2] + sign * b[2]) & MASK64)


def linear(expr):
    """expr as (coefficient, atom, constant): coefficient*atom + constant, mod 2^64.

    The atom is the one non-constant subexpression; anything that is not a sum,
    difference, constant shift or constant multiple of it is itself the atom.
    Returns None when two different atoms appear.
    """
    if isinstance(expr, Const):
        return (0, None, expr.value & MASK64)
    if isinstance(expr, Binary):
        if expr.op in ("add", "sub"):
            left, right = linear(expr.left), linear(expr.right)
            if left is None or right is None:
                return None
            return _combine(left, right, 1 if expr.op == "add" else -1)
        if expr.op in ("shl", "dshl") and isinstance(expr.right, Const):
            inner = linear(expr.left)
            if inner is None:
                return None
            factor = 1 << (expr.right.value & (31 if expr.op == "shl" else 63))
            return ((inner[0] * factor) & MASK64, inner[1], (inner[2] * factor) & MASK64)
        if expr.op == "mul" and isinstance(expr.right, Const) or (
                expr.op == "mul" and isinstance(expr.left, Const)):
            constant, other = ((expr.right, expr.left) if isinstance(expr.right, Const)
                               else (expr.left, expr.right))
            inner = linear(other)
            if inner is None:
                return None
            factor = constant.value
            return ((inner[0] * factor) & MASK64, inner[1], (inner[2] * factor) & MASK64)
    return (1, expr, 0)


def global_name(address: int) -> str:
    return "g_%08X" % (address & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def object_name(address: int) -> str:
    """A global object's name. Distinct from the scalar at the same address: an
    object's first field and the object itself share an address."""
    return "g_%08X_obj" % (address & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def embedded_accessor(offset: int) -> str:
    return "e_%s" % _offset_name(offset)


def accessor(offset: int) -> str:
    return "f_%s" % _offset_name(offset)


def _signed_offset(offset: int) -> int:
    offset &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return offset - (1 << 32) if offset & 0x80000000 else offset


class Typing:
    """Type information for one function's expressions."""

    def __init__(self, catalog: Catalog, function: int) -> None:
        self.catalog = catalog
        self.function = function
        self.used = set()
        self.used_globals = set()        # addresses of scalar globals read or written
        self.used_objects = set()        # (address, type) of global objects
        self.used_global_arrays = set()  # addresses of global arrays indexed

    def type_of(self, expr):
        """The recovered type of a value, as a catalog root, or None."""
        if isinstance(expr, Arg):
            return self.catalog.slot(self.function, expr.index)
        if isinstance(expr, Load):
            access = self.access(expr)
            if access is not None:
                _base, _path, owner, local, _index = access
                return self.catalog.pointee(owner, local)
        return None

    def _candidates(self, address):
        """Each way to reach a typed address, best first.

        Yields (base, path, owner, local, field, index). `index` is None for a plain
        field; an int for an element of a run of fields the code walked with an
        unrolled loop; or an expression when the address is indexed by a variable,
        in which case `local` is element 0 of the array.
        """
        indexed = self.decompose(address)
        if indexed is not None:
            base, root, offset, stride, index = indexed
            field = self.catalog.field(root, offset)
            if field is not None and self.catalog.arrays(root).get(offset, (None,))[0] == stride:
                yield base, [], root, offset, field, index
            return
        try:
            base, offset = _split_address(address)
        except Exception:
            return
        if base is None:
            # A constant address: a global variable, or a field of a global object.
            root = self.catalog.globals
        else:
            root = self.type_of(base)
        if root is None:
            return
        offset = _signed_offset(offset)
        element = self.catalog.element(root, offset)
        if element is not None:
            start, index = element
            yield base, [], root, start, self.catalog.field(root, start), index
        for path, owner, local, field in self.catalog.candidates(root, offset):
            yield base, path, owner, local, field, None

    def decompose(self, address):
        """(base, root, offset, stride, index) for an address indexed by a variable.

        The address must be exactly base + offset + stride * index, with the base a
        typed value (or absent, for a global array). Shifts, multiplies, additions
        and subtractions by constants are exact in the 64-bit model, so
        `arg0 + 0x10 + ((i << 2) + i << 4)` is arg0 + 0x10 + 0x50 * i.
        """
        terms = list(_sum_terms(address_of(address)))
        base, root = None, self.catalog.globals
        rest = []
        for term in terms:
            typed_root = None if isinstance(term, Const) else self.type_of(term)
            if typed_root is not None and base is None:
                base, root = term, typed_root
            else:
                rest.append(term)
        if root is None:
            return None
        form = (0, None, 0)
        for term in rest:
            part = linear(term)
            if part is None:
                return None
            form = _combine(form, part, 1)
            if form is None:
                return None
        coefficient, index, constant = form
        if index is None or not 1 <= coefficient <= MAX_STRIDE:
            return None
        if base is None and not (layout.CURRENT.image_start <= constant & 0xFFFFFFFF
                                 < layout.CURRENT.image_end):
            # A "global array" at 0x20 indexed by a pointer is exact arithmetic but
            # a false description: the pointer is the base, not an index.
            return None
        return base, root, _signed_offset(constant), coefficient, index

    def access(self, load):
        """(base, embed path, owner, offset, index) when a load is exactly a field read."""
        for base, path, owner, local, field, index in self._candidates(load.address):
            if self.catalog.read_flavour(field) == (load.size, load.signed):
                return base, path, owner, local, index
        return None

    def store_target(self, store):
        """(base, embed path, owner, offset, index) when a store is exactly a field write."""
        for base, path, owner, local, field, index in self._candidates(store.address):
            if self.catalog.write_width(field) == store.size:
                return base, path, owner, local, index
        return None

    def object(self, base, path) -> str:
        """The view a field belongs to: the base's view, then any embedded parts.

        With no base the field is global: the first embedded part is then a global
        object, named for its address.
        """
        if base is None:
            at, inner = path[0]
            self.used.add(inner)
            self.used_objects.add((at, inner))
            text, path = object_name(at), path[1:]
        else:
            text = self.view(base)
        for at, inner in path:
            self.used.add(inner)
            text += ".%s()" % embedded_accessor(at)
        return text

    def index_text(self, index) -> str:
        """An element number or index expression, rendered with this typing.

        Installs the hooks itself: it is also called from statement-level code,
        outside any expression rendering, and the default renderer would print a
        typed argument without `.address`.
        """
        if index is None:
            return ""
        if isinstance(index, int):
            return str(index)
        with load_renderer(self.render_load), arg_renderer(self.render_arg):
            return simplify(index).render()

    def read(self, base, path, local, index=None) -> str:
        """The expression reading a located field, or an element of one."""
        arguments = self.index_text(index)
        if base is None and not path:
            (self.used_global_arrays if index is not None else self.used_globals).add(local)
            return "%s(%s)" % (global_name(local), arguments)
        return "%s.%s(%s)" % (self.object(base, path), accessor(local), arguments)

    def write(self, holder, base, path, local, value, index=None) -> str:
        """The statement writing a located field; `holder` is a captured view and
        `index` an element number, an index expression, or text already captured."""
        arguments = value if index is None else "%s, %s" % (
            index if isinstance(index, str) else self.index_text(index), value)
        if base is None and not path:
            (self.used_global_arrays if index is not None else self.used_globals).add(local)
            return "set_%s(%s);" % (global_name(local), arguments)
        return "%s.set_%s(%s);" % (holder or self.object(base, path), accessor(local),
                                   arguments)

    @staticmethod
    def needs_capture(base) -> bool:
        """Whether the view a store goes through reads memory to compute."""
        return base is not None and not isinstance(base, Arg)

    def view(self, expr) -> str:
        """Render a typed value as its view object."""
        root = self.type_of(expr)
        assert root is not None
        self.used.add(root)
        if isinstance(expr, Arg):
            return arg_name(expr.index)
        base, path, owner, local, index = self.access(expr)
        self.used.add(owner)
        return self.read(base, path, local, index)
```
