```py
    def type_name(self, root) -> str:
        return self.catalog.names[root]

    # -- hooks for the symexec renderer ------------------------------------

    def render_arg(self, node) -> str:
        if self.type_of(node) is not None:
            self.used.add(self.type_of(node))
            return "%s.address" % arg_name(node.index)
        return arg_name(node.index)

    def render_load(self, node, render_child) -> str:
        access = self.access(node)
        if access is not None:
            base, path, owner, offset, index = access
            self.used.add(owner)
            text = self.read(base, path, offset, index)
            if self.type_of(node) is not None:
                self.used.add(self.type_of(node))
                return text + ".address"
            return text
        reader = READERS.get((node.size, node.signed))
        if reader is None:
            from .symexec import Unsupported

            raise Unsupported("no reader for %d-byte load" % node.size)
        return "%s(%s)" % (reader, render_child(node.address))


def header(catalog: Catalog, roots, source_name: str, globals_used=(), objects=(),
           global_arrays=()) -> str:
    """The view classes for the given types, and the globals used, as a C++ header."""
    roots = sorted((root for root in roots if root != catalog.globals),
                   key=lambda root: catalog.names[root])
    included = set(roots)
    lines = [
        "/*",
        " * Recovered struct types - GENERATED, do not edit by hand.",
        " *",
        " * Produced by engine/tools/derive.py from %s, using the type recovery in" % source_name,
        " * tools/ps2decomp/structs.py. Each type was inferred from how the original code",
        " * uses pointers: the offsets and widths it accesses, and the arguments, return",
        " * values and pointer fields that carry the same object between functions.",
        " *",
        " * A type is a *view* over a guest address rather than a C++ struct with the",
        " * original layout, because the derived code runs against an emulated address",
        " * space. Each accessor reads or writes one field; a pointer field returns the",
        " * view of the type it points to. Only types the derived functions use are",
        " * listed, each with every field the recovery found, including fields no",
        " * derived function touches yet.",
        " *",
        " * The names are placeholders derived from the evidence: S_0035F0A0_a0 is the",
        " * type of argument 0 of func_0035F0A0, and S_..._p1C is what its field 0x1C",
        " * points to. Global variables are named by address: g_004876E8() reads the",
        " * one at 0x4876E8, S_g004876E8 is what it points to, and g_0049A278_obj is a",
        " * global object of a recovered type.",
        " */",
        "",
        "#ifndef B3_GENERATED_TYPES_H",
        "#define B3_GENERATED_TYPES_H",
        "",
        '#include "ps2rt/generated.h"',
        "",
        "namespace generated {",
        "",
        "/* Every view is a guest address; this is the shared base. */",
        "struct View {",
        "    u64 address;",
        "    View(u64 value = 0) : address(value) {}",
        "};",
        "",
    ]
    for root in roots:
        lines.append("struct %s;" % catalog.names[root])
    lines.append("")

    definitions = []
    for root in roots:
        name = catalog.names[root]
        fields = catalog.roots[root]
        offsets = sorted(fields)
        lines.append("/* %d function(s); %d field(s) at %s..%s */"
                     % (len(catalog.functions(root)), len(fields),
                        _hex(offsets[0]), _hex(offsets[-1])))
        lines.append("struct %s : View {" % name)
        lines.append("    using View::View;")
        for offset in offsets:
            field = fields[offset]
            flavour = catalog.read_flavour(field)
            width = catalog.write_width(field)
            target = catalog.pointee(root, offset)
            kind = catalog.kind(field)
            note = "%d function(s)" % len(field.functions)
            displacement = ("address + 0x%X" % offset if offset > 0 else
                            "address - 0x%X" % -offset if offset < 0 else "address")
            if flavour is not None and flavour in READERS:
                if target is not None and target in included:
                    returns = catalog.names[target]
                    describe = "-> %s" % returns
                else:
                    returns = "u64"
                    describe = "f32 bits" if kind == "float" else VALUE_TYPES[flavour]
                    if target is not None:
                        describe = "pointer to %s" % catalog.names[target]
                lines.append("    %s %s() const;  /* %s  %s, %s */"
                             % (returns, accessor(offset), _hex(offset, signed=True),
                                describe, note))
                definitions.append("inline %s %s::%s() const { return %s(%s); }"
                                   % (returns, name, accessor(offset), READERS[flavour],
                                      displacement))
            if width is not None and width in WRITERS:
                lines.append("    void set_%s(u64 value) const;" % accessor(offset))
                definitions.append(
                    "inline void %s::set_%s(u64 value) const { %s(%s, value); }"
                    % (name, accessor(offset), WRITERS[width], displacement)
                )
        for start, (stride, count) in sorted(catalog.arrays(root).items()):
            field = fields[start]
            flavour = catalog.read_flavour(field)
            width = catalog.write_width(field)
            target = catalog.pointee(root, start)
            element = ("address + 0x%X + index * 0x%X" % (start, stride) if start >= 0
                       else "address - 0x%X + index * 0x%X" % (-start, stride))
            extent = "%d elements" % count if count is not None else "length unknown"
            if flavour in READERS:
                returns = (catalog.names[target] if target is not None and target in included
                           else "u64")
                lines.append("    %s %s(u64 index) const;  /* array: every 0x%X bytes, %s */"
                             % (returns, accessor(start), stride, extent))
                definitions.append("inline %s %s::%s(u64 index) const { return %s(%s); }"
                                   % (returns, name, accessor(start), READERS[flavour], element))
            if width in WRITERS:
                lines.append("    void set_%s(u64 index, u64 value) const;" % accessor(start))
                definitions.append(
                    "inline void %s::set_%s(u64 index, u64 value) const { %s(%s, value); }"
                    % (name, accessor(start), WRITERS[width], element))
        for at, inner in sorted(catalog.embedded(root).items()):
            if inner not in included:
                continue
            lines.append("    %s %s() const;  /* %s  embedded %s */"
                         % (catalog.names[inner], embedded_accessor(at), _hex(at, signed=True),
                            catalog.names[inner]))
            definitions.append("inline %s %s::%s() const { return %s(address + 0x%X); }"
                               % (catalog.names[inner], name, embedded_accessor(at),
                                  catalog.names[inner], at))
        lines.append("};")
        lines.append("")
    lines.append("/* Accessor definitions, after every type is complete. */")
    lines.extend(definitions)
    lines += global_section(catalog, included, globals_used, objects, global_arrays)
    lines += ["", "}  // namespace generated", "", "#endif  /* B3_GENERATED_TYPES_H */", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def global_section(catalog, included, globals_used, objects, global_arrays=()) -> list:
    """Accessors for the global variables and global objects the code uses.

    A scalar global is a pair of functions, `g_004876E8()` and `set_g_004876E8(v)`,
    reading at the width and signedness the code uses it with; one that holds a
    pointer returns the view of what it points to. A global object - one whose
    address is handed to functions that know its type - is a constant view.
    """
    lines = ["", "/* Global variables, by address. */"]
    fields = catalog.roots.get(catalog.globals, {})
    for address in sorted(globals_used):
        field = fields[address]
        flavour = catalog.read_flavour(field)
        width = catalog.write_width(field)
        target = catalog.pointee(catalog.globals, address)
        name = global_name(address)
        location = "0x%X" % (address & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        note = "%d function(s)" % len(field.functions)
        if flavour in READERS:
            if target is not None and target in included:
                returns, describe = catalog.names[target], "-> " + catalog.names[target]
            else:
                returns = "u64"
                describe = "f32 bits" if catalog.kind(field) == "float" else VALUE_TYPES[flavour]
            lines.append("/* %s  %s, %s */" % (location, describe, note))
            lines.append("inline %s %s() { return %s(%s); }"
                         % (returns, name, READERS[flavour], location))
        if width in WRITERS:
            if flavour not in READERS:
                lines.append("/* %s  written only, %s */" % (location, note))
            lines.append("inline void set_%s(u64 value) { %s(%s, value); }"
                         % (name, WRITERS[width], location))
    if global_arrays:
        lines += ["", "/* Global arrays, by address of element 0. */"]
        arrays = catalog.arrays(catalog.globals)
        for address in sorted(global_arrays):
            field = fields[address]
            stride = arrays[address][0]
            flavour = catalog.read_flavour(field)
            width = catalog.write_width(field)
            target = catalog.pointee(catalog.globals, address)
            element = "0x%X + index * 0x%X" % (address & 0xFFFFFFFF, stride)
            lines.append("/* 0x%X  every 0x%X bytes, %d function(s) */"
                         % (address & 0xFFFFFFFF, stride, len(field.functions)))
            if flavour in READERS:
                returns = (catalog.names[target] if target is not None and target in included
                           else "u64")
                lines.append("inline %s %s(u64 index) { return %s(%s); }"
                             % (returns, global_name(address), READERS[flavour], element))
            if width in WRITERS:
                lines.append("inline void set_%s(u64 index, u64 value) { %s(%s, value); }"
                             % (global_name(address), WRITERS[width], element))
    if objects:
        lines += ["", "/* Global objects, by address. */"]
        for address, inner in sorted(objects):
            lines.append("inline const %s %s{0x%X};"
                         % (catalog.names[inner], object_name(address), address & 0xFFFFFFFF))
    return lines


def _walk(expr):
    yield expr
    for child in children(expr):
        yield from _walk(child)


def _accesses(derivation):
    """Every (address, size, signed, is_store) a derivation performs."""
    seen = set()
    for path in derivation.paths:
        roots = list(path.conditions)
        for store in path.stores:
            roots += [store.address, store.value]
        if path.expression is not None:
            roots.append(path.expression)
        for root in roots:
            for node in _walk(root):
                if isinstance(node, Load) and id(node) not in seen:
                    seen.add(id(node))
                    yield node.address, node.size, node.signed, False
        for store in path.stores:
            yield store.address, store.size, None, True


def _untyped_indexed(typing, func, address, graph):
    """Like Typing.decompose, for an indexed access through an argument with no
    type yet - which then gets one. None if the address is not of that shape."""
    terms = list(_sum_terms(address_of(address)))
    for term in terms:
        if isinstance(term, Arg) and typing.type_of(term) is None:
            rest = [t for t in terms if t is not term]
            form = (0, None, 0)
            for other in rest:
                part = linear(other)
                form = None if part is None or form is None else _combine(form, part, 1)
            if form is None or form[1] is None or not 1 <= form[0] <= MAX_STRIDE:
                return None
            node = graph.node(("arg", func["addr"], term.index))
            return term, node, _signed_offset(form[2]), form[0], form[1]
    return None


def add_derived_evidence(graph, verified, rounds: int = 4) -> int:
    """Add the derived functions' own accesses to the type graph as evidence.

    The scan that builds the graph cannot follow a variable index, so an array of
    records walked by a loop contributes nothing. The derivations can: an unrolled
    loop appears as every concrete access it makes, and each one was verified
    against the original. So any access through a typed base at an offset the type
    does not yet have becomes a field, and an argument that has no type at all but
    is dereferenced - typically only inside an inlined callee - gets one.

    Repeated because each new field can type a pointer loaded from it.
    """
    added = 0
    for _round in range(rounds):
        catalog = Catalog(graph)
        before = added
        for func, derivation, _tested, _strong in verified:
            typing = Typing(catalog, func["addr"])
            for address, size, signed, is_store in _accesses(derivation):
                if size not in (1, 2, 4, 8):
                    continue
                indexed = typing.decompose(address)
                if indexed is None:
                    indexed = _untyped_indexed(typing, func, address, graph)
                if indexed is not None:
                    _base, root, offset, stride, _index = indexed
                    node = root
                    field = graph.field(node, offset)
                    if not field.strides:
                        added += 1
                    field.strides[stride] += 1
                    field.uses[(size, "derived", bool(signed) if not is_store else None,
                                is_store)] += 1
                    field.functions.add(func["addr"])
                    continue
                try:
                    base, offset = _split_address(address)
                except Exception:
                    continue
                offset = _signed_offset(offset)
                root = typing.type_of(base) if base is not None else catalog.globals
                if base is None and root is None:
                    node = graph.node(GLOBALS)
                elif root is None:
                    if not isinstance(base, Arg):
                        continue
                    node = graph.node(("arg", func["addr"], base.index))
                elif catalog.locate(root, offset) is not None:
                    continue
                else:
                    node = root
                field = graph.field(node, offset)
                if not field.uses:
                    added += 1
                # A derived load cannot tell `lwc1` from `lwu`, so it says nothing
                # about whether the field is a float.
                field.uses[(size, "derived", bool(signed) if not is_store else None,
                            is_store)] += 1
                field.functions.add(func["addr"])
        if added == before:
            break
    return added

```

`ps2decomp/verdicts.py`:

```py
"""Verification verdicts remembered between runs.

A lifted or structured function is verified by compiling its C++ and running it
against the original on test cases. Its callees run in the interpreter, from the
original machine code, so the verdict depends on nothing but

* the function's own C++ text, and whether it is checked whole or at the
  calling-convention level;
* the environment: the interpreter, the test memory and its seeding, the
  runtime it is compiled with, the verification code, and the game's image
  and analysis.

The text goes into each key; the environment is one fingerprint over the files
that make it up. Change any of them and every verdict is recomputed. Change only
code that produces text - structuring, folding, naming - and only the functions
whose text changed are verified again.

What the key cannot see: the compiler's version, and the order functions run in
within a process (a function needing more fresh pages than
emu.Machine.FAULT_RETRIES can pass after others mapped them). A run with --no-cache recomputes everything
and is the check on both.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import hashlib
import json
import os

# Modules that only produce the text being verified: the text is in every key, so
# a change to them invalidates exactly the verdicts whose text changes.
TEXT_ONLY = {"structure.py", "liveness.py", "naming.py", "signatures.py"}

# Where verification starts; everything they import from the engine is part of
# the environment, and nothing else is - the symbolic deriver, for one.
ROOTS = ("liftverify.py", "testplan.py", "liftcheck.py", "lift.py")


def _imports(path: str) -> set:
    """The engine modules a module imports, as file names."""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        tree = ast.parse(handle.read())
    found = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.level == 1:
            if node.module:
                found.add(node.module.split(".")[0] + ".py")
            else:
                found.update(alias.name + ".py" for alias in node.names)
    return found


def modules(package: str) -> set:
    """The import closure of ROOTS within the package, less TEXT_ONLY."""
    seen, work = set(), list(ROOTS)
    while work:
        name = work.pop()
        path = os.path.join(package, name)
        if name in seen or not os.path.exists(path):
            continue
        seen.add(name)
        work.extend(_imports(path))
    return seen - TEXT_ONLY


def _files(repository: str) -> list:
    engine = os.path.join(repository, "engine")
    package = os.path.join(engine, "ps2decomp")
    files = [os.path.join(package, name) for name in modules(package)]
    # engine/tools/ is left out: lift.py and derive.py only orchestrate. What
    # decides a verdict - liftverify.py, testplan.py - is among the modules above.
    for folder, _dirs, names in os.walk(os.path.join(engine, "runtime")):
        files += [os.path.join(folder, name) for name in names]
    return sorted(files)


def fingerprint(repository: str, inputs=()) -> str:
    """The environment's fingerprint: the source files verification depends on,
    plus `inputs` - bytes or anything with a stable repr (image, analysis, seeds)."""
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for path in _files(repository):
        digest.update(os.path.relpath(path, repository).replace(os.sep, "/").encode())
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            # Line endings differ between checkouts; the code does not.
            digest.update(handle.read().replace(b"\r\n", b"\n"))
    for item in inputs:
        digest.update(item if isinstance(item, bytes) else repr(item).encode())
    return digest.hexdigest()


# Verdicts of this many environments are kept: the current one, and a few before
# it - a full run and a subset run seed test memory differently, so they are
# different environments, and switching between them should not lose either.
KEEP_ENVIRONMENTS = 4


class Verdicts:
    """{key: outcome} on disk, per environment; a key covers form and text."""

    def __init__(self, path: str, environment: str, use: bool = True) -> None:
        self.path = path
        self.environment = environment
        self.use = use
        self.hits = self.misses = 0
        self.stored = []                 # [[environment, {key: outcome}]], newest last
        if os.path.exists(path):
            try:
                with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                    self.stored = [list(pair) for pair in json.load(handle)]
            except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
                self.stored = []
        current = [pair for pair in self.stored if pair[0] == environment]
        self.stored = [pair for pair in self.stored if pair[0] != environment]
        self.entries = current[0][1] if current else {}

    def key(self, text: str, abi: bool) -> str:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(self.environment.encode())
        digest.update(b"abi" if abi else b"whole")
        digest.update(text.encode("utf-8"))
        return digest.hexdigest()

    def get(self, text: str, abi: bool):
        """The remembered outcome, or None (also when not using remembered ones)."""
        outcome = self.entries.get(self.key(text, abi)) if self.use else None
        if outcome is None:
            self.misses += 1
        else:
            self.hits += 1
        return outcome

    def put(self, text: str, abi: bool, outcome: str) -> None:
        self.entries[self.key(text, abi)] = outcome

    def save(self) -> None:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.path), exist_ok=True)
        kept = self.stored[-(KEEP_ENVIRONMENTS - 1):] + [[self.environment, self.entries]]
        temporary = self.path + ".tmp"
        with open(temporary, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(kept, handle)
        os.replace(temporary, self.path)

```

`ps2decomp/vu.py`:

```py
"""Disassembler for PlayStation 2 Vector Unit microcode.

The VUs are not MIPS cores and share nothing with the EE instruction set, so the
R5900 decoder cannot read this code at all - and worse, VU words decode as
*plausible* MIPS about 96% of the time, so nothing short of a dedicated decoder
will do.

Microcode is stored as 8-byte bundles holding two instructions issued together:

    bytes 0-3   lower instruction - loads, stores, integer ALU, branches
    bytes 4-7   upper instruction - the floating-point FMAC pipeline

The upper word also carries the bundle's control flags in its top bits:

    I  bit 31   the lower word is a 32-bit float immediate, not an instruction
    E  bit 30   end of microprogram (one more bundle executes after it)
    M  bit 29   (VU0) interlock with the EE's COP2 transfers
    D  bit 28   debug break
    T  bit 27   debug halt

Bits 24..21 are the destination field mask, naming which of the x/y/z/w lanes a
result is written to; it is rendered as a suffix, so `addx.xy` writes only x and y.

The opcode tables are the hardware's, as the host's micro-mode interpreter
(engine/host/src/vu.cpp) runs them and PCSX2 lays them out:

  * upper: bits 5..0. 0x00-0x2F are the arithmetic forms; 0x3C-0x3F extend into
    bits 10..6, the "special" index being (bits 1..0) | (bits 10..6) << 2.
  * lower: bits 31..25. 0x40 is the special group, named by bits 5..0, which
    extends at 0x3C-0x3F into bits 10..6 the same way as the upper does.

Each decoded instruction also says which registers it reads and writes, as
strings: "vf5x" (one lane of a vector register), "vi3", "ACCx", "Q", "P", "I",
"R", "MAC", "STATUS", "CLIP". The hazard scanner (engine/tools/vuhazards.py)
works from those.

Coverage is reported rather than assumed: `decode_bundle` marks anything it cannot
identify, and `engine/tools/vudis.py --stats` measures how much of a real microcode blob
decodes.  Guessing at an encoding would be worse than admitting the gap.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import struct

VF = ["vf%02d" % i for i in range(32)]
VI = ["vi%02d" % i for i in range(32)]

# Distinctive padding encodings, which is what makes microcode findable in a
# stripped image at all.
LOWER_NOP = 0x8000033C
UPPER_NOP_BASE = 0x000002FF

# Bundle control flags, in the upper word.
FLAG_I = 1 << 31
FLAG_E = 1 << 30
FLAG_M = 1 << 29
FLAG_D = 1 << 28
FLAG_T = 1 << 27

_BC = "xyzw"
_LANES = (("x", 8), ("y", 4), ("z", 2), ("w", 1))


def _dest(word: int) -> str:
    """Render the destination field mask as a lane suffix."""
    mask = (word >> 21) & 0xF
    # Bit 24 is x, descending to bit 21 for w.
    lanes = "".join(c for c, bit in _LANES if mask & bit)
    return lanes or "none"


def _vf(reg: int, lanes: str) -> set:
    """A vector register's lanes; vf0 is a constant and never a dependency."""
    if reg == 0:
        return set()
    return {"vf%d%s" % (reg, lane) for lane in lanes}


def _vi(reg: int) -> set:
    return {"vi%d" % reg} if reg else set()


def _acc(lanes: str) -> set:
    return {"ACC" + lane for lane in lanes}


# -- upper (FMAC) opcodes ------------------------------------------------
#
# Bits 5..0. 0x00..0x1B come in broadcast groups of four: the low two bits select
# which lane of ft is broadcast across the operation.
_UPPER_BC = {
    0x00: "add", 0x04: "sub", 0x08: "madd", 0x0C: "msub",
    0x10: "max", 0x14: "mini", 0x18: "mul",
}

# Forms whose second operand is the Q or I register.
_UPPER_QI = {
    0x1C: ("mulq", "Q"), 0x1D: ("maxi", "I"), 0x1E: ("muli", "I"), 0x1F: ("minii", "I"),
    0x20: ("addq", "Q"), 0x21: ("maddq", "Q"), 0x22: ("addi", "I"), 0x23: ("maddi", "I"),
    0x24: ("subq", "Q"), 0x25: ("msubq", "Q"), 0x26: ("subi", "I"), 0x27: ("msubi", "I"),
}

# Plain three-register forms.
_UPPER_REG = {
    0x28: "add", 0x29: "madd", 0x2A: "mul", 0x2B: "max",
    0x2C: "sub", 0x2D: "msub", 0x2E: "opmsub", 0x2F: "mini",
}

# The special index (bits 1..0 | bits 10..6 << 2) for opcodes 0x3C..0x3F.
_UPPER_SPECIAL_BC = {0x00: "adda", 0x04: "suba", 0x08: "madda", 0x0C: "msuba", 0x18: "mula"}
_UPPER_SPECIAL_CONVERT = {
    0x10: "itof0", 0x11: "itof4", 0x12: "itof12", 0x13: "itof15",
    0x14: "ftoi0", 0x15: "ftoi4", 0x16: "ftoi12", 0x17: "ftoi15",
    0x1D: "abs",
}
_UPPER_SPECIAL_QI = {
    0x1C: ("mulaq", "Q"), 0x1E: ("mulai", "I"),
    0x20: ("addaq", "Q"), 0x21: ("maddaq", "Q"), 0x22: ("addai", "I"), 0x23: ("maddai", "I"),
    0x24: ("subaq", "Q"), 0x25: ("msubaq", "Q"), 0x26: ("subai", "I"), 0x27: ("msubai", "I"),
}
_UPPER_SPECIAL_REG = {
    0x28: "adda", 0x29: "madda", 0x2A: "mula", 0x2C: "suba", 0x2D: "msuba", 0x2E: "opmula",
}

# Which forms read the accumulator (the multiply-adds) or leave the flags alone.
_READS_ACC = ("madd", "msub", "opmsub")
_NO_FLAGS = ("max", "mini", "abs", "itof", "ftoi")


# -- lower opcodes -------------------------------------------------------
#
# Bits 31..25 - seven bits, not six: 0x40 (bit 31 set, the rest clear) selects
# the special group, named by bits 5..0, where the integer ALU, the transfers
# between register files and the elementary function unit live.
LOWER_SPECIAL_GROUP = 0x40

_LOWER_MAIN = {
    0x00: "lq", 0x01: "sq", 0x04: "ilw", 0x05: "isw",
    0x08: "iaddiu", 0x09: "isubiu",
    0x10: "fceq", 0x11: "fcset", 0x12: "fcand", 0x13: "fcor",
    0x14: "fseq", 0x15: "fsset", 0x16: "fsand", 0x17: "fsor",
    0x18: "fmeq", 0x1A: "fmand", 0x1B: "fmor", 0x1C: "fcget",
    0x20: "b", 0x21: "bal", 0x24: "jr", 0x25: "jalr",
    0x28: "ibeq", 0x29: "ibne",
    0x2C: "ibltz", 0x2D: "ibgtz", 0x2E: "iblez", 0x2F: "ibgez",
}

# Special group, by bits 5..0.
_LOWER_SPECIAL = {
    0x30: "iadd", 0x31: "isub", 0x32: "iaddi", 0x34: "iand", 0x35: "ior",
}

# Within the special group, 0x3C..0x3F extend into bits 10..6; the index is
# (bits 1..0) | (bits 10..6) << 2.
_LOWER_SPECIAL_EXT = {
    0x30: "move", 0x31: "mr32",
    0x34: "lqi", 0x35: "sqi", 0x36: "lqd", 0x37: "sqd",
    0x38: "div", 0x39: "sqrt", 0x3A: "rsqrt", 0x3B: "waitq",
    0x3C: "mtir", 0x3D: "mfir", 0x3E: "ilwr", 0x3F: "iswr",
    0x40: "rnext", 0x41: "rget", 0x42: "rinit", 0x43: "rxor",
    0x64: "mfp", 0x68: "xtop", 0x69: "xitop", 0x6C: "xgkick",
    0x70: "esadd", 0x71: "ersadd", 0x72: "eleng", 0x73: "erleng",
    0x74: "eatanxy", 0x75: "eatanxz", 0x76: "esum",
    0x78: "esqrt", 0x79: "ersqrt", 0x7A: "ercpr", 0x7B: "waitp",
    0x7C: "esin", 0x7D: "eatan", 0x7E: "eexp",
}

# Latencies in cycles, for the hazard scanner: when a result can be read.
LATENCY_Q = {"div": 7, "sqrt": 7, "rsqrt": 13}
LATENCY_P = {
    "esadd": 11, "ersadd": 18, "eleng": 18, "erleng": 24, "eatanxy": 54, "eatanxz": 54,
    "esum": 12, "esqrt": 12, "ersqrt": 18, "ercpr": 12, "esin": 29, "eatan": 54, "eexp": 44,
}
LATENCY_FMAC = 4


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class VuInstruction:
    """One half of a bundle."""

    raw: int
    mnemonic: str
    operands: tuple = ()
    known: bool = True
    reads: frozenset = frozenset()
    writes: frozenset = frozenset()

    def format(self) -> str:
        if not self.known:
            return ".word 0x%08x" % self.raw
        if not self.operands:
            return self.mnemonic
        return "%-12s %s" % (self.mnemonic, ", ".join(str(o) for o in self.operands))

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.format()


def _ins(word, mnemonic, operands=(), reads=(), writes=()):
    return VuInstruction(word, mnemonic, tuple(operands), True, frozenset(reads), frozenset(writes))


def _unknown(word, half):
    return VuInstruction(word, half + "?", (), known=False)


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Bundle:
    """An 8-byte microcode bundle: one lower and one upper instruction."""

    addr: int
    lower_raw: int
    upper_raw: int
    lower: VuInstruction
    upper: VuInstruction
    immediate: float = None

    @property
    def flags(self) -> str:
        out = []
        for bit, name in ((FLAG_I, "I"), (FLAG_E, "E"), (FLAG_M, "M"),
                          (FLAG_D, "D"), (FLAG_T, "T")):
            if self.upper_raw & bit:
                out.append(name)
        return "".join(out)

    @property
    def is_end(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.upper_raw & FLAG_E)

    @property
    def fully_known(self) -> bool:
        return self.upper.known and self.lower.known

    def format(self) -> str:
        flags = self.flags
        marker = "[%-5s]" % flags if flags else " " * 7
        if self.immediate is not None:
            lower_text = "loi          %g" % self.immediate
        else:
            lower_text = self.lower.format()
        return "%08x %s %-34s %s" % (self.addr, marker, self.upper.format(), lower_text)


def _arith(word, name, fd, fs, second, second_reads, dest, to_acc):
    """An FMAC operation: `second` is ft (with its lanes) or Q or I."""
    lanes = "".join(c for c, bit in _LANES if (word >> 21) & bit)
    reads = set(second_reads)
    if name.startswith("opm"):
        # The outer product crosses lanes: x from y,z; y from z,x; z from x,y.
        reads = _vf(fs, "xyz") | _vf((word >> 16) & 0x1F, "xyz")
    else:
        reads |= _vf(fs, lanes)
    if name.startswith(_READS_ACC):
        reads |= _acc("xyz" if name.startswith("opm") else lanes)
    writes = _acc(lanes) if to_acc else _vf(fd, lanes)
    if not any(name.startswith(n) for n in _NO_FLAGS):
        writes = writes | {"MAC", "STATUS"}
    target = "ACC" if to_acc else VF[fd]
    return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (name, dest), (target, VF[fs], second), reads, writes)


def decode_upper(word: int) -> VuInstruction:
    """Decode the FMAC half of a bundle."""
    opcode = word & 0x3F
    fd, fs, ft = (word >> 6) & 0x1F, (word >> 11) & 0x1F, (word >> 16) & 0x1F
    dest = _dest(word)
    lanes = "".join(c for c, bit in _LANES if (word >> 21) & bit)

    if opcode < 0x1C:
        name = _UPPER_BC[opcode & 0x1C] + _BC[opcode & 3]
        lane = _BC[opcode & 3]
        return _arith(word, name, fd, fs, "%s%s" % (VF[ft], lane), _vf(ft, lane), dest, False)
    if opcode in _UPPER_QI:
        name, special = _UPPER_QI[opcode]
        return _arith(word, name, fd, fs, special, {special}, dest, False)
    if opcode in _UPPER_REG:
        name = _UPPER_REG[opcode]
        return _arith(word, name, fd, fs, VF[ft], _vf(ft, lanes), dest, False)
    if opcode < 0x3C:
        return _unknown(word, "upper")

    index = (opcode & 3) | (((word >> 6) & 0x1F) << 2)
    if index == 0x2F:
        return _ins(word, "nop")
    if index == 0x1F:
        return _ins(word, "clip", (VF[fs] + "xyz", VF[ft] + "w"),
                    _vf(fs, "xyz") | _vf(ft, "w"), {"CLIP"})
    if index in _UPPER_SPECIAL_CONVERT:
        return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (_UPPER_SPECIAL_CONVERT[index], dest), (VF[ft], VF[fs]),
                    _vf(fs, lanes), _vf(ft, lanes))
    if index < 0x1C and (index & 0x1C) in _UPPER_SPECIAL_BC:
        name = _UPPER_SPECIAL_BC[index & 0x1C] + _BC[index & 3]
        lane = _BC[index & 3]
        return _arith(word, name, 0, fs, "%s%s" % (VF[ft], lane), _vf(ft, lane), dest, True)
    if index in _UPPER_SPECIAL_QI:
        name, special = _UPPER_SPECIAL_QI[index]
        return _arith(word, name, 0, fs, special, {special}, dest, True)
    if index in _UPPER_SPECIAL_REG:
        name = _UPPER_SPECIAL_REG[index]
        return _arith(word, name, 0, fs, VF[ft], _vf(ft, lanes), dest, True)
    return _unknown(word, "upper")


def _imm11(word: int) -> int:
    value = word & 0x7FF
    return value - 0x800 if value & 0x400 else value


def decode_lower(word: int) -> VuInstruction:
    """Decode the load/store/integer/branch half of a bundle."""
    if word == LOWER_NOP:
        return _ins(word, "nop")

    opcode = (word >> 25) & 0x7F
    it, is_, id_ = (word >> 16) & 0x1F, (word >> 11) & 0x1F, (word >> 6) & 0x1F
    dest = _dest(word)
    lanes = "".join(c for c, bit in _LANES if (word >> 21) & bit)
    imm11 = _imm11(word)

    if opcode == LOWER_SPECIAL_GROUP:
        sub = word & 0x3F
        if sub in _LOWER_SPECIAL:
            name = _LOWER_SPECIAL[sub]
            if name == "iaddi":
                imm5 = id_ - 0x20 if id_ & 0x10 else id_
                return _ins(word, name, (VI[it], VI[is_], "%+d" % imm5), _vi(is_), _vi(it))
            return _ins(word, name, (VI[id_], VI[is_], VI[it]), _vi(is_) | _vi(it), _vi(id_))
        if sub < 0x3C:
            return _unknown(word, "lower")
        index = (sub & 3) | (id_ << 2)
        name = _LOWER_SPECIAL_EXT.get(index)
        if name is None:
            return _unknown(word, "lower")
        fsf, ftf = _BC[(word >> 21) & 3], _BC[(word >> 23) & 3]
        if name in ("move", "mr32"):
            source = "yzwx" if name == "mr32" else "xyzw"
            reads = set().union(*(_vf(is_, source[i]) for i, c in enumerate("xyzw") if c in lanes))
            return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (name, dest), (VF[it], VF[is_]), reads, _vf(it, lanes))
        if name in ("lqi", "lqd"):
            text = "(%s++)" % VI[is_] if name == "lqi" else "(--%s)" % VI[is_]
            return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (name, dest), (VF[it], text), _vi(is_), _vf(it, lanes) | _vi(is_))
        if name in ("sqi", "sqd"):
            text = "(%s++)" % VI[it] if name == "sqi" else "(--%s)" % VI[it]
            return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (name, dest), (VF[is_], text), _vf(is_, lanes) | _vi(it), _vi(it))
        if name == "div" or name == "rsqrt":
            return _ins(word, name, ("Q", VF[is_] + fsf, VF[it] + ftf),
                        _vf(is_, fsf) | _vf(it, ftf), {"Q"})
        if name == "sqrt":
            return _ins(word, name, ("Q", VF[it] + ftf), _vf(it, ftf), {"Q"})
        if name in ("waitq", "waitp"):
            return _ins(word, name, (), {name[-1].upper()})
        if name == "mtir":
            return _ins(word, name, (VI[it], VF[is_] + fsf), _vf(is_, fsf), _vi(it))
        if name == "mfir":
            return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (name, dest), (VF[it], VI[is_]), _vi(is_), _vf(it, lanes))
        if name in ("ilwr", "iswr"):
            if name == "ilwr":
                return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (name, dest), (VI[it], "(%s)" % VI[is_]), _vi(is_), _vi(it))
            return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (name, dest), (VI[it], "(%s)" % VI[is_]), _vi(is_) | _vi(it))
        if name in ("rnext", "rget"):
            return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (name, dest), (VF[it], "R"), {"R"},
                        _vf(it, lanes) | ({"R"} if name == "rnext" else set()))
        if name in ("rinit", "rxor"):
            return _ins(word, name, ("R", VF[is_] + fsf), _vf(is_, fsf) | ({"R"} if name == "rxor" else set()), {"R"})
        if name == "mfp":
            return _ins(word, "%s.%s" % (name, dest), (VF[it], "P"), {"P"}, _vf(it, lanes))
        if name in ("xtop", "xitop"):
            return _ins(word, name, (VI[it],), (), _vi(it))
        if name == "xgkick":
            return _ins(word, name, (VI[is_],), _vi(is_))
        if name in ("esadd", "ersadd", "eleng", "erleng"):
            return _ins(word, name, ("P", VF[is_]), _vf(is_, "xyz"), {"P"})
        if name == "esum":
            return _ins(word, name, ("P", VF[is_]), _vf(is_, "xyzw"), {"P"})
        if name in ("eatanxy", "eatanxz"):
            return _ins(word, name, ("P", VF[is_]), _vf(is_, "xy" if name == "eatanxy" else "xz"), {"P"})
        # esqrt ersqrt ercpr esin eatan eexp: one lane.
        return _ins(word, name, ("P", VF[is_] + fsf), _vf(is_, fsf), {"P"})

    name = _LOWER_MAIN.get(opcode)
    if name is None:
        return _unknown(word, "lower")

    if name in ("b", "bal"):
        if name == "b":
            return _ins(word, name, ("%+d" % imm11,))
        return _ins(word, name, (VI[it], "%+d" % imm11), (), _vi(it))
    if name == "jr":
        return _ins(word, name, (VI[is_],), _vi(is_))
    if name == "jalr":
        return _ins(word, name, (VI[it], VI[is_]), _vi(is_), _vi(it))
    if name in ("ibeq", "ibne"):
        return _ins(word, name, (VI[it], VI[is_], "%+d" % imm11), _vi(is_) | _vi(it))
    if name in ("ibltz", "ibgtz", "iblez", "ibgez"):
        return _ins(word, name, (VI[is_], "%+d" % imm11), _vi(is_))
    if name in ("iaddiu", "isubiu"):
        # The immediate is split, with its high bits above the register fields.
        imm15 = (word & 0x7FF) | (((word >> 21) & 0xF) << 11)
        return _ins(word, name, (VI[it], VI[is_], "0x%x" % imm15), _vi(is_), _vi(it))
    if name == "lq":
        return _ins(word, "lq.%s" % dest, (VF[it], "%d(%s)" % (imm11, VI[is_])), _vi(is_), _vf(it, lanes))
    if name == "sq":
        return _ins(word, "sq.%s" % dest, (VF[is_], "%d(%s)" % (imm11, VI[it])), _vf(is_, lanes) | _vi(it))
    if name == "ilw":
        return _ins(word, "ilw.%s" % dest, (VI[it], "%d(%s)" % (imm11, VI[is_])), _vi(is_), _vi(it))
    if name == "isw":
        return _ins(word, "isw.%s" % dest, (VI[it], "%d(%s)" % (imm11, VI[is_])), _vi(is_) | _vi(it))
    imm24 = word & 0xFFFFFF
    if name in ("fceq", "fcand", "fcor"):
        return _ins(word, name, (VI[1], "0x%06x" % imm24), {"CLIP"}, _vi(1))
    if name == "fcset":
        return _ins(word, name, ("0x%06x" % imm24,), (), {"CLIP"})
    if name == "fcget":
        return _ins(word, name, (VI[it],), {"CLIP"}, _vi(it))
    imm12 = (((word >> 21) & 1) << 11) | (word & 0x7FF)
    if name in ("fseq", "fsand", "fsor"):
        return _ins(word, name, (VI[it], "0x%03x" % imm12), {"STATUS"}, _vi(it))
    if name == "fsset":
        return _ins(word, name, ("0x%03x" % imm12,), (), {"STATUS"})
    # fmeq fmand fmor
    return _ins(word, name, (VI[it], VI[is_]), {"MAC"} | _vi(is_), _vi(it))


def decode_bundle(lower_word: int, upper_word: int, addr: int = 0) -> Bundle:
    """Decode one 8-byte bundle.

    When the I flag is set the lower word is not an instruction at all but a
    32-bit float constant, so it is reported as an immediate instead.
    """
    upper = decode_upper(upper_word)
    if upper_word & FLAG_I:
        immediate = struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", lower_word))[0]
        lower = _ins(lower_word, "loi", ("%g" % immediate,), (), {"I"})
        return Bundle(addr, lower_word, upper_word, lower, upper, immediate)
    return Bundle(addr, lower_word, upper_word, decode_lower(lower_word), upper)


def decode_blob(data: bytes, base_addr: int = 0):
    """Decode a whole microcode blob into bundles."""
    count = len(data) // 8
    out = []
    for i in range(count):
        lower, upper = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, i * 8)
        out.append(decode_bundle(lower, upper, base_addr + i * 8))
    return out


def branch_target(bundle: Bundle):
    """Where a branch in the bundle's lower goes, in bytes, or None."""
    if bundle.immediate is not None or not bundle.lower.known:
        return None
    if bundle.lower.mnemonic in ("b", "bal", "ibeq", "ibne", "ibltz", "ibgtz", "iblez", "ibgez"):
        return bundle.addr + 8 + _imm11(bundle.lower_raw) * 8
    return None


def coverage(bundles) -> dict:
    """Summarise how much of a blob decoded.

    All-zero bundles are counted separately rather than as successes.  A zero
    upper word technically decodes - opcode 0 is `addx` - but a run of zeroes is
    padding, and letting it inflate the figure would misrepresent how much real
    microcode the decoder actually understands.
    """
    total = len(bundles)
    real = [b for b in bundles if b.lower_raw or b.upper_raw]
    padding = total - len(real)
    denom = len(real)
    upper_ok = sum(1 for b in real if b.upper.known)
    lower_ok = sum(1 for b in real if b.lower.known)
    return {
        "bundles": total,
        "padding": padding,
        "real": denom,
        "upper_known": upper_ok,
        "lower_known": lower_ok,
        "both_known": sum(1 for b in real if b.fully_known),
        "programs": sum(1 for b in bundles if b.is_end),
        "upper_pct": upper_ok / denom * 100.0 if denom else 0.0,
        "lower_pct": lower_ok / denom * 100.0 if denom else 0.0,
    }

```

`ps2decomp/vu0.py`:

```py
"""VU0 in macro mode: the vector unit driven directly by COP2 instructions.

The game does its vector maths here - 62,000 COP2 instructions across about 700
functions. The state is 32 vector registers of four float lanes (VF0 is the
constant (0, 0, 0, 1)), 16 integer registers, an accumulator, and the Q, I and R
special registers.

VU arithmetic is not IEEE-754, and this module defines one model of it, which the
lifted code (runtime/src/vu0.cpp) follows bit for bit:

* An operand with a zero exponent is zero (denormals are flushed, sign kept); an
  operand with the maximum exponent - an infinity or NaN elsewhere - is the
  largest finite magnitude with its sign.
* An operation is computed in double precision and rounded to single, which is
  the correctly rounded single result; a result that overflows saturates to the
  largest finite magnitude, and one that is denormal becomes zero.
* Multiply-add rounds the product before the addition.
* MAX and MINI compare their operands as sign-and-magnitude integers and hand
  back one of them as it is, uncleaned: a denormal stays (a program builds
  integer constants with `loi` and `maxi` - Burnout 3's GIF tags), and an
  exponent of 255 is simply the largest.

That follows PCSX2's interpreter rather than the hardware, which truncates
rather than rounds in places, so a result can differ from the console's in the
last bit. A port that needs bit-exact physics must revisit this model.

The FMAC operations do not compute the MAC, status or clip flags. A program that
reads them (`cfc2` of control registers 16-18) is refused rather than handed a
flag that was never set, and so is `vcallms`, which runs VU0 microcode.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import struct

MASK32 = 0xFFFFFFFF
SIGN = 0x80000000
MAX = 0x7F7FFFFF
ONE = 0x3F800000

# Control registers: 0-15 are the integer registers VI0-VI15.
REG_STATUS, REG_MAC, REG_CLIP, REG_R, REG_I, REG_Q = 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22
# VPU-STAT: whether VU0 and VU1 are running. No microprogram runs in this model
# (vcallms is refused) and transfers to VU1 complete when they start, so both are
# always idle: it reads 0. Code that waits for VU1 polls it, so it is modelled.
REG_VPU_STAT = 29
UNREADABLE = {REG_STATUS, REG_MAC, REG_CLIP, 26}


# The operations execute() implements (mnemonics without their mask suffix).
SUPPORTED = (
    {"v%s%s" % (op, suffix) for op in ("add", "sub", "mul", "madd", "msub", "max", "mini")
     for suffix in ("", "x", "y", "z", "w", "q", "i")}
    | {"v%sa%s" % (op, suffix) for op in ("add", "sub", "mul", "madd", "msub")
       for suffix in ("", "x", "y", "z", "w", "q", "i")}
    | {"vopmula", "vopmsub", "vmove", "vmr32", "vabs", "vnop", "vwaitq", "vclipw",
       "vdiv", "vsqrt", "vrsqrt", "vmtir", "vmfir", "viadd", "visub", "viand", "vior",
       "viaddi", "vrinit", "vrxor", "vrget", "vrnext"}
    | {"vitof%d" % n for n in (0, 4, 12, 15)} | {"vftoi%d" % n for n in (0, 4, 12, 15)}
) - {"vmaxq", "vminiq", "vmaxa", "vminia"}


class Refused(Exception):
    """An instruction this model does not reproduce."""


def initial_vf():
    vf = [[0, 0, 0, 0] for _ in range(32)]
    vf[0] = [0, 0, 0, ONE]
    return vf


def initial_vc():
    vc = [0] * 32
    vc[REG_R] = ONE
    return vc


def clean(bits: int) -> int:
    exponent = bits & 0x7F800000
    if exponent == 0:
        return bits & SIGN
    if exponent == 0x7F800000:
        return (bits & SIGN) | MAX
    return bits & MASK32


def value(bits: int) -> float:
    return struct.unpack("<f", struct.pack("<I", clean(bits)))[0]


def result(number: float) -> int:
    """A double rounded to a VU single: saturated, with denormals flushed."""
    if number != number:
        return MAX
    try:
        bits = struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", number))[0]
    except OverflowError:
        return (SIGN if number < 0 else 0) | MAX
    if (bits & 0x7F800000) == 0x7F800000:
        return (bits & SIGN) | MAX
    if (bits & 0x7F800000) == 0:
        return bits & SIGN
    return bits


def vu_binary(op: str, a: int, b: int, acc: int = 0) -> int:
    """add, sub, mul, max, mini; madd and msub add to or subtract from `acc`."""
    return _binary(op, a, b, acc)


def vu_abs(x: int) -> int:
    return clean(x) & ~SIGN & MASK32


def vu_itof(x: int, shift: int) -> int:
    return result(_s32(x) / (1 << shift))


def vu_ftoi(x: int, shift: int) -> int:
    return _float_to_int(value(x) * (1 << shift))


def vu_div(num: int, den: int) -> int:
    if value(den) == 0.0:
        return ((num ^ den) & SIGN) | MAX
    return result(value(num) / value(den))


def vu_sqrt(x: int) -> int:
    return result(math.sqrt(abs(value(x))))


def vu_rsqrt(num: int, den: int) -> int:
    root = math.sqrt(abs(value(den)))
    if root == 0.0:
        return (num & SIGN) | MAX
    return result(value(num) / root)


def _fields(word: int):
    dest = (word >> 21) & 0xF
    return [lane for lane, bit in enumerate((8, 4, 2, 1)) if dest & bit]


def _binary(op: str, a: int, b: int, acc: int = 0) -> int:
    x, y = value(a), value(b)
    if op == "add":
        return result(x + y)
    if op == "sub":
        return result(x - y)
    if op == "mul":
        return result(x * y)
    if op == "madd":
        return result(value(acc) + value(result(x * y)))
    if op == "msub":
        return result(value(acc) - value(result(x * y)))
    if op == "max":
        return (b if _order(a) < _order(b) else a) & MASK32
    if op == "mini":
        return (b if _order(b) < _order(a) else a) & MASK32
    raise Refused(op)


def _order(bits: int) -> int:
    """MAX's and MINI's key: the bits as a sign-and-magnitude integer."""
    magnitude = bits & 0x7FFFFFFF
    return -magnitude if bits & SIGN else magnitude


_FMAC = ("madd", "msub", "mini", "max", "add", "sub", "mul")


def _split(base: str):
    """'vmaddax' -> ('madd', True, 'x'); 'vmulq' -> ('mul', False, 'q')."""
    name = base[1:]
    for op in _FMAC:
        if name.startswith(op):
            rest = name[len(op):]
            to_acc = rest.startswith("a") and op not in ("max", "mini")
            if to_acc:
                rest = rest[1:]
            return op, to_acc, rest
    return None, False, ""


def execute(m, word: int, mnemonic: str) -> None:
    """Run one COP2 operation on machine `m` (its vf, vc and vacc state)."""
    base = mnemonic.split(".")[0]
    fd, fs, ft = (word >> 6) & 0x1F, (word >> 11) & 0x1F, (word >> 16) & 0x1F
    vf, vc = m.vf, m.vc
    lanes = _fields(word)

    def write(index, values):
        if index != 0:
            for lane in lanes:
                vf[index][lane] = values[lane] & MASK32

    op, to_acc, operand = _split(base)
    if op is not None and base not in ("vopmula", "vopmsub"):
        if operand in ("x", "y", "z", "w"):
            b = [vf[ft]["xyzw".index(operand)]] * 4
        elif operand == "q":
            b = [vc[REG_Q]] * 4
        elif operand == "i":
            b = [vc[REG_I]] * 4
        elif operand == "":
            b = vf[ft]
        else:
            raise Refused(base)
        a = vf[fs]
        out = [_binary(op, a[lane], b[lane], m.vacc[lane]) for lane in range(4)]
        if to_acc:
            for lane in lanes:
                m.vacc[lane] = out[lane]
        else:
            write(fd, out)
        return

    if base == "vopmula":
        a, b = vf[fs], vf[ft]
        out = [result(value(a[1]) * value(b[2])), result(value(a[2]) * value(b[0])),
               result(value(a[0]) * value(b[1])), m.vacc[3]]
        for lane in lanes:
            if lane < 3:
                m.vacc[lane] = out[lane]
        return
    if base == "vopmsub":
        a, b, acc = vf[fs], vf[ft], m.vacc
        out = [_binary("msub", a[1], b[2], acc[0]), _binary("msub", a[2], b[0], acc[1]),
               _binary("msub", a[0], b[1], acc[2]), 0]
        if fd != 0:
            for lane in lanes:
                if lane < 3:
                    vf[fd][lane] = out[lane]
        return
    if base == "vmove":
        write(ft, list(vf[fs]))
        return
    if base == "vmr32":
        a = vf[fs]
        write(ft, [a[1], a[2], a[3], a[0]])
        return
    if base == "vabs":
        write(ft, [vu_abs(x) for x in vf[fs]])
        return
    if base.startswith("vitof"):
        write(ft, [vu_itof(x, int(base[5:])) for x in vf[fs]])
        return
    if base.startswith("vftoi"):
        write(ft, [vu_ftoi(x, int(base[5:])) for x in vf[fs]])
        return
    if base in ("vnop", "vwaitq", "vclipw"):
        return          # vclipw sets only the clip flag, which is not modelled
    fsf, ftf = (word >> 21) & 3, (word >> 23) & 3
    if base == "vdiv":
        vc[REG_Q] = vu_div(vf[fs][fsf], vf[ft][ftf])
        return
    if base == "vsqrt":
        vc[REG_Q] = vu_sqrt(vf[ft][ftf])
        return
    if base == "vrsqrt":
        vc[REG_Q] = vu_rsqrt(vf[fs][fsf], vf[ft][ftf])
        return
    if base == "vmtir":
        if ft != 0 and ft < 16:
            vc[ft] = vf[fs][fsf] & 0xFFFF
        return
    if base == "vmfir":
        is_ = fs
        extended = vc[is_] & 0xFFFF
        extended = (extended - 0x10000) & MASK32 if extended & 0x8000 else extended
        write(ft, [extended] * 4)
        return
    if base in ("viadd", "visub", "viand", "vior"):
        a, b = vc[fs], vc[ft]
        out = {"viadd": a + b, "visub": a - b, "viand": a & b, "vior": a | b}[base]
        if 0 < fd < 16:
            vc[fd] = out & 0xFFFF
        return
    if base == "viaddi":
        imm = fd - 32 if fd & 0x10 else fd
        if 0 < ft < 16:
            vc[ft] = (vc[fs] + imm) & 0xFFFF
        return
    if base == "vrinit":
        vc[REG_R] = ONE | (vf[fs][fsf] & 0x7FFFFF)
        return
    if base == "vrxor":
        vc[REG_R] = ONE | ((vc[REG_R] ^ vf[fs][fsf]) & 0x7FFFFF)
        return
    if base == "vrget":
        write(ft, [vc[REG_R]] * 4)
        return
    if base == "vrnext":
        if ft == 0:
            return
        r = vc[REG_R]
        bit = ((r >> 4) & 1) ^ ((r >> 22) & 1)
        vc[REG_R] = ONE | ((((r << 1) & MASK32) ^ bit) & 0x7FFFFF)
        write(ft, [vc[REG_R]] * 4)
        return
    raise Refused(base)


def _s32(x: int) -> int:
    x &= MASK32
    return x - (1 << 32) if x & SIGN else x


def _float_to_int(number: float) -> int:
    if number >= 2147483647.0:
        return 0x7FFFFFFF
    if number <= -2147483648.0:
        return 0x80000000
    return int(number) & MASK32


def move_to(m, word: int, mnemonic: str, rt_value: int, rt_high: int) -> None:
    """qmtc2 rt, vfd and ctc2 rt, id: write VU0 state from a general register."""
    index = (word >> 11) & 0x1F
    if mnemonic == "qmtc2":
        if index:
            m.vf[index] = [rt_value & MASK32, (rt_value >> 32) & MASK32,
                           rt_high & MASK32, (rt_high >> 32) & MASK32]
        return
    if index < 16:
        if index:
            m.vc[index] = rt_value & 0xFFFF
    elif index == REG_R:
        m.vc[REG_R] = ONE | (rt_value & 0x7FFFFF)
    else:
        m.vc[index] = rt_value & MASK32


def move_from(m, word: int, mnemonic: str):
    """qmfc2 rt, vfs and cfc2 rt, id: (low 64 bits, high 64 bits or None)."""
    index = (word >> 11) & 0x1F
    if mnemonic == "qmfc2":
        v = m.vf[index]
        return v[0] | (v[1] << 32), v[2] | (v[3] << 32)
    if index in UNREADABLE:
        raise Refused("cfc2 of control register %d (flags are not modelled)" % index)
    if index == REG_VPU_STAT:
        return 0, None
    return m.vc[index], None

```

`runtime/include/ps2rt/generated.h`:

```h
/*
 * Support declarations for the derived accessor functions.
 *
 * The derived functions in src/generated/ read memory through these helpers
 * rather than casting integers to pointers directly. Two reasons: the emitted
 * source stays readable, and a port can define them over whatever memory model it
 * ends up using instead of assuming a flat PS2 address space.
 *
 * Recovered struct types are views over these same helpers; see the generated
 * src/generated/types.h.
 *
 * Every value in the derived code is a u64, because that is the width of an EE
 * general register and the width the derivations were verified at. Arguments are
 * u64 for the same reason: a 32-bit value arrives in its register sign-extended,
 * which is what passing an s32 to a u64 parameter does.
 */

#ifndef PS2RT_GENERATED_H
#define PS2RT_GENERATED_H

#include <cstring>

#include "ps2rt/types.h"

namespace generated {

/*
 * Reads from the game's address space (ReadS8 ... ReadU64 below); on the console
 * they are plain loads.
 *
 * The signed variants matter: the original uses `lb`/`lh`/`lw` (sign-extending)
 * in some places and `lbu`/`lhu` (zero-extending) in others, and the derived code
 * preserves that distinction because callers can depend on it.
 *
 * Each returns the value as it lands in a 64-bit register - already sign- or
 * zero-extended to a u64 - because that is what the derived code computes on.
 * Returning the narrow type instead lets C++'s promotion rules decide the width
 * of the arithmetic, and those make `ReadU8(p) << 24` a signed `int` shift.
 */
/*
 * Main RAM, which almost every access reaches, can be given to the derived code
 * directly: a port that sets `ram_base` to its 32 MB lets the reads and writes
 * below load and store there inline - at 0x00000000, its uncached mirrors
 * 0x20000000 and 0x30000000, and kseg0/kseg1 - and sends everything else (the
 * device registers, the scratchpad, an access running off the end) through the
 * port's functions above. `ram_watched` sends writes through them too, for a
 * port watching addresses.
 */
extern u8* ram_base;
extern bool ram_watched;
/* The scratchpad's 16 KB at 0x70000000, given the same way (or null). */
extern u8* scratchpad_base;

inline u8* RamPointer(u32 address, u32 size) {
    if (address - 0x80000000u < 0x40000000u) address &= 0x1FFFFFFFu;
    const u32 window = address >> 28;
    if (window == 7) {
        const u32 offset = address - 0x70000000u;
        return scratchpad_base && offset + size <= 0x4000u ? scratchpad_base + offset : nullptr;
    }
    if (!ram_base || (window != 0 && window != 2 && window != 3)) return nullptr;
    const u32 offset = address & 0x0FFFFFFFu;
    return offset + size <= (32u << 20) ? ram_base + offset : nullptr;
}

template <typename T>
inline bool RamLoad(u32 address, T* value) {
    const u8* p = RamPointer(address, sizeof(T));
    if (!p) return false;
    std::memcpy(value, p, sizeof(T));
    return true;
}

template <typename T>
inline bool RamStore(u32 address, T value) {
    if (ram_watched) return false;
    u8* p = RamPointer(address, sizeof(T));
    if (!p) return false;
    std::memcpy(p, &value, sizeof(T));
    return true;
}

/* The port's own, for what is not main RAM. */
u64 PortRead(u32 address, u32 size, bool is_signed);
void PortWrite(u32 address, u64 value, u32 size);

inline u64 ReadS8(u32 a) { s8 v; return RamLoad(a, &v) ? u64(s64(v)) : PortRead(a, 1, true); }
inline u64 ReadU8(u32 a) { u8 v; return RamLoad(a, &v) ? u64(v) : PortRead(a, 1, false); }
inline u64 ReadS16(u32 a) { s16 v; return RamLoad(a, &v) ? u64(s64(v)) : PortRead(a, 2, true); }
inline u64 ReadU16(u32 a) { u16 v; return RamLoad(a, &v) ? u64(v) : PortRead(a, 2, false); }
inline u64 ReadS32(u32 a) { s32 v; return RamLoad(a, &v) ? u64(s64(v)) : PortRead(a, 4, true); }
inline u64 ReadU32(u32 a) { u32 v; return RamLoad(a, &v) ? u64(v) : PortRead(a, 4, false); }
inline u64 ReadU64(u32 a) { u64 v; return RamLoad(a, &v) ? v : PortRead(a, 8, false); }

/*
 * Guest stack, for a derived function whose frame a callee can see - one that
 * passes the address of a local, an out-parameter. StackEnter reserves `size`
 * bytes below the current guest stack pointer and returns the new one;
 * StackLeave releases them. Derived code that only spills registers needs no
 * guest stack at all.
 */
u64 StackEnter(u32 size);
void StackLeave(u32 size);

/*
 * A `break` the original executes: a trap (an assertion's failure, usually).
 * The derivation ends that path here; whatever hosts derived code stops the
 * run there, as the console raises the exception. It does not return. (Not
 * `Trap`: lifted::Trap is the lifted code's, and structured code sees both.)
 */
void TrapAt(u32 address);

/*
 * A call through a function pointer or a virtual method: `address` is the guest
 * address the original code jumps to. A port maps guest addresses to its own
 * functions; the arguments are the full register argument vector - eight integer,
 * then eight float - since which function is reached, and so what it reads, is
 * only known at run time. Returns $v0.
 */
u64 CallPointer(u32 address, u64 arg0 = 0, u64 arg1 = 0, u64 arg2 = 0, u64 arg3 = 0,
                u64 arg4 = 0, u64 arg5 = 0, u64 arg6 = 0, u64 arg7 = 0,
                u64 farg0 = 0, u64 farg1 = 0, u64 farg2 = 0, u64 farg3 = 0,
                u64 farg4 = 0, u64 farg5 = 0, u64 farg6 = 0, u64 farg7 = 0);

/* Writes, for the derived functions that have memory effects. */
inline void Write8(u32 a, u32 v) { if (!RamStore(a, u8(v))) PortWrite(a, v, 1); }
inline void Write16(u32 a, u32 v) { if (!RamStore(a, u16(v))) PortWrite(a, v, 2); }
inline void Write32(u32 a, u32 v) { if (!RamStore(a, u32(v))) PortWrite(a, v, 4); }
inline void Write64(u32 a, u64 v) { if (!RamStore(a, v)) PortWrite(a, v, 8); }

/*
 * Single-precision arithmetic over raw bit patterns.
 *
 * Operands and results are 32-bit patterns rather than `float`, because that is
 * what the hardware registers hold: `lwc1`, `swc1`, `mtc1` and `mfc1` move all 32
 * bits without interpreting them, so a copy must preserve a payload exactly.
 * Interpretation belongs to the arithmetic, which is why it lives here.
 *
 * Two Emotion Engine behaviours a port must reproduce rather than "fix":
 *
 *  - The FPU is not IEEE-754. There are no infinities and no NaNs; an operation
 *    that overflows **saturates** to the largest representable magnitude
 *    (0x7F7FFFFF). Letting it produce an infinity instead will make physics
 *    diverge.
 *  - Division by zero does not trap. It yields zero.
 */
/* A double result as the EE's FPU leaves it in single precision: saturated, NaN
   to zero, rounded toward zero, denormals flushed (eefpu.cpp). */
u32 FloatNarrow(double value);
u32 FloatAdd(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 FloatSub(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 FloatMul(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 FloatDiv(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 FloatMin(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 FloatMax(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 FloatNeg(u32 a);
u32 FloatAbs(u32 a);
u32 FloatSqrt(u32 a);
u32 FloatMove(u32 a);

/* 32-bit division as the EE does it (div/divu), results sign-extended into a
   register: quotient and remainder. A zero divisor gives a defined result - see
   engine/ps2decomp/emu.py, divide(). */
u64 DivQuot(u64 a, u64 b);
u64 DivRem(u64 a, u64 b);
u64 DivQuotU(u64 a, u64 b);
u64 DivRemU(u64 a, u64 b);

/* acc + a * b and acc - a * b, rounded once: the FPU accumulator forms. */
u32 FloatMulAdd(u32 acc, u32 a, u32 b);
u32 FloatMulSub(u32 acc, u32 a, u32 b);

/* VU0 arithmetic on one lane, as engine/ps2decomp/vu0.py models it (operands
   flushed and clamped, results rounded and saturated). Shared with lifted code. */
u32 VuAdd(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 VuSub(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 VuMul(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 VuMax(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 VuMin(u32 a, u32 b);
u32 VuMadd(u32 acc, u32 a, u32 b);
u32 VuMsub(u32 acc, u32 a, u32 b);
u32 VuAbs(u32 a);
u32 VuItof(u32 a, u32 shift);
u32 VuFtoi(u32 a, u32 shift);
u32 VuDiv(u32 num, u32 den);
u32 VuSqrt(u32 a);
u32 VuRsqrt(u32 num, u32 den);

/* Conversions between float bit patterns and integers. */
u32 FloatFromInt(u32 bits_as_int);
u32 IntFromFloat(u32 float_bits);

/* Interprets a bit pattern as a float, for use in comparisons. */
float FloatValue(u32 bits);

/* The bit pattern of a float constant, so the source can say `FloatBits(-1.0f)`
   rather than `0xBF800000`. Every literal emitted converts back exactly. */
u32 FloatBits(float value);

}  // namespace generated

#endif  /* PS2RT_GENERATED_H */

```

`runtime/include/ps2rt/lifted.h`:

```h
/*
 * Support for lifted functions: machine code translated instruction by instruction.
 *
 * A derived function (generated.h) is an expression over its arguments and reads
 * like source. A lifted function is a mechanical translation over an explicit
 * register context: every instruction becomes one statement that does exactly
 * what the R5900 does, branches become gotos, and calls pass the whole context.
 * It is less readable, but every function the interpreter can run can be lifted,
 * whatever its size or control flow, and each one is verified the same way: run
 * against the original machine code, comparing the entire register file and every
 * byte of memory written.
 *
 * The semantics follow engine/ps2decomp/emu.py exactly - the interpreter is the
 * reference both are tested against.
 */

#ifndef PS2RT_LIFTED_H
#define PS2RT_LIFTED_H

#include "ps2rt/generated.h"
#include "ps2rt/types.h"

namespace lifted {

/* The register state a function runs on, and the only state it has. */
struct Context {
    u64 r[32];      /* general registers, low 64 bits */
    u64 rh[32];     /* their upper 64 bits, for lq/sq and the 128-bit MMI ops */
    u64 hi, lo;     /* multiply/divide results */
    u64 hi1, lo1;   /* the second pipeline's, as mult1/div1 use */
    u32 f[32];      /* FPU registers, as raw bit patterns */
    u32 acc;        /* the FPU accumulator, as a bit pattern */
    u32 fcc;        /* the FPU condition flag */
    s64 budget;     /* loop iterations left before the run is abandoned */
    u32 vf[32][4];  /* VU0 vector registers, x y z w, as bit patterns */
    u32 vc[32];     /* VU0 control registers: VI0-VI15, then R (20), I (21), Q (22) */
    u32 vacc[4];    /* VU0 accumulator */
    u32 sa;         /* the shift amount qfsrv uses, in bits */
    /* Set by another thread to get control at this context's next loop head
       (Tick), whatever its budget: the host's blank timer, in real time. */
    u32 attention;
};

/* Thrown, and caught at the entry point, when a run cannot go on: a trap
   instruction, an exhausted loop budget, or a callee that failed. */
struct Abort {
    u32 address;
    u32 reason;     /* 1 trap, 2 budget, 3 callee failed, 4 memory fault, 5 COP2 */
};

/* Calls `target` with the whole context, as a jal or jalr does; returns when the
   callee returns. Defined by whatever hosts the lifted code. */
void Call(Context& c, u32 target);

/* The same, with the link register set first: a jal written as one call. */
inline void Call(Context& c, u32 target, u32 return_address) {
    c.r[31] = return_address;
    Call(c, target);
}

/* Transfers control to `target` for good, as a jump out of the function does:
   it runs until control comes back to `return_address` with the stack pointer at
   or above `entry_sp`, which is when the lifted function itself has returned. */
void TailCall(Context& c, u32 target, u32 return_address, u32 entry_sp);

/* A syscall: the host decides what the service does. */
void Syscall(Context& c);

/* A word result, sign-extended into its 64-bit register as the EE does. */
inline u64 Sx32(u64 value) { return (u64)(s64)(s32)(u32)value; }

inline u64 Read64(u32 address) { return generated::ReadU64(address); }

/* A loop head reached with the budget spent. Without a hook the run is
   abandoned. A host that sets `loop_head_hook` is called instead: it can zero a
   context's budget to get control at that context's next loop head - to deliver
   an interrupt, say - and throws Abort itself when the run must stop. */
extern void (*loop_head_hook)(Context& c, u32 address);
void BudgetSpent(Context& c, u32 address);

/* At every loop head, so a loop that never ends cannot hang the host - and
   where another thread gets control of it (`attention`). Not by zeroing the
   budget from there: a loop stores its budget every few cycles, and the store
   still in its core's buffer lands after the other thread's zero - Resident
   Evil Outbreak's spin on a flag (0x0018D650) lost nearly every one, and its
   menus' frames waited 20-80 ms for a blank the timer had long delivered.
   The flag is only read here, never written, so it is never lost. */
inline void Tick(Context& c, u32 address) {
    if (--c.budget < 0 || *static_cast<volatile u32*>(&c.attention)) BudgetSpent(c, address);
}

inline void Trap(u32 address) { throw Abort{address, 1}; }

/* 32x32 multiply into HI/LO, as mult/multu/madd do; the caller copies LO to rd. */
void Multiply(u64& hi, u64& lo, u64 a, u64 b, bool is_signed, bool accumulate);
void Divide(u64& hi, u64& lo, u64 a, u64 b, bool is_signed);

/* Single-precision arithmetic is generated.h's (FloatAdd, IntFromFloat, ...),
   shared with the derived code; comparisons use FloatValue. This is the one the
   accumulator needs besides: acc + a * b (or acc - a * b), rounded once. */
u32 FloatMulAdd(u32 acc, u32 a, u32 b, bool subtract);

/* Per-byte 128-bit add and subtract (paddb, psubb). */
void AddBytes(u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 alo, u64 ahi, u64 blo, u64 bhi, bool subtract);

/* Lane-wise 128-bit MMI operations: each lane of rs (a) and rt (b). */
enum LaneOp { kPmaxw = 1, kPminw, kPsubw, kPadduw, kPaddub, kPabsw, kPaddw, kPaddh,
              /* all ones where rs > rt (signed) or rs == rt; signed halfword max/min */
              kPcgtb, kPcgth, kPcgtw, kPceqb, kPceqh, kPceqw, kPmaxh, kPminh };
void Lanes(int op, u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 alo, u64 ahi, u64 blo, u64 bhi);
/* Lanes and Interleave lane by lane: the model their SSE2 forms are checked against. */
void LanesScalar(int op, u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 alo, u64 ahi, u64 blo, u64 bhi);
void InterleaveScalar(u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 a, u64 b, u32 width);
void ShiftHalfwordsRight(u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 blo, u64 bhi, u32 amount);   /* psrlh */

/* More 128-bit MMI: lane shifts (kind 0 sll, 1 srl, 2 sra), the low-doubleword
   interleave (pextlb/pextlh), ppach, and qfsrv's funnel shift by `sa` bits. */
void ShiftLanes(u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 blo, u64 bhi, u32 width, u32 kind, u32 amount);
/* ShiftLanes lane by lane: the model its SSE2 form is checked against. */
void ShiftLanesScalar(u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 blo, u64 bhi, u32 width, u32 kind, u32 amount);
void Interleave(u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 a, u64 b, u32 width);
void PackHalfwords(u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 alo, u64 ahi, u64 blo, u64 bhi);
void PackBytes(u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 alo, u64 ahi, u64 blo, u64 bhi);     /* ppacb */
void FunnelShift(u64& lo, u64& hi, u64 alo, u64 ahi, u64 blo, u64 bhi, u32 sa);

/* rsqrt.s: fs / sqrt(|ft|), the largest magnitude with fs's sign for a zero root. */
u32 FloatRsqrt(u32 fs, u32 ft);

/* Unaligned loads (they merge into the register's old value) and stores. */
u64 LoadWordLeft(u32 address, u64 old);
u64 LoadWordRight(u32 address, u64 old);
u64 LoadDoubleLeft(u32 address, u64 old);
u64 LoadDoubleRight(u32 address, u64 old);
void StoreLeft(u32 address, u64 value, u32 size);
void StoreRight(u32 address, u64 value, u32 size);

/* VU0 in macro mode (runtime/src/vu0.cpp, mirroring engine/ps2decomp/vu0.py):
   an arithmetic COP2 instruction, and the moves between it and the core. */
void Cop2(Context& c, u32 word);
/* COP2's FMAC operations (ADD, SUB, MUL, MADD, MSUB, MAX, MINI, with their
   broadcast, Q, I and accumulator forms), decoded once and run as often as
   needed - the VU interpreter keeps them per instruction. Cop2 runs them the
   same way. */
struct FmacOp {
    int op = 0;                     /* the arithmetic (vu0.cpp's Op) */
    int operand = 0;                /* the second operand: 0-3 a lane of ft, 4 Q, 5 I, 6 ft */
    bool to_acc = false;            /* into ACC rather than fd */
    u32 fd = 0, fs = 0, ft = 0, dest = 0;
};
bool DecodeFmac(u32 word, FmacOp* out);
void RunFmac(Context& c, const FmacOp& op);
/* Its result alone, the fields dest names (the rest 0), written nowhere: for
   an operation into VF0, which keeps 0, 0, 0, 1 but whose flags are this
   result's. */
void FmacResult(const Context& c, const FmacOp& op, u32 out[4]);
/* The same, a lane at a time through the arithmetic model (vu_math.h):
   what RunFmac's four lanes at once must equal. */
void RunFmacScalar(Context& c, const FmacOp& op);
void Cop2Move(Context& c, u32 word, u32 rt);
/* vcallms / vcallmsr: VU0 runs the microprogram at `address` (bytes in its
   instruction memory) on the registers macro mode shares with it. Defined by
   whatever hosts the lifted code. */
void Vcallms(Context& c, u32 address);

}  // namespace lifted

#endif  /* PS2RT_LIFTED_H */

```

`runtime/include/ps2rt/types.h`:

```h
/*
 * Fixed-width types for the decompiled sources.
 *
 * The PS2 toolchain of the era spelled these as bare typedefs, and the
 * decompiled code keeps that spelling so the source reads the way the original
 * would have.  They are defined against <cstdint> so the same sources also
 * build on a modern host compiler for the eventual port.
 */

#ifndef PS2RT_TYPES_H
#define PS2RT_TYPES_H

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

using s8  = std::int8_t;
using s16 = std::int16_t;
using s32 = std::int32_t;
using s64 = std::int64_t;

using u8  = std::uint8_t;
using u16 = std::uint16_t;
using u32 = std::uint32_t;
using u64 = std::uint64_t;

using f32 = float;
using f64 = double;

/*
 * The Emotion Engine's 128-bit quadword. Several of the game's hot paths move
 * data a quadword at a time via lq/sq, so the type is named explicitly rather
 * than hidden behind a pair of u64s.
 */
struct u128 {
    u64 lo;
    u64 hi;
};

static_assert(sizeof(u128) == 16, "u128 must be exactly one quadword");

#endif  /* PS2RT_TYPES_H */
```
